title: Browser Native Spellcheck Suppression & Firefox Double Underline Elimination
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher suppresses browser-native spellcheck underlines in Firefox to deliver crisp, single wavy highlights through its custom in-app proofing engine.
content:
Browser Native Spellcheck Suppression & Firefox Double Underline Elimination
Proofreading publications requires clear, distraction-free visual feedback. Open Publisher features a custom, publication-grade proofing engine that renders crisp red wavy underlines for spelling mistakes and gentle green wavy underlines for grammatical and punctuation suggestions. However, in Mozilla Firefox, users noticed duplicate red squiggly underlines beneath misspelled words. This visual stutter occurred because Firefox ran its native browser spellchecker simultaneously alongside Open Publisher's custom proofing engine. Version 5.7.6 introduced a dual-layer suppression architecture that completely eliminates native browser underlines while preserving the app's advanced proofing engine.
🔍High-Contrast In-App Proofing Highlights in Firefox Misspelled words render with a single high-contrast red wavy underline across all browser engines and zoom levels.
The Browser Discrepancy & Firefox Duplicate Underlines
The root cause of the duplicate underline bug originated from divergent browser behavior inside transformed canvas containers:
Chromium Container Behavior: Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, NW.js, Opera, Vivaldi) automatically suppress native browser spellcheck marks on editable elements placed inside CSS-transformed or scaled containers (such as Open Publisher's canvas zoom container). As a result, only Open Publisher's custom highlights rendered in Chromium.
Gecko Transform Rendering: Firefox (Gecko) does not suppress native spellcheck inside transformed containers. Because <body spellcheck="true"> was originally enabled, Firefox's native Hunspell dictionary ran concurrently with Open Publisher's proofing engine, drawing two conflicting wavy lines under misspelled words.
Dual-Layer Suppression Architecture
Version 5.7.6 implemented an ironclad two-tier defense across the Document Object Model and CSS styling:
DOM-Level Enforcement: Enforces spellcheck="false" globally on the document <body> in index.html , on boot initialization in core/boot.js , during page load in core/pages.js , and on all newly created text boxes in elements/text/text.js .
CSS-Level Pseudo-Element Suppression: In style.css , native browser pseudo-elements ( ::spelling-error and ::grammar-error ) are comprehensively overridden across all selectors with text-decoration: none !important; -webkit-text-decoration: none !important; .
Decoupled In-App Proofing via data-spellcheck="false"
To prevent Open Publisher's in-app proofing engine from shutting itself down due to the global spellcheck="false" attribute, the proofing scanner was decoupled from standard HTML attributes:
Dedicated Opt-Out Attribute: In tools/proofing/spellcheck-engine.js , element eligibility checks now inspect data-spellcheck="false" instead of standard HTML spellcheck="false" .
Modern CSS Custom Highlight API: The in-app proofing engine continues to paint high-contrast wavy underlines using CSS.highlights ( ::highlight(spelling-error) and ::highlight(grammar-error) ).
Interactive Status Bar Toggle: Users can toggle spellcheck on and off at any time using the proofing icon in the bottom status bar, cleanly clearing or re-analyzing highlights across the document.
Tip: The CSS Custom Highlight API paints wavy proofing marks with vector precision at any zoom level without altering the DOM structure of your text boxes.

title: CMYK Commercial Print Mode
excerpt: Preview how your colours will shift in commercial print with Open Publisher's CMYK Soft-Proof mode, which applies a real-time SVG filter to simulate physical ink output.
content:
CMYK Commercial Print Mode
Professional printing services work in the CMYK colour model (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Key/Black) rather than the RGB model used by screens. CMYK has a smaller colour gamut - it cannot reproduce certain vivid neon or electric colours that look brilliant on screen. A design that appears vibrant on your monitor can look noticeably duller when printed with physical ink.
Open Publisher’s CMYK Soft-Proof mode lets you preview exactly how your colours will shift before sending your file to a commercial printer, so there are no surprises when the physical copies arrive.
Enabling CMYK Mode
Go to File > Info .
Find the Colour Mode toggle and switch from RGB to CMYK .
When CMYK mode is active, Open Publisher applies a custom SVG soft-proof filter across the entire canvas. Vivid, out-of-gamut colours - such as neon greens, electric blues, and hot pinks - are intelligently dulled to give you an accurate real-time preview of how the document will look when printed with physical ink.
Switch back to RGB at any time to return to the full screen-accurate colour display. Your selected colour model is saved into the .opub file and persists between sessions.
When to Use It
CMYK mode is most useful when:
Designing flyers, brochures, or any document that will be sent to a commercial print shop.
Working with bright or vivid brand colours that may not survive the RGB-to-CMYK conversion faithfully.
Checking whether a full-bleed background or image will retain its intended appearance in physical print.

title: Offline Dictionary & Spellchecker Overhaul
excerpt: Explore Open Publisher
content:
Offline Dictionary & Spellchecker Overhaul Accurate, dependable spellchecking is vital for publication publishing. Previous proofing iterations relied on third-party remote API services that introduced network latency, rate limits, missing everyday words (falsely flagging common terms like "highlight" and "highlighted"), offset drift that caused squiggly underlines to start mid-word or span into adjacent blocks, and unrelated suggestions. Version 5.8.5 delivered a complete architectural overhaul, bundling a dedicated 274,000+ word curated offline English lexicon, direct DOM text-node token scanning, and sub-millisecond local phonetic suggestions. 📖 Instant Offline Spellchecking with Contextual Suggestions Misspelled words receive instant local proofing underlines with zero network latency and accurate suggestions on right-click. Comprehensive Curated Offline English Lexicon (274,000+ Words) Version 5.8.5 eliminated remote network proofing dependencies entirely: High-Speed Curated Lexicon: Bundled tools/proofing/dictionary.js combining SCOWL (standard Chromium/Firefox dictionary) and ENABLE1, containing 274,757 curated words loaded into an instant O(1) Set . Zero False Positives for Everyday Words: Words like highlight , highlighted , highlights , highlighter , and highlighting are fully recognized. US, UK & Commonwealth Orthography: Built-in support for both American and British variations (such as colour , favourite , theatre , realise , centre , dialogue , and travelling ). Specialized Prepress & Publishing Vocabulary: Comprehensive vocabulary including bleed , kerning , leading , tracking , cmyk , dpi , ppi , vector , raster , imposition , and dropcap . Direct Text-Node Token Scanning (Zero Offset Drift) Underline misalignment and mid-word squiggles were resolved at the DOM architecture level: The Root Cause of Drift: Remote APIs calculated character offsets against innerText (which inserts newline characters for block elements like
,

, and
). In-app traversals counted textContent without newlines, causing DOM ranges to drift progressively across lines. Direct TreeWalker Scanning: Upgraded paintHighlights() in tools/proofing/spellcheck-engine.js to scan DOM text nodes directly using TreeWalker(NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT) and regex word boundary tokenization ( /[A-Za-z]+(?:['’][A-Za-z]+)?/g ). Precise Range Construction: Range objects are constructed strictly on (textNode, match.index, match.index + rawWord.length) , guaranteeing squiggly underlines never start mid-word, underline partial words, or span across block boundaries. Instant Phonetic & Damerau-Levenshtein Suggestions Contextual replacement suggestions are generated locally in sub-millisecond time: Local Phonetic Matching: Right-clicking misspelled words calculates intelligent phonetic and edit-distance matches locally (e.g. highlite → highlight , recieve → receive , seperate → separate ). Casing Preservation: Capitalized inputs produce capitalized suggestions ( Hightlight → Highlight ), and uppercase inputs generate uppercase replacements. Full Options Suite Preservation: Preserved Custom Dictionary management with word deletion, Ignored Words, Ignored Grammar Rules, and Autocorrect shortcuts. Tip: You can add specialized company names and proprietary technical terms directly to your Custom Dictionary in the Options dialog. 30,000-Word Vocabulary Expansion (Brands & Proper Nouns) Version 5.9.6 expanded the local English proofing dictionary with more than 30,000 modern brand names, high-street supermarkets, retailers, common acronyms, and geographic regions across the UK and US. This substantial offline vocabulary upgrade prevents red squiggly underlines from cluttering marketing flyers, newsletters, and promotional coupons that frequently cite established commercial brand names. Single-Letter Word Recognition ('A', 'I', 'O') Version 5.10.5 optimized word token validation in the proofing engine to recognize valid standalone English single-letter words ("A", "I", and poetic "O"). These entries are pre-seeded in the fast-path dictionary cache, eliminating false-positive red spelling underlines in sentences like "A quick start" or "I am writing", while preserving contextual grammar rules that prompt for uppercase "I" when typed in lowercase. Publishing Vocabulary Expansion & Template Spellcheck Stabilization (v5.18.8) Nothing detracts from layout design like false-positive red underlines beneath legitimate publishing and design terms. In OpenPublisher v5.18.8 , the offline dictionary received a massive expansion: Comprehensive offline proofing dictionary expansion in OpenPublisher v5.18.8. Over 2,500 domain-specific terms across desktop publishing, graphic arts, culinary arts, corporate finance, and seasonal events were ingested into the client dictionary. Built-in templates now open with clean, underline-free copy. Global Names & Cultural Vocabulary Recognition (v5.19.7) Following user feedback on certificates, invitations, and family announcements, OpenPublisher v5.19.7 added over 1,800 globally popular first names, surnames, and geographical landmarks: Global names and cultural vocabulary recognition in OpenPublisher v5.19.7. Names on graduation diplomas, wedding invitations, and volunteer badges are recognized without false alerts, keeping your design view clean and distraction-free.

title: Spell Check
excerpt: Get desktop-grade spelling suggestions in Open Publisher via the right-click menu, powered by the LanguageTool API with smart word detection and undo history support.
content:
Spell Check
Open Publisher provides desktop-grade spell check suggestions built directly into the right-click context menu, powered by the LanguageTool API . Corrections are applied instantly with full undo support, so fixing a misspelling is always safe and reversible.
Using Spell Check
Right-click on any word underlined with the browser’s red squiggly spell-check indicator.
A “Checking spelling…” spinner appears briefly at the top of the context menu while the LanguageTool API fetches corrections.
Up to three top spelling suggestions appear in the menu, each marked with a magic wand icon.
Click any suggestion to instantly replace the misspelled word, preserving your existing formatting and adding the correction to the undo history.
Bulletproof Word Detection
To reliably identify exactly which word you right-clicked, Open Publisher uses a three-tier detection approach:
Tier 1 - Checks whether you explicitly highlighted the word before right-clicking.
Tier 2 - Uses the X/Y pixel coordinates of your click to locate the nearest text node on the page.
Tier 3 - Falls back to the current cursor (caret) position if the click did not land directly on the text.
This layered approach ensures the correct word is always identified and corrected, regardless of how precisely you clicked.

title: The Accessibility Checker
excerpt: Run the Open Publisher Accessibility Checker to find and fix missing alt text, low colour contrast, and illogical heading structure for full WCAG 2.1 compliance.
content:
The Accessibility Checker
The Accessibility Checker scans your entire document for common accessibility violations and provides a dedicated task pane with one-click fixes, ensuring your publications are fully readable by screen readers and comply with WCAG 2.1 guidelines.
Running the Accessibility Checker
Go to the Review ribbon tab.
Click Accessibility Checker .
The Accessibility task pane slides out on the right and scans across all pages.
What It Checks
The checker flags three types of issue:
Missing Alt Text (High severity) - Images without a descriptive alt attribute. Screen readers will be unable to describe these to visually impaired users.
Low Colour Contrast (High severity) - Text and background colour combinations that do not meet WCAG 2.1 minimum contrast ratios.
Illogical Heading Structure (Medium severity) - Detects missing H1 headings, skipped heading levels (for example, jumping from H1 directly to H3), and pages with no headings at all.
Fixing Issues
For each flagged issue, the task pane shows a colour-coded severity indicator (red for high, orange for medium), a description of the problem, and a Fix Issue button that instantly navigates to the offending element and triggers the appropriate repair workflow - for example, opening the Alt Text dialog for a missing alt attribute, or applying a high-contrast theme for a contrast failure.
Auto-Fix Missing Titles
The scanner can automatically generate and insert an H1 page title on any page that is missing one, directly from the Fix Issue button - no manual editing required.

title: The Design Checker
excerpt: Run the Open Publisher Design Checker before printing or sharing to find text overflow, low-resolution images, and off-page objects, with one-click navigation to each issue.
content:
The Design Checker
The Design Checker is a pre-flight diagnostic tool that scans your document for potential problems before you print or share it. Running it before every export is a good habit - it catches issues that are easy to miss visually but that can significantly affect the quality of your printed or shared output.
Running the Design Checker
Go to File > Info > Run Design Checker .
A report is generated listing all flagged issues found across your document.
What It Checks
Text Overflow - Text boxes where typed content exceeds the visible box boundary. Any text beyond the boundary would be cut off in the final output without any visible warning on screen.
Low-Resolution Images - Images that have been stretched beyond their native pixel dimensions, flagged as a pixelation risk when printed. What looks acceptable on screen can appear blurry or blocky in physical print.
Off-Page Objects - Elements that are partially or completely outside the page boundary and would be clipped or absent from the exported or printed output.
Navigating to Issues
Each flagged issue in the report has a crosshair button . Clicking it closes the report, scrolls directly to the problem element, selects it, and flashes a red highlight around it - so you can locate and fix the issue immediately without having to search for it manually.

title: The Integrated Thesaurus
excerpt: Look up synonyms and replace words instantly with Open Publisher's built-in Thesaurus, powered by the LanguageTool API with smart capitalisation preservation.
content:
The Integrated Thesaurus
Enhance your writing, avoid repetitive language, and find the exact word you need without ever leaving your workspace. The Thesaurus is built directly into Open Publisher to streamline your editing process - meaning no more switching tabs, browsing external websites, or tedious copy-pasting. Powered by the reliable LanguageTool API , a rich library of synonyms is fetched live in real-time and can be seamlessly applied to your document with a single click.
Using the Thesaurus
Replacing a word is designed to be quick and intuitive. Just follow these steps:
Navigate to your document and highlight any single word you wish to change. This works across standard text boxes, headers, footers, or within table cells.
Go to the top menu ribbon and click Review > Thesaurus .
The dedicated Thesaurus sidebar will smoothly slide out on the right-hand side of your screen, displaying a comprehensive list of synonyms tailored to your highlighted word.
Browse the suggestions and click any synonym to instantly replace the highlighted word in your active document.
Smart Auto-Replace
Open Publisher is designed to respect the flow and formatting of your document. When you click a synonym, our Smart Auto-Replace feature automatically preserves the original word’s capitalisation. For example, if the original word was written in Title Case or ALL CAPS, the new replacement is dynamically capitalised to match exactly. Your document’s formatting is never disrupted by a thesaurus swap, saving you from manual proofreading and corrections.
Clipboard Fallback
We’ve also built in safeguards to protect your document’s integrity. If you happen to open the Thesaurus and click on a synonym without having any text actively highlighted on the page, Open Publisher employs a handy Clipboard Fallback. Instead of attempting to replace text (which could cause errors) or inserting the word randomly, the system safely copies your chosen synonym directly to your system’s clipboard. A brief notification will appear to confirm this action, allowing you to easily paste the word exactly where you want it without risking accidental changes.
Tips for Best Results
Select Single Words: The Thesaurus is optimized for individual vocabulary words. Highlighting entire phrases or sentences may not return accurate suggestions.
Stay Connected: Because synonyms are fetched live via the LanguageTool API, ensure you have an active internet connection to load the latest suggestions.

title: The Page Parts Library
excerpt: Insert 20 professional drag-and-drop Page Parts in Open Publisher  -  from callouts and testimonials to stat blocks and event dates  -  all inheriting your document's colours and fonts.
content:
The Page Parts Library
The Page Parts library provides 20 professional, drag-and-drop structural building blocks that automatically inherit your document’s current colour scheme and fonts. Rather than building common layout components from scratch, you can insert a ready-made, on-brand block and simply fill it with your content.
Opening the Page Parts Library
Go to Insert > Page Parts . The library opens and displays all available components.
Available Page Parts
Info Callout - Tinted box with a thick left-hand colour accent, ideal for tips or warnings.
Contact Block - Wide footer block with Phone, Email, and Website placeholders.
Numbered Steps (Left & Right) - Bold circular numbered graphic, alternatable for zig-zag step layouts.
Tear-off Coupon - Classic dashed-border box for special offers.
Author Bio - Horizontal profile block for an avatar, credentials, and background text.
Checklist Item - Text item with a green circle and checkmark.
Menu Item - Restaurant menu item with a title, price, and dotted leader line.
Photo Block - Grey image placeholder with a caption slot.
Review Quote - Customer testimonial block with 5 golden stars.
Event Date - Calendar badge (Month + Day) alongside a headline and description.
Stat Callout - Oversized bolded number layout for highlighting key statistics.
Signature Line - Classic dotted “Sign Here” block.
Pros & Cons - Two-column list with a green Pros section and a red Cons section.
Q&A Block - Question and Answer pair with bold coloured Q/A markers.
Key Takeaway - Tinted summary box for highlighting the most important point in a document.
Warning Alert - Bright orange caution box for critical steps or potential dangers.

title: Visual Grammar Engine & Contextual Proofing Underlines
excerpt: Catch grammatical blunders, repeated words, and contextual spelling errors with Open Publisher
content:
Visual Grammar Engine & Contextual Proofing Underlines
While spell checkers flag invalid words, many writing mistakes involve valid words placed in improper grammatical contexts: confusing "there" with "their", typing duplicate words ("in the the box"), or mismatched indefinite articles ("an table"). Version 5.4.7 introduced a dedicated Visual Grammar & Contextual Proofing Engine powered by the W3C CSS Custom Highlight API ( ::highlight(grammar-error) ). Operating alongside red spelling highlights, it renders crisp green wavy squiggly underlines ( #27ae60 ) with zero bundled dictionary overhead.
🟢 Dual Visual Proofing with Green Grammar Underlines & Context Menu  Green squiggly underlines highlight grammatical blunders, paired with a right-click explanation banner and 1-click replacement.
Dual Visual Proofing Architecture
Open Publisher maintains two distinct highlight registries simultaneously, clearly distinguishing vocabulary errors from contextual phrasing rules:
Spelling Highlights (Red): Flags unrecognized dictionary tokens using ::highlight(spelling-error) with red wavy underlines ( #e74c3c ).
Grammar Highlights (Green): Marks grammatical, contextual, and stylistic mistakes using ::highlight(grammar-error) with vibrant green wavy underlines ( #27ae60 ).
Continuous Ink-Skipping Protection: Disables browser ink skipping ( text-decoration-skip-ink: none !important ) across all highlights, keeping green squigglies solid beneath descenders.
Rule-Aware Classification: classifyMatch() routes LanguageTool matches accurately, ensuring confused words, repeated words, and article mismatches display green rather than red.
Multi-Node DOM Range Mapping
Grammar rules frequently span across multiple words or cross text nodes separated by inline formatting (such as bold, italic, or font color spans). The proofing engine uses a robust DOM traversal algorithm:
TreeWalker Character Tracking: createRangeForOffsets() traverses text nodes cumulatively to map character offsets accurately across node boundaries.
Boundary Preservation: Constructs standard DOM Range objects without splitting nodes or altering document markup, preventing formatting corruption during composition.
Interactive Grammar Context Menu & Rule Ignoring
Right-clicking any green squiggly line presents an interactive grammar assistance card directly inside the canvas context menu:
Human-Readable Guidance Card: Displays a green explanation banner explaining the rule violation (e.g., "Did you mean 'their'?" or "Possible agreement error").
1-Click Suggestion Replacement: Clicking any replacement suggestion cleanly swaps the multi-word construct in the document, updates history undo/redo, and refreshes highlights in real time.
Persistent Rule Ignoring: Click "Ignore Rule" to silence specific stylistic warnings. Ignored rule IDs are stored in localStorage and persist across editing sessions.
Print Concealment: All green grammar decorations are hidden automatically during PDF exports and physical printing.
Tip: If you often use intentional sentence fragments for marketing headings, click "Ignore Rule" to suppress warning lines for that specific construction.
Isolated Word Grammar Underlines & Honorific Casing
Versions 5.8.7 and 5.9.7 refined the visual grammar engine to eliminate underline bleed. Green squiggly underlines now isolate exclusively beneath the affected words rather than stretching across spaces or trailing commas. Additionally, the grammar engine includes dedicated casing rules for honorific titles and abbreviations (such as Dr., Mrs., and Prof.), ensuring appropriate capitalization suggestions in formal correspondence.

title: Visual Spell Check Engine & Status Bar Auto-Revert
excerpt: Keep publications polished with Open Publisher
content:
Visual Spell Check Engine & Status Bar Auto-Revert
Producing flawless publications requires instant, accurate proofing feedback as you compose. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, misspelled words inside canvas text boxes failed to display red squiggly underlines. While the right-click menu could fetch suggestions from LanguageTool, native browser spellcheck decorations were suppressed inside scaled canvas containers (such as the default 60% zoom view). Version 5.4.6 introduced a dedicated, high-performance Visual Spell Check Engine built on the W3C CSS Custom Highlight API ( ::highlight(spelling-error) ), paired with an automatic status bar revert timer.
🔤 Scale-Invariant Visual Spell Check Engine with Continuous Wavy Underlines
Crisp red squiggly underlines remain clearly visible across all zoom levels without breaks over character descenders.
Scale-Invariant Visual Spell Check Engine
Chromium-based browsers suppress native ::spelling-error decorations when elements reside inside CSS transformed containers ( transform: scale(...) ). Open Publisher resolves this with a hardware-accelerated highlighting architecture:
W3C CSS Custom Highlight API: Leverages CSS.highlights.set('spelling-error', highlight) to paint crisp, GPU-accelerated wavy red underlines directly through the browser compositor across any zoom level (60%, 75%, 100%, 150%, 200%).
Continuous Underline Coverage: Browsers default to text-decoration-skip-ink: auto , which severs underlines wherever character descenders ( y , g , p , q , j ) cross the baseline. Setting text-decoration-skip-ink: none !important guarantees solid, unbroken squigglies across the entire word.
Non-Destructive DOM Ranges: Identifies misspelled words using native DOM Range objects without touching innerHTML , without inserting wrapper span tags, and without polluting undo/redo history.
Persistent Selection Visibility: Unlike native browser spellcheck lines that disappear when focus leaves a field, CSS highlight underlines remain fully visible when a text box is selected as an object or right-clicked.
Smart Caching & Zero Bundled Dictionary Bloat
Bundling offline dictionaries inflates package sizes by megabytes. Open Publisher integrates seamlessly with its existing LanguageTool proofing service while maximizing local responsiveness:
Batch Online Verification: Queries the proofing API in batches of up to 50 unverified tokens, filtering matches specifically for spelling typos while discarding sentence capitalization rules.
Client-Side Memory Caching: Maintains in-memory caches ( _knownGoodWords and _knownBadWords ) so repeated words never trigger duplicate network calls.
Add to Dictionary & Ignore All: Right-clicking any flagged word provides 1-click options to add the word to your custom dictionary (persisted in localStorage ) or ignore it for the session.
Print & Export Concealment: Dedicated @media print rules guarantee that red wavy squigglies never appear on printed output or exported PDF publications.
Status Bar Auto-Revert & Typing Reset
When moving or duplicating text chunks on the canvas, the bottom-left status bar message ( #status-msg ) previously remained stuck on "Text Moved" or "Text Copied" indefinitely. Version 5.4.6 added an intelligent 2.5-second auto-revert timer along with keystroke listeners, restoring "Element Selected" or "Ready" automatically upon typing resumption.
Tip: You can toggle real-time spell check on or off at any time using the Review tab in the ribbon or the Application Options dialog.

title: Word Count & Text Statistics
excerpt: Track your document length with Open Publisher's live status bar word count, or open the detailed text statistics dialog for character, line, and paragraph counts.
content:
Word Count & Text Statistics
Whether you are drafting a flyer, a brochure, or a full resume, Open Publisher provides tools to help you easily keep track of your text length without leaving the editor.
Live Status Bar Tracking
A dynamic word count indicator is built directly into the bottom status bar, sitting cleanly next to the page count. This indicator automatically appears whenever you select a text box and updates in real-time as you type, giving you an immediate view of your
word count at a glance.
Detailed Statistics Dialog
If you need more detailed metrics beyond a simple word count, you can open the comprehensive Text Statistics modal. You can access this dialog in two ways:
Click the live word count directly in the bottom status bar.
Go to the Review tab in the ribbon and click Word Count in the Proofing group.
The dialog provides an exact breakdown of your text, including:
Words
Characters (no spaces)
Characters (with spaces)
Paragraphs
Lines

title: The Clipart Asset Pipeline & Import Spooler
excerpt: Learn how Open Publisher ingests high-resolution Clipart and Smart Images with the viewport-fixed import spooler and dual-tier CDN failover redundancy.
content:
The Clipart Asset Pipeline & Import Spooler
Inserting high-resolution vector illustrations and remote imagery requires a responsive ingestion engine that keeps you informed during downloads. Open Publisher features a modernized asset import spooler that provides immediate visual feedback, glassmorphic backdrop protection, and dual-tier network redundancy.
🖼️ Visual Clipart Import Spooler
Centered viewport-fixed asset spooler card with theme-reactive loading spinner.
Viewport-Fixed Visual Spooler
When selecting artwork from the Clipart Gallery or web sources, Open Publisher displays a dedicated composite spooler card ( op-image-import-spinner ):
Viewport Pinned: Attached directly to document.body and centered across the viewport, remaining visible regardless of canvas scroll positions or zoom factors.
Glassmorphic Atmosphere: Renders with a translucent backdrop and hardware-accelerated blur ( backdrop-filter: blur(1px) ), preventing inadvertent mis-clicks while large assets transfer.
Theme-Reactive Spinner: The animated spinner icon harmonizes automatically with your chosen UI theme color.
Dual-Tier Network Failover Redundancy
To guarantee asset availability, the clipart ingestion pipeline employs multi-tier fallback routing:
Primary High-Res Stream: Requests print-ready vector assets directly from the primary content delivery network.
Autonomous Proxy Failover: If the primary stream encounters network latency, 404 responses, or corrupt 1x1 error pixels, the spooler automatically reroutes to the thumbnail proxy CDN without dropping the import session.
Instant Canvas Mounting
The moment the asset payload resolves, the spooler cleanly detaches from the DOM and mounts the image onto your active page, complete with aspect-ratio bounding boxes, rotation handles, and full undo/redo history tracking.
Note: Clipart assets automatically retain their natural aspect ratios upon insertion to prevent distortion.

title: Clipart Border Art Engine, Dynamic Element Resizing & 40 Presets
excerpt: Frame pages and text boxes with classic clipart picture borders, featuring 40 festive presets, real-time perimeter tile recalculation, and print fidelity.
content:
Clipart Border Art Engine, Dynamic Element Resizing & 40 Presets
Inspired by classic desktop publishing traditions in Microsoft Publisher, Border Art allows designers to frame pages, event certificates, flyers, and text callouts with repeating decorative clipart patterns (such as Santas, holiday bells, autumn leaves, stars, balloons, pencils, and floral borders). Version 5.7.0 delivered a major evolution of the Border Art engine, expanding the gallery to 40 handcrafted presets, introducing Dynamic Element Resizing with real-time perimeter tile recalculation, resolving print spooler aspect ratio distortion, and integrating border art directly into the text box context menu.
🎨 Border Art Gallery with 40 Clipart Presets & Live Inset Sliders
The gallery provides 40 distinct clipart borders with live size and margin sliders, constrained cleanly to 80% workspace height.
Compact 4-Wide Gallery Grid & 40 Presets
The redesigned dropdown gallery optimizes browsing efficiency across 40 distinct styles:
4-Column Grid System: Displays presets in a compact 410px wide menu with 28px square image previews and 11px labels across six popular themes: Holiday, Celebration, Romantic, Nature & Food, Sports, and Education.
80% Workspace Clearance: Clamps maximum dropdown height to 80% of available space below the ribbon ( spaceBelow * 0.80 ), keeping canvas elements, rulers, and status bar controls visible.
Real-Time Sliders: Interactive sliders allow adjusting tile icon size (16px to 64px) and edge inset margins (0px to 60px) with instant visual updates.
Dynamic Element Resizing & Perimeter Math
When applying Border Art to an individual text box or shape box, borders adapt dynamically:
Real-Time Drag Recalculation: Resizing a box via canvas handles invokes BorderArtEngine.refreshElement(el, w, h) on every frame, dynamically adding or removing tiles along all four edges.
Integrated ResizeObserver: A native observer detects dimensional shifts from sidebar inputs or font scaling, updating border tiles automatically.
Mathematical Corner Alignment: Exact perimeter divisions guarantee that corner tiles align symmetrically at the vertices without overlapping.
Print Fidelity & Context Menu Integration
Version 5.7.0 resolved print preview flattening by appending &fit=contain to clipart CDN queries, delivering 1:1 square transparent tile containers. Right-clicking any text box now includes "Border Art..." directly below "Format Text Box", while the Format Properties dialog features a dedicated button to open the gallery anchored directly to the selected element.
Tip: You can apply Border Art to the entire page via Page Design -> Border Art, or to individual callout boxes via right-click.

title: The Clipart Gallery
excerpt: Access 3,400+ high-quality transparent clipart images in Open Publisher
content:
The Clipart Gallery
Open Publisher includes a built-in Clipart Gallery with 3,403 high-quality, transparent images accessible directly from the Insert ribbon. All clipart is served as transparent PNGs and placed onto your canvas as fully movable, resizable elements.
Opening the Gallery
To open the Clipart Gallery:
Go to Insert > Clipart .
The gallery opens in a full-panel modal window displaying the complete library.
Searching the Gallery
A live search bar is built into the gallery header. As you type, the grid instantly filters to show only matching images. The search engine parses every image filename, strips system formatting, and generates clean human-readable names on the fly - so typing “coffee”, “arrow”, or “star” immediately narrows the gallery to relevant results. Hovering over any thumbnail shows a tooltip with the image’s clean name.
Browsing & Loading
The gallery is designed to open instantly and stay fast no matter how quickly you scroll:
Lazy loading - Thumbnails are only fetched from the network when they scroll into view, so the gallery opens immediately regardless of its size.
Concurrency queue - Thumbnail fetching is limited to 5 images at a time, preventing browser overload when scrolling fast.
Auto-retry - If a thumbnail fails to load, the system waits 1.5 seconds and retries automatically. After two failed attempts it falls back to the full-resolution version instead of showing a broken placeholder.
Vision-aware queue re-sorting - The loading engine continuously tracks which thumbnails are visible on screen and re-sorts the queue so whatever you are currently looking at always loads first, no matter how fast you scroll.
Gallery randomisation - The gallery shuffles its 3,400+ entries every time it opens, so you see a fresh selection each session rather than the same images at the top.
Inserting Clipart
To insert a clipart image:
Double-click any thumbnail to insert it instantly.
Or single-click to select it (highlighted with a teal border), then click OK in the modal footer.
A styled “Importing Image… Please wait” overlay appears while the high-resolution file downloads. The canvas insertion engine includes the following safeguards:
If the server returns a 404 for a high-resolution image, the engine catches the error and automatically falls back to the thumbnail version.
If a network proxy intercepts the error and returns an invisible 1×1 pixel, the engine detects the anomaly by scanning the pixel dimensions and also falls back to the thumbnail - ensuring you never end up with a broken or invisible element on your canvas.
Clipart Technical Details
All clipart images are served as transparent PNGs via the wsrv.nl HTTPS proxy, which converts the external HTTP image library over HTTPS to bypass browser mixed-content restrictions.
The canvas insertion engine includes the following safeguards:
If the server returns a 404 for a high-resolution image, the engine catches the error and automatically falls back to the thumbnail version.
If a network proxy intercepts the error and returns an invisible 1×1 pixel (HTTP 200), the engine detects the anomaly by scanning the pixel dimensions and also falls back to the thumbnail - ensuring you never end up with a broken or invisible element on your canvas.
Fast 3.5s Fallback Racing & Network Resilience
In Version 5.11.8, the Clipart insertion pipeline was upgraded with an intelligent fallback racing engine to guarantee instant response even on slow or unreliable internet connections:
3.5-Second Fast Racing: When fetching high-resolution vector clipart from remote repositories, OpenPublisher initiates a 3.5-second timeout race. If the high-res asset takes longer than 3.5 seconds or encounters connection latency, the engine seamlessly inserts the cached thumbnail onto your canvas so your workflow is never blocked.
Silent Background Upgrading: While you continue positioning and formatting your document, the engine continues downloading the full-resolution asset in the background. Once loaded, it quietly swaps in the high-res vector graphics without shifting dimensions, rotation, or aspect ratio.
Zero-Corruption Safeguard: The system verifies MIME types and byte headers, protecting against 1x1 tracking pixels, captive-portal HTML error pages, and corrupted responses.

title: Vector Clipart Recoloring, Fill Overrides & Transparency
excerpt: Master recoloring vector clipart illustrations, applying custom fill overrides, and adjusting element transparency in Open Publisher.
content:
Vector Clipart Recoloring, Fill Overrides & Transparency
While standard bitmap images (such as JPEG and PNG photos) require destructive pixel editing to alter color balance, Open Publisher's built-in Clipart Gallery utilizes scalable vector graphics (SVG). Because vector clipart consists of mathematical curves and discrete shape layers, authors can recolor illustrations, override fills, customize stroke borders, and apply subtle transparency without degrading image sharpness or requiring external graphic software.
🎨 Vector Clipart Color Inspector & Fill Overrides
Adjust vector fill colors, stroke palettes, and transparency without external graphic design software
The Clipart Color Inspector
Selecting any inserted clipart graphic activates the dedicated formatting inspector in the ribbon:
Vector Layer Parsing: The inspector automatically scans the SVG internal DOM and extracts unique color swatches corresponding to each fill and outline path.
Theme Harmony Mapping: Click "Map to Active Theme" to instantly convert multi-colored illustrations to harmonious shades derived from your publication's primary and accent color theme.
Custom Fill & Stroke Overrides
For precision branding control, users can target individual elements within any illustration:
Discrete Swatch Replacement: Click any extracted color tile in the ribbon to open the color picker and assign custom corporate hex values.
Stroke Thickness & Removal: Modify outer stroke weights to increase visual prominence or eliminate outlines entirely for a contemporary flat-design aesthetic.
Layer Opacity & Watermark Blending
The Clipart Format panel includes an interactive Opacity slider ranging from 0% to 100%. Reducing clipart opacity allows illustrations to blend softly into background patterns, header banners, or serve as full-page watermark decorations beneath body copy.
Tip: To use vector clipart as a subtle background watermark, set its opacity slider to 15% and send the object to the back layer.

title: Dashboard Blank Document Page Size Routing & Paper Format Synchronization
excerpt: Master document creation in Open Publisher with reliable paper size inheritance from the Startup Dashboard, preventing unwanted regional A4/Letter defaults.
content:
Dashboard Blank Document Page Size Routing & Paper Format Synchronization
The Startup Dashboard is the central launching pad for new Open Publisher projects, offering one-click access to standard publication formats: A4, US Letter, US Legal, Tabloid, Business Cards, Posters, and Custom dimensions. However, earlier versions suffered from an aggressive overwrite defect: choosing a specific paper size from the Dashboard (such as Tabloid or Business Card) would often default back to a generic regional A4 or Letter page as soon as the main editor canvas opened. Version 4.19.6 patched the core page creation routines to ensure user-selected dashboard formats are accurately inherited and preserved.
📋 Startup Dashboard Quick-Start Paper Cards & Format Synchronization
Selecting any paper size card on the Dashboard initializes the canvas with exact corresponding pixel dimensions and aspect ratios.
The addNewPage Default Dimension Overwrite Bug
The root cause of incorrect page dimensions on startup was identified in the core page creation logic:
The Aggressive Regional Overwrite: In core/pages.js , addNewPage() evaluated browser locale settings ( navigator.language ) and defaulted new pages to regional A4 or Letter sizes. When starting a document from the Dashboard, addNewPage() executed after the preset had been chosen and aggressively overwrote user selections with regional defaults.
Dimension Inheritance Patch: Refactored addNewPage() to inspect whether the DOM canvas container already has pre-set width and height properties applied by the Dashboard initialization sequence. If explicit dimensions exist, addNewPage() reads and respects them intact.
Multi-Page Format Consistency
Document format preservation extends across subsequent page additions:
Inheriting Current Page Dimensions: When inserting additional pages into an active publication ( Ctrl+M ), the editor duplicates the dimensions and orientation of the active page rather than reverting to standard A4/Letter defaults.
Specialized Format Support: Preserves dimensions for non-standard formats including Business Cards (3.5 x 2.0 in), A3 Posters, Brochures, and custom square social media banners.
Calibrated Rulers & Margin Guides
When a document initializes from the Dashboard, horizontal and vertical rulers, margin guide overlays, and canvas viewport zoom automatically calibrate to the selected format on frame zero, ensuring immediate creative productivity.
Tip: You can change the paper size or orientation of an open document at any time using the Page Setup menu in the Page Design tab.

title: Floating Toolbar Startup Protection & Context Isolation
excerpt: Keep formatting toolbars strictly hidden behind startup dashboards and modal overlays until canvas elements are actively selected in Open Publisher.
content:
Floating Toolbar Startup Protection & Context Isolation
When launching Open Publisher, a clean presentation ensures users can focus on selecting a publication template, opening recent files, or configuring document dimensions. As of version 4.20.7, we introduced a comprehensive context isolation between the startup dashboard and canvas formatting toolbars, guaranteeing that floating toolbars remain completely hidden until a user opens a publication and explicitly selects an element on the canvas.
🛡️ Clean Startup Dashboard Presentation with Protected Toolbar
The startup dashboard displays cleanly without background toolbar bleed or premature interface elements.
Context Isolation Behind Dashboard Overlays
The dashboard system operates with strict visual and DOM layer separation:
Dashboard Open State: When the dashboard modal opens on launch or via File > New, a global dashboard-open class is applied to the document body.
CSS Hard Guards: The stylesheet enforces display: none !important; on #float-toolbar and all contextual formatting overlays whenever the dashboard state is active.
Backdrop Occlusion Protection: Prevents toolbars, color palettes, or floating widgets from bleeding through semi-transparent backdrops or showing above dashboard cards.
Interaction-Driven Display Lifecycle
The floating toolbar lifecycle is strictly bound to user intent:
Default Hidden Geometry: In style.css and the core HTML markup, #float-toolbar initializes with an inline style="display: none;" attribute, eliminating visual flash on page load.
Runtime Show Guards: The showFloatToolbar() function in elements/text/text.js immediately aborts execution if the dashboard or any full-screen setup modal is active.
Selection Activation: The floating toolbar appears smoothly only after a publication is loaded and the user clicks or double-clicks an editable text box.
Clean Kiosk & Web Presentation
This architecture provides a reliable presentation whether running in the Electron desktop wrapper, standalone kiosk mode, or web browsers. When returning to the dashboard to switch projects, the toolbar immediately hides, keeping your workspace uncluttered.
Note: Clicking outside an active text box onto the pasteboard or canvas background automatically dismisses the floating toolbar.

title: Mobile-Responsive Dashboard & Portrait Experience
excerpt: Experience Open Publisher
content:
Mobile-Responsive Dashboard & Portrait Experience
While desktop monitors and landscape tablets provide ample workspace for browsing templates, visiting the Open Publisher dashboard on a smartphone in portrait orientation historically presented significant layout collisions. A fixed 250px vertical sidebar consumed up to 70% of narrow screens, crushing the template gallery into an unreadable vertical strip while desktop carousel arrow buttons floated directly over preview cards. Version 5.6.3 introduced a complete mobile-responsive redesign for the Startup Dashboard under modern media queries ( @media (max-width: 768px) ), transforming portrait mobile navigation into a fluid, app-like experience.
📱 Mobile Portrait Dashboard with Horizontal Pill Navigation & 2-Tier Header
The mobile start screen presents edge-to-edge fullscreen modal geometry, touch-scrollable navigation chips, and an expansive search bar.
Two-Tier Header Architecture
Narrow mobile viewports cannot accommodate a 400px search input, branding logo, and multiple action buttons on a single horizontal row. Version 5.6.3 reorganizes header elements using CSS flexbox order:
Row 1 (Branding & Actions): Places the Open Publisher logo on the left ( order: 1 ) and action buttons on the right ( order: 2 ). The skip button automatically swaps its label from "Skip / Open Editor" on desktop to a compact "Editor" badge on mobile, avoiding text wrapping.
Row 2 (Full-Width Search): The search input ( order: 3 ) expands to 100% width on the lower tier, providing a spacious touch target with clear placeholders for fast template discovery.
Safe Area Inset Respect: Fullscreen modal geometry honors device hardware notches and navigation bars ( env(safe-area-inset-top) ) on iOS Safari and Android Chrome.
Horizontal Touch-Scrollable Navigation Pills
Replacing the fixed 250px vertical sidebar with horizontal chips frees up the entire screen height for template content:
Compact Chip Bar: Converts navigation into an inline-flex pill chip row ( max-height: 52px; overflow-x: auto; ) featuring Home, New, Open, and Recent tabs alongside all publication categories.
Momentum Touch Scrolling: Equipped with native momentum scrolling ( -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch ) and invisible scrollbars for a clean, app-like feel.
Active Theme Highlighting: Selected chips highlight in signature brand teal ( var(--ui-theme-color) ) with subtle pill elevation.
Touch Carousels & Adaptive 2-Column Grid
Template presentation adapts smoothly between quick horizontal carousels and full catalog exploration:
Natural Thumb Swiping: Bulky desktop circular arrow buttons are hidden on touch screens ( display: none !important ), enabling unobstructed horizontal thumb swiping across "Blank Documents" and "Featured" rows.
Adaptive 2-Column Grid: Expanding a category or entering a search query displays templates in a balanced 2-column card grid ( repeat(2, 1fr) ) with dynamic card width calculation.
Zero Desktop Regressions: Laptops and desktop screens above 768px retain the standard floating modal layout, 250px sidebar, and desktop drag controls.
Tip: You can swipe horizontally across template categories or tap any pill chip to instantly filter publication styles.

title: Recent Documents Management, Pinning & Workspace Recovery
excerpt: Explore the Startup Dashboard
content:
Recent Documents Management, Pinning & Workspace Recovery
The Startup Dashboard serves as the central operational hub for Open Publisher, bridging new project creation with ongoing publication management. In busy design studios and production environments where authors manage dozens of concurrent newsletters, flyers, brochures, and advertisements, finding the exact publication required without hunting through operating system folder trees is critical. Open Publisher's Recent Documents system combines visual thumbnail previews, instant keyword filtering, priority document pinning, and automatic workspace state recovery.
📌 Startup Dashboard Recent Documents Grid with Pinned Items
Manage recent publications with persistent pin toggles, live search filtering, and thumbnail previews.
The Recent Documents Grid
Every document opened or saved in Open Publisher is logged in the dashboard's local index:
Visual Thumbnail Cards: Each entry presents a high-resolution canvas snapshot of the document's front spread, alongside the publication title, last modified date, and page count.
Paper Format Badges: Standard badges (such as "A4 Portrait", "Letter", or "Custom") indicate document geometry at a glance.
Live Search Filter: A dedicated filter input lets you type document keywords to narrow down dozens of projects in milliseconds.
Document Pinning for Priority Access
Frequently accessed publications (such as weekly store circulars, school event programs, or master template designs) can be pinned to prevent them from dropping off the recent list. Clicking the pin icon on any document card locks it permanently to the top of the grid.
Seamless Workspace State Recovery
When reopening a publication from the Recent Documents grid, Open Publisher restores more than just the document content. It automatically re-establishes canvas zoom percentage, viewport scroll offsets, ruler origin coordinates, and active navigation panel selections, allowing you to resume work without reconfiguring your environment.
Tip: In desktop client wrappers, your pinned recent publications also appear in the operating system Taskbar Jump List and System Tray context menu.

title: The Dashboard
excerpt: The Open Publisher Startup Dashboard gives you instant access to 250 premium templates and new document creation in a draggable, fully themed modal window.
content:
The Dashboard
When you open Open Publisher, the Dashboard appears at Startup as a large, centred modal window giving you instant access to your template library, recent work, and new document creation - all before you touch the editor. It can also be reopened at any time without restarting the application.
Opening the Dashboard
The Dashboard opens automatically every time Open Publisher loads. If you close it and need to return to it later, you can reopen it at any time via File > New > Dashboard from the ribbon - even while you have a document open.
This allows you to browse templates or start a new project without closing your current work.
A Draggable Modal Window
The Dashboard is a 95% full-screen draggable modal window rather than a rigid full-screen overlay. Click and drag the Dashboard header to move the entire window around your screen, letting you peek at the editor workspace beneath it. This gives you spatial context - you can see your existing document waiting underneath while you browse templates.
Browsing Templates
The Dashboard provides access to a library of 250 premium templates spanning categories including Resumes, Flyers, Menus, Certificates, Business Cards, Magazines, Invitations, and more. Each template thumbnail displays a page size badge in the bottom-right corner, showing you the format (A4, Letter, Square, 1080p, etc.) at a glance before loading it.
The Featured section at the top of the Dashboard showcases 12 hand-picked, top-tier templates - including designs such as Executive Summary, Luxury Wedding, and Film Festival - ensuring
you are immediately presented with the platform’s finest work.
Starting a New Document
To begin with a blank canvas, click the Skip / Open Editor button. This dismisses the Dashboard and opens a fresh blank document in the editor immediately. The button is styled as a bright white button with teal text and is always prominently visible in the Dashboard header.
Closing the Dashboard
The Dashboard features a smart close button in the top corner that behaves differently depending on your situation:
Cold start (no document open) - Clicking the close button generates a fresh blank A4 page and takes you straight into the editor, identical to pressing Skip.
Active session (document already open) - Clicking the close button dismisses the Dashboard modal and safely returns you to your existing document without overwriting or disrupting your work.
Auto-Close on File Drop
If you drag and drop an .opub file into the application while the Dashboard is still open, Open Publisher loads the file in the background and automatically closes the Dashboard the moment the document finishes rendering - taking you straight into your file without any manual dismissal needed.
Theme Compatibility
The Dashboard header is styled with Open Publisher’s signature teal green and white. When a high-brightness UI theme is active (such as Snapchat Yellow), the Dashboard intelligently adapts - flipping the header text, logo, and buttons to dark colours so everything remains clearly legible regardless of which theme you are using.
Enhanced Search Bar & Focus Reliability (v5.14.2)
Finding the right template is immediate thanks to significant usability upgrades introduced in v5.14.2:
Instant Desktop Auto-Focus: When launching the Dashboard on desktop screens (wider than 768px), OpenPublisher automatically focuses the template search input field. You can begin typing your search term immediately without having to click inside the box first.
Global Keyboard Typing Redirection: While browsing templates on the dashboard, any printable keystroke automatically routes directly into the search bar, ensuring you never miss a keystroke.
Full-Boundary Click Focusing: Clicking anywhere within the 400px search container (including padding, borders, and the magnifying glass icon) immediately focuses the input without interfering with window dragging.
Escape Key Quick Reset: Pressing Esc while inside the search input instantly clears your query and resets the view back to the featured template catalog.
Instant High-Resolution WebP Thumbnail Pipeline (v5.16.7)
Browsing hundreds of publication templates is fluid and instantaneous thanks to the dedicated WebP asset pipeline introduced in v5.16.7:
Pre-Rendered WebP Previews: All 297+ built-in templates across all 15 categories are indexed with optimized WebP preview images, reducing asset footprints from tens of megabytes down to lightweight, crisp image cards.
Sub-Millisecond Dashboard Rendering: The dashboard loads smoothly with lazy-loaded thumbnails, allowing you to scroll through flyers, brochures, certificates, and resumes with zero frame lag.
Curated Featured Carousel: Newly added community and seasonal templates (such as the Dear Santa Letter and Santa Nice List Certificate) are automatically highlighted within the top Featured carousel for one-click auditioning.
Blank Document Card Redesign & Quick Presets (v5.19.4)
The Startup Dashboard received a visual and functional modernization in OpenPublisher v5.19.4 . Blank document selection cards now feature realistic vector paper sheets with refined depth shadows, upfront physical measurements, and clear orientation tags:
The redesigned blank document paper cards and quick dimension presets in OpenPublisher v5.19.4.
Visual Aspect Ratios: Cards accurately reflect standard portrait and landscape proportions (such as A4 210 x 297 mm, US Letter 8.5 x 11 in, and Tabloid 11 x 17 in) before you click.
One-Click Orientation Switcher: Instantly toggle between vertical and horizontal orientations directly on each card without digging through sub-menus.
Unified Version Synchronization: The dashboard footer displays verified client build synchronization, assuring you are running the latest desktop or web release.
Publication Loading Modal & Desktop File Launch (v5.16.13)
When opening complex publications containing hundreds of graphics or embedded tables, OpenPublisher v5.16.13 introduces an elegant Publication Loading Modal:
The Publication Loading Modal in OpenPublisher v5.16.13 providing clear visual deserialization progress.
This modal provides clear visual feedback during project unpacking. Furthermore, v5.16.13 resolved a desktop file association issue in NW.js, ensuring that double-clicking any .opub file in Windows File Explorer immediately boots the client and loads the document seamlessly.

title: Emoji Search, Unicode Skin Tone Modifiers & Category Filtering
excerpt: Learn how to search through 1,540+ emojis in Open Publisher, insert them onto your canvas, and adjust skin tones using the floating micro-toolbar.
content:
Emoji Search, Unicode Skin Tone Modifiers & Category Filtering
Emojis bring vibrant, modern, and expressive visual accents to flyers, promotional banners, event invitations, and certificates. However, with the Unicode standard expanding to encompass thousands of distinct pictograms, scrolling manually through an unorganized symbol grid can severely impede workflow velocity. Open Publisher features a comprehensive, high-speed Emoji Picker equipped with real-time keyword search, categorical taxonomy filtering, and support for Unicode skin tone diversity modifiers.
🔍 Emoji Picker Search Bar & Skin Tone Modifier Palette
Search emojis by keyword, filter by categorical taxonomy, and customize skin tone modifiers.
Real-Time Search & Keyword Indexing
The Emoji Picker integrates an instant search engine designed for rapid keyboard operation:
Instant Keystroke Filtering: Type terms such as "celebrate", "heart", "calendar", "trophy", or "star" into the search bar at the top of the picker to filter results on the fly.
Synonym & Emotion Tagging: The search dictionary indexes colloquial synonyms and emotional states (for example, searching "happy" returns smiling faces, laughing expressions, and party poppers).
Keyboard Navigation: Use the arrow keys to navigate the filtered grid and press Enter to insert the highlighted glyph directly at the active text caret.
Unicode Skin Tone Modifiers
Open Publisher respects modern representation standards through interactive modifier support:
Fitzpatrick Scale Palette: Human and hand gesture emojis support all five standard Fitzpatrick skin tone modifiers (ranging from Light to Dark).
Contextual Tone Selector: Right-click or long-press on any customizable emoji to display the floating skin tone selector bar.
Persistent Preference: The selected skin tone persists as the default for subsequent insertions, streamlining batch drafting.
Categorical Taxonomy & Recent History
For visual discovery, the picker organizes emojis into eight primary tabs (Smileys, People, Nature, Food, Travel, Activities, Objects, and Symbols). The top bar maintains a "Frequently Used" cache displaying your most recently inserted glyphs for immediate one-click access.
Tip: You can change the size and line height of inserted emojis just like standard text by selecting them and adjusting the Font Size dropdown in the Home tab.

title: Emojis
excerpt: Insert scalable Twemoji SVG emojis in Open Publisher. Emojis stretch freely to any size without letterboxing, and older emoji elements are auto-upgraded on open.
content: Emojis The Emojis gallery (formerly labelled “Classic Clipart”) provides access to the full Twemoji library - Twitter’s open-source, high-quality emoji set rendered as scalable SVG graphics. Because they are SVGs rather than raster images, emojis remain perfectly crisp at any size on screen, in PDFs, and in print. Inserting an Emoji To insert an emoji: Go to Insert > Emojis . The Emoji modal opens, displaying the full Twemoji library. Browse or use the search bar to find an emoji, then double-click it to insert it. Alternatively, click once to select it and then click OK . Scalable & Stretchable Emojis Emojis in Open Publisher are inserted as inline SVGs rather than linked image files, with preserveAspectRatio=”none” applied. This means they stretch freely to fill any bounding box - useful for creating oversized decorative emoji elements - without leaving white letterbox space around the sides. This resolves a limitation present in the older implementation. Automatic Upgrade of Older Documents When you open a document that contains older emoji elements, Open Publisher automatically upgrades them to the new inline SVG format in the background. No manual action is required - your existing documents are silently updated to benefit from the improved scalability and rendering.

title: Formatting Emojis
excerpt: Unlock advanced image editing for Emojis in Open Publisher. Use the Picture Tools ribbon to apply custom filters, recolour graphics, and lock aspect ratios.
content:
Formatting Emojis
Unlike standard text-based emojis that rely on your operating system to render-and often look completely different depending on the device you are using-emojis in Open Publisher are powered by a custom, high-quality SVG vector library. This means they scale infinitely without ever losing crispness or becoming pixelated. Because Open Publisher treats these vector emojis as first-class graphical elements rather than standard typed characters, they fully support the advanced formatting, manipulation, and styling features normally reserved for standard pictures and imported photos.
Emoji Picture Tools
Treating emojis as image assets unlocks a new level of design flexibility. When you click on any inserted emoji on your canvas, the Picture Tools contextual ribbon tab automatically appears at the top of your screen. From this dedicated ribbon, you can:
Lock Aspect Ratio - Keep your graphics looking professional. By toggling this setting, you ensure your vector emojis stay perfectly proportioned when dragging the corner resize handles, preventing them from becoming accidentally squashed or stretched out of shape.
Apply Filters - Open the Format Picture sidebar to precisely tweak the brightness, contrast, and transparency of the emoji exactly like you would a standard PNG or Clipart graphic. This is highly useful if you want to wash out an emoji to use it as a subtle background watermark.
Recolour Engine - Use the Hue/Recolour dropdown to completely shift the colour palette of the emoji to match your specific document’s theme or corporate branding. The native print engine guarantees that your modified emoji colours will print and export to high-resolution PDFs perfectly, maintaining flawless fidelity without any graphical distortion.
Layering and Arrangement
Because they function as standalone graphical objects, your formatted emojis can be freely dragged, rotated, and layered anywhere on the page. You can easily send them behind text boxes, bring them to the front of other images, or group multiple emojis together to build custom composite illustrations directly on your canvas.
High-Resolution 300 DPI Print Export for Ribbon Emojis
Version 5.10.1 upgraded the print rendering pipeline for emojis inserted from the ribbon palette. Emojis now render through high-resolution vector downsampling at 300 DPI during PDF generation and physical printing, ensuring vibrant colors and smooth, crisp outlines without fuzzy pixelation.

title: Booklet Printing
excerpt: Print professional saddle-stitched booklets in Open Publisher with automatic printer spread assembly, correct page pairing, and full background gradient support.
content:
Booklet Printing
Booklet Printing assembles your pages into printer spreads ready for saddle-stitch binding - ideal for zines, magazines, programmes, and folded brochures. Open Publisher automatically calculates the correct page pairing order so you don’t have to.
How to Print a Booklet
Go to File > Print Booklet , or select the Booklet option from the print modal.
Print double-sided on your printer.
Fold and staple through the central spine to complete the booklet.
How Pages Are Paired
The engine automatically calculates which pages print together on each sheet. For an 8-page document, the pairings are:
Sheet 1 front: Pages 8 + 1
Sheet 1 back: Pages 2 + 7
Sheet 2 front: Pages 6 + 3
Sheet 2 back: Pages 4 + 5
Background Rendering in Booklet Mode
Page backgrounds applied via Format Background or the Theme Studio render correctly in booklet mode. Gradients are physically converted to DOM layers to bypass browser backgroundColor limitations, ensuring your backgrounds print faithfully on every spread.

title: Desktop App Async Print Pipeline & Native API Interception
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher refactored its core print sequence into an asynchronous pipeline supporting desktop wrapper interception and seamless web fallback.
content:
Desktop App Async Print Pipeline & Native API Interception
Printing from a modern desktop publishing application requires bridging two distinct runtime models: standard web browsers (which rely on browser-level print dialogs) and native desktop client shells (such as NW.js or Electron, which spool directly to operating system hardware drivers, generate background PDFs, and communicate with prepress production queues). Earlier builds of Open Publisher used a purely synchronous print dispatch that could block the UI thread and prevented external client shells from capturing the flattened staging DOM before system dialogs engaged. Version 4.19.10 refactored the print sequence into a robust asynchronous pipeline featuring native desktop API interception and transparent web fallback.
🖨️ Asynchronous Print Pipeline Architecture & Spooler Interception
The print sequence evaluates native desktop API hooks asynchronously while ensuring zero interruption for standard web users.
Asynchronous Print Architecture in file-io.js
Version 4.19.10 modernized print execution across the codebase:
Async Handler Modernization: In io/file-io.js , printFullDocument() was refactored from a blocking function into a modern async routine.
Sequential DOM Preparation: Heavyweight pre-print operations (including font glyph harvesting, image pre-baking, CSS transform flattening, and staging iframe resolution) execute sequentially using await , preventing race conditions before print capture begins.
The OP_Desktop_API Interception Hook
To allow native wrappers to intercept and handle print jobs directly, Open Publisher introduced a dedicated runtime bridge hook:
API Presence Verification: In extensions/print-engine.js , the physical print engine checks whether window.OP_Desktop_API is defined in the host environment.
Print Pipeline Suspension: If window.OP_Desktop_API is present, the standard browser print sequence pauses and awaits window.OP_Desktop_API.triggerCustomPrint() . This gives the native desktop client complete control to capture the rendered iframe DOM, access raw postscript drivers, and route jobs to OS spoolers.
Iframe Resolver Interception: The Physical Print Engine iframe resolver intercepts the custom desktop API wrapper, enabling silent background PDF generation and print queue monitoring.
Transparent Web Experience & DOM Cleanup
For standard web users, the refactored pipeline guarantees zero friction:
Automatic Browser Fallback: If OP_Desktop_API is not detected, the system immediately invokes window.print() without hesitation.
Safe Synchronous Teardown: Once printing concludes or the user dismisses the print dialog, cleanup routines execute cleanly, dismantling offscreen staging iframes and reclaiming memory.
Tip: In the V5 desktop client, asynchronous printing routes directly to the Export & Print Queue Monitor in the system tray.

title: Double-Page Spreads
excerpt: Design magazine, booklet, and brochure layouts in Open Publisher using Double-Page Spreads mode, with a wide facing-page canvas and automatic spreads-aware page sizing.
content:
Double-Page Spreads
For magazine, booklet, and brochure layouts, Open Publisher supports Double-Page Spreads - a wide landscape canvas that represents two facing pages side by side. This lets you design across both pages simultaneously, seeing exactly how your layout will look when the publication is open in front of a reader.
Enabling Spreads
To switch to Double-Page Spread mode:
Go to View > Spreads , or use the Spreads toggle in the Layout ribbon.
The canvas immediately switches to a wide landscape format - 1588px wide for A4 - giving you the full two-page working area. To return to single-page view, simply toggle Spreads off using the same control.
The Book-Fold Line
A visual book-fold line appears in the centre of the spread canvas to mark the spine of the publication.
This is a purely decorative guide - it has pointer-events: none applied, meaning it cannot be selected, clicked, or accidentally moved while you are working. It will never appear in your exported PDF or print output.
Spreads-Aware Page Sizing
The page size menu is fully spreads-aware. If you switch paper size while in Spread mode, the engine automatically doubles the new dimension to preserve the double-wide layout. You can freely switch between A4, Letter, A3, and other sizes without having to manually recalculate or reset your spread canvas.
Designing Across the Spread
While in Spread mode, elements can be placed, resized, and moved freely across the entire double-width canvas. This makes it straightforward to create designs that bleed across both pages - such as a full-width hero image, a panoramic background, or a headline that spans the spine - which are then correctly split across the two pages when exported or printed.

title: Export as HTML
excerpt: Export your Open Publisher document as a standalone HTML file with options for email client compatibility, offline images, mobile scaling, SEO meta tags, and more.
content:
Export as HTML
The Export as HTML feature turns your Open Publisher document into a standalone .html file for use as an email newsletter, a mobile-responsive flyer, or a web page. An Advanced HTML Export modal gives you full control over exactly how the file is generated.
How to Export as HTML
Go to File > Save as HTML .
The Advanced HTML Export modal opens. Choose your export options (see below).
Click Generate HTML File to download the result.
Export Options
Seamless Newsletter Layout - Removes margins and shadows between pages for a single unified scrolling canvas.
Optimise for Email Clients - Converts all pages to high-fidelity screenshots wrapped in a legacy <table> structure, ensuring 100% layout compatibility with strict email clients such as Gmail, Outlook, and Mailchimp, where modern CSS often fails.
Embed External Images (Single-File) - Converts all remote images (such as Clipart) into inline Base64 Data URIs, so the .html file works completely offline without broken image links.
Auto-Scale to Fit Screen - Injects a dynamic CSS transform: scale() rule so fixed-width flyer layouts shrink correctly onto small mobile screens.
Enable Text Selection / Copying - Controls whether viewers are able to highlight and copy text from the exported HTML page.
Inject SEO & Social Meta Tags - Runs a headless analysis of your document’s text, extracts the top 5 keywords, formulates a 150-character description, and injects og:title , og:description , and standard meta tags into the <head> - generating correct preview cards when shared on iMessage, Twitter, and Facebook.
Minify HTML - Strips away as much of the whitespace left behind as possible from the raw HTML so that the final file size is much more reduced.
Include Google Fonts - Appends <link> tags for all fonts used in the document, preserving your typography correctly in the browser.

title: Export as Image
excerpt: Export any page as a high-quality image in Open Publisher, with UI elements automatically stripped and CSS filters correctly applied for a clean, production-ready result.
content:
Export as Image
You can export any individual page as a high-quality image file directly from Open Publisher, with all UI elements automatically removed so the output is clean and production-ready.
How to Export as Image
Go to File > Export > Export as Image , or click Export Image in the Export ribbon group.
The engine captures a clean snapshot of the current page using html2canvas .
Before taking the snapshot, all margin guides, selection boxes, and resize handles are stripped from a temporary clone of the page, ensuring no UI artefacts appear in the output.
All CSS filters - hue rotation, brightness adjustments, and more - are correctly applied to the exported image.
Maximum Canvas Size
A maximum canvas dimension of 2000px is enforced during image export to prevent browser out-of-memory crashes on very large or high-resolution documents. This ensures reliable export performance regardless of your document’s canvas size.

title: Export as XPS
excerpt: Export your Open Publisher document as an XPS file for Windows and corporate environments, using the built-in Microsoft XPS Document Writer without any third-party software.
content:
Export as XPS
For Windows users or corporate environments where PDF is not supported, Open Publisher can produce an XPS (XML Paper Specification) file - Microsoft’s built-in alternative to PDF. XPS files work natively on virtually any Windows machine without requiring Adobe Acrobat or any third-party software.
Note: Because XPS is a proprietary Microsoft format, this export method relies on the Windows operating system. macOS and Linux users will not have access to the XPS Document Writer in their native print dialogs.
How to Export as XPS
Click Export XPS in the File or Home ribbon tab (next to the PDF export button).
A dialog opens explaining the process. Because web browsers cannot natively generate XPS files on their own, the button hooks into your browser’s native print engine and instructs you to select “Microsoft XPS Document Writer” as your printer destination.
When the print dialog opens, confirm that Microsoft XPS Document Writer is selected as the printer destination. Click Print , choose a destination folder on your computer, enter a file name, and click Save .
Troubleshooting
Missing XPS Document Writer: If this option does not appear in your printer list, it may be disabled on your machine. Go to Windows Settings > Apps > Optional Features , click “Add a feature,” and install the Microsoft XPS Document Writer.
Print Dialog Blocked: If clicking the export button does nothing, ensure your web browser’s pop-up blocker is not preventing the print dialog from launching. Look for a blocked pop-up icon in your URL address bar.

title: Export to PDF
excerpt: Export print-quality PDFs from Open Publisher with automatic pre-processing for WordArt, image filters, shape crops, 3D rotations, and Master Page headers and footers.
content:
Export to PDF
Open Publisher produces print-quality PDF output via the native browser Save as PDF workflow, with an automated pre-processing pipeline that ensures everything in your document - effects, crops, filters, and Master Pages - is accurately captured in the final file.
How to Export as PDF
Go to File > Export to PDF , or click the Export PDF button in the Export group of the File ribbon.
A guidance dialog opens explaining the process. Open Publisher opens your system’s print menu and instructs you to select “Save as PDF” as the printer destination.
Click through to generate and save the file.
PDF Pre-Processing Pipeline
The PDF export uses the same high-resolution print engine as standard printing, with the following
additional pre-processing steps applied automatically
before the snapshot is taken:
WordArt - Converted to a 1:1 PNG using the Canvas Compositor.
CSS filters -  Hue rotation, brightness, contrast, and other image filters are baked into images via canvas rendering.
Shape crops, clip-paths, and 3D rotations - All flattened and rasterised.
Master Page headers and footers - Correctly applied to every page in the document.
Margin guides and selection boxes - Stripped from the snapshot so they never appear in the exported file.

title: Multiple Copies per Sheet, Card & Label Imposition & Multi-Up Printing
excerpt: Print multiple business cards and labels per sheet with automated imposition grids (10-up, 12-up), Avery stock alignment, cut marks, duplex flipping, and DTP margins.
content:
Multiple Copies per Sheet, Card & Label Imposition & Multi-Up Printing
Designing business cards, event badges, raffle tickets, and product labels is one of the most common applications of desktop publishing. However, printing these small items traditionally required users to manually copy and paste their artwork into awkward 10-up grids across an entire Letter or A4 page, making subsequent design edits tedious and error-prone. Version 5.8.1 delivered a complete Card & Label Sheet Imposition Engine, allowing designers to design a single card on a dedicated canvas and automatically print multiple copies per sheet with calibrated stock margins, cut marks, and duplex alignment.
📇 Card & Label Sheet Imposition Dialog with Live SVG Sheet Preview
Single card designs tile automatically across standard Letter or A4 sheets with calibrated Avery stock margins and cut guides.
Single-Card Workflow & Automated Grid Imposition
The Card & Label Imposition engine ( ui/modals/card-sheet-modal.js ) liberates users from manual grid creation:
Dedicated Single-Card Canvas: Design cards on standard dimensions (such as 3.5 in x 2.0 in or 85 mm x 55 mm). All edits occur on a single focused card canvas.
Automated Grid Calculation: calculateCardGridLayout() calculates optimal sheet tiling across US Letter and A4 sheets, supporting 10-up (2 x 5), 12-up (2 x 6 and 3 x 4), 8-up (2 x 4), and customizable rows and columns.
Avery Perforated Stock Compatibility: The 10-up (2 x 5) layout on US Letter aligns directly with Avery 5371, 8371, and 8871 perforated business card stock (0.75 in side margins, 0.5 in top/bottom margins, 0 in gutter). For European A4 paper, a pre-calibrated 2 x 5 layout matches Avery C32011 / C32016 specifications.
High-Precision Cut Guidelines: Renders 14px hairline crop marks and dashed dividing lines outside card perimeters, enabling precise trimming with scissors or rotary paper cutters when using plain cardstock.
