Double-Sided Duplex Alignment & Pre-Flight Detection
Multi-page card publications benefit from specialized duplex alignment and smart printing prompts:
Horizontally Mirrored Back Columns: When printing double-sided cards (Page 1 Front, Page 2 Back), the engine automatically mirrors column ordering on Sheet 2 ( effectiveCol = cols - 1 - c ). When the sheet is flipped along the long edge in the printer, front and back designs align with microscopic accuracy.
Context-Aware Ribbon Tool: Added a dedicated "Card Sheet" button in the File ribbon next to Print and Booklet. The button dynamically displays only when working on a card-sized publication, keeping standard document ribbons uncluttered.
Smart Pre-Flight Detection: When printing any card-sized document, Open Publisher automatically prompts the user whether to print a single card or customize and tile multiple copies per sheet.
Compact Progress Dialog: Enhanced the print preparation modal with a clean 380px to 420px width, dark mode styling, and informative status updates ("Arranging & rendering card sheet X of Y...").
Smart DTP Business Card Margins (1/8 in / 0.125 in)
Standard 0.5 in margins consume 50% of a 2-inch business card height, leaving an awkward, cramped text box. Version 5.8.1 implemented industry-standard safe margins:
Automatic Safe Margin Switching: Switching page format to BusinessCard automatically sets safe margins to 1/8 in (0.125 in / 12px at 96 DPI), matching commercial printing standards (Avery, VistaPrint, Moo). Switching back to A4 or Letter restores 0.5 in defaults.
Dedicated Margin Preset: Added "Card / Label (1/8 in)" preset to the Margins dropdown menu for instant application.
Print Image Pipeline Restoration: Added universal CORS header assignment ( crossOrigin = 'anonymous' ) and layout fill normalization, ensuring cliparts, placeholders, and remote images appear crisply on imposed print sheets.
Tip: You can use the live SVG sheet preview in the Card Sheet dialog to audition different grid layouts and paper orientations before printing.

title: Pack & Go
excerpt: Use Open Publisher's Pack & Go tool to bundle your document, all embedded images, and a font manifest into a single zip file ready for any commercial print shop.
content:
Pack & Go
Pack & Go is Open Publisher’s professional handoff tool for commercial print shops. When you send a document to a printer, they need more than just the file - they need all embedded images as standard image files and a list of every font used. Pack & Go bundles everything into a single .zip folder that any printer can open and work with immediately, saving you the time and risk of manually locating and packaging assets yourself.
How to Use Pack & Go
Go to File > Export > Pack & Go .
Open Publisher runs an intelligent client-side algorithm that automatically prepares all your assets.
A .zip file is compiled and downloaded to your computer.
Hand the single .zip file to your commercial printer - they have everything they need to open, edit, and print your document.
What Pack & Go Includes
The Pack & Go algorithm performs the following steps automatically:
Image extraction - Scans your entire .opub file for all embedded Base64 image strings, extracts the raw binary data of every graphic, and converts them into standard image files (for example: image_1.jpeg , image_2.png ), organised neatly inside an Images/ folder.
Link rewriting - Rewrites the .opub project file’s internal image links to reference the newly extracted image files, so everything remains correctly connected.
Font manifest - Performs a deep scan of every font-family declaration across all elements and pages, compiles a definitive list, and generates a Fonts.txt manifest. This tells the print shop exactly which Google Fonts need to be installed to reproduce your document’s typography faithfully.
Compression - Compresses the project file, all extracted images, and the font manifest into a single .zip file and downloads it automatically.
Privacy
The entire Pack & Go process happens natively in your browser using the open-source JSZip library. Your documents and images are never uploaded to any external server - all processing takes place locally on your machine.

title: Physical Measurement Units, DPI Conversion & Print Precision
excerpt: Design documents with real-world print units (cm, mm, in, px), live DPI conversions, 300 DPI print engine precision, and zoom-invariant handles in Open Publisher.
content:
Physical Measurement Units, DPI Conversion & Print Precision
Desktop publishing requires precision that bridges on-screen pixels and physical paper dimensions. Open Publisher features a comprehensive physical measurement unit and DPI conversion subsystem. Designers can plan documents in Centimeters , Millimeters , Inches , or Pixels , switch between web (96 DPI) and commercial print (300 DPI) resolutions with live conversions, and print without multi-sheet slicing or blank page overflows.
📐 New Document & Resize Physical Units Dialog
Live physical unit conversion between Centimeters, Millimeters, Inches, and Pixels with DPI selection and canvas preview.
Centralized Physical Unit & DPI Engine
The window.UnitConversionService in core/units.js handles bidirectional mathematical conversions across the entire application:
Supported Measurement Units: Centimeters ( cm ), Millimeters ( mm ), Inches ( in ), and Screen Pixels ( px ).
Resolution Presets: Choose from 96 DPI (Standard Web / CSS default), 72 DPI (Draft / Screen), 140/150 DPI (Medium Print), 300 DPI (High-Resolution Commercial Print), or enter custom DPI values.
Canonical Paper Presets: Direct physical dimensions for standard formats including A4 (210 x 297 mm), Letter (8.5 x 11 in), A3 (297 x 420 mm), A5 (148 x 210 mm), Legal, Tabloid, Business Card (3.5 x 2 in), and Square.
Smart Format Detection: The detectFormat(w, h, dpi) engine accurately classifies paper formats regardless of whether the document is configured at 96 DPI or 300 DPI.
Print Engine Precision & Blank Sheet Elimination
High-resolution printing requires exact physical mapping to printer drivers:
Multi-Sheet Slicing Elimination: Physical @page CSS dimensions evaluate dynamically using masterPW / masterDpi . At 300 DPI, an A4 page maps to exact physical paper dimensions rather than oversized poster dimensions, fitting onto a single sheet of paper without slicing.
Sub-Pixel Rounding Fix: Height calculations apply calc(${heightInches}in - 1px) to eliminate fractional rounding overflows that previously triggered unintended blank sheets between pages.
Strict Page Breaks: Pages utilize break-inside: avoid !important; , and the final document page enforces break-after: avoid !important; to prevent empty trailing sheets.
DPI-Aware Rulers, Margins & Adaptive Viewports
Canvas tools automatically adapt to physical resolution changes:
Metric Centimeter Default: Rulers default to Centimeters ( cm ), accurately ticking from 0 to 21 cm across an A4 page regardless of chosen DPI. Right-click any ruler to switch units to Inches, Millimeters, or Pixels.
DPI-Invariant Margins: Margin guides maintain constant physical distances (e.g. 0.5 inches / 1.27 cm) across DPI changes, scaling internal pixel counts automatically so margins do not collapse against page borders.
Adaptive Multi-Page View: The multi-page overview threshold calculates dynamically as 0.45 * (96 / dpi) . On 300 DPI documents, a 20% zoom fit remains in clean single-page view rather than prematurely triggering multi-page layout.
Zoom-Invariant Control Handles: Selection and resize handles use inverse-zoom CSS custom properties to maintain a constant, comfortable 10px optical screen size even when zoomed out to 15% on high-DPI canvases.
Interactive Status Bar DPI Badge & Toast
The bottom status bar features an unobtrusive #dpi-status-display badge showing active resolution (e.g., 300 DPI). Hovering reveals a translucent highlight, and clicking the badge instantly opens the Page Setup / Resize Document dialog. When DPI is modified, a signature teal toast notification confirms that dimensions and content scaled proportionally.
Tip: When resizing an existing document to 300 DPI, leave "Scale page content automatically" checked to proportionally scale all text boxes, images, and shapes to the new resolution.

title: Print Engine html2canvas Background Parsing Fix & Export Resilience
excerpt: Explore Open Publisher
content:
Print Engine html2canvas Background Parsing Fix & Export Resilience
Documents in Open Publisher often feature rich visual backdrops: full-bleed photographic textures, base64 data URLs, imported company watermarks, and compound background shorthands. Printing or exporting these documents requires the rasterization pipeline to interpret background properties cleanly without stalling. Earlier versions could encounter an immediate "Print Error: Failed to generate print file." alert dialog when printing pages with complex background rules. Version 5.7.4 resolved this issue through centralized background color sanitization, defensive rasterization fallbacks, and comprehensive protections across image and email export workflows.
🖨️ High-DPI Print Spooler with Complex Image Background
Pages containing high-resolution photographic backgrounds and shadows and data URLs print seamlessly with zero syntax rejections.
html2canvas parseColor Syntax Rejection Root Cause
The print failure stemmed from an incompatibility between compound CSS background declarations and the html2canvas canvas configuration:
Compound Background Forwarding: In extensions/print-engine.js , the print loop computed h2cBg = page.background || '#ffffff' . While linear and radial gradients were guarded against, image URLs ( url(...) ) and multi-token CSS shorthands (such as url("data:image/webp;base64,...") center center / cover no-repeat ) were passed directly into the backgroundColor parameter.
Strict Color Token Parser: The html2canvas library strictly parses its backgroundColor option as a single CSS color value. When provided space-separated tokens or image URLs, its internal CSS parser threw a fatal SyntaxError : "Error parsing CSS component value, multiple values found when expecting only one".
Repeated Fallback Failure: Because the lower-resolution fallback raster pass reused the exact same backgroundColor argument, both attempts crashed in succession, triggering the modal error alert.
Centralized Sanitization via sanitizeH2cBackgroundColor
To resolve the parsing conflict cleanly at the source, Open Publisher introduced a universal sanitizer utility in core/core.js :
Strict Color Pattern Matching: window.sanitizeH2cBackgroundColor(bg, hasActiveTheme) checks if a background string matches valid single CSS color notation: hexadecimal ( #fff , #123456 ), RGB/RGBA, HSL/HSLA, or recognized single named colors.
Transparent Fallback for Complex Styles: If the background includes url(...) , gradient , multiple shorthand values, or an active theme, the function returns null (transparent canvas).
DOM-Level Background Rendering: Because pageWrapper.style.background already applies the complete CSS background to the DOM element itself, html2canvas renders the imagery and tiling directly on the element surface without crashing the canvas background parser.
Multi-Tier Fallback & Export Pipeline Resilience
In addition to background sanitization, Open Publisher added multi-tiered defenses across all raster-based export features:
Emergency Transparent Retry: In extensions/print-engine.js , the fallback raster pass is wrapped in a nested try/catch block. If rasterization ever fails with a background color, it immediately performs an emergency retry with backgroundColor: null before failing.
Export to Image Parity: In io/export/canvas-renderer.js , the high-resolution image exporter routes background properties through sanitizeH2cBackgroundColor , ensuring PNG and JPEG exports never crash on complex backgrounds.
Email Attachment Export: In io/export/export.js , the HTML email generator applies identical sanitization to page raster attachments, guaranteeing dependable email sharing.
Tip: When designing publications with full-bleed backgrounds, you can freely mix photographic wallpapers with overlay shapes; the print engine will preserve all layers with exact fidelity.

title: Printing Your Document
excerpt: Print your Open Publisher document with full-bleed support, automatic mixed-orientation handling, and a micro-bleed correction to eliminate fractional white borders.
content:
Printing Your Document
Open Publisher’s print engine is designed to produce accurate,professional output - handling full-bleed designs, mixed page orientations, and fine edge corrections automatically so your printed result matches what you see on screen.
Standard Printing
To print your document, go to File > Print or use the print button in the ribbon. This opens your system’s print modal where you can select your printer, paper size, and number of copies.
Mixed Page Orientations
If your document contains a mix of portrait and landscape pages, Open Publisher handles this automatically. The print engine detects each page’s orientation and recalculates dimensions mathematically before feeding them into the print stream - so a landscape page between two portrait pages prints perfectly without any manual intervention.
Micro-Bleed Correction
A 100.4% micro-bleed is automatically applied during printing to eliminate the fractional white border that can appear on full-bleed designs This subtle scaling ensures your design fills the page edge-to-edge on physical output.

title: Share via Email
excerpt: Share any Open Publisher page as the visual body of an email. Exports a .eml file that opens in Outlook, Apple Mail, or Thunderbird ready to address and send.
content:
Share via Email
The Share via Email feature lets you send any page as the visual body of an email - without manually attaching files, screenshotting, or dealing with complex email formatting. Open Publisher handles the entire process and hands you a ready-to-send file.
How to Share a Page via Email
Go to File > Share > Email , or click the Email button in the Share group.
Open Publisher captures a high-resolution snapshot of the current page (with all selection boxes hidden), encodes it as Base64, and wraps it in a standard multi-part MIME .eml file structure.
The .eml file is automatically downloaded to your computer.
Open the downloaded file - your default email client (Outlook, Apple Mail, Thunderbird, etc.) opens with your page perfectly embedded in the email body, ready to address and send.
Filter Accuracy
All CSS filters applied to images,such as hue rotation and brightness adjustments are correctly reflected in the emailed image.
The email export uses the same capture pipeline as the image export, so what you see on screen is exactly what your recipients will see.

title: Smart Arrow Printing Engine & Export Visibility Architecture
excerpt: Ensure 100% vector fidelity and print visibility for Smart Arrows with clean DOM replacement, self-describing SVGs, and high-DPI raster baking.
content: Smart Arrow Printing Engine & Export Visibility Architecture A primary requirement of professional desktop publishing software is absolute export reliability: every graphic designed on screen must appear in final output with identical positioning, color, and sharpness. In version 5.3.4, Open Publisher resolved a critical regression where Smart Arrows disappeared from printed pages, PDF documents, and image exports due to an invalid DOM nesting structure during rasterization. The updated export architecture guarantees 100% visibility, crisp vector rendering, and zero edge clipping. 🖨️ Clean Print Spooler DOM & High-DPI Arrow Export Smart Arrows are converted into clean high-resolution image elements during print staging, ensuring complete visibility across all printers. The Root Cause of Invisible Printed Arrows Deep architectural auditing revealed three interconnected flaws in the print staging pipeline: Invalid HTML-in-SVG Insertion: In prior iterations, bakeSmartArrowForPrint() targeted the inner element container. When executed on print staging divs, it mistakenly inserted an HTML directly inside the ). Modern browser print engines and html2canvas discard illegal HTML inside SVG, causing arrows to vanish completely. Attribute Loss in Print DOM: Print staging elements created in buildPrintDOM() and printFullDocument() omitted custom data attributes, causing arrows to collapse to default dimensions. Detached Theme Variable Invalidation: Offscreen print staging containers could not resolve CSS custom properties (such as var(--ui-theme-color) ), leading to transparent or blank fills. The Robust Node-Replacement Engine Version 5.3.4 re-engineered the print baking pipeline in elements/arrow/arrow.js and extensions/print-engine.js : Clean Node Replacement: Replaced innerHTML injection with explicit DOM replacement: svg.parentNode.replaceChild(img, svg) . The baked high-resolution completely replaces the SVG node, guaranteeing valid DOM structure. Self-Describing SVGs: Stamped style IDs, tip lengths, and stroke properties directly onto SVG root attributes. SVGs now carry their own complete geometry metadata even when processed in isolated print threads. Staging Attribute Preservation: Updated print staging builders to copy all arrow attributes ( data-type , data-arrow-style , data-arrow-head , data-arrow-stroke-width ) onto staging elements. Universal Export Coverage: Integrated arrow pre-baking across native browser print spooling, PDF document generation, image export, and email HTML attachments. Tip: Baked print images include dynamic stroke bleed margins, ensuring thick decorative borders never suffer from clipped corners on paper or PDF.

title: Spreads Mode Document Metadata & High-DPI Persistence
excerpt: Ensure multi-page publications open in their intended single-page or two-page spread layout with metadata-driven persistence in Open Publisher.
content:
Spreads Mode Document Metadata & High-DPI Persistence
Designing multi-page booklets, magazines, and greeting cards often involves switching between single-page layouts and side-by-side two-page spreads. In version 5.1.9, Open Publisher resolved an issue where single-page publications configured with high-DPI print resolutions (such as 200 DPI or 300 DPI) accidentally opened in two-page spread mode. Spreads mode is now driven entirely by explicit document metadata rather than arbitrary pixel dimension thresholds.
📖 Single-Page vs. Two-Page Spread Layout Mode
Spreads mode is preserved authoritatively in document metadata, preventing high-resolution files from opening as spreads.
The Legacy Pixel Width Inference Flaw
Investigation revealed that the file loader contained a legacy inference rule intended for early document versions that lacked dedicated spreads metadata:
Width Threshold Assumption: The loader in io/publisher-file-loader.js executed state.isSpreadMode = w >= 1500 , assuming that any page width of 1500px or greater represented two facing pages side-by-side (such as 2x A4 at 96 DPI = 1588px).
High-DPI Collision: While this assumption worked at 96 DPI, any standard single-page document saved at higher print resolutions exceeded the 1500px boundary (for instance, single A4 at 200 DPI is 1654px; single A4 at 300 DPI is 2480px).
Unintended Mode Activation: Consequently, single-page print flyers and brochures saved at 300 DPI reopened with Spreads mode enabled, splitting single pages across two facing viewports.
Metadata-Driven Spreads Contract
The width-based inference was removed across the loading and saving architecture:
Authoritative Metadata: The application now reads state.isSpreadMode = !!data.isSpreadMode directly from the file schema. If a publication was saved with spreads active, it opens with spreads; if saved in single-page mode, it remains strictly single-page.
Safe Legacy Default: For older legacy documents predating the metadata field, the loader defaults cleanly to false . Users can toggle spreads manually from the Layout menu whenever desired.
Comprehensive Load Path Audit: Verified full consistency across native file loading, Dashboard recent cards, history undo/redo snapshots, and document serialization.
Designing Booklets & Facing Pages
When designing facing spreads (such as magazine centerfolds or event programs), toggle Two-Page Spread from the Page Setup menu under the Layout tab. Open Publisher aligns even and odd pages side-by-side, allowing you to design continuous graphics across the binding gutter with full export fidelity.
Tip: When exporting a spreads publication to PDF, you can choose between individual single sheets for commercial printing or composite two-page spreads for digital viewing.

title: Bulk Selection Transform Support & Clean Multi-Selection Overlay Engine
excerpt: Resize and orbit multiple canvas elements together with Open Publisher
content:
Bulk Selection Transform Support & Clean Multi-Selection Overlay Engine
Designing intricate publications frequently requires manipulating clusters of elements: resizing a composite logo alongside its caption, rotating an angled diagram with its callout arrows, or scaling a complex product card arrangement. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, selecting multiple items permitted collective movement, but resizing or rotating in bulk was unsupported. Furthermore, individual dashed boxes remained visible around every selected element, creating cluttered overlapping outlines. Version 5.6.4 introduced complete Bulk Selection Transform Support paired with the Clean Multi-Selection Overlay Engine.
🔲 Unified Group Selection Box with 8 Resize Handles & Orbit Rotate Stem
Multiple elements are enclosed in a single master bounding box with collective resize handles and a top rotation stem.
Unified Master Bounding Box Architecture
When two or more elements are selected via marquee drag or Ctrl -clicking, Open Publisher computes collective geometric boundaries:
Projected Corner Calculation: Evaluates the unrotated and rotated corners of all active elements in paper space, establishing an exact enclosing master rectangle ( #group-selection-overlay ).
Suppression of Inner Dashed Boxes: Redundant individual selection rectangles are suppressed during multi-selection, presenting a crisp, unified outline without visual clutter.
In-Place DOM Synchronization: Selection handles maintain persistent DOM identity, updating positions at 60 FPS without tearing or node destruction during interaction.
Proportional Multi-Element Resizing
Dragging any of the eight collective resize handles ( nw , n , ne , e , se , s , sw , w ) scales the entire cluster:
Relative Position Scaling: Calculates scale factors ( factorX , factorY ) from the group origin, scaling each element's width, height, and offset to preserve exact relative spacing.
Modifier Keys: Hold Shift to constrain group scaling to the cluster's original aspect ratio, or hold Ctrl ( Cmd on macOS) to resize outward symmetrically from the group center.
Smart Component Adaptation: Image frames scale preview dimensions, text boxes reflow content, and smart arrow geometry recalculates proportionally.
Circular Orbit Rotation Around Collective Center
The top rotation stem allows rotating entire layouts with intuitive pivot physics:
Group Center Orbit: Dragging the top rotate handle calculates angular delta ( deltaDeg ) around the collective centroid (cx, cy) , orbiting each element's center point in real time.
Individual Rotation Updating: Simultaneously updates each object's individual CSS transform angle, preserving flips and orientations.
Single-Keystroke History Undo: Every bulk transform commits atomic pre- and post-interaction undo snapshots, allowing instant rollback with Ctrl + Z .
Tip: Group elements visually by selecting them together, then drag the top green handle to orbit the entire group as a unified graphic.

title: Cloud Conversion Tunnel Resilience & Legacy Document Import
excerpt: Explore Open Publisher
content:
Cloud Conversion Tunnel Resilience & Legacy Document Import
A cornerstone capability of Open Publisher is its ability to import and convert legacy publication formats, including Microsoft Publisher ( .pub ), legacy Microsoft Word ( .doc ), and modern Word documents ( .docx ). Because parsing proprietary legacy desktop publishing schemas requires specialized server-side libraries (such as libmspub ), Open Publisher routes uploaded files through secure cloud conversion worker tunnels. When external network disruptions impacted tunnel routing, conversion jobs could stall or fail silently. Version 4.19.4 deployed a targeted resilience patch to restore robust conversion connectivity.
☁️ Cloud Document Conversion Pipeline & Tunnel Failover
Cloud conversion API routes legacy .pub and Word documents through encrypted tunnel endpoints.
Secure Cloudflare Tunnel Architecture
The conversion pipeline in io/file-io.js delegates binary parsing to dedicated conversion microservices:
Resilient Endpoint Routing: Following upstream tunnel downtime, API calls in file-io.js were re-routed to newly configured, hardened trycloudflare.com tunnel endpoints.
Dedicated Conversion POST Routes: Conversion requests are dispatched to specialized endpoints:
convert-pub : Deserializes complex Publisher binary streams, extracting vector coordinates, text frame chains, and embedded images.
convert-doc : Converts Word documents into structured HTML layouts mapped to Open Publisher text boxes and paragraph styles.
Error Handling & Timeout Recovery
Version 4.19.4 hardened client-side network error recovery:
Graceful UI Notifications: Instead of silent promise rejections, network errors display clear status notifications guiding users on connection status or file size limitations.
Client-Side Validation: File types and payloads are validated prior to upload, preventing transmission of corrupted or unsupported files.
Global Cachebuster Synchronization
To ensure all users received the updated endpoints immediately, cachebusters across index.html , dashboard.js , and templates.js were bumped to ?v=4.19.4 , clearing stale worker scripts from browser caches.
Tip: When importing Microsoft Publisher files, ensure embedded images and custom fonts are saved within the source document for maximum conversion fidelity.

title: Direct PDF Import & Editable Layout Reconstruction Engine
excerpt: Open and edit PDF files directly in OpenPublisher with client-side layout reconstruction, Editable Text Mode, Flattened Image Safe Mode, and column-safe baseline alignment.
content:
Direct PDF Document Opening & Editable Layout Reconstruction
Opening and editing existing PDF documents has traditionally required costly subscriptions or cumbersome conversion utilities. Starting with OpenPublisher v5.13.1 and v5.13.2 , you can now open standard PDF documents directly inside OpenPublisher with zero cloud dependencies. Every page, text line, heading, and graphic is unpacked and reconstructed on your physical-measurement canvas using our high-fidelity, client-side ingestion engine.
100% Client-Side Privacy: Your PDF files never leave your computer. OpenPublisher processes document streams locally in memory through pure client-side PDF rendering pipelines, keeping sensitive business contracts, financial summaries, and personal documents completely private.
How to Open a PDF Document in OpenPublisher
You can bring any standard PDF into OpenPublisher using three simple workflows:
Direct Drag-and-Drop: Drag any .pdf file straight from your desktop or File Explorer and drop it anywhere over the OpenPublisher workspace or Start Screen.
File Menu: Navigate to File > Open (or press Ctrl + O on Windows/Linux or Cmd + O on macOS) and select your PDF file.
Startup Dashboard Dropzone: On the Startup Dashboard, drop your document onto the Open tab dropzone (which officially supports .opub , .pdf , .pub , .docx , and .xlsx ).
The Pre-Flight Import Dialog: Choosing Your Mode
Whenever a PDF document is selected, OpenPublisher displays an interactive Pre-Flight Import Dialog that lets you choose exactly how you want your document processed based on your project goals:
1. Editable Text Mode (Recommended)
Deconstructs the PDF into live, independent text boxes, headings, and paragraphs placed at their exact physical coordinates. You can immediately highlight words, fix typos, alter font families, change colors, and reposition blocks freely across the canvas.
2. Flattened Image Safe Mode
Bakes each page into an ultra high-resolution 2.5x raster canvas backdrop. This guarantees 100% visual parity for highly complex vector illustrations, exotic proprietary fonts, or forms where you simply need to stamp new text boxes or signatures over an existing form without altering underlying text.
Under the Hood: High-Fidelity PDF Reconstruction (v5.13.2)
Converting arbitrary PDF streams into clean desktop publishing layouts is a notorious technical challenge because PDFs often store words as individual character glyphs without innate column or paragraph boundaries. Version 5.13.2 introduced an architectural overhaul to the PDF reconstruction pipeline:
Column-Safe Line Grouping: Previous tools frequently merge words from adjacent table columns if they share a similar horizontal baseline. OpenPublisher v5.13.2 introduces bidirectional gap testing. If two text runs are separated by a natural column gutter, they are preserved as distinct text boxes, ensuring table cells and status badges remain strictly within their intended columns.
Measured Font Ascent Positioning: Instead of guessing container height based on nominal font size, the engine computes the exact distance between the PDF font baseline and the measured ascent of the local substitute font. This prevents headings and labels from drifting upward or downward.
Accurate Width Fitting & Letter Spacing: A subtle, clamped letter-spacing micro-adjustment is calculated for every text run so that imported lines occupy the exact physical width of the source document without awkward word wraps.
Automatic Contrast Guard: Detects whether text runs share the same hue as the underlying background (such as white text on a colorful button or dark text on a dark banner). The Contrast Guard automatically flips the fill to high-contrast white or deep charcoal to ensure labels never vanish into invisibility.
