Practical Workflow: Re-Exporting Your Revisions
Once you have opened a PDF and made your desired edits, you can save your working project as a native .opub file to preserve all new layers and adjustments. When you are ready to distribute your finished work, head to File > Export > Export to PDF to generate a brand new, clean 300 DPI PDF document complete with embedded vector typography.
Need More Details? Check out our guides on Opening & Importing Files and Exporting to PDF .

title: Drop Cap
excerpt: Add a classic Drop Cap to any text box in Open Publisher with a single right-click, creating a large decorative first letter in the style of newspapers and magazines.
content:
Drop Cap
A Drop Cap (short for “dropped capital”) stylises the first letter of a paragraph as a large, decorative capital that drops down into the lines of text below. This is a classic typographic technique widely used in newspapers, magazines, novels, and editorial layouts. Incorporating a drop cap is an excellent way to draw the reader’s eye directly to the opening of a body of text, break up intimidating walls of copy, and instantly give your overall layout a highly polished, professional feel.
How to Apply a Drop Cap
Adding a drop cap in Open Publisher is incredibly straightforward and bypasses the need for complex formatting menus:
Ensure you have typed your paragraph, then right-click anywhere on the desired text box on your canvas.
From the context menu that appears, select Drop Cap .
Once clicked, the first letter of the selected text box is immediately enlarged and dynamically formatted as a decorative capital. The surrounding text will automatically shift and wrap around the newly sized letter seamlessly. This feature works on any standard text box in your document and is applied instantly with no additional configuration needed.
Tips for Effective Design
Use Sparingly: Drop caps are most effective when used at the very beginning of an article, a new chapter, or a major section. Applying them to every single paragraph can clutter your page and make the text difficult to read.
Dynamic Editing: If you decide to rewrite the beginning of your paragraph or delete the first word, Open Publisher automatically applies the drop cap styling to the new first letter, keeping your layout intact without requiring you to reapply the setting.
.

title: Mac Keyboard Backspace Delete Support
excerpt: Delete selected canvas objects on macOS keyboards using the primary Backspace key with smart text-editing protection in Open Publisher.
content:
Mac Keyboard Backspace Delete Support
On Apple keyboards, the primary key used to erase text is labeled Delete , but it emits the standard Backspace key signal. In previous releases of Open Publisher, canvas object deletion was strictly bound to the forward Delete keycode, leaving Mac users unable to remove selected images, shapes, tables, or publication frames without using on-screen context menus. Open Publisher introduces dual-key parity, allowing Mac and PC users alike to delete selected canvas items instantly using either Delete or Backspace .
⌨️ Canvas Object Selection and Mac Keyboard Deletion
Selecting image frames, vector shapes, or text boxes and pressing Delete (Backspace) on macOS instantly removes the selected object.
Dual-Key Canvas Deletion Engine
The keyboard listener in core/keyboard.js has been updated to evaluate both key codes simultaneously:
Delete and Backspace Parity: Pressing either Delete or Backspace removes any actively selected canvas element, multi-element grouping, or image frame.
Native Browser Interception: When Backspace is pressed with a canvas item selected, the application calls e.preventDefault() . This eliminates the risk of browsers interpreting Backspace as a "Navigate Back" command and unloading your document.
Multi-Object Selection Support: If multiple elements are selected using Shift-click or marquee selection, pressing Delete or Backspace clears the entire group in a single undoable action.
Smart Text Editing Protection
A critical consideration when supporting the Backspace key on the canvas is preventing accidental deletions while users are typing inside text frames or table cells:
Active Context Inspection: The isTextEditing() detection engine checks whether the user's cursor or caret resides inside a content-editable container, paragraph node, or table cell.
Protected Character Erase: When editing text, Backspace performs its normal typographic function - erasing characters to the left of the caret - without triggering canvas element removal.
Nested Hierarchy Traversal: The detection scans nested formatting nodes (such as spans, bold tags, and hyperlinks), ensuring that complex formatted text never suffers premature element deletion.
Cross-Platform Workflow Parity
Whether designing on Windows, macOS, or Linux, your muscle memory remains consistent. Mac notebook users without full-sized numeric keypads can work at full speed without needing external keyboards or multi-key modifier combinations.
Tip: If you accidentally delete an element on macOS or Windows, press Cmd + Z or Ctrl + Z to restore it immediately with all formatting intact.

title: Multi-Select, Grouping & Flip
excerpt: Select multiple elements in Open Publisher using marquee selection, Ctrl+Click, or Shift+Click, and flip any element horizontally or vertically by dragging its resize handle.
content:
Multi-Select, Grouping & Flip
Open Publisher provides several ways to select and work with multiple elements at once,
as well as a quick gesture for mirroring any element without using a menu.
Selecting Multiple Elements
There are three ways to select more than one element at a time:
Marquee Selection - Click and drag on an empty area of the canvas to draw a selection rectangle. Any element whose bounds fall within the rectangle is selected automatically.
Ctrl+Click / Cmd+Click - Hold Ctrl (Windows / Linux) or Cmd (Mac) and click additional elements to add them to the current selection one by one.
Once multiple elements are selected, you can move, resize, and delete them all at once.
Flipping & Mirroring
To flip any element horizontally or vertically, drag one of its resize handles past the element’s opposite edge . Dragging past the left or right edge mirrors it horizontally; dragging past the top or bottom edge mirrors it vertically. No menu required - it happens naturally as part of the resize gesture.
A Note on Grouping
The Group feature is currently unavailable and is greyed out in the menu. Use the multi-select methods above as a working alternative for managing several elements together.

title: Opening & Importing Files
excerpt: OpenPublisher can open and import PDF documents, Word files, Excel and CSV spreadsheets, legacy Microsoft Publisher (.pub) files, SVGs, and images directly onto the canvas with editable text and flattened safe modes.
content:
Opening & Importing Files
Open Publisher is designed to act as a versatile hub for all your design assets. In addition to saving and loading its native .opub format, the software can effortlessly open and import a wide variety of standard file types. You can bring external content into your project traditionally via the File > Open menu, or for a faster workflow, you can simply drag & drop files directly from your computer’s desktop.
Supported File Types
File Type
Extension(s)
Description
Native Format
.opub, .json
Full fidelity project loading - restores your entire working session exactly as it was saved, preserving all layers, text boxes, master pages, styling, and high-resolution assets.
PDF Documents
.pdf
Direct client-side layout reconstruction with zero cloud dependencies. Choose between Editable Text Mode (converts lines and headings into live editable text boxes) or Flattened Image Safe Mode (high-res 2.5x raster plates for form stamping and signatures).
Word Documents
.doc, .docx
Word processor documents trigger an intelligent Import Wizard with two modes: extract flowing text into editable OpenPublisher text boxes or flatten pages into pixel-perfect backdrop images.
Excel Spreadsheets & Data
.xlsx, .xls, .csv
Spreadsheets and comma-separated data are intelligently rendered as fully interactive, movable, and resizable table objects on the canvas, preserving your grid structure and cell values.
Publisher Files
.pub, .pubx
Legacy Microsoft Publisher import engine converts older binary and XML publication files into editable canvas elements, text frames, shapes, and images.
Images & Vectors
.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .svg
Dropped or opened images and SVG vector files are instantly placed directly onto the active canvas as movable, resizable elements, ready to be cropped, styled, or filtered.
Direct PDF Document Opening & Layout Reconstruction
Starting with OpenPublisher v5.13.1 and v5.13.2 , you can open and edit standard PDF files directly inside the workspace without any third-party conversion software or subscriptions. Every page, paragraph, heading, and graphic element is parsed locally in memory through our high-performance client-side reconstruction pipeline.
100% Client-Side Privacy Guarantee: Your PDF documents never leave your computer. OpenPublisher performs all stream decoding, vector extraction, and text positioning directly inside your local browser or desktop sandbox.
Whenever you drag and drop a .pdf file into OpenPublisher or select it from File > Open , the interactive Pre-Flight Import Dialog appears, letting you select how to reconstruct the document:
1. Editable Text Mode (Recommended)
Deconstructs the PDF into live, independent OpenPublisher text boxes, headings, and lines placed at their precise canvas coordinates. You can immediately edit copy, fix typos, alter font families, change colors, and reposition blocks freely.
Column-Safe Line Grouping: Bidirectional gap testing preserves distinct columns and tables.
Measured Font Ascent Positioning: Prevents upward or downward text baseline drifting.
Automatic Contrast Guard: Ensures white text on dark backgrounds remains legible.
2. Flattened Image Safe Mode
Bakes each page into an ultra high-resolution 2.5x raster canvas backdrop plate. This guarantees 100% visual layout accuracy for intricate vector illustrations, architectural blueprints, or documents with rare embedded fonts.
Zero Formatting Shifts: Pixel-perfect reproduction of complex print proofs.
Form Stamping & Signing: Overlay new text boxes, checkboxes, or signatures on top of existing forms.
Non-Destructive Background: Underlying source imagery remains locked and protected.
Read Full Deep Dive: Direct PDF Import & Layout Reconstruction Engine →
Word Document Import Modes
Word processors use "flowing" text rather than absolute page coordinates. Because of this, dropping or opening a .doc or .docx file triggers an intelligent Import Wizard with two specific modes, allowing you to choose how the text is handled based on your project needs:
Import Mode
Description
Editable Text Mode
The engine extracts all paragraphs, fonts, and colours, and intelligently converts them into editable Open Publisher text boxes. This is best for articles, essays, and standard documents where you want to continue rewriting or styling the content after importing.
Flattened Image Mode
(Safe Mode)
The document is rendered as a crisp, high-resolution, uneditable background image, locking everything in place to guarantee 100% layout accuracy. Highly recommended for complex forms, technical medical tables, or any document where pixel-perfect formatting fidelity matters more than the ability to edit the text.
Excel Spreadsheets & CSV Data Ingestion
Unlike standard word processors that paste spreadsheet content as unformatted tabbed text, OpenPublisher automatically converts incoming .xlsx , .xls , and .csv files into full native Table Objects .
Automatic Cell Grid Formatting: Preserves row heights, column widths, headers, and numeric cell alignments directly from the spreadsheet.
Interactive Editing on the Canvas: Click any cell to modify text, insert or delete rows and columns, split and merge cells, or apply alternate row shading.
Ribbon Table Tools: When an imported table is selected, the Table Tools ribbon appears with styling palettes, cell margins, and border controls.
Learn More in Tables Documentation →
Legacy Microsoft Publisher Import (.pub & .pubx)
With Microsoft Publisher scheduled for official retirement in October 2026, OpenPublisher includes a dedicated Publisher Ingestion Engine designed to migrate legacy assets without requiring an active Microsoft 365 subscription.
Frame Translation: Deconstructs proprietary Publisher text frames, shapes, clipart, and WordArt objects into native OpenPublisher canvas elements.
Direct Drag-and-Drop: Simply drop your .pub file onto the workspace to begin the conversion process.
Post-Import Inspection: Because legacy Publisher documents often use proprietary font metrics, check for any slight text overflow badges or line wrap differences and tweak text box widths accordingly.
Fast Ingestion Workflows & Content Migration
Canvas Drag-and-Drop
Drop files directly from File Explorer, Finder, or your desktop onto any open page or the surrounding scratch area to place them instantly.
Startup Dashboard Dropzone
Open documents straight from the Startup Dashboard Open tab with dedicated drop targets supporting all recognized formats.
Insert > File (Merging)
Merge pages and design elements from another .opub project into your current publication using Insert File .
External File Watcher
When external image files are edited in third-party tools like Photoshop or GIMP, the File Watcher updates them automatically on the canvas.

title: QoL & Workflow Shortcuts
excerpt: Discover essential workflow shortcuts in Open Publisher, including the Escape key to close modals, direct text-box editing, and smart spread cleanup.
content:
Quality of Life & Workflow Shortcuts
Open Publisher is built on the philosophy that great software should get out of your way. Alongside our major features, the engine includes several subtle, behind-the-scenes enhancements designed specifically to speed up your daily design workflow, reduce repetitive clicking, and eliminate the minor friction points that often slow down creative projects.
Direct Text Box Editing
In many traditional design applications, text boxes are treated strictly as layout shapes-meaning you have to click once to select the object, and then double-click again just to access the text inside. Open Publisher removes this barrier entirely. You don’t need to double-click a text box to start editing it. If you have an unselected text box on your canvas, simply clicking directly on the text inside it will instantly place the text cursor at that exact spot. This allows you to highlight text natively or start typing immediately, bypassing “drag mode” completely for a much more natural writing experience.
Note: Hovering and clicking on the outer bounding box edges or empty space of a text box will still correctly trigger the “Move” cursor, allowing you to quickly grab and reposition the box without accidentally highlighting the text.
Escape Key Modal Dismissal
When you are deep in a creative flow, constantly switching between your keyboard and mouse to close pop-up menus can break your momentum. To keep you moving quickly, every single modal dialog window in Open Publisher - including the Accessibility Checker, Page Parts Library, Custom Colour Picker, Document Settings, and Export tools - is tied into a global keyboard listener. You can instantly close any open modal window simply by pressing the Escape (Esc) key on your keyboard, saving you from having to hunt for the mouse to click the small ‘X’ close button.
Smart Spread Cleanup
Designing a booklet or magazine often requires toggling viewing modes to see how pages sit next to one another. If you toggle Double-Page Spread mode on to preview your layout, Open Publisher automatically generates a blank right-hand page to mathematically complete the spread on your canvas. However, if you decide you don’t need that layout and immediately toggle Spread Mode back off, the application uses a smart cleanup routine to automatically detect and purge that newly generated blank artifact. This ensures you aren’t left with an empty, unwanted trailing page ruining your document structure or your final PDF export.
Note: This system is completely safe for your content. If you have placed any text, images, or elements on that generated right-hand page while in Spread Mode, the cleanup routine will detect your work, safely preserve the page, and append it to your standard single-page document normally.

title: Save As Functionality
excerpt: Safely branch publications and create duplicate templates in Open Publisher using the dedicated Save As ribbon command and Ctrl+Shift+S shortcut.
content:
Save As Functionality
In professional desktop publishing, protecting original master templates while creating new publication variants is essential. Open Publisher features a dedicated Save As function, allowing you to branch off existing projects into new files without altering or overwriting your original source document.
💾 Open Publisher Save As Dialog Prompt
Dedicated Save As prompt requesting a new filename to branch publications securely.
Dedicated Ribbon Integration
The Save As command is seamlessly integrated into the application interface:
File Tab Placement: Access Save As directly from the main Ribbon under the File tab, positioned conveniently right below the standard Save option.
Filename Prompt: Clicking Save As triggers the saveDocumentAs backend handler, which gracefully prompts you for a new document title before writing to disk.
Active Session Switching: Once saved, your active working session immediately updates to the new publication, leaving your previous file intact in its original folder.
Keyboard Shortcuts
For high-speed workflows, Save As can be triggered without lifting your hands from the keyboard:
Windows & Linux: Press Ctrl + Shift + S .
macOS: Press Cmd + Shift + S .
Native Interception: The shortcut is mapped natively at the system patch level, preventing web browsers from opening browser save dialogs instead of Open Publisher's file routine.
Safe Template Branching
Save As provides the ideal foundation for document templates. You can open a standardized corporate brochure or newsletter template, make project-specific alterations, and save the result as a new .opub file with complete confidence that your original template remains pristine.
Note: All embedded graphics, page layouts, and custom theme swatches are carried over into the new publication file.
Desktop File Path Detachment & Overwrite Prevention (v5.18.0)
When creating iterative revisions or saving variations of an existing project, ensuring you never accidentally overwrite your base publication is vital. OpenPublisher v5.18.0 introduced a crucial safety enhancement to the desktop client:
Desktop client file path detachment in OpenPublisher v5.18.0, preventing accidental project overwriting.
When you select File > Save As and specify a new filename, OpenPublisher immediately detaches the old file path handle in memory. Subsequent standard save operations ( Ctrl + S ) write exclusively to the newly chosen destination, ensuring your original template or earlier draft remains completely untouched.
Web Browser File Saving Restoration & Defensive Fallbacks (v5.19.2)
In web environments where browser security policies restrict direct file system access, OpenPublisher v5.19.2 delivers a robust, multi-tiered saving architecture:
Web application file saving restoration with defensive Blob download fallback in OpenPublisher v5.19.2.
Native File System Access API: In Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave), OpenPublisher uses the native File System Access API to save changes directly back to your local file without repeated download prompts.
Defensive Blob Fallback: In Firefox, Safari, or strict private browsing windows where the File System API is blocked, OpenPublisher automatically triggers a seamless client-side Blob download. Your project is preserved safely with zero data loss.

title: Text Fit: Best Fit
excerpt: Use Open Publisher's Text Fit Best Fit to automatically scale your font size so text fills any text box perfectly, with no manual trial and error required.
content:
Text Fit: Best Fit
Say goodbye to the tedious trial-and-error of manually guessing point sizes. Text Fit: Best Fit is a powerful layout tool that automatically scales your font size up or down so that your text fills its container exactly. Instead of repeatedly highlighting text and tweaking the size until it looks somewhat right, Open Publisher mathematically calculates the optimal font dimensions for your specific text box and applies it instantly with a single click, perfectly balancing your text within its boundaries.
How to Use Text Fit
Applying the Best Fit setting is quick and requires no advanced formatting menus:
Right-click anywhere inside or on the border of the text box you wish to adjust on your canvas.
From the context menu that appears, select Text Fit > Best Fit .
The font size will adjust immediately, scaling proportionally so that the text spans both the width and height dimensions of the box as closely as possible without overflowing or causing clipping.
When to Use It
While manual text sizing is standard for regular body paragraphs, Text Fit: Best Fit is a massive time-saver for specific design scenarios:
Headings and titles - Perfect for front covers or article headers where you want the text to span the full width of its container at whatever size fits naturally, eliminating awkward gaps and ensuring a bold, unified look.
Fixed-size layout boxes - Essential when working with rigid templates, brochures, or grids where the physical box dimensions are strictly set by your overall design. In these cases, the font must adapt to fit the space provided, rather than the box stretching to accommodate the text.
Banners and labels - Ideal for certificates, name tags, and promotional graphics where text needs to fill the available space for maximum visual impact, regardless of whether a name or word is remarkably long or exceptionally short.
A Quick Design Tip
Because Best Fit dynamically changes the font size based on the volume of text and the size of the container, we recommend avoiding it for standard body text, especially in multi-column layouts. Using it on linked paragraph boxes can result in inconsistent, mismatched font sizes across your document, which can reduce readability. Reserve Best Fit for your standout, high-impact text elements!

title: The Custom Colour Picker
excerpt: Open Publisher's colour picker features a tabbed interface, a professional 2D gradient wheel, RGB and Hex inputs, an eyedropper tool, and real-time synchronised colour selection.
content:
The Custom Colour Picker
Achieving the perfect visual aesthetic requires precise control over your palette. Open Publisher includes a professional-grade custom colour picker, intuitively accessible whenever you need to select a colour for text, backgrounds, geometric shapes, or page borders. Designed to accommodate both rapid prototyping and strict corporate design guidelines, it features a seamless tabbed interface that lets you instantly switch between a library of quick swatches and a full custom colour selection suite.
Feature / Control
Description
Interface Tabs
Swatches
A grid of predefined, vibrant preset colours. Perfect for rapid design work or maintaining a standard, consistent palette across basic documents.
Custom
Unlocks the full manual colour selection toolset, giving you precise control over millions of colours for exact brand-matching (see controls below).
Professional Gradient Wheel
2D Saturation/Brightness Canvas
Click or drag your cursor anywhere on the interactive canvas to intuitively set your colour’s saturation (intensity) and brightness (lightness) simultaneously.
1D Hue Slider
Drag the slider to sweep through the full visible colour spectrum and select your foundational base hue before fine-tuning it on the 2D canvas.
RGB & Hex Inputs
Hex Input
Type or paste a 6-character hex colour code directly (for example: #007670 ). Essential for web designers or adhering to strict corporate brand guidelines.
RGB Inputs
Fine-tune the Red, Green, and Blue channels individually using precise number fields (0-255). All numerical inputs are synchronised in real time with the visual gradient picker, updating instantly as you type.
Eyedropper Tool
An integrated eyedropper tool is built directly into the colour picker interface, functioning as an indispensable asset for cohesive design. Use it to sample any colour currently visible on your screen and instantly apply it as your active selected colour. This is the ideal method for perfectly matching text or background colours to a specific hue found within a client’s logo, an imported reference photo, or an existing design element already sitting on your canvas.
Smart Undo Fallback
Nothing disrupts a creative workflow more than a broken undo function. The colour picker incorporates a sophisticated behind-the-scenes fix for a common browser limitation: normally, pressing Ctrl+Z while actively editing inside a text box would fail to undo broader canvas-level actions (like colour changes) if the browser’s internal text-undo history was empty. Open Publisher intelligently detects this trap and automatically falls back to the main canvas undo function. This ensures that Ctrl+Z always works flawlessly and predictably, reversing your last action regardless of where your cursor is currently focused.

title: Crop & Compress Images
excerpt: Learn how to crop images in Open Publisher using rectangular and shape-based cropping, then compress your photos to reduce file size without losing quality.
content:
Cropping & Compressing Images
Open Publisher’s image tools include a non-destructive cropping system and a built-in compression utility, letting you frame your photos perfectly and keep your document file size under control.
Image Cropping
The cropping tool lets you non-destructively trim an image to show only the part you want, while keeping the original file intact.
To crop an image:
Select the image on the canvas.
In the Picture Tools contextual ribbon, click Crop .
The element enters crop mode: black crop handles appear at the edges and corners. Drag them inward to set the visible area.
While in crop mode, you can also click and drag the image itself to pan it within the crop frame - repositioning the content without changing the frame boundaries.
Click anywhere outside the element (or click the Crop button again) to confirm the crop and exit crop mode.
The crop parameters - frame position, image pan offset, and zoom - are all saved into the element’s data and persist across undo/redo and save/load cycles. The print engine honours your exact crop settings and does not reset to the full image during printing.
Crop to Shape
In addition to rectangular cropping, Open Publisher can clip any image to a custom shape. The shape library includes 14 options: circle, star, triangle, heart, diamond, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, cross, arrows, trapezoid, parallelogram, shield, and speech bubble .
To apply a shape crop:
Select the image on the canvas.
In the Picture Tools ribbon, click Shape Crop (or select it from the right-click context menu).
Choose a shape from the one-click button grid. The interface features a 2-column grid with built-in preview icons - simply click your desired shape to instantly apply the crop and close the dialog.
Note on existing documents: If older documents contain shape crops saved before version 4.13.20, re-apply the shape via Picture Tools > Shape Crop to force the updated data into the file.
Compressing Pictures
To reduce the file size of your .opub document, use the Compress tool to reduce the embedded size of large image files without significantly affecting their visible quality.
To compress a picture:
Select the image on the canvas.
In the Picture Tools ribbon (or under Adjust in the Insert ribbon), click Compress .
A modal appears with a live progress bar tracking the estimated size reduction in real time.
When complete, the image in the document is replaced with the compressed version.
The compression tool includes built-in safeguards:
If the image is already fully optimised, a dialog appears explaining it cannot be reduced further - no redundant processing occurs.
If an unsupported element type is selected (such as Clipart, WordArt, or a vector Shape), the tool halts and displays a clear “Not Supported” message rather than failing silently.

title: Format Picture Sidebar: Dynamic Sliders, Rounded Corners & Color Sync
excerpt: Learn how to use OpenPublisher Format Picture sidebar with its 0-100px rounded corners slider, dynamic slider gradient fills, and universal font color synchronization.
content:
Format Picture Sidebar: Dynamic Sliders, Rounded Corners & Color Sync
Fine-tuning photo frames and graphic styling should feel fluid and effortless. Through OpenPublisher v5.16.8 and v5.16.9 , the Format Picture Sidebar received a series of elegant visual and ergonomic upgrades: a continuous 0px to 100px rounded corners slider with a live numeric badge, dynamic teal progress fills on range sliders, smooth cross-fading selection transitions, and universal font color synchronization across both the ribbon and floating toolbars.
Figure 1: The upgraded Format Picture sidebar displaying dynamic gradient progress fills on sliders and seamless selection transitions.
1. The Continuous Rounded Corners Slider (v5.16.9)
While right-clicking an image has long offered stepped radius presets (such as 8px, 16px, 24px, or 32px), precision layouts often call for custom corner curves (such as a subtle 12px card curve or an expressive 48px capsule curve).
Continuous 0px to 100px Range: Located prominently inside the Format Picture sidebar under the Borders & Corners group, the new slider lets you drag to any exact pixel radius.
Live Numeric Readout Badge: A dedicated badge beside the slider shows the current pixel value in real time as you drag.
Bi-Directional Canvas Sync: Adjusting the slider updates the image's canvas clip-path and border-radius instantly on every frame. If you later apply a preset from the right-click context menu, the sidebar slider automatically repositions its thumb to match.
Full Print & PDF Export Parity: Custom corner radii are serialized into page history snapshots, ensuring your rounded photos print cleanly at 300 DPI without pixelated edges.
Figure 2: Real-time image corner radius slider adjustment with synchronized font color indicator bars across ribbon and floating toolbars.
2. Dynamic Slider Progress Bar Fill Effect (v5.16.8)
Standard browser range sliders typically show a plain gray track behind the slider thumb. Version 5.16.8 introduced dynamic progress fills across all OpenPublisher range sliders:
Real-Time Track Filling: As you drag any slider (whether adjusting corner radius, shadow blur, border width, or opacity), the track from 0% up to the active thumb position fills with a vibrant teal gradient ( var(--ui-theme-dark) / #007670 ).
Theme Adaptive: The fill dynamically inherits your active UI theme color or dark mode settings, maintaining consistent visual aesthetics across all 700+ themes.
Smooth Selection Transitions: When clicking between different photos or deselecting to an empty canvas, the sidebar cross-fades smoothly without abrupt flickering, visual jumping, or layout recalculation lag.
3. Universal Font Color Indicator Synchronization (v5.16.8 & v5.16.9)
When formatting typography, you frequently switch between the main ribbon toolbar at the top of the screen and the floating action toolbar that hovers right beside your selected text.
In earlier releases, changing font color via the CSS Color Studio, quick swatches, or 1-click designer themes did not always update the visual colored bar underneath the "A" icon on both toolbars simultaneously.
Versions 5.16.8 and 5.16.9 unified font color synchronization across the entire application:
Bi-Directional Bar Mirroring: The color indicator bar on the Text Box Tools ribbon ( #ctx-text-color-bar-text ) and the Floating Toolbar color bar ( #float-text-color-bar ) are now unified. Changing a color from either location immediately updates both bars.
Caret & Selection Awareness: When clicking into a text box or placing your text caret inside words with different colors, both toolbars instantly update their indicator bars to match the exact font color at the caret position.
Designer Theme & Quick-Swatch Parity: Applying whole-page palettes or 1-click designer themes instantly propagates active font colors to all toolbar indicators without requiring a canvas refresh.
Try it out: Select any photo on your canvas to open the Format Picture sidebar and drag the Rounded Corners slider to see the instant live preview and dynamic track fill in action!
Rounded Corner Shadow Underlay Synchronization (v5.17.5)
When pairing drop shadows with rounded image corners, earlier engines could produce rectangular shadow boxes extending beyond the curved picture corners. In OpenPublisher v5.17.5 , the shadow underlay engine was completely synchronized with corner curvature:
Shadow underlay corner radius synchronization in OpenPublisher v5.17.5.
Dynamic Curvature Matching: As you drag the Rounded Corners slider from 0px to 100px, the drop shadow underlay recalculates its vector clipping path simultaneously.
Print & PDF Fidelity: Eliminates square shadow artifacts on 300 DPI pre-flight PDF exports, ensuring soft, natural drop shadows that hug the rounded contours of photos.

title: Image Crop Print Fidelity & Live Editor Rounded Corners
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher delivers retina-grade 2x rasterization for cropped pictures on print and PDF export, while enabling live rounded corners on cropped images.
content: Image Crop Print Fidelity & Live Editor Rounded Corners Framing photographs tightly and softening image perimeters with elegant rounded corners or geometric contours are core design techniques in desktop publishing. However, combining image cropping with styling filters historically revealed subtle rendering gaps: cropped images could bypass canvas rasterization and print completely uncropped, applied filters could trigger aspect-ratio distortion, and rounded corners applied to cropped photos appeared on prints but remained sharp 90-degree rectangles in the canvas editor. Version 5.8.2 resolved these discrepancies, introducing retina-grade 2x sub-viewport rasterization for print, distortion-free filter scaling, and live editor rounded corner masking. 🖼️ Cropped Image with 24px Rounded Corners in Canvas Editor and Print Cropped images display smooth rounded corners in the active editor and print with razor-sharp 2x sub-viewport rasterization. Cropped Image Print Fidelity & Sub-Viewport Rasterization The print engine overhaul in Version 5.8.2 eliminated uncropped output and filter distortion: Automated Crop Detection: In extensions/print-engine.js , the raster pre-baking condition now explicitly checks const isCropped = !isDefaultFillImageLayout(savedImgStyle) . Any image with custom offsets or crop dimensions automatically triggers high-resolution canvas baking. Retina 2x Sub-Viewport Sampling: When baking cropped images, bakeImageForPrint() allocates a dedicated staging canvas at double resolution ( displayW * 2 by displayH * 2 ), sampling source pixels with exact 1:1 aspect ratio fidelity. Hardware-Accelerated Fallback Clipping: Print staging element wrappers are initialized with overflow: hidden and contain: paint . If external cross-origin security restrictions prevent canvas baking, the browser fallback cleanly clips uncropped portions at exact crop boundaries. Aspect-Ratio Stretch Elimination: Applying image adjustments (such as hue rotation, saturation, brightness, contrast, or sepia) to cropped pictures now preserves exact rectangular proportions without stretching to source dimensions. Live Canvas Rounded Corner Masking for Cropped Images Earlier builds exhibited an editor visual defect where rounded corners appeared on prints but left sharp rectangular corners on the canvas: Container Hierarchy Cascading: Rounded corner clipping (8px, 16px, 24px, 32px) now cascades across the entire container hierarchy: the outer element ( .pub-element ), the content wrapper ( .element-content ), and the inner image ( ). Crop to Shape Synchronization: Geometric shape clipping (circles, ellipses, stars, polygons) applies across the element hierarchy, ensuring custom crop shapes display identically on canvas and print. Crop Mode Exit Persistence: Exiting interactive crop mode ( state.cropMode = false ) inspects existing rounded corner attributes ( data-rounded-corners ) and re-applies smooth masking immediately. Document Serialization & Thumbnail Precision Saved documents and thumbnail navigation reflect accurate crop styling: Page Load Restoration: In core/pages.js , renderPage() restores border-radius and clip-path onto element wrappers from serialized data ( effectiveBorderRadius ). Thumbnail Mirroring: In createPageThumbnail() , rounded corners and shape paths propagate to thumbnail scale boxes, ensuring sidebar previews match the canvas. Tip: You can crop an image tightly around a subject, apply a 24px corner radius, and adjust brightness all in one workflow with complete visual fidelity.

title: Image Drag-Through Mirroring & Preview Fidelity
excerpt: Master image and shape reflection in Open Publisher by dragging resize handles through opposing edges to invert graphics across horizontal and vertical axes.
content:
Image Drag-Through Mirroring & Preview Fidelity
Reflecting images, decorative motifs, and illustrations is a cornerstone of symmetrical document layout. While users can click "Flip Horizontal" or "Flip Vertical" in the ribbon, the most natural method is dragging an element's resize handle directly through itself to invert it. Earlier revisions had inadvertently disabled this gesture with minimum dimension clamping and suffered from preview letterboxing when images were stretched non-uniformly. Version 5.8.4 restored full four-way drag-through mirroring, continuous reversible tracking, and live preview fidelity.
🪞 Interactive Drag-Through Resize Mirroring Across Horizontal Axis
Dragging a handle past its opposite boundary smoothly inverts the graphic with rotation-aware edge pinning.
Restoration of Four-Way Drag-Through Mirroring
Version 5.8.4 decoupled layout safety guards from interactive graphic transforms:
Signed Dimension Processing: Clamping checks now verify canMirror = !state.cropMode && !isTable && !isArrow . Elements permitted to mirror allow raw dimensions to transition through zero into negative numbers during dragging. Physical element dimensions are assigned via Math.abs(rawW) , while negative coordinates toggle data-scaleX: -1 and data-scaleY: -1 .
Multi-Directional Support: Dragging an East handle left past West inverts horizontal scale; dragging West right past East inverts it symmetrically. Pulling South up past North inverts vertical scale, and corner handles ( nw , ne , se , sw ) mirror across both axes simultaneously.
Continuous Reversible Drag Tracking: Users can drag through the inversion point to mirror, then drag back across zero to un-mirror in the same continuous mouse gesture without coordinate jitter.
Rotation-Aware Pivot & Anchor Geometry
Mirroring operates accurately on rotated objects across any angle:
Rotated Basis Vectors: The rotation-aware engine utilizes local unit basis vectors ( u , v ) to calculate fixed-edge anchors. When dragging past an opposing edge at arbitrary angles (such as 30 deg or 45 deg), the opposite boundary remains strictly pinned in place while the active handle extends into mirrored space.
Aspect-Ratio Lock Compatibility: When holding Shift or when data-aspect-lock="true" , the engine computes the dominant scale magnitude while preserving signed coordinate direction, enabling proportional scaling and mirroring simultaneously.
Preview Stretch Elimination & Isolation Safeguards
Thumbnail navigation and layout components were hardened:
Fill Styling for Previews: Updated page thumbnail styling to respect object-fit: fill , ensuring non-uniform stretching on the canvas is faithfully displayed in navigation previews without letterbox bars.
Center Transform Origins: Configured transform-origin: center center across preview renderers, allowing thumbnail graphics to mirror in place around their own center rather than clipping into negative coordinate space.
Smart Arrow & Table Safeguards: Smart arrows are explicitly exempted from drag-through inversion to protect stroke geometries and pointer heads, enforcing a 10px minimum boundary. Table containers similarly enforce physical content constraints.
Tip: You can quickly duplicate and mirror decorative corner flourishes by holding Ctrl while dragging an element, then pulling the outer handle through itself.

title: Image Filters & Alt Text
excerpt: Apply non-destructive hue, brightness, contrast, sepia and other filters to images in Open Publisher, and add alt text for WCAG 2.1 accessibility compliance.
content: Image Filters & Alt Text The Picture Tools sidebar provides real-time, non-destructive image filter controls alongside alt text support, giving you both creative control and accessibility compliance in one place. Image Filters All filter adjustments are live on the canvas and applied using CSS filters - your original image file is never modified. The following controls are available in the Picture Tools sidebar: Hue Rotation - Shifts the colour tones of the image across the colour wheel (0° - 360°). Useful for recolouring clipart or creating dramatic tinted effects. Brightness - Lightens or darkens the image. Contrast - Increases or reduces the difference between light and dark areas. Saturate - Boosts or strips the colour intensity of the image. Sepia - Applies a warm, vintage brown tone. Blur - Softens the entire image. Invert - Reverses all colours, creating a negative effect. Note: Filters are non-destructive while on the canvas. Before printing or exporting to PDF, they are automatically “baked” into the image. The export engine waits for the filtered image source to be fully resolved before capturing the snapshot, ensuring your PDF and exported files correctly reflect all filter settings. Alt Text Every image in Open Publisher can have Alt Text attached for accessibility compliance. Alt text describes the image to screen readers and is embedded in all HTML exports. To add Alt Text: Right-click any image on the canvas. Select Edit Alt Text from the context menu. Type a descriptive label for the image (for example: “Company logo in teal green” or “Bar chart showing Q1 sales”). Click Save . The text is stored on the element’s data-alt-text attribute. It is written into the alt attribute of the tag in all HTML exports, and is also reported by the Accessibility Checker as part of its WCAG 2.1 scan.

title: Image Rounded Corners & Crop-to-Shape Complete Engine Fix
excerpt: Crop pictures into circles, stars, polygons, and rounded corners with Open Publisher
content:
Image Rounded Corners & Crop-to-Shape Complete Engine Fix
Creative document design often calls for non-rectangular image framing: softening photos with gentle rounded corners, cropping team portraits into circular avatars, or masking promotional callouts into stars, hexagons, and speech bubbles. In earlier builds, the "Crop to Shape" dialog suffered from a critical JavaScript error that rendered all shape buttons inert, while the physical print spooler stripped CSS clip paths, reverting curved graphics to hard rectangular boxes. Version 5.6.9 delivered a complete architectural overhaul, activating instant shape cropping, right-click context menu integration, and full vector clipping across printing, PDF exports, and saves.
✂️ Interactive Crop to Shape Modal with 19 Geometric Presets
Clicking any geometric preset crops the selected photo immediately, preserving transparency and shadow boundaries.
Interactive Crop to Shape Modal & Context Menu
Version 5.6.9 resolved modal input reference issues and streamlined shape application:
Direct Shape Execution: window.applyCropShape(shape) applies clipPath , -webkit-clip-path , and borderRadius directly to both the image and container wrapper, closing the modal smoothly upon card selection.
19 Handcrafted Shape Presets: Supports circles, ellipses, teardrops, diamonds, triangles, pentagons, hexagons, octagons, 4-point to 8-point stars, banners, and speech callouts.
Context Menu Integration: Added "Crop to Shape" directly to the right-click image menu in ui/menus.js alongside "Rounded Corners" (None, 8px, 16px, 24px, 32px) and "Crop Image".
Vector Print Engine Geometry Clipping
Browser print engines and html2canvas historically ignored CSS clip paths during rasterization. Open Publisher incorporates a vector path clipper in extensions/print-engine.js :
Path Parser: Decomposes inset(0 round Xpx) , circle(...) , ellipse(...) , and polygon coordinates in pixels and percentages.
Raster Canvas Clipping: Clips the offscreen raster context prior to drawing pixels, ensuring areas outside the shape mask remain transparent.
Natural Drop Shadow Radiation: Because transparency is preserved outside the shape, drop shadows radiate naturally from the curved or angled contour rather than square box edges.
Full History & Serialization Parity
Shape masks and corner radii are serialized into data.clipPath , data.borderRadius , and data-rounded-corners within the .opub file format, restoring accurately across page navigation, saves, and undo/redo operations.
Tip: Right-click any photo and select Crop to Shape -> Circle to create professional circular portrait badges in seconds.

title: Image Transparency & Filter Preservation Across Undo/Redo
excerpt: Retain image opacity and Format Picture filters across undo, redo, and page switches with Open Publisher
content:
Image Transparency & Filter Preservation Across Undo/Redo
Fine-tuning imagery often involves subtle adjustments: softening a background photo with 40% transparency, boosting saturation on a product shot, or applying a sepia tone for vintage aesthetics. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, performing an undo operation (even for an unrelated action like typing a character or repositioning a text box) inadvertently stripped transparency and filter effects from all edited images across the publication, reverting them to 100% opacity. Version 5.6.2 delivered a comprehensive architectural fix, establishing multi-tier filter serialization that preserves transparency and visual effects across undo, redo, page transitions, and file saves.
✨ Image Transparency and Filter Preservation Across Undo History
Image opacity and Format Picture filters survive undo/redo actions with 100% fidelity.
Multi-Tier History Serialization & Deserialization
The root issue stemmed from incomplete property extraction during document history snapshotting. Version 5.6.2 overhauled serialization across both history and page rendering subsystems:
Dedicated Filter Attributes Dictionary: serializeCurrentPage() captures all element wrapper attributes ( data-filter-* , data-waf-* , data-shadow-* , data-aspect-lock ) into a structured data.filterAttributes dictionary.
Explicit Inline Opacity Persistence: data.imgStyle.opacity is explicitly saved in history snapshots. If inline opacity is present without an explicit transparency attribute, the engine automatically calculates and persists the percentage value.
Dynamic Reconstitution: When renderPage() restores elements from undo or redo, it reapplies all filter attributes to the wrapper, restores image opacity with fallback calculation, and reconstructs composite CSS filter strings dynamically.
Synchronous Sidebar Slider Reactivity
Selecting an image must instantly reflect its current visual state in the Format Picture sidebar:
Synchronous Slider Population: When an image is selected following an undo, redo, or page switch, refreshVisibility() runs immediately and synchronously, populating transparency, brightness, contrast, saturation, and hue-rotate sliders with exact restored values.
Undoable Filter Reset: Clicking "Reset" in the Format Picture sidebar now pushes a history snapshot before clearing parameters, enabling users to easily undo accidental resets with Ctrl + Z .
Cross-Page State Isolation: Undoing actions on one page preserves the transparency and filter settings of images on all other pages without interference.
Thumbnail Opacity & Filter Rendering
Sidebar thumbnails accurately reflect image transparency and CSS filters. In style.css , global image selectors were updated to direct child targeting ( .page-thumb > img ), ensuring thumbnail styling never overrides custom user opacity settings inside .pub-thumb-element .
Tip: You can experiment freely with photo filters and transparency in the Format Picture tab, confident that any change can be cleanly undone or redone.

title: In-Memory Batch Page Generation & Modal Interaction
excerpt: Eliminate layout thrashing and pointer event capture bugs in desktop webviews with Open Publisher
content:
In-Memory Batch Page Generation & Modal Interaction
Following the introduction of the bulk image import system in version 5.1.1, users running Open Publisher inside standalone desktop wrappers (NW.js) occasionally experienced unresponsive buttons inside the import routing dialog, and importing large batches of high-resolution pictures caused noticeable CPU layout thrashing. Version 5.1.2 re-engineers both the modal interaction architecture and the multi-page creation pipeline, constructing pages directly in memory for instant, glitch-free bulk imports.
Bulk image imports build page structures in memory before rendering, providing instant multi-page generation without UI stutter.
Pointer-Events Shields & Webview Optimization
Investigation into the unclickable modal issue revealed that clicks inside desktop webviews were being swallowed by nested elements:
Sub-Element Click Trapping: Clicks landing directly on SVG icons or descriptive subheadings failed to bubble up to the parent card's onclick listener in certain webview engines.
Pointer-Events Shield: Added .batch-import-card * { pointer-events: none !important; } in style.css , ensuring that clicks anywhere on the card surface hit the parent container cleanly.
Multi-Event Listeners: Cards are wired with programmatic click , pointerdown , and keyboard ( Enter / Space ) listeners, with explicit accessibility roles ( role="button" and tabindex="0" ).
Intuitive Iconography: Replaced the ambiguous fa-copy icon with fa-file-circle-plus , clearly signaling the creation of new pages rather than clipboard actions.
In-Memory Batch Page Pipeline
The core multi-page creation loop in extensions/smart-images.js was completely overhauled:
Eliminating DOM Layout Thrashing: Previously, the loop invoked addNewPage() for each picture, forcing full-page re-renders, DOM reflows, and expensive base64 serialization on every iteration.
Direct Memory Construction: Pages are now constructed directly inside state.pages . Each new page inherits the active document's dimensions, margins, and DPI without touching the live DOM.
Single Consolidated Render: Canvas rendering, sidebar thumbnail generation, and undo history recording are performed once at the conclusion of the entire batch.
Desktop Wrapper Zero-Rebuild Architecture
Because the Open Publisher desktop application ( publisher.exe ) is an NW.js wrapper hosting the web app, all architectural fixes take effect immediately upon deployment without requiring users to download or reinstall desktop binaries.
Note: Batch imports of 20 or more large photos now execute in seconds with zero dropped frames.

title: Insert, Swap & Manage Images
excerpt: Learn how to insert, manage, and scale images in Open Publisher. Master picture placeholders, batch image swapping, and the Graphics Manager to streamline your workflow.
content:
Inserting, Swapping & Managing Images
Open Publisher offers powerful, drag-and-drop image handling and batch processing tools. Whenever an image is selected on the canvas, the Picture Tools contextual tab appears automatically in the ribbon, providing access to all formatting and management options.
Inserting Images
Images can be brought into your document in several ways:
Ribbon: Go to Insert > Picture and browse for an image file on your system.
Drag-and-Drop: Drag any JPG or PNG file from your desktop or file manager directly onto the canvas. Open Publisher automatically pre-loads the image in the background, measures its natural dimensions, and scales it down to fit the canvas while perfectly maintaining the original aspect ratio - no more fixed 200×100 default boxes.
Paste: Copy an image to your clipboard and press Ctrl+V / Cmd+V while the canvas is focused.
URL: In the Insert menu, choose Insert from URL and paste in a direct web image link.
Once inserted, the image is a movable, resizable canvas element with selection handles on all edges and corners. Drag to reposition; drag the handles to resize.
Picture Placeholders
When you are designing a layout but don’t yet have your final photos ready, Picture Placeholders let you block out exactly where images will go, at the exact dimensions you want, without needing the real photos.
Go to Insert > Picture Placeholder .
A styled empty frame with a dashed border and camera icon appears on the canvas. Resize and position it as needed.
When your real image is ready, double-click the placeholder to open a file browser and swap it with the actual photo immediately.
Placeholders carry the data-is-placeholder=”true” attribute, which the Batch Picture Swap engine uses to find and fill them automatically.
Batch Picture Swap
If you have a layout with multiple Picture Placeholders and a folder of photos ready, the Batch Picture Swap feature lets you fill all of them in one drag-and-drop action.
Select multiple image files from your desktop or file manager.
Drag the entire batch and drop them onto the Open Publisher canvas.
Open Publisher detects that you have dropped multiple files and automatically scans the canvas for empty placeholders.
If no placeholders are explicitly selected, the engine finds all empty placeholders and sorts them top-to-bottom, left-to-right based on their geometric position on the page.
Each photo is assigned to a placeholder in order and swapped in instantly.
Tip: If you want to control which placeholder receives which photo, select specific placeholders before dropping the batch. The engine respects your selection and fills only the targeted elements.
Precise Size Controls
When an image is selected, the Picture Tools contextual ribbon includes a Size group with:
Width and Height spinners: Type an exact pixel value or use the up/down arrows to nudge in 1px increments.
Lock Aspect Ratio checkbox: When checked, changing the width automatically recalculates the height proportionally (and vice versa), preventing distortion. This is identical to holding Shift while dragging a resize handle.
The Graphics Manager
The Graphics Manager gives you a complete audit of every image and graphic in your entire document - across all pages - in one unified, searchable panel.
To open it, go to File > Info > Graphics Manager , or click Graphics Manager in the Picture Tools ribbon. It displays a scrollable list of every image in the document, showing:
A thumbnail preview
The image name or URL
The page number it lives on
Its current status (OK, Missing, Low-Resolution)
From the Graphics Manager you can click any entry to instantly jump to that image’s page and select the element ( Navigate ), or click the Update button to replace it with a new file from your system without changing its position or size on the canvas.

title: Lock Aspect Ratio & Picture Tools Precision
excerpt: Maintain precise image proportions with Open Publisher
content:
Lock Aspect Ratio & Picture Tools Precision
Preserving accurate aspect ratios when resizing photographs, logos, and vector illustrations is essential for maintaining brand integrity and visual balance. In version 5.1.8, Open Publisher resolved an intermittent interaction bug in the Picture Tools ribbon tab where the Lock Aspect Ratio checkbox suffered from a double-toggle race condition. The updated architecture provides reliable, browser-native proportional locking across all picture manipulation workflows.
🔒 Picture Tools Lock Aspect Ratio Ribbon Toggle
The Picture Tools ribbon tab features a reliable browser-native toggle for locking and unlocking image proportions.
The Double-Toggle Race Condition
Investigation revealed that the previous control structure mixed manual JavaScript event handlers with native browser click behaviors:
Dual Event Collision: The checkbox and text label were wrapped in a plain <div onclick="..."> that manually toggled the input, while the inner <input type="checkbox"> also handled native clicks.
Double-Toggle Glitch: Clicking the checkbox box fired the native toggle (turning it on), and then the parent container click fired immediately afterward (turning it back off). As a result, the checkbox appeared completely unresponsive.
Event Propagation Mismatch: Attempting to use stopPropagation() on the change event failed because browser click and change events traverse separate dispatch pipelines.
Browser-Native Label Architecture
The control was refactored in ui/ui.js to use semantic HTML standard associations:
Semantic Label Association: Wrapped the input in <label for="ribbon-el-lock"> . Clicking anywhere on the checkbox box, label text, or padding gap triggers exactly one browser-native toggle.
Clean Change Pipeline: The input directly executes ContextRibbonActions.toggleAspectLock(this.checked) upon change, eliminating redundant JavaScript state tracking.
Theme Accent Styling: The checkbox utilizes accent-color: var(--ui-theme-color) , integrating seamlessly with Open Publisher's signature teal interface theme.
Proportional vs. Freeform Sizing Controls
When Lock Aspect Ratio is enabled, dragging any corner resize handle on the canvas scales width and height in strict proportion, preventing distortion. If you need to stretch an image to fit an irregular column, uncheck the toggle to unlock freeform non-uniform resizing.
Tip: Holding the Shift key while dragging a resize handle temporarily enforces proportional aspect ratio locking regardless of whether the ribbon checkbox is toggled.

title: Picture Frame & Border Engine (Framing Modal, Custom Styles & Shadows)
excerpt: Discover how to frame any image or photo in OpenPublisher with the Picture Frame & Border Engine, interactive framing modal, custom frame styles, and shadow underlays.
content:
Picture Frame & Border Engine: Professional Photo Framing & Styling
Elevate your publications with polished, studio-quality borders around images, graphics, and photo collages. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.19.0 , the Picture Frame & Border Engine introduces an interactive framing modal, an expanded gallery of border presets, synchronized dropdown styling, and dynamic drop shadow underlays that preserve clean vector boundaries on print exports.
The Picture Frame & Border Engine in OpenPublisher v5.19.0, featuring the Interactive Framing Modal and real-time live preview.
Live Non-Destructive Framing: All frames and borders applied through OpenPublisher are completely non-destructive. The underlying high-resolution image asset remains unaltered, meaning you can tweak widths, colors, or frame styles at any point without degrading graphic quality.
The Interactive Framing Modal
To open the Framing Modal, select any image or graphic on your canvas and click the Picture Frame icon in the Picture Format ribbon (or select Format Picture > Frame Options from the context menu). The modal offers an intuitive, real-time control room with five primary adjustment controls:
1. Border Width Slider
Slide continuously between 0px (hairline borderless) and 50px (dramatic wide matting). The canvas updates live as you drag, allowing you to gauge visual weight relative to nearby text blocks.
2. Corner Radius Control
Pair frame strokes with gentle rounded corners or full pill curves. The border contours automatically wrap around the rounded corners with perfect curvature matching.
3. Frame Color Palette
Choose from publication theme colors, curated neutral matting tones (e.g. Crisp White, Charcoal Matte, Cream Linen), or specify custom RGB/Hex color codes.
4. Shadow Underlay Offset & Blur
Give framed pictures realistic depth. Adjust drop shadow distance, direction, soft blur radius, and opacity with instant visual feedback.
Expanded Frame Styles Gallery
OpenPublisher v5.19.0 introduces an expanded dropdown gallery of pre-configured frame styles, easily accessible directly from the ribbon dropdown or within the Framing Modal:
Frame Preset
Visual Characteristics
Ideal Publication Context
Classic Solid
Single uniform stroke with sharp or slightly rounded corners.
Newsletters, technical articles, and clean catalogs.
Gallery Float
Generous white matting border surrounded by a gentle, diffused drop shadow.
Photography portfolios, art club flyers, and wedding programs.
Beveled Studio
Subtle gradient highlights and inner edge beveling giving physical depth.
Product showcases, certificates, and presentation covers.
Ornate Double Border
Concentric outer thick stroke paired with an interior fine hairline accent.
Formal certificates, menus, and memorial booklets.
Neon Stroke
High-saturation perimeter outline paired with a vibrant luminous outer glow.
Concert posters, gaming flyers, and club announcements.
Step-by-Step: How to Frame an Image
Select Your Image: Click to highlight any picture, photo, or clipart element on your page.
Open Picture Tools: Look for the contextual Picture Format tab appearing in the top ribbon menu.
Click Picture Frames: Click the Picture Frames split button to choose a quick preset, or click More Frame Styles... to launch the modal.
Customize in the Modal: Adjust the border width, corner radius, color, and shadow parameters until your frame matches your publication aesthetic.
Apply to Selection: Click Apply Frame to confirm. You can also click Apply to All Images if you want a unified look across your document.
Print & High-Resolution Export Fidelity
When printing to high-resolution paper or exporting to 300 DPI PDF, the Picture Frame & Border Engine converts frame strokes directly into clean vector path instructions. Unlike raster-based filters that become blurry when scaled, OpenPublisher frames stay razor-sharp at any zoom level or paper size (from pocket business cards to A0 event posters).
