- Shadows & Glow Effects Guide

title: Picture Tools Image Glow & Drop Shadow Print Rendering Fidelity
excerpt: Learn how Open Publisher ensures full visual fidelity when printing image glow and drop shadow effects across HTML5 Canvas rasterization and desktop spooler pipelines.
content:
Picture Tools Image Glow & Drop Shadow Print Rendering Fidelity
Visual styling effects such as soft drop shadows and radiant outer glows give photographs, illustrations, and imported artwork depth and emphasis on the printed page. In desktop publishing, these effects must render with identical fidelity whether viewed on screen, exported to high-resolution PDF, or sent to a physical desktop printer. Earlier releases experienced an issue where image drop shadows and glows applied via the Picture Tools ribbon displayed accurately on the interactive editor canvas, but disappeared or clipped on physical prints and PDF exports. Version 5.7.3 resolved this across both print pipelines, restoring complete visual parity across HTML5 Canvas 2D rasterization and the native desktop print spooler DOM.
🌟 Picture Tools Glow & Drop Shadow Print Preview Comparison
Images styled with vibrant outer glow and deep drop shadows retain full blur radiuses and color fidelity on print and PDF outputs.
CSS Filter Color Parentheses Truncation in bakeImageForPrint()
The primary cause of missing shadow and glow effects on printed documents was traced to regular expression parsing in the image pre-baking pipeline:
The Single-Level Regex Flaw: In extensions/print-engine.js , bakeImageForPrint() used a shallow pattern ( /drop-shadow\(([^)]+)\)/g ) to extract and scale drop shadow parameters for 300 DPI canvas baking.
Premature Termination on rgba() Colors: Modern browsers serialize computed CSS filter colors using functional notation containing inner parentheses (such as rgba(0, 191, 255, 0.8) ). The shallow regex terminated on the first closing parenthesis, creating malformed CSS strings lacking an outer closing parenthesis.
Silent Canvas Context Rejection: When assigned malformed filter strings, the HTML5 Canvas 2D context ( ctx.filter ) silently rejected the syntax and reverted to none , causing shadows and glows to vanish completely from the baked image.
Balanced Nested Parsing: The parser was upgraded to balanced nested parentheses matching ( /drop-shadow\(((?:[^)(]+|\([^)(]*\))*)\)/g ). This captures complete multi-token color structures, allowing blur radiuses and offsets to be scaled accurately to print resolutions.
History Serialization & Filter Consolidation
Ensuring filters persist across document navigation and auto-saves required synchronizing DOM layers:
Multi-Element Inspection: In core/history.js , serializeCurrentPage() was enhanced to inspect and combine filter directives across img.style.filter , content.style.filter , and el.style.filter .
Sanitizing Obsolete Tokens: Rogue none filter tokens are stripped during serialization, and the consolidated filter definition is saved into both data.filter and data.imgStyle.filter .
Ribbon Action Cleanliness: Picture Tools ribbon handlers ( ContextRibbonActions.addGlow and addDropShadow ) clean obsolete tokens before appending new effects, triggering immediate undo/redo state capture.
Container Overflow Unclipping & Desktop Spooler DOM Parity
Drop shadow blurs and glowing halos naturally radiate beyond the rectangular perimeter of the source image:
Unclipped Element Containers: In core/pages.js and buildPrintPageDOM() , container elements ( elDiv , cropDiv , and .element-content ) explicitly apply overflow: visible and contain: none when drop shadows or glow effects are present.
Native Desktop Spooler DOM Parity: The NW.js desktop native spooler pipeline in buildPrintDOM() and io/file-io.js extracts serialized filters directly from state objects, applies them to img.style.filter , and unclips container wrappers.
Automated Pixel Verification: Automated raster test suites verify that glowing images generate over 29,000 radiant pixels and drop-shadowed images produce over 6,600 realistic shadow pixels without edge truncation.
Tip: You can layer multiple Picture Tools effects (such as combining a soft black drop shadow with rounded corners) and preview the exact print output anytime in the Document Presentation Preview.
Rounded Corner Contour Shadow Baking & WordArt Support
Version 5.10.2 and 5.10.4 expanded the print pipeline to support rounded corner images and Beta WordArt drop shadows. By decoupling the shadow rasterization into an isolated Canvas 2D layer, Open Publisher bakes smooth, contour-following drop shadows directly beneath curved image borders and styled WordArt glyphs, preventing unsightly white bounding boxes on print outputs.

title: Quick Rounded Corners
excerpt: Quickly apply non-destructive rounded corners to your images in Open Publisher using the right-click context menu, featuring 8px, 16px, 24px, and 32px radiuses.
content:
Quick Rounded Corners
You can instantly soften the edges of any picture in your document using the Quick Rounded Corners tool. This provides a fast way to apply modern, curved edges to your photos without needing to manually draw shapes or open complex masking menus.
Applying Rounded Corners
Select the image you want to modify on your canvas.
Right-click the image to open the context menu.
Hover over Rounded Corners to reveal the flyout menu.
Select your desired corner radius: 8px (subtle), 16px (standard), 24px (soft), or 32px (pill-like).
The corners will instantly apply to the image. Because this is a non-destructive crop , your original image data is preserved perfectly. You can change the radius at any time, or remove it entirely, without losing any quality or cutting off your picture permanently.
The Crop to Shape Modal
The four rounded corner presets are also fully integrated into the main Crop to Shape modal. If you prefer working from the ribbon instead of the right-click menu:
Select your image.
Navigate to the Picture Tools contextual tab.
Click Crop to Shape .
You will find the new rounded rectangle presets prominently listed alongside the other standard shapes.

title: Rotation-Aware Object & Image Resizing Engine
excerpt: Master element resizing at any angle with Open Publisher
content: Rotation-Aware Object & Image Resizing Engine Desktop publishing layouts rely heavily on rotated elements: angled banners, rotated photo collages, slanted headings, and upside-down badges. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, resizing rotated elements produced counter-intuitive behavior: grabbing a handle on an element rotated 180 degrees caused the object to shrink instead of expand, while the opposite anchor moved unexpectedly. Version 5.5.0 introduced a complete mathematical overhaul of the canvas resizing system with the Rotation-Aware Affine Transform Resizing Engine. 🔄 Rotation-Aware 2D Affine Handle Resizing at Arbitrary Angles Selection handles track cursor movement precisely at any angle, pinning the opposite anchor in place. 2D Affine Basis Extraction & Delta Projection Screen mouse coordinates do not align with the local width and height axes of a rotated element. The v5.5.0 engine decomposes transformations into local coordinate frames: Basis Vector Extraction: getElementTransformBasis() parses 2D/3D CSS transforms ( matrix , rotate , scale ) to extract orthonormal basis vectors: u (width axis) and v (height axis). Local Dot Product Projection: Screen mouse deltas ( dx, dy ) are projected onto local axes via dot products ( localDx = dx * u.x + dy * u.y and localDy = dx * v.x + dy * v.y ), ensuring dimensions expand or contract strictly along element edges. Anchor Pinning via Center Shift: Calculates the element's local center shift and transforms it back to paper coordinates ( deltaCenterPaper = deltaCenterLocalX * u + deltaCenterLocalY * v ), guaranteeing that the opposite handle stays pinned at zero displacement in world space. Dynamic Orientation-Aware Handle Cursors When an object is rotated 90 or 180 degrees, static resize cursors point in the wrong physical directions. Open Publisher dynamically computes cursor visuals: Visual Direction Matching: getRotatedHandleCursor(dir, rotDeg) adds the element rotation angle to each handle's base angle, assigning the appropriate cursor icon ( ns-resize , ew-resize , nesw-resize , nwse-resize ) to match physical on-screen motion. Real-Time Updates: As elements rotate, handle cursor styles update immediately to preserve intuitive user feedback. Universal Compatibility & Image Protection The rotation-aware resizing engine integrates across all element types and layout workflows: Aspect Ratio Locking: Holding Shift or toggling the lock aspect ratio badge scales rotated elements proportionally with zero jumping or distortion. Center Resizing: Holding Ctrl (or Cmd ) expands both sides symmetrically along local axes while keeping the center stationary. Uncropped Image 100% Fill Protection: Ensures inner tags retain CSS percentage sizing ( 100% ) during resize, with automatic self-healing via healUncroppedImage() . Full Support Across All Elements: Works identically on images, shapes, text boxes, tables, clipart, and WordArt objects. Tip: Hold Shift while dragging any corner handle of a rotated image to preserve its exact proportions.

title: Shadows & Glow Effects
excerpt: Add and customise drop shadows and glow effects on images and shapes in Open Publisher, with real-time controls for colour, blur, offset, and transparency.
content:
Shadows & Glow Effects
Open Publisher lets you apply drop shadows and glow effects to both images and shapes directly from the Picture Tools or Shape Format contextual ribbon, with all controls updating in real time as you drag.
Shadow Options
The Shadow Options pane gives you fine-grained, real-time control over drop shadows on both images and shapes.
To open Shadow Options:
Select an image or shape on the canvas.
In the Picture Tools or Shape Format contextual ribbon, click the Shadow button.
The Shadow / Glow Options sidebar slides open on the right.
The sidebar contains five live controls :
Colour Picker - Sets the shadow colour.
Transparency Slider - Controls shadow opacity from solid to fully transparent.
Blur Radius Slider - Adjusts softness. Low values produce sharp, hard shadows; high values produce soft, diffuse halos.
X Offset Slider - Shifts the shadow left or right.
Y Offset Slider - Shifts the shadow up or down.
All five controls update the shadow in real time as you drag. When you click an element that already has a shadow applied, the sidebar automatically reads the existing values and snaps its sliders to match - so the UI always reflects the exact current state.
Shadows are applied using CSS drop-shadow filters on the element’s content wrapper, allowing the shadow to organically overflow the element’s bounding box without being clipped.
Glow Effects
Glow is a specialised variant of the shadow effect, designed to make transparent PNG logos, shapes, and cutout graphics pop against dark or busy backgrounds.
To add a glow:
Select an image or shape on the canvas.
Click the Glow button (sun icon) in the Picture Tools or Shape Format ribbon, located next to the Shadow button.
A default electric-blue glow is applied immediately.
Use the same Shadow / Glow Options sidebar to adjust the blur radius, transparency, and colour - creating anything from a tight neon outline to a broad, soft luminous halo.
Printing Shadows and Glows on Rounded Images and Shapes
In earlier editions, applying a shadow or glow to an image with rounded corners or custom crop shapes could result in squared shadow clipping when printed or exported to PDF. Version 5.10.2 and 5.10.4 upgraded the print engine with dynamic Canvas 2D underlay baking: drop shadows and outer glows now follow the exact rounded contour of the cropped image or vector Smart Arrow, eliminating harsh rectangular borders and rendering with smooth 300 DPI anti-aliasing.

title: Unified Bulk Image Import & Multi-Page Automation
excerpt: Import batches of images simultaneously with dual-entry file picking, canvas drag-and-drop, and automated multi-page publication generation in Open Publisher.
content:
Unified Bulk Image Import & Multi-Page Automation
Publishing photo books, catalogs, newsletters, and localized publications often requires importing dozens or hundreds of image assets. Rather than forcing you to select and position pictures one by one, Open Publisher features a unified bulk image import pipeline. Users can choose multiple files via the Ribbon or drag and drop a batch of photos straight onto the canvas, with intelligent routing that automates both collage layouts and multi-page document generation.
🖼️ Bulk Image Import Interactive Routing Dialog
Interactive choice dialog prompting whether to place multiple images onto the current canvas or generate dedicated pages.
Dual Entry Points with Unified Handling
The bulk import engine unifies file picker workflows and desktop drag-and-drop operations:
Ribbon Picture Upload: The standard Insert Picture button on the Ribbon now supports multi-file selection. Hold Ctrl or Shift in your operating system's file browser to pick multiple PNG, JPEG, SVG, or WebP images simultaneously.
Desktop Drag and Drop: Select multiple pictures from Windows File Explorer, macOS Finder, or Linux file managers and drop them directly onto the publication canvas.
Centralized Pipeline: Both entry paths flow into window.handleBatchImageFiles , guaranteeing consistent processing, error handling, and memory management.
Smart Single vs. Batch Interception
The import pipeline evaluates file volume to provide the fastest user experience:
Single Image Fast Path: If only 1 image is selected or dropped, the app bypasses all dialog prompts, instantly placing the picture on your active page with zero extra clicks.
Multiple Image Choice Modal: When 2 or more images are detected, Open Publisher presents an interactive choice dialog with two distinct routing modes:
Option A - Place All on Current Page: Imports every image onto the active page, arranging them in an orderly staggered cascade with slight offsets so all elements remain visible and easily selectable.
Option B - Create New Page for Each Image: Generates a dedicated publication page for each picture automatically. Every image is scaled and centered within page margins, creating an instant photo book or presentation ready for print.
Deterministic Asynchronous Architecture
Handling dozens of high-resolution images requires strict sequence preservation:
Sequential Promise Loop: Images are processed via an async/await sequence, ensuring pages are created in exact file-order without race conditions or page scrambling.
Immediate Serialization: Each generated page is serialized to disk memory immediately upon image placement, preventing data loss during rapid page transitions.
Unified Undo Step: History recording is consolidated at the completion of the batch. A single Ctrl + Z cleanly reverts the entire import operation.
Tip: After generating pages automatically from images, you can use the Navigation Pane on the left to reorder, duplicate, or delete individual pages.

title: Boot Splash Screen Refresh & Offline Asset Modernization
excerpt: Learn how Open Publisher eliminated third-party proxy latency by embedding local boot splash assets with hue-rotate dynamic theming and aggressive cache busting.
content:
Boot Splash Screen Refresh & Offline Asset Modernization
The initial application loading sequence establishes the user's first impression upon launching Open Publisher. In previous releases, the boot splash screen loaded its visual background graphic from an external Imgur URL routed through a DuckDuckGo privacy proxy. While this approach functioned adequately in active web connections, it introduced unnecessary third-party network roundtrips, added startup latency, and occasionally failed when running inside offline desktop environments or behind restrictive enterprise firewalls. Version 4.19.3 overhauled the boot splash screen by replacing external dependencies with a pristine, locally bundled asset.
🚀 Modernized Boot Splash Screen with Native Hue Adaptation
The local startup splash screen eliminates network latency while preserving dynamic CSS theme filter support.
Locally Bundled Startup Asset
Version 4.19.3 replaced external network hops with internal resources:
Local Asset Migration: The splash background was relocated directly to ui/components/startupinfobg.png , ensuring immediate availability on disk.
Privacy & Air-Gap Reliability: Eliminating the third-party DuckDuckGo/Imgur proxy hop removed outbound connection requests during boot, providing complete privacy and flawless performance in air-gapped environments.
Visual Parity: The graphic mirrors the updated v5 application aesthetic introduced in 4.19.2, presenting clean geometric lines and professional prepress framing.
Dynamic CSS Hue-Rotate Theme Adaptation
Despite being a raster graphic, the local boot splash screen participates fully in Open Publisher's dynamic styling system:
CSS Filter Chaining: The boot pipeline applies dynamic hue-rotate() and brightness filters to the #splash-screen container based on saved user theme settings.
Zero-Latency Color Harmonization: Whether configured for Deep Teal, Crimson, Royal Purple, or Slate, the splash graphic renders in the user's chosen palette before the main editor workspace loads.
Aggressive Cachebuster Deployment
To prevent browser caches and webview storage from serving outdated splash graphics:
Hardened URL Query Parameter: In index.html , the splash screen image src attribute was appended with an explicit ?v=4.19.3 cachebuster.
Global Secondary Synchronization: Cachebusters across index.html , dashboard.js , and templates.js were synchronized to guarantee immediate adoption across all application modules.
Tip: In desktop client wrappers, the boot splash screen appears instantly while the underlying engine initializes background scripts.

title: Desktop Detection Pipeline & Client Download Suppression
excerpt: Learn how Open Publisher identifies native NW.js and desktop environments to suppress redundant download buttons and PWA prompts inside installed desktop apps.
content:
Desktop Detection Pipeline & Client Download Suppression
Open Publisher operates across multiple deployment targets: standard desktop web browsers, mobile and tablet touch devices, and native installed desktop packages for Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD. When users run the installed desktop application (packaged with NW.js or Electron), displaying "Download App" buttons in the ribbon or download icons in the title bar is redundant and confusing. Version 5.7.1 implemented a comprehensive 8-point Desktop Detection Pipeline that accurately identifies native desktop client environments on launch and permanently suppresses install controls.
🛡️ Clean Native Desktop Title Bar & Ribbon with Download Buttons Suppressed
Inside the installed desktop application, install and download buttons are cleanly omitted from the title bar and File ribbon.
The 8-Point Desktop Detection Pipeline
The unified isDesktopApp() engine in extensions/pwa-install.js and extensions/system-patches.js evaluates environment indicators:
Point 1 - Global NW Object: Inspects nw , window.nw , and globalThis.nw namespaces native to all NW.js environments.
Point 2 - Process Versions: Checks Node runtime flags ( process.versions.nw , process.versions['node-webkit'] , and process.versions['nw-flavor'] ).
Point 3 - Electron & FreeBSD Shells: Detects process.versions.electron and standalone desktop packages.
Point 4 - IPC Bridges & Window Flags: Checks desktop bridge flags ( _desktopBridgeActive , desktopIPC , _isDesktopClient ).
Point 5 - User Agent Regex: Employs case-insensitive matching ( /OpenPublisher|nwjs|nw\.js|node-webkit|Electron/i ).
Point 6 - Packaged App Protocols: Identifies chrome-extension: protocols when operating in packaged app containers.
Point 7 - Native GUI Module: Checks availability of require('nw.gui') .
Point 8 - Root Class Defense: Adds .is-desktop-app to root elements on boot, enforcing CSS display: none !important prior to UI script initialization.
Preserved Web Browser Download Flows
The detection pipeline strictly isolates native clients without degrading browser access:
Desktop Web Browsers: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari sessions evaluate isDesktopApp() to false, displaying the download button and in-app modal.
Mobile Web Touch Devices: iOS and Android browsers evaluate isMobileOrTablet to true, presenting the standard PWA home screen installation prompt.
Tip: The options dialog Save tab displays a dedicated Desktop Mode badge when running inside installed applications, confirming background recovery is managed by the native OS shell.

title: Easter Egg: Tetris
excerpt: Enter the Konami Code in Open Publisher to unlock a fully playable retro Tetris game with 8-bit sound effects, a custom theme, scoring, and a one-click exit back to your document.
content:
Easter Egg: Tetris
Hidden inside Open Publisher is a fully playable retro Tetris game, built from scratch with its own standalone game engine, a custom soundtrack, procedurally generated 8-bit sound effects, and a dynamic scoring system. Unlocking it takes exactly one classic cheat code.
How to Unlock It
At any time while Open Publisher is open, type the classic Konami Code on your keyboard:
↑  ↑  ↓  ↓  ←  →  ←  →  B  A
A background key listener monitors for this exact sequence. The moment the final key is pressed, the document editor seamlessly transforms into a fully playable Tetris game rendered directly on the canvas.
The Game Engine
The Tetris game is powered by a lightweight, standalone JavaScript engine built entirely from scratch. It includes:
Accurate piece rotation & collision detection - Pieces rotate and collide using correct rotation mathematics, behaving exactly as you would expect from a classic Tetris game.
“Coyote time” lock delays - A 500ms lock delay is applied before pieces settle, giving you a brief window to slide or adjust after a piece lands - the same technique used in professional Tetris implementations for a polished, forgiving feel.
Dynamic responsive sizing - The game board automatically scales edge-to-edge to fit your current document canvas size, regardless of the page size or zoom level you are working at.
Line-clearing animations & scoring - Lines clear with dynamic animations and the score updates in real time.
Sound & Music
The audio is generated and played entirely within the browser using the Web Audio API :
8-bit sound effects - Procedurally synthesised retro sound effects play for every piece movement, rotation, lock, drop, line clear, and game over.
The Open Publisher Tetris Theme - A custom background music track (Created with Gemini) plays throughout the game, carefully mixed at 25% volume so it complements rather than overpowers the sound effects.
The 3D Credit Overlay
When the game starts, an elegant pixel-styled credit overlay unrolls into the grey workspace area using a CSS 3D rotateX and clip-path transition - a cinematic opening sequence before the first piece drops.
Exiting the Game
While Tetris is active, an Exit Tetris button is injected directly into the Home ribbon, giving you a highly visible one-click way out at any time. Clicking it immediately ends the game and restores the document editor to its exact previous state - every element, every layer, and every edit perfectly preserved, as if you never left.

title: Complete Options Overhaul, Ribbon Re-arrangement & Startup Preview
excerpt: Tailor your publishing workflow with Open Publisher
content:
Complete Options Overhaul, Ribbon Re-arrangement & Startup Preview
Configurability, visual elegance, and seamless startup workflows define professional software. Version 5.6.7 of Open Publisher delivered an extensive overhaul of the File -> Options settings dialog across all seven configuration tabs (General, Proofing, Save, Language, Advanced, Customize Ribbon, and Trust Center). Every setting is actively wired to live application state and persistent storage, activating independent grammar proofing controls, an interactive AutoCorrect manager, a dynamic Ribbon Re-arrangement Engine, signature teal form theming, and guaranteed Page 1 cold start previews.
⚙️ Overhauled Options Dialog with Ribbon Customization & Proofing Controls
All seven Options tabs are fully active, featuring ribbon group reordering, proofing controls, and teal checkboxes.
Ribbon Re-arrangement & Button Group Engine
The Customize Ribbon tab allows users to personalize the primary application toolbar:
Per-Tab Group Reordering: Select any toolbar tab (Home, Insert, Page Design, Review, View) and freely adjust the left-to-right order of its command groups using Move Up (shift left) and Move Down (shift right) buttons.
Live DOM Synchronization: Adjusting group order immediately updates the toolbar on the canvas in real time without requiring an application reload.
Persistent Layouts & Reset: Custom arrangements persist in localStorage ( opub_ribbon_custom_order ) and reload automatically on boot, with dedicated buttons to reset individual tabs or restore factory defaults.
Proofing Options & Grammar Toggle Activation
The Proofing tab provides granular control over writing assistance:
Independent Grammar Checking: "Mark grammar errors as you type" is fully functional ( opub_grammarcheck ), allowing users to toggle green wavy grammar underlines independently of spelling check. Disabling grammar check instantly clears markings from the canvas.
AutoCorrect Manager: Accessible via "AutoCorrect Options...", offering an interactive manager for typing substitutions (such as (c) to © or --> to → ), custom shortcut pairs, and single-entry removal.
Custom Dictionary & Rule Reset: View and manage personal custom words, and reset skipped grammar rules with a single click.
Teal Form Theming & Startup Preview Guarantee
Interface aesthetics and application boot reliability received significant polish:
Signature Teal Theming: Form checkboxes, radio controls, and sliders utilize accent-color: #007670 , replacing generic browser blue boxes with branded teal styling across light and dark themes.
Guaranteed Cold Start Preview: Clicking the [X] close button on the startup dashboard initializes Page 1 immediately, presenting an active canvas and a rendered sidebar thumbnail without blank screens.
Desktop Application Integration: Detects native desktop environments ( window.isDesktopApp() ) to suppress duplicate web timers, avoid double exit modals, and harmonize with native OS notifications.
Tip: Open File -> Options -> Customize Ribbon to arrange your most frequently used tool groups on the left side of the Home tab.

title: The Document Info Menu
excerpt: Access all advanced document settings in one place via Open Publisher's Document Info menu  -  including Properties, Inspector, Design Checker, CMYK mode, and more.
content:
The Document Info Menu
Navigating through multiple ribbon tabs to find crucial document settings can slow down your workflow. To solve this, File > Info opens a centralised hub for advanced document settings, metadata, and diagnostics. Inspired by the “Backstage View” found in industry-leading professional publishing software, this dedicated menu ensures that everything you need to prepare, protect, and finalise your document is conveniently located in one intuitive panel. Whether you are prepping a file for commercial print or securing it for private distribution, the Info menu acts as your pre-publication control centre.
What You Can Access from File > Info
The Info menu houses several critical utilities for managing your file’s background data and output readiness. From this screen, you can access:
Document Properties - Define essential metadata such as Author, Company, Subject, and Keywords. This is highly recommended for keeping your files organised, improving internal searchability, and ensuring proper attribution when sharing digital copies with clients or colleagues.
Document Inspector - Protect your privacy and clean up your workspace. This tool thoroughly scans your file to identify hidden metadata, stray off-canvas elements, and empty text boxes that you may want to purge before sharing the document publicly.
Run Design Checker - Consider this your pre-flight diagnostic scan. It reviews your layout for common publishing errors-such as unseen text overflow, low-resolution images, and objects sitting outside the printable margins-ensuring your document is flawless before exporting.
CMYK / RGB Colour Mode - Easily toggle your project’s underlying colour profile depending on its final destination.
Switch to CMYK for accurate ink mixing in commercial printing,
or use RGB for vibrant digital and web-based viewing.
Protect Document - Secure sensitive information by applying or removing robust AES-GCM password encryption.
This guarantees that only authorized individuals with the password is able to open and view your Open Publisher document.
Graphics Manager - Open the full image asset management panel, allowing you to track, update, relink, or replace images across your entire document from a single streamlined list.
Because these are powerful and comprehensive tools, each one has its own dedicated article in this Knowledge Base containing full, step-by-step instructions. Think of the Document Info menu as your fast, centralised launchpad giving you immediate access to all of them from one convenient place.

title: The Startup Splash Screen
excerpt: When Open Publisher loads, a terminal-style splash screen logs nearly 100 initialising modules in real time, with a progress bar, draggable window, and auto-dismiss countdown.
content:
The Startup Splash Screen
Instead of a static image that leaves you wondering if the application has frozen, every time Open Publisher loads, a dynamic Startup Splash Screen modal appears. This screen displays a real-time, terminal-style log of the application’s full initialisation sequence. As the software boots up, over 100 core modules are listed transparently as they load into memory - including the Print Spooler, WordArt Engine, Minimap System, and many more. This gives both everyday users and advanced troubleshooters a live, under-the-hood view of exactly what the software is doing during startup.
The Progress Bar
A sleek teal progress bar floats beneath the console output to help you track the boot process at a glance. Unlike fake loading bars that simply run on a generic timer, this bar is synced precisely to the percentage of modules that have successfully finished loading. As each individual module initialises, the bar advances in real time, giving you an accurate and reliable visual indicator of exactly how far through the boot sequence the application is at any given millisecond.
Realistic Boot Feel
We wanted the startup experience to reflect the actual work the software is doing. The boot sequence runs at a fast 10ms base speed, but with an 8% chance to pause briefly on heavier, more resource-intensive modules. This creates the authentic feel of a real terminal boot sequence allocating system resources, rather than a uniform, pre-rendered animation. The result is a loading experience that feels highly responsive, tactile, and genuinely connected to your computer’s performance.
Draggable & Dismissible
We know that a splash screen shouldn’t hijack your workflow. The modal is completely draggable, meaning it can be easily moved out of the way if you need to view files or folders on your desktop while Open Publisher loads. Once the boot sequence completes and all modules are ready, a smooth 1-second countdown begins before the modal automatically dismisses itself, bringing you straight into the workspace. If you are a power user or simply want to review the terminal log, you can press any key during this countdown to pause it, keeping the log open on your screen until you are ready to close it manually.
Instant Cold Boot & WebP Splash Optimization (v5.18.3)
To ensure rapid startup across all devices and desktops, OpenPublisher v5.18.3 migrated all startup splash branding, background geometry, and initialization console backdrops to modern WebP compression:
High-efficiency WebP splash screen asset compression in OpenPublisher v5.18.3.
Startup asset optimization reducing splash screen memory footprint by over 78%.
78% Image Payload Reduction: Replaced legacy startupinfobg.png (456 KB) with ultra-efficient startupinfobg.webp (under 98 KB) while preserving 100% pixel-perfect alpha transparency and console borders.
Instant Cold Launch: Eliminates network download bottlenecks on slower connections and accelerates offline desktop launch times to near-instantaneous speeds.
Historical Continuity: The original PNG asset is securely archived as startupinfobg_v1.png within the codebase for version lineage.

title: V5 Branding Preview & Modern Logo Integration
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher introduced the bespoke v5 application logo with dynamic CSS masking, Base64 caching, and instant theme inheritance across all primary UI surfaces.
content:
V5 Branding Preview & Modern Logo Integration
As Open Publisher progressed toward its major version 5 architecture, modernizing the visual identity and user interface became a primary objective. In earlier releases, the application relied on generic FontAwesome printer glyphs ( fa-print ) across the title bar and informational dialogs. While functional, using a standard printer icon as the primary application brand created visual ambiguity with actionable print buttons in the ribbon and file menu. Version 4.19.2 introduced an early preview of the official Open Publisher v5 branding by integrating the bespoke inappv5.svg vector graphic across all primary identity touchpoints.
🏷️ V5 Brand Logo Integration & Dynamic CSS Masking
The custom v5 vector logo dynamically inherits theme accent colors while eliminating confusion with functional print buttons.
The Bespoke V5 Vector Asset ( inappv5.svg )
The branding refresh targeted high-visibility surfaces to establish a unified modern look:
Primary Branding Surfaces: The new vector asset replaced legacy icons in the main Application Title Bar, the Startup Dashboard Header, and the Help & About dialog.
Functional UI Separation: Standard printer glyphs were strictly reserved for functional document operations (such as the "Print Document" ribbon trigger, spooler commands, and physical output settings), removing visual ambiguity between brand graphics and actionable tools.
Dynamic Theming via Advanced CSS Masking
Rather than maintaining dozens of color-tinted SVG files for different workspace themes, Open Publisher leveraged CSS masking:
The .v5-logo-icon Class: Implemented in style.css , this class converts the static SVG image into a dynamic, font-like glyph using CSS mask-image and -webkit-mask-image .
Instant Theme Inheritance: The logo automatically adopts currentColor and active CSS variables. It seamlessly inherits contrast colors across Dark Mode, Bright Mode, High Contrast, and all 700+ Theme Studio color palettes without requiring image re-renders.
Optical Proportions & Offset: To match the visual optical weight of surrounding FontAwesome icons and compensate for internal SVG padding, the mask was calibrated with a width/height of 1.3em and a vertical alignment offset of -0.15em .
Base64 Embedding & CORS Resilience
To guarantee instant rendering in desktop wrappers and offline environments:
Inlined Stylesheet Asset: The SVG graphic was Base64 encoded directly into the core stylesheet, eliminating separate HTTP asset roundtrips.
Local File Protocol Bypass: Inlining the graphic prevents strict browser CORS blocking when executing from file:/// URLs or localized offline distributions.
Tip: The v5 brand icon automatically shifts hue and luminosity when changing workspace themes in the UI Themes dialog.

title: Webview Guest Bridge Detection & Download Button Suppression
excerpt: Explore Open Publisher
content:
Webview Guest Bridge Detection & Download Button Suppression
Native client architecture often utilizes specialized wrapper windows running host containers that embed web applications inside isolated Chromium webview guest tags ( <webview id="app-view"> ). In this guest context, Node and NW namespaces are not exposed directly to the page, and the bridge connection attaches asynchronously several hundred milliseconds after boot. Version 5.7.2 resolved the timing gap where download buttons momentarily flashed or persisted inside native client apps, introducing reactive property traps, computed style recognition, and an 800ms settling delay defense.
🌉 Webview Guest Bridge Architecture & Button Suppression Handshake
Reactive property traps intercept wrapper bridge attachment, suppressing install controls immediately upon guest injection.
The Asynchronous Webview Timing Gap
In guest webviews, standard checks fail during initial script execution because host bridge scripts attach asynchronously upon contentload :
Isolated Guest Context: Inside the webview, typeof nw is undefined and navigator.userAgent mimics standard web browsers.
Timing Discrepancy: UI scripts initialize within 0 to 150ms of DOM load, whereas the host wrapper injection executes after a 500ms handshake interval. Without reactive listening, buttons evaluated to browser mode before the bridge attached.
Reactive Property Traps & Setter Interceptors
Version 5.7.2 defined property traps ( Object.defineProperty ) in the <head> script of index.html :
Injected Property Interception: Traps assignments to window._opBridgeActive , window.desktopIPC , startDesktopSaveAnimation , and extractDocumentSnapshot .
Immediate Suppression Trigger: As soon as the host wrapper assigns any bridge property, markAsDesktopClient() fires, applying .is-desktop-app and invoking hideInstallButtons() .
Save Document Setter Interception: In extensions/system-patches.js , reassignment of window.saveDocument triggers immediate client tagging.
Computed Styles, macOS Themes & Settling Delay
Multi-layer defense mechanisms ensure bulletproof detection across all operating systems:
Wrapper Computed Style Inspection: Detects wrapper-injected CSS styling on #coord-display ( zIndex === '999999' ).
macOS Theme Defense: On macOS client machines, the wrapper applies body.mac-theme , which activates explicit CSS suppression rules for download buttons.
800ms Settling Delay & Heartbeat: Desktop browsers wait 800ms before revealing download buttons, allowing adequate time for native wrappers to complete handshakes, backed by a 7.5-second polling heartbeat.
Tip: These multi-layered defenses guarantee that installed native apps remain clean and uncluttered while web visitors always see direct download options.

title: Contributors Showcase, Security Integration & UI Polish
excerpt: Celebrate community contributions with Open Publisher
content:
Contributors Showcase, Security Integration & UI Polish
Open Publisher thrives as an open-source desktop publishing platform driven by community innovation, code contributions, and real-world testing. Version 5.6.5 introduced a dedicated, unified Contributors Showcase inside the About dialog, honoring open-source developers and contributors while highlighting core team roles. In addition, this release integrated critical security protections from community contributions, resolved hover clipping artifacts across button borders, and synchronized version manifests across the entire ecosystem.
🤝 Unified Contributors Showcase Inside the Open Publisher About Dialog
The compact 2-column showcase highlights core developers in signature teal alongside community contributors.
Unified Contributors Showcase
Accessible via Help -> About Open Publisher , the dialog features an ultra-compact, 2-column grid celebrating key project contributors:
Core Developers: Features @rmellis (Main Developer) and @tallulah95 (Main Designer & Tester), highlighted with brand green/teal background tints ( color-mix ) and primary theme borders.
Community Contributors: Displays @anupamme (Security Protections) and @lucastucious (High-DPI Feature Suggestion), linking directly to their public GitHub profiles.
AI Assistance Recognition: Acknowledges Gemini (Complex Problem Solver) with a custom gradient sparkle badge and link.
Ultra-Compact Geometry: Streamlines badge height to 22px with clean typography, fitting multiple contributor rows into a max 82px container with smooth scrolling for future additions.
Hover Border Stabilization
Previous interface buttons experienced subtle vertical translation jitter ( translateY(-1px) ) during mouse hover, occasionally clipping the top border against adjacent modal elements. Version 5.6.5 replaced translation offsets with elevation box-shadows and container padding, ensuring all four border lines remain crisp and stable during mouse interactions.
Security Protections & Asset Integrity
Version 5.6.5 merged community Pull Request #7 from @anupamme, reinforcing document data isolation and default asset protections across publication storage. Cachebusters and Service Worker manifests were bumped across all subsystems to guarantee instant client updates.
Tip: You can open the About dialog anytime from the Help menu to check your current build version and view project contributors.

title: Desktop App Download Router for Windows, macOS, Linux & FreeBSD
excerpt: Discover Open Publisher
content:
Desktop App Download Router for Windows, macOS, Linux & FreeBSD
Providing users with seamless access to native application binaries is essential for modern desktop publishing. While mobile devices and tablets benefit from the Progressive Web App (PWA) "Add to Home Screen" workflow, desktop computers require standalone installers and portable packages for offline productivity. Version 5.6.8 introduced an intelligent in-app modal download router and device classification engine, embedding download.openpublisher.app directly inside the application so desktop users can browse native releases without leaving their active document.
💻 In-App Desktop App Download Router Modal Window
Desktop users can inspect and download Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD builds in an embedded modal without leaving the editor.
(This model shows Windows Only due to being displayed on Windows, but you can select any OS from the top.)
The In-App Modal Download Architecture
Desktop web sessions bypass disruptive tab navigation by rendering the downloads portal in a native modal window:
Embedded Dialog Window: Leverages Open Publisher's DialogSystem.show architecture to render https://download.openpublisher.app/?in_app=true within an interactive iframe.
Fluid Resizing & Centering: Sized at 92vw by 85vh (up to 1200px width) with bidirectional CSS resizing ( resize: both ) and keyboard Esc dismissal.
Zero Page Leave Conflicts: Because the download window runs as an in-app overlay, users never trigger browser page-leave confirmations or risk losing unsaved document changes.
Device & Platform Classification Engine
The routing engine distinguishes desktop computers from mobile devices via PwaInstallSystem :
Desktop Environments: Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD computers route directly to native desktop installers (.exe, .dmg, .AppImage, .deb, .rpm, and FreeBSD standalone packages).
Mobile & Tablet Preservation: Smartphones and tablets (including iPadOS desktop user agents on MacIntel ) retain the PWA workflow, receiving native Chromium install banners and iOS Safari Home Screen instructions.
Native Client Suppression: When Open Publisher is running inside an installed desktop shell (Electron or NW.js), all download and install buttons hide automatically ( display: none ).
User Interface Access Points
Users can access native downloads from two primary locations:
Title Bar Quick Action: The tray download icon ( #pwa-install-btn ) displays an informative tooltip and opens the download modal.
File Ribbon Tool Button: The Share & App group in the File ribbon features a dedicated "Download App" button with a desktop monitor icon ( fa-desktop ).
Tip: You can also open the downloads dialog programmatically from the browser console or scripts using window.showDownloadModal().

title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
excerpt: Find answers to frequently asked questions about OpenPublisher, including desktop and web features, file formats (.pub, .opub, .docx, PDF), typography, image editing, tables, charts, and troubleshooting.
content:
Welcome to the official OpenPublisher Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) directory. Whether you are transitioning away from the retired Microsoft Publisher suite, looking to design flyers and brochures in your browser, or mastering our desktop publishing tools for Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD, this comprehensive knowledge base addresses the most common questions gathered from real-world user queries, Microsoft Webmaster analytics, and Copilot community searches.

Quick Reference: Top Questions & Quick Answers

Choose "Best Fit" or "Shrink Text on Overflow" to automatically scale typography to container bounds.

Resizing Images Proportionally

1. General Information & Platform Availability
What is OpenPublisher, and what are its main features?
OpenPublisher is a free, completely open-source desktop publishing application designed for creating professional flyers, brochures, multi-page newsletters, restaurant menus, promotional coupons, certificates, and booklets without advertisements, paywalls, subscriptions, or telemetry tracking.
You can use it immediately in your modern web browser at openpublisher.app without creating an account, or download the native standalone desktop application for Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD from download.openpublisher.app .
Key highlights include:
True Physical-Measurement Canvas: Design documents with millimetre, centimetre, inch, or pixel accuracy, including support for bleed margins and custom paper formats.
Extensive Asset Libraries: Includes over 50 publication templates, 3,400+ vector and raster clipart graphics, 200+ customizable geometric shapes, and 60+ 3D WordArt styles.
Professional Typography: Advanced text boxes with 100 preset card and banner styles, drop caps, multi-column linking, and automatic font best-fitting.
Built-in Utility Suites: Native Charts & Graphs Studio, QR Code Generator, freehand brush drawing engine, and interactive progress bars.
High-Fidelity Export: Direct export to 300 DPI print-ready PDF, high-resolution PNG/JPG, XPS, HTML, and self-contained Pack & Go bundles.
How do you use OpenPublisher? Is there a beginner's guide?
When you launch OpenPublisher, you are greeted by the Startup Dashboard (accompanied by a guided First Run Wizard on the desktop client). From here, you can select a standard blank page size (such as A4, US Letter, A3, or custom dimensions) or choose from pre-designed templates across flyers, certificates, and greeting cards.
If you have prior experience with Microsoft Publisher, Microsoft Word, or LibreOffice Draw, the top ribbon interface will feel immediately intuitive. Tools are categorized under familiar tabs: File , Home , Insert , Page Design , Review , and contextual tabs like Picture Tools and Table Layout that appear whenever an element is active.
Full Walkthrough Guide: For detailed step-by-step tutorials, explore our comprehensive Introduction & Getting Started guide and the Application Interface Overview .
How do I download OpenPublisher, and is there a Windows desktop shortcut?
You can download the V5 standalone desktop installer for Windows, macOS, Linux, or FreeBSD directly from download.openpublisher.app or inspect release packages on the official GitHub releases page .
On Windows 10 and Windows 11, the installer automatically registers native Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts. Furthermore, it creates OS-level file associations for .opub documents, allowing you to double-click any project directly from File Explorer to launch OpenPublisher instantly.
Can I use OpenPublisher on my Xbox with a keyboard and mouse?
Almost! Because OpenPublisher runs entirely client-side in standard web browsers with no installation or account registration required, you can launch Microsoft Edge on your Xbox console and navigate to openpublisher.app to design right from your television screen.
Xbox Controller Note: The Xbox version of Microsoft Edge does not provide full mouse pointer integration for canvas-heavy web applications. Therefore, you will need to utilize a USB/wireless keyboard combined with your standard Xbox controller to navigate and enter text.
Does OpenPublisher have a Wikipedia page or a Telegram group?
Currently, there is no official Telegram group and no Wikipedia article:
Telegram: We have not created a Telegram channel because community discussions are centralized on GitHub discussions and issue trackers where technical feedback and bug tracking can be managed transparently.
Wikipedia: In accordance with Wikipedia's strict Conflict of Interest (COI) and Neutral Point of View policies (WP:COI and WP:AUTOBIO), project maintainers and developers are not permitted to author encyclopedia articles about their own software. An independent, third-party Wikipedia editor must initiate the article based on reliable secondary coverage.
In the meantime, the best channels for reporting bugs, submitting feature suggestions, or communicating with the developers are our GitHub Issues Tracker or via email at info@openpublisher.app .
Does OpenPublisher work completely offline without an internet connection?
Yes! The standalone desktop application for Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD operates 100% offline with zero cloud dependencies. It never phones home, logs telemetry, or requires internet connectivity to create documents, insert clipart, or export 300 DPI PDFs.
Furthermore, the web application at openpublisher.app incorporates a progressive web app (PWA) service worker cache, enabling it to load and operate seamlessly even when your browser loses connection.
2. File Formats, Imports & Compatibility
How do I upload or open a file in OpenPublisher?
You can open files through two quick methods:
File Menu: Click the File ribbon tab and choose Open (or press Ctrl + O on Windows/Linux or Cmd + O on macOS).
Direct Drag-and-Drop: Simply drag any supported document or image directly from your desktop or folder window onto the OpenPublisher canvas.
Supported file formats include:
Native Projects: .opub (OpenPublisher native layout project format).
Raster & Vector Images: .png , .jpg , .jpeg , .gif , .webp , and .svg .
Word Documents: .docx and .doc files (with options for editable text or layout-locked safe mode).
Spreadsheets & Data: .xlsx , .xls , .csv , and .tsv tabular data.
Microsoft Publisher: Legacy .pub and .pubx files.
How do I import a Microsoft Publisher (.pub) file into OpenPublisher to edit?
To open a Microsoft Publisher document, select File > Open or drag your .pub or .pubx file directly into the application workspace.
OpenPublisher features a dedicated Publisher Import Engine backed by our open-source document conversion server (located in the ServerSide branch of our main repository). This conversion pipeline unpacks the binary Compound File Binary Format (CFBF) streams and XML layers, extracting text runs, vector shapes, embedded pictures, tables, and page geometry directly into editable canvas elements.
Formatting Tip: While the import engine accurately preserves text blocks, pictures, and color palettes, complex legacy Microsoft Publisher documents containing overlapping WordArt envelopes or linked nested columns may require brief manual positioning adjustments after import.
How do I save as .pub in OpenPublisher?
OpenPublisher saves editable working projects in its own open, native .opub format rather than Microsoft's proprietary and retired .pub format.
Because Microsoft Publisher is scheduled for complete retirement by Microsoft in October 2026, saving to .opub guarantees long-term preservation, ensuring that your layered layouts, vector illustrations, custom gradient themes, and high-resolution assets remain fully editable on modern computers without requiring legacy Office licenses.
When you are ready to distribute or print your publication, OpenPublisher offers comprehensive export targets:
300 DPI PDF: Commercial-grade CMYK/RGB print proofs with embedded fonts.
High-Resolution Images: Crisp PNG and JPG exports for websites, social sharing, and email.
Web & Document Formats: Interactive HTML previews, Microsoft XPS, and self-contained Pack & Go ZIP packages.
Can I edit a PDF with OpenPublisher?
Yes! OpenPublisher features native client-side Direct PDF Document Opening & Editable Layout Reconstruction . Simply drag any PDF file straight onto the canvas or choose File > Open .
An interactive pre-flight modal allows you to choose your preferred processing mode:
Editable Text Mode: Deconstructs the PDF into live, repositionable text boxes, headings, and columns. Advanced baseline grouping prevents table text from drifting across columns, while an automatic Contrast Guard ensures white labels on dark buttons remain completely legible.
Flattened Image Safe Mode: Renders each page into an ultra high-resolution 2.5x raster backdrop plate, perfect for stamping signatures, adding annotations, or filling out forms while guaranteeing 100% visual fidelity to the original file.
Where is OpenPublisher's installed data on Windows?
OpenPublisher keeps 100% of your data completely local on your machine with zero cloud tracking. On Windows 10 and 11 systems, the application and user settings are stored in standard local application directories:
Application Program Files:
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Programs\Open Publisher
Local User Data & Preferences:
C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\OpenPublisher\User Data
Your document files are stored wherever you choose to save your .opub files. In addition, if you ever experience a sudden system restart or power interruption, you can utilize the Interactive Backup Manager button located directly on the top application bar to restore auto-saved revisions, atomic recovery journals, and previous project snapshots.

3. Text Boxes & Typography
How do I create a text box, and how can I make it look fancy and visually appealing?
Navigate to the Insert tab on the ribbon and click Text Box to draw a standard text container anywhere on the canvas. Alternatively, click the small dropdown arrow directly underneath the Text Box button to open the Styled Text Box Gallery .
The gallery features 100 pre-designed text presets , including Gradient Header Cards, Outlined Callouts, Sidebar Highlights, and Magazine Pull Quotes.
Whenever any text box is selected, the contextual Text Box Tools tab activates in the ribbon, providing instant controls for:
Color Schemes & Gradients: Choose from 32 themed palette swatches or 8 smooth linear gradient fills.
Border Styling: Customize borders with solid, dashed, or dotted strokes, custom pixel thickness, and corner rounding.
Border Art: Apply 40 classic decorative Border Art frames (scalloped corners, vintage ribbons, modern geometric frames).
Can I outline text in OpenPublisher?
Yes! OpenPublisher provides two distinct ways to outline and stylize text:
WordArt Engine: For eye-catching titles and display headings, go to the Insert tab and select from over 60 WordArt Styles . WordArt renders full vector outlines, 3D extrusions, metallic chrome gradients, and neon glow effects that print cleanly at 300 DPI.
Standard Text Strokes: For standard text boxes, select your text, open the Format Properties sidebar window, and navigate to the Line & Border tab to configure precise text stroke color and outline thickness.
Does OpenPublisher have a Drop Cap feature?
Yes! OpenPublisher includes a dedicated editorial Drop Cap feature. Simply click inside any paragraph within a text box, right-click to bring up the context menu, and select Drop Cap .
OpenPublisher will automatically transform the initial letter of your paragraph into an enlarged, magazine-style capital letter spanning multiple text lines, formatted with proper baseline alignment.
Can you condense or auto-fit text in OpenPublisher?
Yes. If your text is slightly too long or short for its assigned container, right-click the text box, select Text Fit , and choose Best Fit (or toggle Shrink Text on Overflow ).
OpenPublisher calculates the bounding box area and dynamically scales the font size down or up so your text fits cleanly without manual point-by-point experimentation or awkward overflow clipping. You also have exact point-level line spacing and paragraph spacing controls on the Home ribbon tab.
How do I spell check in OpenPublisher?
OpenPublisher features a built-in Spell Check & Visual Grammar Engine accessible under the Review tab. The engine automatically proofreads text across both standard text boxes and individual table cells.
Whenever a misspelled word or grammar warning is detected, a subtle wavy underline appears. Right-click the underlined word to see immediate correction suggestions, add the term to your local dictionary, or launch the Integrated Thesaurus to look up synonyms and contextual definitions.
4. Images, Graphics & Media Tools
How do I insert symbols or emojis into OpenPublisher?
Typographic Symbols: Open the Insert ribbon tab and click Symbols to launch the glyph palette. This allows you to insert copyright symbols (©), registered marks (®), currency signs (£, €, ¥), arrows, and mathematical operators.
Vector Emojis: Click the Emojis button on the ribbon. Unlike operating system font emojis that display differently on each platform, OpenPublisher renders high-resolution SVG vector emojis . Once placed, emojis function as full vector artwork: you can resize them to poster dimensions without pixelation, adjust fill tints via the Picture Tools tab, and export them at crisp 300 DPI print quality.
How do I convert a PNG so it can be uploaded to OpenPublisher?
You do not need to convert PNG files at all! OpenPublisher natively supports standard .png files, along with .jpg , .gif , .webp , and .svg formats, with full 8-bit and 16-bit alpha channel transparency preservation.
Simply drag your PNG file directly from your computer folder onto the canvas, or click Insert > Picture on the ribbon.
How do I resize pictures in OpenPublisher?
Click on any picture on the canvas to expose its eight surrounding transform handles. Click and drag any corner handle to resize the image.
To prevent accidental squashing or stretching of your photos, ensure that Lock Aspect Ratio is active in the contextual Picture Tools ribbon tab. You can also hold the Shift key while dragging any handle to temporarily enforce proportional aspect ratio locking.
How do I round the corners of an image or put a border around pictures?
Rounding Corners: Right-click any image and select Rounded Corners to choose a corner radius preset (8px, 16px, 24px, or 32px), or click Quick Rounded Corners in the Picture Tools ribbon. You can also select Crop to Shape to clip the image into a circle, oval, shield, or one of 19 geometric vector silhouettes.
Adding Borders: Select your image and use the Picture Tools ribbon or the Format Properties sidebar to add a solid stroke border, drop shadow, soft glow effect, or decorative Border Art frame.
How do I draw in OpenPublisher?
Go to the Insert ribbon tab and look for the Drawing group located on the far right. Select a brush or spray-paint tool, set your desired thickness (from 1px up to 50px), select a stroke color, and sketch directly onto the document.
When you click outside the drawing area, OpenPublisher's raster engine automatically crops away empty bounding whitespace and commits your sketch as a crisp, transparent PNG object. You can double-click any drawing later to resume editing, or select an existing photo and click Edit in Picture Tools to paint annotations directly over an image.
Can you insert ClipArt or create QR codes in OpenPublisher?
Clipart Gallery: Yes! OpenPublisher includes a built-in gallery with over 3,400 transparent graphics categorized across business, education, holidays, nature, and food. You can search by keyword, insert items with one click, and recolor vector elements directly on the canvas.
QR Code Generator: Go to the Insert tab and click QR Code . Enter your website link or text, and customize the module style (Standard square grid, Rounded corners, or Circular badge) along with custom foreground and background colors for high-contrast scanning.
5. Tables, Data & Charts Studio
How do I resize a table or insert columns in OpenPublisher?
Resizing Table Columns & Rows: Hover your mouse cursor over any interior grid line until the cursor transforms into a double-ended resize arrow, then click and drag. OpenPublisher preserves the surrounding cell dimensions so altering one column width will not disturb adjacent table structures. To normalize cell dimensions evenly, click Distribute Rows or Distribute Columns in the Table Layout sidebar. To relocate the entire table, click and drag its outer boundary frame.
Inserting Columns: Right-click inside any cell and select Insert Column (left or right), or click the column insertion buttons in the Table Layout ribbon. You can also import a complete CSV or spreadsheet to populate a structured table instantly.
Newspaper Text Columns: If you need flowing editorial columns instead of a data table grid, link multiple text boxes together or select a multi-column template from the Styled Text Box Gallery.
How do I convert text to a table (or a table to text) in OpenPublisher?
OpenPublisher provides seamless two-way conversion between raw delimited text and structured table grids:
Text to Table: If you have tab-separated or comma-separated values (CSV/TSV) copied from a text file, email, or spreadsheet, paste it onto the page or launch the CSV & Spreadsheet Import Assistant under the Insert tab. OpenPublisher parses the rows and delimiters into a formatted, customizable table.
Table to Text: To extract tabular data back into raw text, select the outer boundary of the table, right-click, and select Convert Table to Text (also available under the Table Design ribbon). The contents are converted into cleanly tab-delimited text paragraphs.
Can I add a pie chart in OpenPublisher?
Yes! OpenPublisher features a native Charts & Graphs Studio . Click Chart on the Insert ribbon tab (or right-click the canvas and select Chart or Graph... ) to open the studio.
You can generate Pie Charts alongside 8 other chart styles:
Pie & Donut Charts
Vertical Column & Stacked Column Charts
Horizontal Bar Charts
Line Charts & Area Charts
Semi-Circular Gauge Meters & Radar Charts
You can customize slice hues, data labels, values, and legends in real time, or paste tabular figures directly from Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets. The chart is rendered on your page as an ultra-crisp vector SVG graphic printing at 300 DPI, and you can double-click it at any time to modify data points or change chart types.
6. Layout Tools, Positioning & Troubleshooting
How do I group objects, and how can I arrange objects forward and backward (including shortcuts)?
Grouping (Bulk Selection Workaround): Permanent container grouping is temporarily decoupled in the codebase to safeguard the stability of the Undo/Redo history stack. However, you can easily work with multiple items simultaneously using Bulk Selection :
Hold Ctrl and click each object, or click and drag a rectangular selection marquee over multiple elements.
A unified bounding box encloses all selected items, allowing you to move, resize, rotate, and align them together as a single cohesive unit until you click away.
Arranging Layers Forward and Backward: Right-click any element to access stacking options:
Bring to Front: Ctrl + Shift + ] (moves item to the very top layer).
Send to Back: Ctrl + Shift + [ (moves item beneath all other objects).
Bring Forward / Send Backward: Steps the element one layer up or down.
Selection Pane: Open The Selection Pane from the Layout ribbon to visually drag and reorder every object layer in your publication.
How do I copy and paste in OpenPublisher?
You can use standard OS keyboard shortcuts ( Ctrl + C to copy and Ctrl + V to paste on Windows/Linux; Cmd + C and Cmd + V on macOS), or right-click any element to use the context menu.
Additionally, OpenPublisher includes a Scrapbook Drawer on the ribbon. The Scrapbook saves a visual history of recently copied objects as interactive thumbnails, enabling you to stamp frequently used logos, badges, or headers onto different pages with a single click.
Can you add grid squares onto OpenPublisher for positioning?
Yes! Under the Layout and Page Design tools, you can enable three powerful alignment aids:
Grid Guides: Overlays a customizable grid across the canvas with magnetic element snapping.
Baseline Guides: Displays horizontal ruled notebook lines to align typography baselines across disparate text boxes and columns.
Draggable Custom Guides: Click and drag custom guide markers directly from the top horizontal or left vertical rulers to establish precise custom alignment boundaries.
How can the OpenPublisher online version use A3 paper size, or print a C4 envelope?
When starting a document, the Startup Dashboard provides preset page formats, which can also be modified at any time via Page Design > Size :
A3 Paper Size: A3 (297 x 420 mm / 11.7 x 16.5 inches) is built directly into the Startup Dashboard and the Page Design ribbon menu. Simply select A3 to configure the workspace canvas immediately.
C4 Envelopes: While C4 is not listed in the standard pre-configured drop-down menu yet (expanded envelope presets are planned for future updates), you can easily create one using the Custom Size dialog. Enter the official C4 dimensions: 229 mm x 324 mm (or 9.0 x 12.75 inches ). OpenPublisher will generate the exact envelope canvas with full 300 DPI print fidelity.
Why can't I drag my app window around after installing on Windows 10?
This issue occurs if you inadvertently downloaded and installed the legacy Windows XP-specific build (which utilizes the legacy Gecko runtime) on a modern Windows 10 or Windows 11 computer.
The specialized Windows XP edition relies on a legacy non-client window drag implementation that was necessary for XP compatibility, but modern Windows 10 and 11 desktop window managers block this legacy behavior for security isolation.
Solution: Visit download.openpublisher.app and download the modern Windows 10/11 standalone package. The standard installer provides seamless titlebar dragging, native snap layouts, and complete Windows integration.
Community & Modern Capabilities Updates (v5.18.1)
Official Facebook page launch and direct PDF editing highlights in the About Dialog (v5.18.1).
Does OpenPublisher have an official social media community?
Yes! Starting in v5.18.1 , OpenPublisher launched its official Facebook community page at facebook.com/openpublisherapp . You can follow the page for release announcements, community design highlights, helpful tutorials, and tips. You can also connect with our development team on GitHub and by emailing info@openpublisher.app.
Can I edit PDF files directly in OpenPublisher without another tool?
Yes! As highlighted in the updated About Dialog in v5.18.1, OpenPublisher features full client-side PDF document opening, text box reconstruction, and high-fidelity PDF export. You can drag and drop any PDF straight onto the canvas to edit text boxes, swap graphics, or stamp notes, with zero subscription fees or cloud uploads.
Have a Question Not Answered Here?
Our documentation is continuously updated based on community feedback. If you have an inquiry, feature request, or need technical assistance with document migration, our support resources are freely available:
Help & Support Directory
GitHub Issues
Email Us: info@openpublisher.app

title: Help and Support
excerpt: Learn how to report software bugs in OpenPublisher, contribute, submit private security vulnerabilities, and review our community code of conduct.
content:
Getting Help & Community Support
Thank you for your interest in OpenPublisher! Currently, the application is maintained by a very small core team of two people. To keep the project focused and stable, please review our community guidelines before making changes or reporting issues.
Bugs & Feature Requests
The best way to contribute right now is by thoroughly documenting bugs or proposing well-thought-out features via our GitHub issue tracker:
Bugs: Include clear steps to reproduce the issue, your operating system, and your specific OpenPublisher version.
Features: Open an issue to discuss your idea first, explaining exactly why it is crucial and how it benefits the broader user base.
Code Contributions (Pull Requests)
Because our bandwidth for reviewing new code is strictly limited, we are highly selective about accepted Pull Requests (PRs). We generally only accept contributions that represent significant, high-impact improvements and are fully aligned with our immediate roadmap.
Open an Issue First: Do not write code or submit a PR without discussing it with maintainers first. Detail your proposed changes and implementation strategy.
Wait for Approval: Wait for an explicit “go-ahead” before working on the PR. Unapproved PRs will likely be closed to save everyone time.
Code Quality: If approved, your code must match the existing project style, be extensively commented, and avoid introducing unnecessary dependencies.
Security Policy & Vulnerability Reporting
OpenPublisher operates on a continuous, rolling release model. The application automatically pulls the latest updates and security patches silently upon launch (though major releases with large client-side changes may require manual updates).
Private Reporting: We ask that you report vulnerabilities directly and privately to security@openpublisher.app before opening public GitHub issues.
Include Details: Provide a clear description of the vulnerability, steps to reproduce it, and your operating system
Code of Conduct
We pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone. We expect all contributors to demonstrate empathy, respect differing viewpoints, and gracefully accept constructive feedback. Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior can be reported confidentially to community leaders at info@openpublisher.app .

title: How to Open and Edit .PUB Files After the October 2026 Microsoft Publisher Retirement
excerpt: Microsoft Publisher reaches End of Life in October 2026. Learn how to open, edit, convert, and print legacy .PUB files for free on Windows, Mac, and Linux using OpenPublisher - the #1 free Microsoft Publisher replacement with 214 WordArt styles, 700+ themes, and 300 DPI PDF export.
content:
How to Open and Edit .PUB Files After the October 2026 Microsoft Publisher Retirement
Official Migration Guide - Updated for 2026
TL;DR: The Fastest Free Way to Open & Edit Microsoft Publisher (.PUB) Files
Microsoft officially retires Microsoft Publisher in October 2026 , removing it from Microsoft 365 and ending support for .pub files. Unlike Microsoft Word or Canva (which cannot open .pub files) or complex prepress tools like Scribus, OpenPublisher was built from the ground up as the direct, free, drop-in replacement for Microsoft Publisher:
Instant .PUB & .PUBX Drag-and-Drop Import: Keeps your text boxes, fonts, tables, vector shapes, and photo layouts 100% editable.
Zero Learning Curve: Features the familiar Microsoft Office Ribbon UI, 214 authentic WordArt styles , 700+ Theme Studio palettes , and 100+ Styled Text Box presets .
100% Free Forever: No subscriptions, no watermarks, and no account required. Runs instantly in any web browser or natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Launch OpenPublisher in Browser (Free) Download Desktop App (Win / Mac / Linux)
When Microsoft announced that Microsoft Publisher will reach End of Life (EOL) in October 2026 , millions of organizations worldwide were caught off guard. For over three decades, Publisher has been the quiet workhorse behind school newsletters, church bulletins, community flyers, restaurant menus, event programs, certificates, and small-business brochures. Once Microsoft removes Publisher from Microsoft 365 subscriptions and terminates support, organizations face a critical question: how do you open, edit, and maintain decades of archived .pub documents without rebuilding everything from scratch?
What Happens When Microsoft Publisher Retires in October 2026?
Understanding the exact impact of Microsoft's retirement schedule is essential for IT administrators, school districts, and business owners:
Removal from Microsoft 365 Subscriptions: Starting in October 2026, Microsoft 365 (formerly Office 365) subscribers will no longer be able to launch or install Microsoft Publisher. Automatic updates will deactivate or remove the application from managed endpoints.
End of Security Patches (Compliance Risk): On-premises perpetual versions receive zero security updates after October 2026. Keeping unpatched Office binaries on school, government, or corporate networks violates modern cybersecurity insurance and compliance frameworks (such as Cyber Essentials, NIST, and ISO 27001).
Orphaned .PUB File Archives: Because .pub is a proprietary binary compound file format that even other Microsoft Office apps cannot read, millions of templates risk becoming permanently locked away.

excerpt: Learn how to install Open Publisher on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Follow this step-by-step guide to download and set up your free desktop publishing app.
content:
Installation Guide
Windows
Open Publisher on Windows ships in two forms to suit different preferences and environments:
Standard Installer (.exe): Run the installer to have Open Publisher set up automatically. It creates Start Menu and Desktop shortcuts, and registers the .opub file extension in the Windows registry so that double-clicking any .opub file will instantly launch the app and load your document.
Portable Version (.exe): If you prefer not to install anything, the self-contained portable .exe runs completely in isolation - no registry modifications, no administrator privileges required. Simply drop it in any folder and run it.
How to Install on Windows:
Download your preferred version (Standard or Portable) from the official repository.
Double-click the downloaded .exe file.
If using the Standard Installer, follow the on-screen setup wizard to complete the installation.
In both cases, Windows will correctly associate .opub and legacy .pub files with Open Publisher after setup.
macOS
On macOS, Open Publisher integrates deeply with the operating system’s native conventions:
A fully native macOS menu bar maps all of the app’s tools to the top of your screen, categorised by ribbon tab (File, Home, Insert, Page Design, Review, View, Picture).
The app correctly identifies itself as “Open Publisher” in the menu bar, Dock, and system UI.
A native warning modal prevents you from accidentally closing the app with unsaved changes.
A custom splash screen and an offline connection error screen are built in for a polished experience.
How to Install on macOS:
Download the Open Publisher .dmg (Disk Image) file.
Double-click the file to mount the disk image.
Drag and drop the Open Publisher icon into your Applications folder.
Launch the application from Launchpad or Spotlight search.
Linux
Open Publisher is packaged for Linux in three formats to accommodate different distributions and preferences:
`.deb` - for Debian/Ubuntu-based distributions.
`.rpm` - for Fedora/RHEL-based distributions.
`.AppImage` - a portable, self-contained format that runs on virtually any Linux distribution without installation.
How to Install on Linux:
Debian/Ubuntu: Download the .deb file and install via your graphical software center, or use your package manager in the terminal.
Fedora/Suse/RHEL: Download the .rpm file and double-click to install, or run it through your terminal package manager.
Portable AppImage: Download the .AppImage file. Right-click the file, select Properties, and check the box to “Allow executing file as program”. Double-click to run instantly.
The application installs into the /opt/ directory and registers application/x-openpublisher MIME types so that file associations work correctly out of the box. An automation script runs at the end of installation to refresh your system’s icon cache and MIME database.

title: Linux AppImage Type 2 Specification & AppStream Compliance
excerpt: Run Open Publisher portably on Linux with Type 2 AppImage packaging, universal xz compression, POSIX permissions, and AppStream compliance.
content:
Linux AppImage Type 2 Specification & AppStream Compliance
Linux users require portable, dependency-free software packaging that runs reliably across distributions without root privileges or complex package managers. Version 5.1.11 delivers a comprehensive overhaul of the Linux AppImage packaging and runtime specification for Open Publisher v5. This release resolves upstream AppImageKit Type 2 runtime mount failures, catalog warnings, missing AppStream metadata, and permission restrictions in containerized sandboxes.
🐧 Open Publisher Portable Execution on Linux
The standalone Open Publisher AppImage launches seamlessly on any modern Linux distribution without installation.
Universal SquashFS Compression & ELF Alignment
Investigation into upstream runtime mount failures identified compression incompatibilities in the packaging pipeline:
Universal xz Compression: Replaced zstd with standard xz compression using mksquashfs -comp xz -b 1M -root-owned -noappend . The official Type 2 runtime embeds a static squashfuse build that natively mounts xz without requiring host-level zstd-squashfuse utilities.
Precise ELF Header Alignment: Repositioned the runtime's Section Header Table so that appimage_get_elf_size() evaluates to exactly 196,608 bytes - the precise offset where the SquashFS superblock begins.
Standardized Naming: Standardized output naming to OpenPublisher-5-x86_64.AppImage , satisfying AppImageKit linters and software catalog standards.
POSIX Permissions & Sandbox Safety
Directories and binaries inside the SquashFS payload previously had restrictive 0700 permissions that blocked execution in sandboxes:
Normalized Permissions: Enforced standard POSIX permissions across the entire AppDir payload: 0755 ( rwxr-xr-x ) for directories and executable binaries, and 0644 ( rw-r--r-- ) for regular data assets.
Sandbox Traversal: Guarantees that unprivileged users and containerized sandboxes (such as Firejail in AppImageHub CI suites) can traverse and execute the binary without permission errors.
AppStream & FreeDesktop Compliance
Open Publisher integrates smoothly into Linux desktop environments:
AppStream Metainfo: Added and validated usr/share/metainfo/org.openpublisher.OpenPublisher.metainfo.xml , enabling seamless discovery in KDE Discover, GNOME Software, and AppImageHub.
Desktop Thumbnailing: Integrated .DirIcon symlink at the AppDir root for instant desktop icon previews in file managers like Nautilus and Dolphin.
MIME Associations: Registered file associations for .opub documents in usr/share/mime/packages/openpublisher.xml .
Tip: To run the AppImage on Linux, make it executable with chmod +x OpenPublisher-5-x86_64.AppImage and launch it directly.
