title: The Application Interface
excerpt: Master the Open Publisher interface. Learn how to navigate the ribbon, canvas, floating toolbar, and the new startup dashboard in this complete workspace guide.
content:
The Application Interface
When you first open OpenPublisher, the workspace is divided into five key areas:
Area
Description
Ribbon
The tabbed toolbar at the top. Contains all tools, organised into tabs: File, Home, Insert, Page Design, Review, View, and contextual tabs that appear when elements are selected.
Canvas
The central white page area where you design your document.
Navigation Pane (Sidebar)
The panel on the left showing thumbnail previews of all pages in your document.
Status Bar
The bar at the very bottom of the screen. Displays the current zoom level with a slider control, cursor coordinates, and page information.
Floating Toolbar
A compact, context-sensitive toolbar that appears directly above selected text boxes, providing quick access to typography controls without navigating the ribbon.
The Ribbon
The ribbon is organised into tabs. Clicking a tab reveals a new row of tool groups relevant to that area of the application. When you select an element such as a text box, image, shape, or table, Open Publisher automatically switches to a contextual tab (e.g., Text Box Tools , Picture Tools , Drawing Tools , Table Design ) that contains controls specifically relevant to that element type. Each contextual tab includes an Arrange group for positioning, sizing, layering, rotating, and deleting elements.
If the ribbon is too narrow to show all its tools at your current window width, translucent scroll arrows appear at the left and right edges of the toolbar, allowing you to pan horizontally through the full set of tools by clicking and holding them.
The Navigation Pane
The left-hand sidebar shows a vertically scrolling column of miniature page previews. These thumbnails are automatically refreshed whenever you make changes to your document, giving you a real-time map of your entire publication. Right-clicking anywhere in the blank grey area of this sidebar opens a context menu with quick access to page management actions such as inserting, duplicating, and deleting pages, as well as document-level settings.
The Status Bar
The status bar at the bottom of the screen contains the zoom slider - a control inspired by Microsoft Publisher and Word. It features:
A minus (-) button to decrease zoom by 10% per click.
A draggable slider for smoothly scrubbing between 10% and 300%.
A plus (+) button to increase zoom by 10% per click.
A percentage readout that shows the current zoom level. Clicking this readout resets the view to 100%.
A Pan Tool toggle on the far left that locks your canvas elements in place, turning your cursor into a hand so you can click and drag the canvas freely without accidentally moving design objects.
The Floating Toolbar
When you double-click into a text box to begin editing, a compact floating toolbar materialises above the text box.
This “Frost Mint” styled bar
provides immediate, one-click access to font family, font size, bold, italic, underline, text colour, highlight colour, and text alignment - all without leaving the canvas. The toolbar remembers exactly where you position it on a per-element basis, so it will reappear in the same spot the next time you select that same text box.
Startup & Splash Screen
When Open Publisher launches, a dynamic splash screen appears as a draggable floating modal
window. It provides a real-time scrolling terminal output of all the core modules and features being initialised in the background - bridging the brief gap between clicking the app icon and the fully interactive workspace appearing.
The splash screen includes a dynamic progress bar synchronized to the percentage of features loaded, and uses a realistic “boot physics” engine that simulates the stuttering terminal feel of a heavy operating system startup. Once the boot sequence completes, the modal begins a short countdown before fading out automatically. Pressing any key during this window will keep the modal open indefinitely so you can review the log output.
The Startup Dashboard
The Open Publisher dashboard is a, 90% ~ 95% full-screen draggable modal window with a light dark (depending on if you use dark mode or light mode), translucent frosted backdrop. This design allows you to see the editor waiting underneath for better spatial context while providing lightning-fast, access to your projects.
Key features of the dashboard include:
Featured Templates: The top of the dashboard showcases a completely revamped “Featured” section, displaying 12 hand-picked, premium designs drawn from an expanded library of 250 templates.
Smart Close Button: The context-aware close button intuitively manages your session. On a cold start, clicking it generates a fresh, blank A4 (or letter) page.
If you summon the dashboard during an active session, clicking close safely returns you to your existing work without destructively overwriting your project.
Draggable Header: By default it’s themed in the signature Open Publisher Teal Green, the header features custom mouse drag logic, allowing you to freely drag the entire dashboard around the screen to peek at the workspace beneath it.
Ribbon Integration: A dedicated “Dashboard” button is available in the File > New ribbon group, allowing you to easily re-summon the startup dashboard at any time without needing to reload the application.

title: The .opub File Format
excerpt: Learn about the native .opub file format. Discover how to create, save, and open documents, and import legacy Microsoft Publisher and Word files.
content:
Document Basics & The .opub File Format
Open Publisher uses the .opub file extension as its native document format. When you save your work, your entire publication is written to a single, portable .opub file that you can store anywhere on your computer.
Key Things to Know About the .opub Format
Everything is stored locally: The file stores all of your pages, custom ruler origins, page notes, margin settings, master page overrides, and Theme Studio preferences.
Double-click to open: On all supported operating systems, simply double-clicking an .opub file automatically launches Open Publisher and loads your document.
Backwards compatible: Open Publisher continues to fully support its older .json save files. Both file types are recognized and loaded seamlessly.
AES-GCM Encryption: The format fully supports native password protection, saving your document as a secure, encrypted binary blob if you choose to lock it.
Creating, Saving, & Opening Documents
Creating a New Document: Go to File > New to open the template browser. From here, you can select from a wide range of professionally designed templates or choose a standard blank canvas size.
Saving Your Work: Press Ctrl+S (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+S (macOS). Open Publisher cleverly intercepts this keyboard shortcut at the application level and routes it directly to its internal save engine, downloading your file without triggering the browser’s default “Save Page As” dialog.
Drag-and-Drop Loading: You can drag an .opub or .json file directly onto the Open Publisher canvas. The smart drag-and-drop router instantly detects the file and restores your working session.
Importing Legacy Files (Microsoft Publisher & Word)
Format
How it imports
`.opub` / `.json`
Native format - full fidelity, restores your entire working session exactly.
Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, etc.)
Dropped or opened images are placed directly onto the current page canvas.
Publisher Files (`.pub`, `.pubx`)
Experimental import of legacy Microsoft Publisher files. Layout fidelity varies.
Excel Spreadsheets (`.xlsx`, `.xls`)
Rendered as fully interactive, movable, resizable table objects (see Section 5).
Word Documents (`.doc`, `.docx`)
Two import modes available (see below).
You can directly import Microsoft Publisher files ( .pub , .pubx ) and Microsoft Word documents ( .doc , .docx ). When opening these files, a pre-flight menu offers two import modes:
Editable Text Mode: Extracts your layout, text, and fonts into editable Open Publisher text boxes. It uses an optical color scanner to read the original text colors directly from the file’s PDF layers. This is best for documents you want to continue editing.
Flattened Image Mode (Safe Mode): Renders the document as a high-resolution, pixel-perfect background image. While less editable, it guarantees 100% layout accuracy. Recommended for complex medical tables or forms where visual fidelity matters more than editability.
Note: You can also drag-and-drop Excel spreadsheets ( .xlsx , .xls ) to open the interactive Table Import Wizard, or drop standard images directly onto the canvas.
Document Properties & Metadata
Open Publisher allows you to embed rich metadata directly into your .opub file. Go to File > Info > Properties to set the document’s Author , Company , Subject , and Keywords . This information is stored within the save file and improves context and searchability for collaborators.
Creating a New Document
To start a fresh publication, go to File > New . This opens the template browser, where you can select from a range of professionally designed publication templates (newsletters, flyers, posters, business cards, etc.) or choose a blank canvas at a standard size. Once selected, a new, untitled document opens at the specified dimensions.

title: Web App Manifest & iOS PWA Installation Engine
excerpt: Install Open Publisher as a Progressive Web App on iOS, Android, and desktop with W3C manifest compliance, Service Worker caching, and Apple meta tags.
content:
Web App Manifest & iOS PWA Installation Engine
For desktop publishing on mobile hardware such as iPads, Android tablets, and Chromebooks, running in a full-screen, chromeless window is essential for maximizing screen real estate. Prior to version 5.1.12, adding Open Publisher to an iOS home screen merely opened a standard Safari tab with visible URL bars, and desktop Chromium browsers failed installability audits. Version 5.1.12 delivers a standardized W3C Web App Manifest, Apple iOS web app meta tags, a background Service Worker, and a dedicated PWA installation engine.
📱 Progressive Web App Standalone Window on Tablet & Desktop
Open Publisher installs directly from the browser as a standalone application with full offline capability and no browser address bar.
W3C Manifest Standardization
To fulfill modern installability criteria across Chromium, Safari, and Firefox, manifest.json and site.webmanifest were synchronized to strict W3C standards:
Explicit Start URL and Scope: Defined "start_url": "./?source=pwa" and "scope": "./" , enabling browsers to identify the root navigation boundary.
Unique Application ID: Assigned "id": "openpublisher-pwa" , ensuring persistent desktop shortcuts and system taskbar grouping.
Dual-Purpose Icons: Provided separate asset entries for both "purpose": "any" and "purpose": "maskable" across 192x192 and 512x512 resolutions, satisfying Android and Chrome OS adaptive icon audits.
Theme & Category Declarations: Added brand teal theme colors ( #007670 ) and categorized the app under productivity , design , and office .
iOS Safari Integration & Apple Meta Tags
Because iOS Safari does not support the Chromium beforeinstallprompt event, Open Publisher integrates native Apple mobile web app tags into the document head:
Standalone Capable: Injected <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes"> , ensuring home screen launches run in full-screen standalone mode without browser chrome.
Status Bar Styling: Configured <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent"> for edge-to-edge canvas immersion.
Static Theme Color: Replaced dynamic CSS variable strings with a valid static hex value ( <meta name="theme-color" content="#007670"> ) so mobile browsers correctly color navigation headers.
Background Service Worker & PWA Coordinator
The dedicated Service Worker ( sw.js ) provides network-first resource routing with automatic cache eviction. The client-side installation manager in extensions/pwa-install.js coordinates the user experience:
Desktop Wrapper Suppression: Detects if Open Publisher is already running inside an Electron, NW.js, or native desktop container, automatically suppressing install prompts for desktop users.
Interactive iOS Walkthrough: On iPad and iPhone browsers, clicking "Install App" opens an illustrated modal showing how to tap the Safari Share button and select "Add to Home Screen".
Tip: To install Open Publisher on Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, click the Install button located in the right side of the browser address bar.

content:
What is Open Publisher?
Open Publisher is a WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) desktop publishing application built as a free, open-source alternative to premium tools like Microsoft Publisher. It provides the precision layout tools, rich typography, shape and image manipulation, and comprehensive export capabilities you would expect from a professional suite-with no ads, no subscriptions, and no compromises.
Because it is a true WYSIWYG editor, the document you design on your screen will match your printed or exported output exactly. Every element-text boxes, shapes, images, WordArt-is positioned using absolute coordinates on a fixed-dimension canvas, giving you pixel-perfect control over your layout at all times.
Cross-Platform Availability
Open Publisher is highly versatile and can be accessed exactly how you prefer to work:
Windows: Available as a standard installer ( .exe ) or a self-contained Portable Version that requires no installation.
macOS: Integrates deeply with native macOS conventions, including the menu bar and system UI.
Linux: Available in .deb , .rpm , and .AppImage formats for maximum distribution compatibility.
Web: Fully accessible as a Progressive Web App (PWA) directly inside any modern browser-no installation required. It can also be added to your home screen or desktop for offline use.
The Ribbon Interface
Open Publisher uses a familiar tabbed ribbon interface , keeping every tool within easy reach. The ribbon is divided into the following tabs:
File - Open, save, export, print, and manage document settings.
Home - Core formatting, clipboard, paragraph alignment, and common export actions.
Insert - Add text boxes, pictures, shapes, WordArt, tables, page parts, clipart, QR codes, and more.
Page Design - Manage page size, orientation, margins, colour schemes, backgrounds, borders, and guides.
Review - Spelling checker, thesaurus, word count, the full Writer’s Analysis Suite, and accessibility auditing.
View - Zoom controls, rulers, grid, baseline guides, spread mode, scratch area, and colour-blindness proofing.
Picture (context tab) - Appears when an image is selected; provides recolouring, adjustments, cropping, compression, and arrange tools.
The ribbon also supports a customisable UI theme system with multiple colour presets (Classic Teal, Dark, and others), so the interface itself can be personalised to your taste.
Core Features at a Glance
The platform is designed to handle a wide variety of professional and personal design tasks-like newsletters, flyers, brochures, event posters, menus, and business cards-through a massive suite of built-in tools.
Advanced Typography
Full font control over every text element, including:
Font family selection from a rich, searchable font list (including Google Fonts support via web fonts).
Font size, bold, italic, underline, and colour, accessible both from the ribbon and a floating mini-toolbar that appears on text selection.
Tab stops with leaders - set custom tab positions with dot, dash, or line leader styles for professional layouts like menus or tables of contents.
Precise line spacing - control leading with a dedicated line spacing modal.
Drop caps - apply large decorative first letters to article-style text boxes.
Vertical alignment - align text to the top, middle, or bottom of its container.
Auto-hyphenation - automatically hyphenate long words in text boxes to produce cleaner line breaks (configurable in Options).
Linked text boxes - flow a single body of text across multiple connected boxes, enabling multi-column and multi-page article layouts.
Paragraph alignment - left, centre, right, and justified alignment, available from both the ribbon and the floating toolbar.
Special characters & symbols - insert copyright marks, em dashes, bullets, currency symbols, and more via the Symbol picker.
Dynamic page numbers - insert auto-updating page number tokens directly into any text box.
Hyperlinks - add or remove hyperlinks on selected text via the right-click context menu.
Shapes & 3D Elements
Over 200 scalable SVG vector shapes organised across multiple categories: standard fills, outlines & symbols, and hollow arrows.
Shapes support solid, gradient, texture, and pattern fills , as well as custom border colours and weights.
A full 3D rotation engine lets you tilt and spin any shape element in three-dimensional space via a dedicated rotation modal.
Shapes can be freely resized, rotated, layered (bring to front / send to back), and grouped with other content.
Image Manipulation
Drag-and-drop image insertion from your local file system or directly from the clipboard.
Picture Placeholders - insert a placeholder frame first, then swap in an image later, useful for templating layouts before final assets are ready
Batch image swapping - replace all instances of one image across a document in a single action.
Non-destructive cropping - crop images to a rectangular frame while retaining the original data; uncrop at any time.
Crop-to-shape - crop images to fit inside any of 14 preset shapes (circles, stars, rounded rectangles, and more).
Image recolouring - apply tints and colour filters to images via the Picture tab.
Brightness/contrast corrections - make quick tonal adjustments with one click.
Image compression - compress a selected picture to reduce document file size.
Smart image loading - images load with a loading indicator and graceful error fallback to keep the canvas stable.
Graphics Manager - a dedicated sidebar panel (View tab) that gives you a bird’s-eye view of every image in your document, making it easy to locate, replace, or audit visuals across a multi-page project.
In-canvas drawing on images - use the built-in drawing tools directly on top of a selected picture element for annotations or creative effects.
Tables
Insert tables using an interactive grid picker (up to 10×10) or via a custom row/column dialog for larger grids.
Apply styling using 100 pre-designed table templates .
Support for multi-cell selection and standard cell content editing.
Import from spreadsheet - load table data directly from Excel ( .xlsx / .xls ) files.
WordArt & Text Effects
Legacy WordArt - a gallery of classic text effect presets for quick stylised headings.
Beta WordArt (Image-Based) - over 60 high-quality WordArt styles , including neon glow, holographic, 3D extrusion, metallic, grunge, and many more. Each style renders as a high-resolution image, making effects achievable that are impossible with CSS alone.
Clipart & Emojis
A built-in gallery of 3,403 high-quality transparent clipart images , categorised and searchable directly inside the app. No internet connection required after the initial load.
A web clipart panel that pulls in additional clipart from an online source, with a smart image loader and fallback system to handle connectivity issues gracefully.
An emoji picker for inserting any standard emoji as a scalable canvas element.
Drawing Tools
The Insert → Drawing group provides a full freehand drawing canvas directly on your page:
Pencil - fine, hard-edged strokes.
Brush - soft, pressure-style brush strokes.
Spray - airbrush-style spray effect.
Eraser - remove drawn strokes selectively.
Adjustable brush size via a slider, and full colour picker integration.
An undo action for drawing steps.
Drawing layers are preserved as part of the document’s element stack.
Page Parts Library
The Page Parts system (Insert tab) provides a library of pre-designed, ready-to-drop structural elements to speed up layout work. Available parts include:
Sidebar, Pull Quote, Section Heading, Info Callout
Contact Block, Author Bio, Photo Block (with caption)
Checklist Item, Numbered Step (Left & Right)
Tear-Off Coupon, Review Quote (5-star rating), Event Date Block, Menu Item (title + dotted leader + price)
And more - each previewed visually before insertion.
Marketing & Interactive Elements
QR Code Generator - create scannable QR codes that link to any URL and insert them directly onto the page as a scalable element.
Coupon Builder - generate styled coupon layouts with dashed borders for print-ready promotions.
Ad Builder - quickly compose advertisement-style blocks.
Business Information System
Open Publisher includes a persistent Business Info panel that stores your organisation’s details locally:
Individual Name, Job Title, Organisation Name, Address, Phone/Fax/Email, Tagline or Motto, and Logo.
Once saved, any field can be inserted into any text box in a single click from the Business Info dropdown (Insert tab).
Bulk placement options instantly generate a complete Letterhead, Signature Block, or Business Card layout using your saved details-ideal for maintaining brand consistency across multiple documents.
Themes & Styling
Apply document-wide colour schemes from a scrollable palette of presets - Classic, Pastel, Neon, Corporate, and many more. Schemes update all matching elements simultaneously.
Choose from a wide range of background textures and solid fills for the page canvas.
Insert any of 100 unique, scalable SVG page borders to frame your design.
Toggle headers and footers on or off from the Design tab for multi-page documents.
Set custom margins and choose from standard guide presets.
Snap-to options (grid, guides, objects) ensure accurate alignment when placing elements.
View & Layout Tools
Zoom controls - 60%, 75%, 100%, 150%, Fit Page, and Fit Width presets, plus keyboard shortcuts.
Rulers - horizontal and vertical rulers to measure and align elements precisely.
Grid and baseline guides - toggle on/off for structured layouts.
Spread Mode - view facing pages (left/right spreads) side by side, as you would in a booklet or magazine layout.
Scratch Area - a workspace outside the page canvas where you can park elements temporarily while composing your layout.
Object Boundaries - toggle visible outlines around all elements for layout auditing.
Paragraph Block Markers (¶) - visualise text block extents across the canvas.
Colour Blindness Proofing - simulate how your document appears to users with various types of colour vision deficiency, directly in the View tab, to make informed accessibility decisions
The Writer’s Analysis Suite
Available in the Review tab, the Writer’s Suite is a powerful set of text analysis tools aimed at writers and content creators using Open Publisher for newsletters, reports, or editorial layouts. Select any text box and run any of the following analyses:
Tool
What it does
Grade
Calculates the Flesch-Kincaid readability grade level of the selected text.
Tone
Detects the dominant emotional tone - Urgent, Enthusiastic, Professional, or Casual - based on keyword frequency.
Concise
Identifies wordy phrases and suggests shorter, punchier replacements.
Passive
Flags sentences written in passive voice.
Echoes
Detects repeated word usage that may make writing feel monotonous.
Stats
Reports word count, character count (with and without spaces), sentence count, and paragraph count.
Time
Estimates reading time based on an average adult reading speed.
Sentiment
Scores the overall positive/negative/neutral sentiment of the text.
Keywords
Analyses keyword density for SEO awareness.
Jargon
Flags complex or overly technical vocabulary that may not be accessible to a general audience.
Cadence
Analyses sentence length variation to reveal whether writing feels rhythmically varied or monotonous.
The suite also includes a Focus Mode (Environment group) which hides the entire interface and surrounding chrome, leaving only the page canvas visible for distraction-free writing and editing.
The Review tab also provides:
Spelling checker - real-time spell checking with underline highlighting as you type (configurable in Options).
Thesaurus - look up synonyms for selected words without leaving the app.
Word Count - a dedicated word count modal for the current page.
Proofing & Quality Tools
Design Checker
The Design Checker (Review / Proofing) scans your entire document and flags common print-readiness issues, including:
Text Overflow - text boxes where content is cut off and not fully visible.
Low-Resolution Images - pictures that have been stretched beyond their native resolution and may look pixelated when printed.
Off-Page Objects - elements positioned fully or partially outside the page canvas boundary.
Each issue is reported with a description and a button to jump directly to the offending element.
Accessibility Checker
The Accessibility Checker (Review tab) audits your document against core accessibility standards and reports:
Missing Alt Text - images that lack descriptive alternative text (essential for screen readers and HTML export).
Low Colour Contrast - text/background combinations that fall below the WCAG minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
Heading Structure - flags cases where heading levels skip (e.g., jumping from H1 to H3), which breaks assistive technology navigation.
Missing H1 - pages that lack a primary heading entirely.
Results are shown in a collapsible sidebar panel, and clicking an issue jumps directly to the affected element on the canvas.
Document Security
AES-GCM password encryption - protect your .opub files with industry-standard encryption. A password is required to open the document.
Document Inspector - scrub hidden metadata (author information, revision history) from your file before sharing it.
Native Files & Professional Exporting
Projects are saved using the native .opub file format , which stores the full document state including all pages, elements, styles, and embedded images as a structured JSON bundle.
When you are ready to share your work, Open Publisher offers an impressive suite of professional export options:
Format
Details
PDF (High-Resolution)
Renders the canvas at high DPI for crisp print output.
Image (PNG/JPEG)
Exports the current page as a raster image at a chosen resolution.
XPS
Generates an XPS (XML Paper Specification) document, widely used in Windows print workflows.
HTML (Advanced)
Exports a fully self-contained HTML file with granular options (see below).
Email ( .eml )
Packages the design as an email file that opens directly in your default email client, ready to send.
Pack & Go
Creates a ZIP archive containing your .opub file, all extracted images, and a font manifest - the standard handoff package for commercial print shops.
Save as Template
Saves the current document as a reusable .opub template for future projects.
Advanced HTML Export Options
The HTML exporter includes a dedicated options modal with fine-grained control over the output:
Seamless Newsletter Layout - removes page gaps and shadows for continuous scrolling (ideal for web newsletters).
Optimise for Email Clients - renders the document as a single image inside a legacy table structure for maximum compatibility with Mailchimp, Gmail, and Outlook.
Embed External Images - converts external Clipart URLs to Base64 Data URIs, producing a fully offline-capable, single-file HTML document.
Auto-Scale to Fit Screen - injects a viewport meta tag so fixed-width designs shrink gracefully on mobile screens.
Enable Text Selection - allow visitors to highlight and copy text from the exported page.
Inject SEO & Social Meta Tags - uses the Analysis Suite to extract keywords and summary text, and injects them as <meta> tags for search engine indexing and Twitter/Facebook link preview cards.
Minify Output - strips whitespace from the HTML to reduce file size.
Include Web Fonts - embeds Google Fonts links so typography renders accurately in any browser.
Application Options
The Options panel (accessible from the File menu) mirrors the familiar settings layout of professional desktop suites:
General - personalise your username and choose a UI theme.
Proofing - toggle real-time spell checking.
Save - configure auto-save behaviour (coming soon).
Language - set the display language (coming soon).
Advanced - enable automatic hyphenation in new text boxes.
Customise Ribbon - configure which ribbon groups are shown (coming soon).
Trust Centre - security and trusted location settings (coming soon).
Open Source & Privacy
Open Publisher is fully open source and available on GitHub. There is no account system, no telemetry, no tracking, and no data ever leaves your device. All document data is stored locally in your browser’s storage or on your file system. It is free to use, fork, and edit however you want under its open-source licence.

title: Baseline Guides
excerpt: Use Open Publisher's Baseline Guides to set evenly spaced horizontal lines that align text across columns and text boxes to a consistent typographic rhythm.
content:
Baseline Guides
Baseline Guides overlay evenly spaced horizontal lines across your canvas, mirroring the baseline rhythm of your body text. They work like ruled paper for your document - helping text in separate text boxes, columns, and layout areas sit on a consistent horizontal baseline across the full page. This technique is a cornerstone of professional editorial and typographic design.
Baseline Guides are non-printing and only visible in the editor - they never appear in exported or printed output.
Opening Baseline Guide Settings
Go to Page Design > Guides > Grid and Baseline Guides .
The customisation modal opens as a draggable window so it can be moved out of the way while you preview your changes live on the canvas.
What You Can Customise
Baseline spacing - Set the interval between baseline lines to match the leading (line height) of your body text. When the spacing matches your text’s line height, text across multiple columns and separate text boxes naturally aligns to the same horizontal rhythm without manual adjustment.
Baseline colour - Set a colour for the baseline lines independently from the grid guides, so both can be visible at the same time without visual confusion.
When to Use Baseline Guides
Baseline Guides are most valuable when:
Working with multi-column layouts where you want body text to align horizontally across adjacent columns.
Designing newsletters or magazines where consistent text rhythm across the full page is essential.
Placing text alongside images where you need the text to start and end at the same vertical positions as neighbouring elements.

title: Canvas Marquee Selection Viewport Clamping & UI Bleed Prevention
excerpt: Learn how Open Publisher clamps drag-selection marquee boxes to viewport and paper intersections, eliminating interface visual bleed across toolbars and sidebars.
content:
Canvas Marquee Selection Viewport Clamping & UI Bleed Prevention
Dragging a selection marquee across the canvas is an everyday action for grouping objects, moving layouts, and making bulk formatting edits. However, when working zoomed in (150%, 200%, or 300%), earlier versions suffered from an intrusive visual artifact: the selection marquee bled outside the canvas boundaries and drew across ribbon toolbars, ruler bars, page preview sidebars, and status bars. Version 5.8.3 engineered strict mathematical intersection clamping, active sidebar occlusion awareness, and z-index layer isolation, ensuring selection boxes stay strictly confined to the editable canvas viewport.
🔲 Zoomed-In Marquee Selection Strictly Clamped to Canvas Viewport
Drag selection boundaries stop cleanly at ruler, sidebar, and ribbon edges when navigating at high magnification.
Mathematical Intersection Clamping
The root cause of interface bleeding originated from single-container coordinate clamping:
The Zoomed-In Paper Expansion: Previously, marquee coordinates were clamped solely against the physical paper container ( #paper ). When zoomed in, the paper bounding box expands hundreds of pixels beyond the browser viewport. Because the marquee element used fixed positioning with an elevated z-index, dragging near screen edges caused the selection box to draw directly on top of interface controls.
Dual-Boundary Intersection: In canvas/interaction-mouse.js , extensions/smart-images.js , and extensions/system-patches.js , the drag engine computes the mathematical intersection of paper.getBoundingClientRect() and viewport.getBoundingClientRect() :
minX = Math.max(paperRect.left, viewRect.left)
maxX = Math.min(paperRect.right, viewRect.right)
minY = Math.max(paperRect.top, viewRect.top)
maxY = Math.min(paperRect.bottom, viewRect.bottom)
Zoomed-Out Preservation: When working at low zoom levels or viewing whole pages, the selection box remains locked to document paper edges, preventing the marquee from escaping into outer margins.
Sidebar Occlusion Awareness & Layer Isolation
The selection engine coordinates with active floating panels across the workspace:
Active Sidebar Detection: Detects open floating sidebars (including Picture Tools, Shadow Options, Accessibility Scanner, and Table Design) and dynamically clamps the right-hand selection limit to the left edge of visible panels.
Z-Index Layer Re-Balancing: Lowered marquee overlay z-index from 9999 to 45 with box-sizing: border-box , ensuring selection graphics remain cleanly beneath ribbons, rulers, and modal dialogs.
Thresholding & Dark Mode Theming
Marquee interaction includes safety thresholds and visual polish:
3px Drag Threshold: Marquee containers initialize with display: none . Element hit testing enforces a minimum 3px movement threshold before engaging selection mode, preventing accidental multi-selections on simple canvas clicks.
Dark Mode High-Contrast Styling: Features dedicated dark mode CSS for #marquee-box , rendering vibrant teal borders and translucent fills against dark backgrounds.
Tip: You can hold Shift while dragging a marquee to add new objects to your current selection without deselecting existing elements.

title: Canvas Scratch Area Scrolling in All Directions & Floating Return Button
excerpt: Learn how Open Publisher enables smooth four-directional scratch area scrolling in single and multi-page modes, auto-extending boundaries, and an intelligent return button.
content:
Canvas Scratch Area Scrolling in All Directions & Floating Return Button
Professional publication layout requires a flexible, expansive pasteboard around the document. Designers frequently use the pasteboard (the "scratch area") to stage draft headlines, store alternative images, and experiment with design ideas before placing them on the active page. In standard web applications, scroll containers hit hard boundaries whenever scrolling upward or to the left of the page origin. Version 5.7.7 introduced complete four-directional scratch area scrolling across Single-Page and Multi-Page modes, boundary auto-extensions, cross-browser delta normalization, and an intelligent floating "Return to Page" button.
🧭 Four-Directional Scratch Workspace with Floating Return Button
Users can scroll into the scratch area in all four directions with an intelligent directional button to return to the active page.
Four-Directional Scrolling & Hybrid Coordinate Translation
Browser scroll containers with overflow: auto enforce a hard lower bound: coordinates cannot drop below zero ( scrollTop = 0 , scrollLeft = 0 ). Any upward or leftward wheel events at the boundary are normally discarded. Version 5.7.7 engineered a hybrid scroll and translation system in canvas/canvas.js :
Upward Scratch Scrolling: When scrollTop <= 2 and the user scrolls upward with the mouse wheel or trackpad ( deltaY < 0 ), the engine smoothly translates the canvas downward via style.top , opening visible pasteboard above the document.
Leftward Scratch Scrolling: When scrollLeft <= 2 and the user scrolls leftward ( deltaX < 0 ), the engine translates the canvas rightward via style.left , opening visible pasteboard to the left.
Smooth Directional Restoration: When scrolling back toward the document, custom offsets restore cleanly to their base positions before native document scrolling engages.
Ruler & Guide Synchronization: In Single-Page Mode, top and left rulers ( syncRulers ) and margin guide overlays ( syncMarginGuideOverlay ) track the paper position in real time.
Multi-Page Overview Parity & Zoom Boundary Extensions
The scratch area navigation engine operates with complete parity across all document view modes:
Multi-Page Overview Parity: In Multi-Page Overview mode, the engine dynamically targets #multi-page-wrapper , allowing designers to pan and scroll across wide overview grids without artificial boundaries.
Vertical Scratch at High Zooms: Fixed an issue where canvas scrollbars refused to scroll past the bottom of the page when zoomed between 110% and 150%. The workspace guarantees at least 25% to 45% (minimum 200px) of visible scratch space below the document at all zoom factors.
Dynamic Boundary Auto-Extension: Canvas scroll limits automatically expand when scrolling near edge perimeters, accommodating sprawling multi-page layouts.
Cross-Browser Normalization & Floating Return Button
Version 5.7.7 guarantees an identical tactile scrolling feel across all operating systems and browsers:
Delta Normalization: Normalizes Firefox line-based deltaMode ( deltaMode === 1 ) with Chromium pixel deltas ( deltaMode === 0 ), delivering uniform scroll velocity.
Shift-Wheel Horizontal Navigation: Holding Shift while scrolling with the mouse wheel smoothly navigates horizontally into left and right scratch areas.
Directional Floating Return Button: If the user pans so far into the scratch area that the active document is completely offscreen, an elegant floating button ( #floating-return-to-page-btn ) appears with a directional arrow indicating where the document is located ( fa-arrow-up , fa-arrow-down , fa-arrow-left , or fa-arrow-right ). Clicking the button smoothly recenters the page.
Tip: You can use the Hand Tool (hold the Spacebar while dragging) to pan across the scratch workspace freely in any direction.

title: Classic MS Publisher Cursor Engine & Real-Time Drag Controls
excerpt: Discover OpenPublisher classic MS Publisher cursor engine, featuring the iconic Move Truck and crosshair cursors, ribbon toggle, and real-time text box resizing.
content:
Classic MS Publisher Cursor Engine & Real-Time Drag Controls
For millions of users who grew up designing newsletters, certificates, and flyers in Microsoft Publisher, few interface elements are as instantly recognizable as the classic "Move Truck" cursor. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.16.10 , the Classic MS Publisher Cursor Engine faithfully recreates that iconic cursor experience alongside significant layout enhancements, including real-time text box resizing without border lag and elevated transform handle hit-zones.
Figure 1: The classic Move Truck border hover cursor in action, with the dedicated 'Classic Drag' toggle button active in the View ribbon tab.
1. The Classic Move Truck & Precision Crosshair Engine
Enabled by default out of the box, the cursor engine dynamically adapts to what you are doing on the canvas:
The Move Truck Hover Cursor: Whenever your mouse hovers over the draggable border perimeter of a selected text box, shape, image, or table (or any active edge drag strip), the cursor turns into a crisp 28x28 pixel-art moving truck. This gives you instant visual confirmation that you can click and drag to reposition the element.
The Precision Crosshair Drag Cursor: As soon as you press your mouse button down and begin moving the object across the canvas, the truck switches to a precision crosshair cursor, providing unobstructed visibility of your alignment guides, ruler ticks, and neighboring content.
Specialized Handle Cursors Protected: Corner and edge resize handles ( .openpublisher-resize-handle ) strictly retain their directional resize cursors ( nwse-resize , nesw-resize , ns-resize , ew-resize ), while text boxes preserve the standard I-beam text cursor when editing inside words.
2. How to Toggle Classic vs. Modern Cursors
While many creators love the classic Publisher nostalgia, some users prefer standard modern desktop publishing system cursors. OpenPublisher makes toggling effortless:
View Ribbon Toggle ("Classic Drag")
Head to the View ribbon tab and look in the Show group. Click the Classic Drag button (featuring a theme-adaptive teal truck icon) to turn classic cursors on or off with a single click.
Options Modal Preference
Go to File > Options > General and check or uncheck "Use classic MS Publisher drag cursors (Move Truck & Crosshair)" . Your preference is saved locally across browser sessions.
3. Real-Time Text Box Resizing & Elevated Handle Layering
Alongside cursor aesthetics, v5.16.10 fixed a longstanding layout quirk with text box resizing:
Immediate Bounds Tracking: In earlier builds, dragging a text box's bottom resize handle could occasionally lag or freeze the selection outline until the mouse button was released. Version 5.16.10 updates overlay heights dynamically on every frame, so the bounding box expands or shrinks synchronously in real time.
Elevated Handle Z-Index (1005): Transform handles are elevated above border drag strips ( z-index: 1005 vs 998 ), completely preventing accidental moves when you intended to grab a corner handle.
Expanded 4px Invisible Hit-Zones: Each handle now includes an invisible 4px perimeter margin, making it effortless to click and drag corner handles even on high-DPI displays or touch trackpads.
Theme Matched: The ribbon toggle icon dynamically adjusts its hue to match your active UI theme or dark mode setting, keeping your workspace beautifully cohesive.

title: Context Menus
excerpt: Open Publisher replaces the browser's default right-click menu with custom context menus throughout the workspace, ribbon, title bar, canvas, and page thumbnails.
content:
Context Menus
Open Publisher replaces the browser’s default right-click menu with custom, application-specific context menus throughout the entire workspace. Every area of the interface has its own tailored menu with relevant options for that location.
Canvas Right-Click Menu
Right-clicking on an empty area of the document canvas (not on an element) opens a menu with:
Insert sub-menu - Table, Styled Tables, Text Box, Picture, Shape, Drawing, QR Code, and more.
Format Background - Opens the background colour and texture dialog.
Snap to toggles - Grid, Guides, and Objects.
Show/Hide Rulers, Toggle Grid, Page Design/Size.
Element Right-Click Menus
Right-clicking a canvas element opens a contextual menu specific to that element type:
Text Box - Layering controls (Bring Forward, Send Backward, etc.), formatting options, Save as Picture, and copy/paste actions.
Table - Insert Row/Column, Delete Row/Column/Table, Merge Cell options, and Clear Cell Text.
Image - Layering controls, crop options, and Save as Picture.
Page Thumbnail Right-Click Menu
Right-clicking a page thumbnail in the left sidebar opens a page management menu with:
Duplicate Page
Move Page Up / Down
Delete Page
Add Note (add a custom label to the thumbnail)
Master Pages sub-menu (Set Master, Ignore Master, None)
Workspace Background Right-Click Menu
Right-clicking the grey workspace area outside the document canvas opens a menu with:
Add new blank page
Show/Hide Rulers
Toggle page margins
Page Design/Size
Format Background
Ribbon Right-Click Menu
Right-clicking the empty grey space in the ribbon toolbar opens a menu with:
Toggle Fullscreen
Export to PDF
Save Project
Toggle Grid Background
Reload App
Title Bar Right-Click Menu
Right-clicking the empty space in the top menu bar (where the document title is displayed) opens a menu with:
Rename Publication
Copy / Paste
Page Setup
Save / Export / Print
Reload App and About
Zoom Bar Right-Click Menu
Right-clicking the zoom slider in the bottom-right corner opens a quick scale menu with preset zoom levels from 60% to 200%, for instant one-click access to the most common zoom settings.

title: Crisp Margin Guides at All Zoom Levels
excerpt: Experience razor-sharp page margin guides at every zoom level in Open Publisher with the fixed viewport compositor overlay and theme-reactive borders.
content:
Crisp Margin Guides at All Zoom Levels
Precision alignment demands margin guides that remain sharp and clearly visible whether you are zoomed in to 300% on a logo or zoomed out to 40% on a multi-page spread. Open Publisher features a dedicated margin guide compositor engine that bypasses GPU downsampling blur and maintains device-pixel clarity across all zoom levels.
📐 Open Publisher Margin Guide Overlay at Low Zoom
Crisp, non-blurry margin guide dotted lines rendered at device-pixel sharpness during canvas zooming.
The Fixed Viewport Compositor Layer
Traditional canvas elements scale via CSS transform scaling ( transform: scale(z) ). When Chromium encounters fine details below 1.5 physical pixels (such as a 1px dotted guide line at 60% zoom), the lines blur away during GPU downsampling. Open Publisher solves this permanently:
Decoupled Compositor Overlay: The margin guide renders as a top-level, fixed body element ( #margin-guide-overlay ) positioned directly in viewport coordinates.
Device-Pixel Sharpness: Because the overlay sits outside the canvas transform layer, it is never downsampled by the GPU, guaranteeing razor-sharp lines at all zoom settings.
Non-Uniform Margin Support: The overlay dynamically reads state.margins to faithfully represent Normal, Narrow, Wide, and custom user margins.
Continuous requestAnimationFrame Tracking
Rather than relying on discrete scroll or zoom events that can drop frames during fast navigation, the overlay tracks the paper canvas inside a continuous requestAnimationFrame loop. This guarantees that margin guides remain pixel-perfectly locked to the paper boundaries during rapid panning and window resizing.
Theme-Reactive Border Colors & Stacking
The margin guide engine is finely tuned for visual comfort:
Automatic Palette Sync: The overlay reads --ui-theme-color on every frame, instantly updating guide colors when switching between Classic Teal, Word Blue, Sunset Orange, or Dark Mode.
Recalibrated Z-Index: Indexed to z-index: 1001 so guides float cleanly above canvas objects but remain strictly beneath ribbon menus and font dropdowns.
Note: Margin guides can be toggled on or off at any time via Page Design → Margins on the Ribbon.

title: CSS Syntax Recovery & Workspace Viewport Layout Restoration
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher restored workspace viewport geometry, bottom status bar docking, and off-canvas sidebar isolation following a stylesheet syntax hotfix.
content:
CSS Syntax Recovery & Workspace Viewport Layout Restoration
Complex desktop-grade web applications rely on strict, balanced stylesheet architectures to maintain viewport boundaries, flexbox hierarchies, and off-canvas panel transitions. During the deployment of version 5.5.1, an unclosed curly brace on the status bar zoom container inadvertently compromised downstream CSS block scoping across thousands of rules. Version 5.5.2 delivered an immediate, targeted recovery hotfix that restored 100% syntactic balance to the stylesheet, re-established workspace viewport geometry, docked the status bar cleanly at the screen bottom, and reinforced off-canvas sidebar isolation.
📐 Restored Viewport Hierarchy and Bottom Status Bar Docking
The workspace expands to fill the vertical viewport while the status bar docks firmly at the bottom edge.
The Anatomy of a Cascading Flexbox Failure
Understanding the cascading interaction illustrates the vital importance of balanced stylesheet scoping in browser layout engines:
Unclosed Selector Block: An unclosed brace following #zoom-slider-container caused modern browser parsers to interpret all downstream rules (including .workspace and #op-image-sidebar ) as nested selectors rather than top-level declarations.
Fixed-Position Collapse: Without its position: fixed declaration, the Format Picture sidebar reverted to normal in-flow rendering inside document.body .
Vertical Space Starvation: Because body operates as a flex column container ( height: 100vh ), the 515px height of the in-flow sidebar crushed .workspace down to 0px, causing the editing canvas and rulers to vanish and displacing the status bar upward against the ribbon.
Viewport Geometry & Status Bar Realignment
Version 5.5.2 restored balanced CSS scoping across all 5,236 lines of style.css , re-establishing the four-tier vertical viewport hierarchy:
Tier 1 - Title Bar (y: 0px, h: 35px): Houses document naming, coordinates readout, and window management controls.
Tier 2 - Ribbon Container (y: 35px, h: 150px): Houses tabs, command groups, and tool palettes.
Tier 3 - Workspace (y: 185px, h: 594px): Expands with flex-grow: 1 to fill all available space, hosting the pages sidebar, interactive rulers, and centered paper canvas.
Tier 4 - Status Bar (y: 779px, h: 21px): Docks permanently at the bottom edge, displaying page counts, document DPI, protection badge, and zoom slider controls.
Floating Sidebar Isolation
With fixed positioning restored, contextual panels like #op-image-sidebar utilize off-canvas CSS transforms ( translateX(calc(100% + 50px)) ) to stay hidden off-screen until explicitly invoked by selecting an image or opening the Format tab.
Tip: If you ever notice UI elements shifting unexpectedly, a hard browser refresh (Ctrl + F5) clears cached stylesheets and ensures all layout rules reload cleanly.

title: Document Load Page Focusing & Viewport Auto-Centering
excerpt: Center documents automatically on load, eliminate off-screen canvas offsets, remove focus outline rings, and restore smooth horizontal scrolling in Open Publisher.
content:
Document Load Page Focusing & Viewport Auto-Centering
When opening an existing publication, template, or recent project, designers expect their canvas to appear immediately in view. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, loading files - particularly high-resolution 300 DPI print documents measuring 2480px by 3508px - occasionally caused the canvas to spawn off-screen or at distant scroll offsets, requiring manual scrollbar dragging. Version 5.1.7 introduces a centralized page focusing coordinator and dynamic scroll bounds engine, ensuring documents always open centered, full-viewport, and cleanly focused.
🎯 Centered Document Load & Smooth Horizontal Scroll Bounds
Publications center automatically in the viewport upon opening with smooth side-to-side scrolling and no focus borders.
Centralized Page Focus Engine
The window.focusPage() coordinator in canvas/canvas.js synchronizes workspace viewport states on load:
Single-Page View Reset: Automatically exits multi-page grid or overview modes, resetting state.viewMode = 'single' .
Scroll Offset Normalization: Resets viewport scrollTop and scrollLeft to zero, clearing residual offsets left over from prior editing sessions.
Resilient Optical Zoom: Invokes an enhanced fitToPage() calculation with multi-tier fallback dimension checks, scaling the document perfectly to fit within the available workspace window.
Universal Lifecycle Integration: Hooked into native .opub and .docx file loading, template gallery imports, blank document creation, and Recent Files card clicks.
Elimination of the Dark Focus Outline
In previous iterations, focusing the canvas added a temporary tabindex to the paper element, prompting browsers to draw an unsightly 1px dark focus rectangle around the document. Version 5.1.7 completely eliminates this artifact:
CSS Hard Guards: Added outline: none !important; to #paper , #paper:focus , and #paper:focus-visible .
Attribute Sanitization: Removed programmatic tabindex assignments and focus calls, preserving pure document aesthetics.
Dynamic Canvas Scroll Bounds Engine
When zoomed in beyond 100% on high-DPI canvases, standard CSS flex centering causes scaled content to expand symmetrically into negative coordinates, cutting off the left edge. The window.updateCanvasScrollBounds() engine solves this:
Intelligent Shift Compensation: When scaled content exceeds the viewport, the paper shifts right so its left edge maintains at least 50px of comfortable breathing room at scrollLeft = 0 .
Dynamic Scroll Sizer: Injects a scroll-sizer element that expands scrollWidth symmetrically, providing equal 50px margins on both left and right edges.
Native Side-to-Side Navigation: Smooth horizontal scrolling via scrollbar track dragging, horizontal trackpad swiping, and Shift + Mouse Wheel scrolling across all zoom levels (1.0x to 3.0x).
Tip: Press Ctrl + 0 (or Cmd + 0 on macOS) at any time to instantly re-center and fit your active page to the workspace.

title: Draggable Custom Guides
excerpt: Pull custom horizontal and vertical alignment guides directly from the rulers in Open Publisher  -  with smart snapping, locking, and one-click clearing from the Guides menu.
content:
Draggable Custom Guides
Open Publisher lets you pull custom alignment guides directly from the rulers onto the canvas. These are fully interactive teal lines that you drag into any position to mark out precise alignment points for your layout - and elements on the canvas will snap to them automatically.
Creating a Custom Guide
Hover over the top ruler to pull out a horizontal guide , or the left ruler to pull out a vertical guide .
Click and drag away from the ruler onto the canvas.
The guide appears as a 2px teal line and tracks your mouse 1:1, regardless of your current zoom level or scroll position.
Release the mouse to drop the guide into position.
You can place as many custom guides as you need. Each guide is elevated above all other document elements so it is always visible and never hidden beneath objects on the canvas.
Smart Snapping to Custom Guides
Custom guides are fully integrated into Open Publisher’s global snapping engine. As you move shapes, text boxes, and images near a guide, the element’s edges and centre points will snap precisely to it, flashing a bright teal highlight when the alignment is perfect. This makes it effortless to line up multiple elements along a consistent axis without any manual measurement.
Locking & Clearing Guides
Custom guide controls are available from the Page Design > Guides dropdown:
Lock Guides - Freezes all custom guides in place so they cannot be accidentally clicked or moved while you are working. Locked guides still display and snap to elements, but ignore any interaction until unlocked.
Clear Guides - Removes all placed custom guides from the canvas instantly with a single click.

title: Symmetrical Floating Colors & Style Toolbar, Zoom Scaling & Object Selection
excerpt: Work faster with OpenPublisher symmetrical floating colors and style toolbar, proximity illumination, zoom-responsive scaling, and object defocus controls.
content:
Symmetrical Floating Colors & Style Toolbar
Speed up your layout workflow with contextual tools that stay right where you work. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.16.11 and v5.16.12 and enhanced in v5.18.4 , the Floating Colors & Style Toolbar hovers gracefully above selected shapes, images, and text boxes. Featuring symmetrical geometry, zoom-responsive scaling, proximity illumination, auto-hiding during dragging, and seamless text defocus, it delivers instant styling power without cluttering your workspace.
The Symmetrical Floating Colors & Style Toolbar with Zoom-Responsive Scaling in OpenPublisher v5.16.12.
Text box defocus and selection isolation on image/object click in OpenPublisher v5.18.4.
Contextual Intelligence: The floating toolbar dynamically shifts its controls depending on what you have selected: showing fill, stroke, and opacity for shapes; border and frames for pictures; and font families, size, and alignment for text boxes.
Ergonomic Design & Smart Behaviors
The toolbar is engineered to feel weightless and unobtrusive:
Proximity Illumination (v5.16.11): The toolbar sits at a comfortable semi-translucent rest state and smoothly brightens to full opacity as your mouse approaches, keeping your canvas view clean while designing.
Drag Auto-Hide: While dragging or rotating an element across the canvas, the floating toolbar automatically tucks away so it never blocks your alignment guides or view of surrounding content.
Symmetrical Centering (v5.16.12): The toolbar anchors with symmetrical geometry centered above the object's upper edge.
Zoom-Responsive Scaling (v5.16.12): Whether working at 25% overview zoom or 400% detail zoom, dynamic inverse CSS scaling keeps the toolbar buttons crisp, sharp, and physically easy to click.
Collision Guard: If an object is near the very top of your canvas or ribbon edge, the toolbar automatically flips beneath the selection to prevent clipping.
Text Box Defocus & Selection Isolation (v5.18.4)
When typing inside a text container, clicking away onto a picture, clipart, or another shape now cleanly releases text focus immediately. OpenPublisher v5.18.4 isolates object events so the clicked graphic is selected on the first click without leaving ghost cursor carets behind or requiring multiple clicks to deselect.

title: Grid Guides
excerpt: Customise the spacing and colour of Open Publisher's grid overlay for precise element alignment. Accessible via Page Design > Guides > Grid and Baseline Guides.
content:
Grid Guides
Grid Guides overlay a regular pattern of intersecting lines across your canvas, giving you a precise visual reference for aligning elements and maintaining consistent spacing throughout your layout. The grid is non-printing - it is only visible in the editor and never appears in your exported or printed output.
Opening Grid Guide Setting
Go to Page Design > Guides > Grid and Baseline Guides .
The customisation modal opens as a draggable window so it can be repositioned while you preview changes on the canvas live.
What You Can Customise
Grid spacing - Set the distance between grid lines to any value that suits your layout. Tighter spacing gives you greater precision for positioning small elements; wider spacing works well for block-based, modular layouts.
Grid colour - Change the colour of the grid lines to something that contrasts clearly against your page background without becoming visually distracting during design work.
Locking & Clearing Guides
Lock Guides - Freezes all guides in place via
Page Design > Guides > Lock Guides , preventing accidental movement during active design work.
Clear Guides - Removes all placed guides from the canvas instantly via Page Design > Guides > Clear Guides .

title: Insert File (Content Migration)
excerpt: Use Open Publisher's Insert File tool to extract and migrate text content from an old document into a new template without disrupting your carefully built layout.
content:
Insert File (Content Migration)
The Insert > File tool solves a common problem when migrating between templates. Because Open Publisher is a precise page-layout tool, simply swapping a template would destroy a carefully crafted layout. Insert File lets you extract and pour your text content from an old document directly into a new template safely.
How to Migrate Content
Open the new template you want to use via File > New .
Click inside the text box in the new template where you want your old content to go.
Go to Insert > File and select your old .opub document.
Open Publisher opens the old file in the background, scans every page, and extracts all text elements.
All the extracted text is poured directly into the selected text box automatically.
Note: Images and shapes are not transferred by this method, as they require precise manual placement in the new layout. Only text content is migrated.

title: Insert Ribbon Layout Streamlining
excerpt: Single-line typography alignment and streamlined Illustrations group toolbar layout in OpenPublisher Insert ribbon tab.
content:
Insert Ribbon Layout Streamlining Open Publisher features a streamlined, polished layout refinement for the Illustrations toolbar group within the Insert ribbon tab ( #ribbon-insert ). Multi-line text wrapping on toolbar buttons has been replaced with clean single-line typography, leveling button heights and baselines across the toolbar for a spacious, professional aesthetic. Visual Balance & Breathing Room: Eliminating awkward line breaks prevents toolbar buttons from crowding into group footer labels, giving the entire ribbon a balanced, professional hierarchy. Before vs. After Layout Comparison The layout refinement resolves several visual inconsistencies in the Illustrations toolbar group: Toolbar Element Legacy Implementation Streamlined Implementation Ergonomic Benefit Insert File Button "Insert
File" (2-line split) "Insert File" (Single line) Consistent horizontal baseline across all 9 tools Template Button "Template
Page" (2-line split) "Template" (Single line) Concise naming matching adjacent tools (Picture, Clipart, Emojis) Vertical Group Margin Tight 2px margin above group label Generous 8px margin above group label Eliminates visual crowding near category footers Illustrations Group Tools Uneven button heights Strict 100% height parity Symmetrical click targets across all display resolutions Uniform Alignment Across All 9 Illustration Tools All tools within the Illustrations group now share a unified typographic baseline and vertical centering: Text Tools: Text Box, Styled Text Box Document Elements: Insert File, Page Parts, Template Visual Media: Picture, Picture Placeholder, Clipart, Emojis This typographic leveling ensures that as you switch between the Home, Insert, Page Design, and View tabs, the ribbon maintains consistent height benchmarks without jarring layout shifts or wrapped button boundaries.

title: Margin Guide Stacking Context & Dropdown Layering
excerpt: Ensure canvas margin guides sit cleanly beneath ribbon dropdowns and UI chrome with recalibrated viewport stacking contexts in Open Publisher.
content:
Margin Guide Stacking Context & Dropdown Layering
In version 4.20.0, Open Publisher introduced crisp device-pixel margin guides using a fixed viewport overlay ( #margin-guide-overlay ) to bypass Chromium GPU downsampling during canvas zoom transforms. However, that overlay was originally assigned an arbitrary z-index: 9999 , while Ribbon dropdown menus such as the Font Family picker used z-index: 6000 . When opening dropdown menus that extended downward over the page, dotted teal margin lines visibly bled through the menu options. Version 4.20.2 recalibrates the entire workspace layer architecture to ensure absolute visual isolation.
📐 Margin Guides Rendered Beneath Font Dropdown
The dotted margin guide overlay floats cleanly above page elements while remaining subordinate to open Ribbon dropdowns.
Stacking Context Collision & Root Cause
The visual conflict occurred because both the margin overlay and ribbon dropdowns exist in viewport coordinate space:
Fixed Overlay Architecture: The margin overlay is a direct child of <body> with position: fixed , allowing it to draw 1-pixel guide lines sharply regardless of canvas zoom.
Stacking Priority Inversion: Because 9999 exceeded the dropdown container's 6000 , the browser compositor layered the dotted margin border on top of the open font menu items.
Layer Recalibration: In canvas/canvas.js and style.css , the overlay was reduced to z-index: 1001 . This aligns with canvas guide standards, floating cleanly above user elements ( z-index: 10 ) while remaining strictly below UI chrome.
Authoritative Dropdown Elevation
To prevent future layering collisions, all dropdown elements were elevated to maximum UI priority:
Custom Dropdown Class: The base .custom-dropdown selector in style.css was raised to z-index: 999999 !important .
Inline Ribbon Dropdown Alignment: The ribbon handler in ui/sidebar-context.js explicitly sets menu.style.zIndex = '999999' during dropdown activation.
Theme Override Normalization: Color palettes, font size pickers, and zoom flyouts all inherit this top-level stacking contract.
Workspace Visual Hierarchy
Open Publisher now maintains a disciplined layer stack: Canvas Paper (0 - 10) → Canvas Guides & Margin Overlay (1001) → Title Bar & Ribbon Chrome (100 - 101) → Dropdowns & Menus (999999) → Modal Dialogs (9999999). This guarantees that interface menus remain completely unobstructed during intricate layout editing.
Tip: Margin guides can be quickly toggled on or off using the Guides button under the View tab on the main Ribbon.

title: Multi-Page Overview Decoupling & Viewport Architecture
excerpt: Zoom freely across high-DPI publications without unwanted layout mode switching using decoupled view architecture and status bar controls in Open Publisher.
content:
Multi-Page Overview Decoupling & Viewport Architecture
In version 5.1.5, Open Publisher underwent a major architectural overhaul to its canvas viewport and page navigation engines. In earlier versions, zooming out on high-resolution publications (such as 140 DPI or 300 DPI A4 documents) automatically triggered an unexpected mode switch into a multi-page overview grid, freezing sidebar navigation, causing rulers to repeat erratically across the pasteboard, and detaching margin guides into empty canvas space. Version 5.1.5 completely decouples Multi-Page Overview from camera zoom scale, putting full control back in the designer's hands.
🔍 Decoupled Single-Page Zoom vs. Multi-Page Overview
Designers can zoom down to 5% in single-page mode or switch to Multi-Page Overview via dedicated status bar buttons.
Decoupled View Architecture
The camera zoom scale and document view mode now operate independently:
Eliminating Automatic Threshold Switches: Dynamic threshold triggers have been removed from setZoom() . You can zoom out freely from 300% down to 2% to view full-page layouts without ever triggering a multi-page grid switch against your intent.
Explicit View State Management: The active mode is governed by state.viewMode = 'single' | 'multipage' . Zooming in Single-Page mode scales #paper smoothly, while zooming in Overview mode scales the multi-page grid container.
Global Control APIs: Manage view modes programmatically via window.setViewMode(mode) , window.toggleMultiPageView() , and window.updateViewModeUI() .
Realigned Status Bar & Ribbon View Toggles
View switching is integrated into intuitive interface touchpoints:
Status Bar Cluster: Quick switcher buttons ( [Single] and [Multi] ) are positioned directly in the center status group alongside the page counter and DPI badge: Page 1 of 5 | 300 DPI | [Single] [Multi] .
Dedicated Ribbon Group: Access the Views group under the View tab on the Ribbon to toggle between layouts.
Canvas Context Menu: Right-click anywhere on the pasteboard or canvas background to toggle Multi-Page Overview instantly.
Overview Navigation, Rulers & Shortcuts
Multi-Page Overview provides seamless navigation across large publications:
Single-Click to Center: Clicking any page slot in the overview grid or sidebar highlights it with a teal border ( .multi-page-slot-active ) and smoothly centers the target slot in view.
Double-Click to Edit: Double-clicking any page slot immediately opens that page in Single-Page editing mode and executes fitToPage() for comfortable editing.
Keyboard Shortcuts: Use ← and → arrow keys to cycle between pages, Enter to open the selected page, and Escape to exit overview mode.
Scoped Ruler Suppression: Single-origin rulers ( #ruler-h , #ruler-v ) and floating margin guides are cleanly hidden while in multi-page mode to prevent misleading coordinate readouts, restoring automatically when returning to single-page mode.
Tip: When entering overview mode for the first time, an informative dialog explains navigation shortcuts with a "Do not show again" option.

title: Multi-Page to Single-Page Return Auto-Focus, True Visual Centering & Zoom Preservation
excerpt: Discover Open Publisher
content:
Multi-Page to Single-Page Return Auto-Focus, True Visual Centering & Zoom Preservation
Switching between a macro bird's-eye view of your entire publication and detailed single-page editing is central to multi-page publication design. Designers frequently jump into Multi-Page Overview to assess balance and page flow, then double-click a page thumbnail to resume fine-tuning. Earlier releases had a disorienting transition defect: returning to single-page mode left the viewport at the top-left pasteboard origin ( scrollLeft = 0, scrollTop = 0 ), stranding users on blank pasteboard while the document sat hundreds of pixels to the right. Additionally, single-page editing zoom was lost. Version 5.7.9 introduced an automated return pipeline featuring true visual centering, instant transitions, and zoom level preservation.
🎯 Instant View Mode Transition with Centered Page Focus
Exiting Multi-Page Overview immediately brings the chosen page into center focus while restoring prior editing zoom.
Universal Return Pathway Auto-Focus
Version 5.7.9 unified every exit pathway from Multi-Page Overview into an automated centering pipeline:
Unified Exit Handling: Whether leaving multi-page mode via the ribbon "Single" button, bottom status bar button, double-clicking a thumbnail slot, pressing Enter on a selected slot, pressing Esc , or calling focusPage() , execution flows through exitMultiPageView() .
True Visual Centering: The centering formula dynamically calculates paperVisualCenter = paper.offsetLeft + (paper.offsetWidth / 2) , centering the document symmetrically regardless of whether the app is running in standard browser flexbox or NW.js desktop client margin layouts.
Zero-Delay Instant Snapping: Added an instant flag to returnToPage(true) ( scrollBehavior: 'auto' ). On view transitions, this instantly positions the viewport over the page, eliminating sluggish 500ms gliding animations across empty pasteboard space.
Double-Shot Micro-Syncs: Scheduled secondary micro-syncs at 30ms and 100ms in exitMultiPageView() to absorb asynchronous desktop wrapper reflows, ensuring 0px horizontal center offset.
Zoom Level Preservation Across View Modes
In earlier versions, entering Multi-Page Overview overwrote the application zoom state with overview zoom (~35%), leaving the document shrunken when returning to single-page view:
Editing Zoom Caching: In enterMultiPageView() , the active zoom setting is preserved in window._preMultiPageZoom before switching to overview scale.
Automatic Restoration: In exitMultiPageView() , the prior zoom magnification (e.g. 100%, 120%, or 60%) is reinstated, with automatic updates dispatched to the ribbon zoom slider and percentage indicator.
Page Switch Execution Ordering & Overlay Guards
Internal function ordering was also hardened to guarantee visual stability:
Sequential Page Switching: In openPageInSingleMode(index) , switchPage(index) is called prior to view mode switching, guaranteeing that active page elements serialize cleanly and the selected page content renders before the view changes.
Lazy Dialog Overlay Initialization: In ui/ui.js , DialogSystem.show() incorporates lazy initialization to prevent null overlay references if modals are triggered before explicit DOM setup.
Tip: Double-clicking any page card in Multi-Page Overview instantly opens that specific page in full editing mode at your preferred zoom level.

title: Non-Destructive Selection
excerpt: Open Publisher's non-destructive selection overlay allows you to select, resize, and rotate elements without disturbing your document's layered stacking order.
content:
Non-Destructive Selection
When building complex layouts with overlapping elements, maintaining your visual hierarchy is critical. Open Publisher uses a Non-Destructive Selection system that ensures selecting an object never temporarily pops it to the front or disturbs your carefully arranged layers.
Preserved Stacking Order
When you select an element that is layered behind other objects, it stays exactly where it is in the visual stack. The image and element stacking order you manually create using the Bring Forward and Send Backward tools remains completely untouched during active selection and editing.
Note: how the selected image displays its selector bounding box and handles, despite being placed at the very bottom of the document stack.
The Floating Selection Overlay
To allow you to manipulate elements without changing their Z-index (layer depth), Open Publisher renders the selection highlighter on a dedicated, floating overlay layer high above the workspace. This overlay includes:
The blue dashed bounding box
The white resize dots on the edges and corners
The rotation stick handle
Top-Level Handle Interaction
Because the resize and rotation handles are rendered on this top-level floating overlay, they are always fully interactive. This ensures that even if you select an object that is deeply buried underneath large shapes or text boxes, you can still easily grab its controls to scale or rotate it without having to move the blocking elements out of the way first.

title: Object Lock in Place & Quick Actions Padlock Controls
excerpt: Learn how to freeze background elements, master plates, and text boxes using OpenPublisher floating quick actions padlock and Lock in Place controls.
content:
Object Lock in Place: Layout Protection & Quick Actions Padlock
When crafting intricate multi-layer designs like flyers, newsletters, and catalogs, accidentally selecting or dragging a background plate, header banner, or decorative border can disrupt carefully aligned layouts. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.19.6 , the Object Lock in Place engine and contextual Quick Actions Padlock allow you to instantly freeze any element directly on the canvas with a single click.
The Floating Quick Actions Padlock button in OpenPublisher v5.19.6, offering instant one-click layout freezing.
Complete Layout Protection: When an element is locked, it cannot be accidentally moved, resized, rotated, deleted, or nudged with arrow keys. You can comfortably drag selection boxes over it without disturbing its position.
The Floating Quick Actions Padlock
Whenever you select any object on the canvas, a subtle floating quick-action toolbar appears alongside the selection bounding box. The toolbar features an intuitive Padlock Icon :
One-Click Locking: Click the open padlock icon on the floating toolbar to instantly lock the selected element.
Gold Lock Visual Feedback: Once locked, the bounding box handles shift to a distinctive gold outline accompanied by a small closed padlock badge in the upper corner, confirming the element is secure.
Direct Unlocking: To unlock an element, simply click on the object to reveal its gold padlock badge and click the padlock again, or right-click the element and choose Unlock Object .
Alternative Ways to Lock Elements
In addition to the floating quick-action padlock, OpenPublisher offers multiple flexible methods to suit your preferred workflow:
Context Menu
Right-click any selected object or group and select Lock in Place from the context menu. To release, right-click and choose Unlock .
Keyboard Shortcut
Press Ctrl + L (or Cmd + L on macOS) to instantly toggle the lock state of currently highlighted items.
Arrange Ribbon Menu
In the top ribbon under the Layout & Arrange group, click the Lock Selection button. A drop-down allows locking all objects on the active page simultaneously.
When Should You Lock Objects?
Full-Bleed Background Images: Lock background photos so you can select and edit overlaid text boxes without dragging the backdrop.
Page Mastheads & Folios: Lock header logos, page numbers, and issue dates across multi-page newsletters.
Complex Vector Illustrations: Once an intricate clipart or shape composition is positioned, lock it to prevent accidental component misalignment.
Table Grids: Lock financial tables in place while editing individual cell contents or annotating notes beside columns.
