title: Page Margins
excerpt: Set page margins in Open Publisher using five instant presets or fully custom values. Margin guides appear on canvas but are automatically excluded from all PDF exports.
content:
Page Margins
The Margins button in the Page Design ribbon controls the safe-zone guides on the canvas. Five presets are instantly available, each represented by a small dynamic page icon that visually previews the margin layout before you click.
Margin Presets
Normal - 0.5” on all sides.
Narrow - 0.25” on all sides.
Moderate - 1” top and bottom, 0.75” left and right.
Wide - 1” on all sides.
Zero - 0” (borderless, full-bleed printing).
Custom Margins
For precise control, click Custom Margins… to open a configuration modal where you can set independent top, bottom, left, and right margin values in pixels. Your custom margins are saved to the document and persist when the file is reopened.
How Margins Appear
Margins appear as dotted blue snapping guides on the canvas, giving you a clear visual safe zone while you design. They are automatically excluded from exported images and PDFs - they never appear in your final output.

title: Page Notes
excerpt: Add custom Page Notes to individual page thumbnails in Open Publisher to label and organise complex multi-page documents at a glance in the sidebar.
content:
Page Notes
For complex multi-page documents, Page Notes let you add short custom labels to individual page thumbnails in the sidebar, making it easy to stay organised and navigate long publications at a glance.
Adding a Page Note
To add a note to a page:
Right-click the page thumbnail in the left sidebar.
Select Add Note .
Type a short identifier (for example: “Front Cover”, “TOC”, “Advertorial”, or “Back Cover”).
Press Enter or click OK .
The note displays directly beneath the thumbnail in a bold teal font. To remove a note, repeat the process and leave the field blank.

title: Page Size & Format
excerpt: Set your canvas to A3, A4, A5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid or Business Card size in Open Publisher, with automatic locale-aware defaults for US and international users.
content:
Page Size & Format
Open Publisher supports a comprehensive range of international page sizes. You can change your canvas size at any time from the Page Design ribbon using the Size button.
Available Page Sizes
A3 - 297 × 420mm
A4 - 210 × 297mm (European / UK default)
A5 - 148 × 210mm
Letter - 8.5 × 11” (US / Canada / Mexico default)
Legal - 8.5 × 14”
Tabloid - 11 × 17”
Business Card - 3.5 × 2”
Each preset is represented by a unique icon in the dropdown and the top-right corner of the canvas always displays the correct format indicator.
Locale-Aware Defaults
When you create a new document, Open Publisher automatically selects the correct default page size for your region. Users in the US, Canada, Mexico, Colombia, Venezuela, Chile, and the Philippines default to US Letter ; users everywhere else default to A4 . This happens automatically in the background without any setup required.
Page Format Indicator
The page format indicator in the top-right corner of the canvas always reflects your current format precisely. It is wired directly into the rendering engine and updates instantly whenever you change size, switch pages, undo, or redo.

title: Real-Time Drag Previews & Complete Element Fidelity
excerpt: Experience ultra-fluid sidebar previews with Open Publisher
content:
Real-Time Drag Previews & Complete Element Fidelity
In professional document design, visual feedback must be immediate and effortless. When moving, resizing, or rotating a headline, photo, or callout box on the canvas, users expect the sidebar thumbnail to mirror those adjustments live rather than waiting for mouse release. Version 5.6.1 established the high-performance Real-Time Drag Synchronization Engine, synchronizing canvas object interactions with sidebar previews at a smooth 60 frames per second while guaranteeing complete element fidelity across all graphic types.
⚡ 60 FPS Real-Time Element Synchronization During Canvas Drag
Canvas elements and their sidebar thumbnail counterparts move in lockstep during drag, resize, and rotation.
The 60 FPS Direct Synchronization Pipeline
Previous preview updates relied on heavyweight history snapshots and full thumbnail re-renders upon mouse release. Version 5.6.1 introduced direct 1:1 DOM coordinate pairing:
Persistent Element ID Pairing: Every canvas element ( .pub-element ) pairs with its thumbnail counterpart ( .pub-thumb-element ) via the persistent data-target-id attribute.
Direct Transform Reflection: During mouse movement, syncRealtimeThumbnailDrag() streams updated coordinates ( left , top , width , height , transform ) directly into the paired thumbnail element.
Hardware-Accelerated Scaling: Because thumbnail containers use CSS downscaling ( transform: scale(...) ), updates execute with zero complex coordinate recalculations, running at full GPU-accelerated 60 FPS.
Strict Active Page Scoping: Real-time streaming targets strictly #thumb-[state.currentPageIndex] , ensuring inactive thumbnails remain untouched with zero performance overhead.
Complete Element Fidelity Across All Types
The synchronization pipeline supports every object type supported by Open Publisher:
WordArt Typography: Both high-resolution Beta WordArt canvas renders and Classic WordArt text scale and reposition smoothly within the thumbnail.
Images & Clipart: Photos, vector clipart, and inline SVGs maintain aspect ratios, rounded corners, and clip paths during drag operations.
Shapes & Smart Arrows: Polygons, rectangles, stars, and parametric smart arrows reflect stem stretching and rotation angles live.
Tables & Text Boxes: Multi-cell tables and formatted text blocks update positions in real time as you adjust page layouts.
Tip: Glancing at the sidebar thumbnail while dragging objects near page margins gives you an instant bird's-eye view of your layout balance.

title: Ruler Selection Span Markers & Smooth Real-Time Cursor Position Indicators
excerpt: Master document alignment with Open Publisher
content:
Ruler Selection Span Markers & Smooth Real-Time Cursor Position Indicators
Precision alignment is the cornerstone of desktop publishing. Whether placing a banner image, sizing a three-column article text frame, or aligning logo marks to margins, designers rely on horizontal and vertical rulers to verify object dimensions and mouse positions. Earlier builds featured basic ruler highlights that suffered from coordinate drift, missed multi-selections, and lacked cursor position feedback. Version 5.7.10 introduced an overhauled ruler tracking engine featuring high-contrast selection span markers, lighter marquee feedback, and compositor-driven cursor indicators that track the pointer with zero lag.
📏 Dual-Ruler Selection Spans & Real-Time Hairline Cursor Pips
The top and left rulers highlight exact object coverage while 1px cursor hairlines follow the mouse in real time.
Dual-Ruler Selection Span Highlights
Version 5.7.10 replaced detached body overlays with markers embedded directly inside the ruler containers:
Direct Ruler Nesting: Selection and cursor markers are injected directly into #ruler-h and #ruler-v . Because rulers use overflow: hidden , marker coordinates map simply as targetRect - rulerRect without requiring manual clamping math.
Vertical Ruler Highlight Restoration: Resolved a legacy bug where the left vertical ruler failed to highlight selected objects due to a shared visibility cache key between horizontal and vertical markers. Both rulers now update independently.
Multi-Selection Union Bounding: When multiple elements are selected ( Ctrl or Shift click), the rulers display the combined bounding span covering all selected objects.
Lighter Marquee Span Feedback: While dragging a marquee selection box across the canvas, the rulers display a lighter 12% tint with delicate 1px border edges ( .is-marquee ), clearly distinguishing drag selection from committed objects.
Smooth Compositor-Driven Cursor Tracking
Earlier cursor tracking prototypes felt sluggish and trailed behind the mouse cursor because layout coordinates were read repeatedly on every mouse event. Version 5.7.10 engineered a high-performance tracking loop:
Zero Layout Reads During Mousemove: Geometry for rulers, viewport, and canvas is sampled and cached once per animation frame ( requestAnimationFrame ). Mousemove handlers execute zero layout reads.
GPU Compositor Positioning: Hairlines are translated via transform: translate3d(...) with will-change: transform and transition: none , rendering position updates instantly on the GPU.
Hairline with Triangular Pointer Pip: The indicator features a 1px theme-colored hairline plus a subtle 3px triangular pointer pip at the inner edge of the ruler pointing inward toward the page.
Clean Departure Behavior: Cursor markers hide automatically when the pointer leaves the workspace or window focus is lost. Markers also cleanly suppress in Multi-Page Overview mode.
Ruler Guide Deletion & Context Menu Fixes
Interaction with ruler guides was also refined: dragging an existing guide back onto either ruler now cleanly deletes the guide rather than sticking to the paper edge. Additionally, right-clicking a ruler to switch measurement units (inches, centimeters, millimeters, points, pixels) no longer creates accidental ghost guides.
Tip: You can right-click anywhere on the horizontal or vertical ruler to switch between Inches, Centimeters, Millimeters, Points, and Pixels.

title: Rulers & Ruler Origin
excerpt: Show pixel rulers in Open Publisher and set a custom ruler origin to redefine the zero point anywhere on the canvas for precise spatial positioning and layout work.
content:
Rulers & Ruler Origin
Pixel rulers run along the top and left edges of the canvas, giving you a precise spatial reference while you work. The ruler origin can be repositioned to any point on the page for even more accurate placement.
Showing & Hiding Rulers
To show or hide rulers:
Go to View > Show > Rulers , or
Right-click in the workspace background and select Show/Hide Rulers .
Custom Ruler Origin (Zero Point)
By default, the ruler’s 0,0 origin sits at the top-left corner of the canvas. You can redefine this origin to any point on the page:
Drag the grey intersection box where the horizontal and vertical rulers meet, at the very top-left corner of the canvas.
As you drag, dashed guide lines follow your cursor across the page to help you visually pinpoint the target coordinates.
Release to set the new zero point. All ruler ticks and labels immediately recalculate from the new origin.
Double-click the intersection box at any time to instantly reset the rulers back to their default position.
Your custom ruler origin is saved into the .opub file and persists across sessions.

title: Snapping & Smart Guides
excerpt: Use Open Publisher's three independent snapping modes and smart alignment guides to position elements precisely, with instant Ctrl override and 8px snap tolerance.
content:
Snapping & Smart Guide
Open Publisher provides three independent snapping systems and a smart alignment guide system to help you position elements with precision. Each can be controlled separately to suit your workflow.
Snapping Modes
Three snapping modes can be toggled individually:
Snap to Grid - Elements snap to an invisible pixel grid as you drag.
Snap to Guides - Elements snap to the margin guide lines.
Snap to Objects - Elements snap to the edges and centres of other elements on the page.
To manage snapping, use the Snap To dropdown in the View tab, the Text Box Tools ribbon, or the Picture Tools ribbon. You can also right-click the canvas and toggle snapping options from the context menu.
Temporarily Bypassing Snapping
Hold Ctrl while dragging to temporarily bypass grid snapping without toggling the setting off. This is the most efficient way to place something between grid positions without changing your snapping configuration.
Snap Tolerance
The magnetic pull distance for Snap to Guides and Snap to Objects is set to 8 pixels.
This provides a subtle and predictable snap feel that matches professional desktop publishing software.
Smart Grid Prompt
If you turn off Snap to Grid while the visual grid overlay is currently visible, a dialog intelligently asks if you also want to hide the visual grid to clear up your workspace - so you are never left with a grid overlay that serves no purpose.
Smart Guides (Alignment Lines)
When you drag any element on the canvas, Smart Guides appear as semi-transparent teal lines indicating when the element is aligned with the edges or centres of other elements on the page.
Smart Guides use a smooth fade-in and fade-out transition rather than abruptly flashing on and off, preserving high responsiveness while eliminating visual flicker. The guide colour is a soft, semi-transparent teal - visible enough to be useful but not heavy enough to overpower your design.
Smart Guides work alongside the snapping system, not instead of it. Snapping “pulls” the element to the alignment point; Smart Guides show you where that alignment point is.

title: The Scratch Area
excerpt: Store elements off-canvas in Open Publisher's Scratch Area without deleting them, then toggle visibility on and off instantly to keep your workspace uncluttered.
content:
The Scratch Area
Any element dragged outside the page boundary is stored in the Scratch Area - an off-canvas holding space useful for keeping elements in reserve without cluttering your document.
Showing & Hiding the Scratch Area
To show or hide Scratch Area items:
Go to View > Show > Scratch Area , or
Right-click in the workspace and toggle the option.
When the Scratch Area is hidden, off-page objects become invisible and non-interactive - but they are not deleted . Toggle it back on to bring them back immediately.
Note: Any new element dragged off-page while the Scratch Area is hidden is also hidden instantly - so your workspace stays clean automatically.

title: The Selection Pane
excerpt: Use the Open Publisher Selection Pane to select, show, hide, and rename every element on your canvas, with real-time Z-index visibility and bulk show/hide controls.
content:
The Selection Pane
The Selection Pane gives you full visibility and control over every element on the canvas, making it easy to select, hide, or rename even deeply buried, stacked, or obscured objects.
Opening the Selection Pane
Go to Home > Select > Selection Pane . The pane slides out on the right side of the workspace and displays a scrollable list of every object on the canvas, sorted top-to-bottom to match their true visual Z-index - the topmost element in the list is the one in front on the canvas.
What You Can Do
Select an element - Click its entry in the pane and it is immediately highlighted on the canvas.
Show / Hide - Click the eye icon on any entry to toggle its visibility. Hidden elements are invisible on screen and excluded from PDF exports.
Show All / Hide All - Use the bulk buttons at the top of the pane to toggle all elements at once.
Rename an element - Click the element’s name in the pane to activate an inline edit field. Type a descriptive name (for example: “Background Logo” or “Footer Bar”) and press Enter to save it.
Real-Time Updates
The Selection Pane updates in real time via a native MutationObserver - no manual refresh is needed. Add an element, delete one, or move something on the canvas and the pane reflects it instantly.

title: Workspace Initialization Race Condition Fix & Preview Recovery
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher eliminated workspace startup race conditions, preventing phantom pages, corrupted thumbnails, and premature history snapshots.
content:
Workspace Initialization Race Condition Fix & Preview Recovery
When opening Open Publisher or creating a new publication from the Startup Dashboard, the workspace canvas should load smoothly and display a crisp page preview in the left navigation sidebar. In earlier builds, an asynchronous race condition during document bootstrap could corrupt new sessions: closing the dashboard or creating a new document could trigger a history save before the page DOM was fully assembled, resulting in unwanted "phantom" pages, empty sidebar previews, or corrupted page sizes. Version 4.19.7 resolved these initialization conflicts with strict empty workspace guards and session index resets.
🛠️ Clean Document Workspace Initialization with Active Page Preview
New publications initialize with verified document geometry and instant page thumbnail preview generation.
The Premature History Snapshot Bug
The primary cause of phantom pages and corrupted previews was traced to early history capture:
The Empty Workspace History Save: During document startup, setPageSize() was invoked to establish initial dimensions. However, setPageSize() unconditionally triggered pushHistory() , capturing a snapshot before the initial page was rendered.
Phantom Page Creation: Saving an incomplete state object into the undo/redo stack caused the history engine to treat the empty initialization state as "Page 1" and the subsequent rendered document as "Page 2", creating duplicate phantom entries.
Empty Workspace Guard: In layout/document.js , setPageSize() is now guarded against executing pushHistory() when the workspace is completely empty during initialization.
Dashboard startBlank Index Safety Reset
Session initialization was hardened to prevent index collision:
Stale Index Resolution: In earlier versions, creating a new document could retain a stale currentPageIndex from a previous session, causing newly created pages to reference invalid slot offsets.
Explicit Index Re-Zeroing: Added an explicit safety reset for currentPageIndex = 0 inside the dashboard's startBlank workflow, ensuring every new document starts from a clean zero index.
Thumbnail Preview Recovery
By preventing premature history snapshots and index corruption, sidebar thumbnail previews generate accurately upon session start, displaying correct page dimensions and background styling across all browsers without requiring manual page refresh.
Tip: If you ever need to reset your workspace to a clean state, you can click "New Document" in the File menu or press Ctrl+N.

title: Zoom Controls
excerpt: Control zoom levels in Open Publisher from 10% to 500% with a slider, keyboard shortcuts, and right-click presets, plus automatic multi-page view below 45% zoom.
content:
Zoom Controls
The zoom level is shown in the bottom-right corner of the workspace. A zoom slider allows smooth, continuous zoom from 10% all the way to 500%, giving you precise control over how much of your canvas is visible at any time.
Keyboard Shortcuts
F9 - Toggles between your current zoom level and 100% actual size. Pressing again returns to your previous zoom.
Ctrl + Shift + L - Whole Page View: instantly zooms to fit the entire page within the window.
Ctrl + Shift + O - Toggles element boundary boxes on and off.
Quick Zoom Presets
Right-click the zoom slider to open a context menu with instant one-click access to common zoom levels: 60%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 120%, 130%, 150%, 175%, and 200%.
Multi-Page View
When the zoom level drops below 45% and your document has more than one page, Open Publisher automatically switches to Multi-Page View , rendering all pages side-by-side in the workspace.
Read-only preview clones of all non-active pages appear alongside the live editable page. Click any preview page to switch to editing it instantly - without leaving multi-page view.
Zoom-Invariant Selection Handles
Selecting and transforming objects remains seamless whether working at 25% overview zoom or 500% high-precision zoom. Version 5.10.3 introduced scale-compensated selection overlays: the corner and edge resize handles dynamically scale inversely to viewport zoom, maintaining a comfortable, crisp 8px grab size at all zoom levels so you never struggle to click tiny handles when zoomed out.

title: Business Information
excerpt: Store your business details once in Open Publisher and instantly generate auto-populated letterheads, business cards, and signature blocks across any document.
content:
Business Information
The Business Information feature lets you store your core business details once and then instantly generate pre-formatted, auto-populated templates across your documents - no retyping required.
Setting Up Your Business Information
To set up your Business Information:
Go to Insert > Business Information (or Insert > Business Card / Letterhead ).
The Business Information dialog opens.
Fill in the fields: Name , Job Title , Organisation , Address , Contact Info , Tagline , and Logo URL .
Click Save . Your details are stored securely in your browser’s LocalStorage and will be available every time you open Open Publisher.
Using Your Business Information
From the Insert ribbon, open the Business Information dropdown and choose from three ready-made templates, each auto-populated with your stored details:
Letterhead - A formatted header block for professional correspondence, auto-populated with your name, company, and contact details.
Business Card - A compact, formatted business card layout pre-filled with all your stored information and logo.
Signature - A compact email or document signature block.
Each template is inserted as a fully editable group on the canvas, positioned and sized for immediate use.

title: Coupon Templates
excerpt: Insert and customise 12 professionally designed coupon templates in Open Publisher, including gift vouchers, raffle tickets, event tickets, loyalty cards and more.
content:
Coupon Templates
Open Publisher includes a dedicated suite of marketing and promotional tools accessible from the Insert ribbon, all designed to produce print-ready content that renders perfectly in PDF and physical print output. The Coupon insertion tool provides a library of 12 distinct, fully designed templates in a compact 3-column gallery.
Inserting a Coupon
To insert a coupon:
Go to Insert > Coupon .
The Coupon gallery opens showing all 12 template options.
Click a template to insert it onto the canvas.
Edit the text, prices, and details by clicking into the text blocks.
Available Templates
Buy 1 Get 1 Free (BOGO) - Uses custom high-density PNG barcode rendering.
Gift Voucher - Classic bordered certificate style.
Flash Sale - High-contrast, attention-grabbing block for urgent promotions.
Loyalty Card - “Buy 4 Get 1 Free” graphical punch card.
VIP Pass - Elegant gold and black styling for premium admissions.
Free Drink - Warm, coffee-shop aesthetic.
Promo Code - Clean blue e-commerce style discount block.
Event Ticket - Realistic rotated stub design, engineered with native HTML tables to prevent structural collapse during print rendering.
Store Credit - Simple, high-visibility cash value voucher.
Raffle Ticket - Split-design ticket with a perforated-style tear-off section.
Barcode Print Safety
All barcode generation in coupon templates bypasses CSS structural layouts entirely. Barcodes are drawn to an off-screen HTML5 Canvas and exported as a single flat PNG, preventing print engines from stripping backgrounds or shifting elements during PDF export.

title: Direct Mail & Postcard Layout Design Standards
excerpt: Create postal-compliant direct mailers, postcards, and EDDM promotional layouts with postal clearance zones, barcode clearings, and address blocks.
content:
Direct Mail & Postcard Layout Design Standards
Direct mail marketing (including standard promotional postcards, oversized announcement mailers, and Every Door Direct Mail [EDDM] circulars) remains a powerful promotional channel for businesses, non-profits, and event organizers. However, postal authorities (including the United States Postal Service, Royal Mail, and Deutsche Post) enforce stringent dimensional standards, address block placements, and barcode keep-out zones. Failing to respect these parameters can result in surcharge penalties or rejected mail runs. Open Publisher provides built-in postal templates and non-printing alignment guides to guarantee full postal compliance.
📮 Postcard Layout with Postal Clearance Zones & Barcode Blocks
Ensure postal compliance with automated address block clearing, barcode keep-out zones, and bleed guides.
Postal Dimensional Presets
Open Publisher includes standardized presets tailored for postal automated sorting machines:
Standard Postcard (4.0 x 6.0 in): Qualifies for lowest first-class postcard rates.
Oversized / Continental (5.0 x 7.0 in & 6.0 x 9.0 in): Maximizes visual impact while qualifying for standard letter postal processing.
EDDM Flats (6.5 x 9.0 in & 8.5 x 11.0 in): Formatted specifically for Every Door Direct Mail saturation marketing routes.
Automated Clearance & Barcode Keep-Out Zones
Enabling postal guides reveals mandatory clear zones on the reverse spread:
Barcode Clear Zone: Displays a 5/8-inch non-printing strip along the bottom edge where optical sorting machines apply the barcode.
Address Block Bounding Box: Ensures the recipient address box is positioned with required clearance from edges and postage indicia.
Postage Indicia Frame: Marks exact coordinates for postal permit imprints or stamp cancellation boxes.
Prepress Export for Commercial Print Houses
When completing your postcard design, Open Publisher's export pipeline packages the document with 0.125-inch (3mm) bleed margins and optional crop marks, ensuring commercial print shops can trim finished cards cleanly without unsightly white borders.
Tip: Turn on 'Show Postal Guides' in the Page Design tab to display non-printing address and barcode keep-out boundaries while designing.

title: Promotional Badge Studio & Modern Vector Advertisement Engine
excerpt: Create eye-catching promotional badges, starbursts, discount seals, and sales tags with OpenPublisher 50-preset vector library and Badge Studio modal.
content:
Promotional Badge Studio: Vector Advertisement & Sales Callout Engine
Adding attention-grabbing sales stickers, clearance bursts, discount percentages, and promotional ribbons is essential for high-converting marketing flyers and store signage. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.19.1 , the Promotional Badge Studio brings a full vector advertisement engine directly into your workspace: featuring an interactive design modal, 50 professional vector presets, real-time typography scaling, and canvas green margin text positioning.
The Promotional Badge Studio modal in OpenPublisher v5.19.1, showcasing live typography preview and 50 vector presets.
Lossless Vector Geometry: Every badge created in the studio is built as native SVG vector geometry. You can scale badges from a tiny 1-inch product sticker to a huge 4-foot promotional window banner with crisp edges and perfect vector print output.
50-Preset Vector Badge Library
The studio categorizes 50 versatile vector badge templates across six popular marketing applications:
Starbursts & Explosions
Dynamic 8-point, 16-point, and 24-point starburst contours designed for urgent callouts like "HUGE SALE!", "NEW!", and "FLASH DEAL!".
Ribbon Banners & Sashes
Folded 3D ribbons with tails, corner diagonal sashes, and curved header banners perfect for book covers and product badges.
Discount Seals & Percent Off
Circular and scalloped discount medals highlighting percentages ("50% OFF", "BUY 1 GET 1 FREE", "SAVE $20").
Quality Guarantee & Seals
Notched wax seals, golden warranty medals, and certified organic rosettes that establish trust and credibility on product packaging.
Inside the Badge Studio Modal
You can launch the studio anytime by navigating to Insert > Promotional Badge from the top ribbon menu. The studio interface provides instant live-preview tools:
Dual-Line Typography Inputs: Dedicated fields for primary headline text (e.g., "50% OFF") and supporting secondary subtext (e.g., "THIS WEEKEND ONLY").
Real-Time Font Scaling: As you type longer phrases, the text scaling algorithm automatically calculates the optimal point size to fill the badge center without overflowing the boundary.
Canvas Green Margin Positioning Guard: A smart bounding guard that ensures text stays comfortably within the safe inner contour of complex starburst or ribbon shapes, preventing jagged point intersections.
Gradient & Solid Fill Studios: Choose from preset color palettes (Crimson Sale, Gold Luxury, Vibrant Electric, Emerald Fresh) or customize each stop of the linear or radial gradient.
Drop Shadow & Glow Sliders: Give the badge separation from busy photographic backgrounds with adjustable soft shadows or luminous outer highlights.
Editing Badges on the Canvas
Once inserted onto your canvas, the badge functions as a grouped smart object. You can freely drag, scale, or rotate the entire badge. If you wish to edit individual components, right-click the badge and choose Ungroup , allowing you to tweak individual vector paths, change text content, or alter stroke weights independently.

- Generating Scalable Vector QR Codes
- Working with Vector Shapes & Callouts

title: Publication Templates
excerpt: Browse and open professionally designed publication templates in Open Publisher for newsletters, flyers, brochures, menus and more, ready to fill with your content.
content:
Publication Templates
The Publication Templates library provides full-page, professionally designed starting points for common publication types - newsletters, flyers, brochures, menus, and more. Templates open as complete documents, ready for your content.
Using a Template
To open a publication template:
Go to File > New , or click New in the File ribbon tab.
Browse the template gallery.
Double-click a template to open it.
Smart Template Behaviour
If you open a template while on a new blank page, Open Publisher adds the template layout to your current page rather than replacing the whole document. This lets you mix and match layouts within a single publication.
Note: Loading a template replaces the content of your currently selected page only - not the entire document.

title: QR Code Generator
excerpt: Generate fully customised QR codes in Open Publisher with rounded or circular styles, custom colours, and a canvas bake method that guarantees perfect PDF output.
content:
QR Code Generator
The QR Code Generator lets you create fully customised, print-safe QR codes that point to any URL, text, or contact information, directly from the Insert ribbon.
Inserting a QR Code
To insert a QR code:
Go to Insert > QR Code .
Enter the URL or text content for the QR code.
Customise the appearance using the options below.
Click Insert to place the QR code on the canvas.
Customisation Options
Foreground Colour - Dynamic colour picker for the QR code pattern colour.
Background Fill - Dynamic colour picker for the QR code background.
Standard - Default square QR code.
Rounded Corners - QR code with softly rounded module corners.
Circular Badge - QR code masked into a perfect circle.
Print-Safe Canvas Bake Method
WebKit-based print engines (Chrome, Safari, and Edge) have a long-standing bug where CSS border-radius and clip-path shapes applied to images are ignored during printing, causing circular or rounded QR codes to revert to plain squares in your PDF.
To bypass this, Open Publisher uses a Canvas Bake Method every time a QR code is exported:
The generator fetches the raw QR image and draws it to an invisible canvas.
It physically cuts out the transparent corners pixel-by-pixel.
A visible boundary border is drawn around the result.
The final output is exported as a flat PNG with pre-cut transparent corners already baked in.
The print engine receives a standard flat image, guaranteeing perfect shape retention for rounded and circular QR codes in every PDF and print output - with no manual action required.

title: 700 Themes Expansion & Fine Tactile Textures Catalog
excerpt: Explore Open Publisher
content:
700 Themes Expansion & Fine Tactile Textures Catalog
Professional publications (such as heritage books, event programs, corporate diplomas, and product catalogs) require authentic, tactile paper foundations rather than generic digital gradients. Version 5.4.2 marked a massive milestone for Open Publisher, expanding the Theme Studio library to 700 curated, production-ready themes. The centerpiece of this expansion is a 366% increase in the Fine Papers, Fabrics & Materials category, providing 280 tactile textures audited for zero duplicate entries.
📜 700-Theme Studio Popover with 280 Fine Papers & Materials
The catalog popover displays 280 tactile textures, from archival vellums to woven fabrics, with real-time search filtering.
280 Fine Papers, Fabrics & Architectural Materials
Textured materials now comprise 40% of the entire Theme Studio library, pairing verified transparent PNG patterns with authentic base paper tones:
Archival Papers & Vellums: Chancellor Diploma Vellum, Museum Rag Matboard, Hand-Pressed Kozo Paper, Scriptorium Calfskin, Double-Entry Ledger Sheet, and Antiquarian Vellum.
Bespoke Fabrics & Suiting: Raw Belgian Flax Linen, Savile Row Pinstripe Wool, Highland Tweed, Lustrous Silk Sateen, Royal Fleet Serge, and Raw Selvedge Denim.
Plasters & Masonry: Venetian Plaster, Carrara Marble Dust, Honed Roman Travertine, Whitewashed Loft Brick, Tuscan Terracotta, and Welsh Blue Slate.
Fine Leathers & Exotic Woods: Shell Cordovan Polish, Tuscan Saddle Leather, Macassar Ebony Veneer, Crown Walnut, and Yacht Bleached Teak.
Technical & Drafting Surfaces: Cartesian Math Grid, Canary Legal Pad, Blueprint Grid, Isometric Cube Relief, and Anechoic Studio Wedge.
Balanced 700-Theme Architecture across 5 Categories
The complete 700-theme library is organized across five distinct categories with zero duplicate IDs or display names:
Fine Papers, Fabrics & Materials (280 themes): Tactile papers, woven textiles, stone plasters, natural woods, and architectural surfaces.
Modern & Vibrant Gradients (105 themes): High-energy color transitions, cyber neons, sunset glows, and oceanic auroras.
Corporate, Legal & Editorial (105 themes): Dignified slates, parchment washes, ivory stationery, and international chancery tints.
Dark Mode & Luxury (105 themes): Smoked titanite, obsidian gold, midnight velvet, gothic plum, and matte noir foundations.
Soft Pastels & Earthy Naturals (105 themes): Sage matcha, blush rose, terracotta clay, chamomile cream, and coastal fog tones.
High-Performance Auditioning & Print Parity
All 700 themes integrate seamlessly with Open Publisher's performance engines:
Pin-Open Auditioning: Clicking swatches in the catalog popover updates the canvas instantly without closing the menu, letting you test dozens of paper textures in seconds.
Full 6-Slider Control: Adjust Pattern Zoom (25% to 300%) to scale the texture grain, and tune Texture Opacity, Contrast, Brightness, Saturation, or Hue Shift.
Canvas 2D Print Pre-Baking: Renders texture tiles onto an offscreen canvas at 2x resolution, guaranteeing 100% identical output on physical presses and PDF exports.
Tip: Type keywords like "linen", "vellum", or "grid" into the popover search box to instantly find the ideal paper texture for your project.

title: Auto-Reset Hue Shift & Modular Theme Studio Engine
excerpt: Ensure swatch-to-canvas visual parity with automatic hue shift resets and explore Open Publisher
content:
Auto-Reset Hue Shift & Modular Theme Studio Engine
When exploring background themes in digital publishing, designers rely on catalog swatches to accurately predict what will appear on the canvas. Following the introduction of the 360-degree Hue Shift slider in version 5.4.1, an unexpected usability issue arose: when users changed themes after shifting hue, the new theme inherited the previous theme's rotated colors, causing unexpected mismatches between the preview card and the canvas. Version 5.4.3 introduced an automated hue reset hook upon theme selection and decoupled the entire Theme Studio subsystem into a clean, dedicated engine.
🎯 Auto-Reset Hue Shift to 0° on Theme Selection
Selecting any theme swatch automatically resets the Hue Shift slider to 0°, guaranteeing that the canvas matches the catalog preview.
The Hue Distortion Carryover Problem
Investigation into user workflows revealed the source of the preview discrepancy:
Persistent Hue Carryover: If a designer rotated the Hue Shift slider by 180 degrees while testing a theme, subsequent clicks on other themes preserved that 180-degree rotation.
Swatch-to-Canvas Mismatch: Clicking a classic navy theme caused it to appear as bright amber on the canvas; clicking crimson rendered as cyan. Users were confused by why themes did not match their catalog preview cards.
The Auto-Reset Lifecycle Hook
Version 5.4.3 added an automatic hue reset hook inside applyThemeToCanvas() :
Instant Slider Reset: When any theme swatch is clicked, #ts-hue-slider resets to 0 , the badge updates to 0° , and the track progress gradient resets to 0%.
Exact Visual Parity: The canvas immediately renders the authentic base palette of the selected theme, ensuring 100% visual parity with the catalog card.
Intentional Shifting Preserved: The reset fires only on new swatch clicks. Once a theme is loaded, users can adjust the Hue Shift slider freely, and saved files with custom hue rotations continue to reload accurately.
Modular Architecture: `extensions/theme-studio.js`
Historically, the Theme Studio lived inside extensions/legacy-fixes.js . Successive feature additions expanded that file to nearly 10,000 lines. Version 5.4.3 extracted the entire Theme Studio into its own dedicated module:
Dedicated Engine: The entire 7,420-line Theme Studio subsystem now resides in extensions/theme-studio.js , containing the 700-theme catalog, 6-slider suite, and Canvas 2D raster print baking engine.
Streamlined Legacy Code: Shrunk legacy-fixes.js back to its intended scope (~2,380 lines), improving maintainability and code clarity.
Tip: You can quickly restore any altered theme parameter (including Saturation, Brightness, or Contrast) to default by clicking its pill badge above the slider.

title: 6-Slider Dual-Column Background Suite & Pattern Controls
excerpt: Fine-tune publication backgrounds with Open Publisher
content:
6-Slider Dual-Column Background Suite & Pattern Controls
Setting the perfect background ambiance for a document often requires nuanced adjustments: softening a vibrant gradient, boosting contrast on textured paper, or scaling the weave of a canvas pattern. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, background adjustment sliders were non-functional placeholders because CSS filters on DOM containers vanished during print rasterization. Version 5.4.1 debuted the feature-rich 6-Slider Dual-Column Background Adjustment Suite in the Theme Studio, paired with an offscreen Canvas 2D raster pre-baking engine that guarantees 100% physical print fidelity.
🎛️ Symmetrical Dual-Column 6-Slider Background Adjustment Suite
The Theme Studio ribbon features six dedicated sliders for color tone, 360-degree hue rotation, and pattern scaling.
The Symmetrical Dual-Column Control Suite
Fitting six precise controls into the ribbon without vertical crowding required a balanced two-column architecture:
Column 1 (Color & Tone): Contains Saturation (0% to 200%), Brightness (50% to 150%), and Contrast (50% to 150%). Boosting contrast deepens shadows and sharpens texture definition, while reducing contrast produces delicate pastel tones.
Column 2 (Effects & Patterns): Features Hue Shift (0° to 360°), Texture Opacity (0% to 100%), and Pattern Zoom (25% to 300%). Rotating the hue shift slider transforms a navy theme into emerald, amethyst, amber, or ruby with zero distortion.
Interactive Click-to-Reset Badges: Each slider includes a pill badge showing exact numeric values. Clicking any badge instantly resets that specific parameter to its default setting (100% or 0°).
Context-Aware Disabling: When a flat gradient is active, Texture Opacity and Pattern Zoom gracefully dim with "None" badges, reactivating instantly when a textured theme is selected.
Natural Pattern Zoom & Scaling
Repeating background patterns previously suffered from rigid tile sizes. The pattern zoom engine calculates scaling relative to intrinsic image dimensions:
Natural Dimension Preloading: When a textured theme is selected, the engine preloads the image to capture its natural width and height ( naturalWidth , naturalHeight ).
Proportional Pixel Scaling: Scrubbing Pattern Zoom scales background-size smoothly in real pixels ( baseW * (size / 100) ), allowing users to expand fine weaves into bold textures or shrink coarse grids into subtle paper grain.
Universal Canvas 2D Raster Print Baking
Because browser print engines and html2canvas ignore CSS filters applied to DOM elements, Open Publisher implements an offscreen Canvas 2D rasterizer in extensions/print-engine.js :
2x Print Resolution Rendering: Renders solid fills, linear gradients, and pre-tiled textures onto an offscreen canvas at twice the display resolution.
Hardware Context Filtering: Applies composite context filters ( saturate , brightness , contrast , hue-rotate ) directly onto the canvas pixels.
100% Physical Parity: Injects the pre-baked background raster directly into the print spooler, guaranteeing that adjusted tones and pattern sizes export to PDF and paper exactly as previewed on screen.
Tip: All six adjustment settings are automatically saved in your .opub publication file and restore smoothly when reopening documents.

title: Ignore Theme Toggle & Master Theme Restoration Engine
excerpt: Override document themes with a bidirectional ribbon toggle, preventing accidental theme lockout with auto-resets and multi-page synchronization.
content:
Ignore Theme Toggle & Master Theme Restoration Engine
Multi-page publications such as magazines, newsletters, and catalogs often feature custom cover designs or stark white photo spreads that should not share the universal background applied to the rest of the document. In earlier versions, clicking "Ignore Theme" was an irreversible one-way action that permanently locked that page out from receiving themes again. Version 5.3.5 transformed "Ignore Theme" into a fully reactive, bidirectional toggle button with active ribbon feedback, smart auto-resets, and instantaneous master theme recovery.
🎨 Bidirectional Ignore Theme Ribbon Toggle & State Indicator
The Ignore Theme button highlights with active ribbon styling when engaged, and clicking again restores the document theme.
The One-Way Lockout Flaw
Auditing the legacy Page Design ribbon revealed why users experienced theme lockouts:
Permanent Flag Assignment: The original routine assigned ignoreBackground = true to the page without providing any toggle back to false.
Watchdog Deletion: The background self-healing engine monitored pages and automatically removed newly selected themes if the ignore flag was set, making the theme picker appear broken.
Ribbon Tab Jumping: Restoring theme containers created new element wrappers that stole focus and jumped the user away from the Page Design tab.
The Bidirectional Toggle Architecture
Version 5.3.5 implemented an intuitive, reactive toggle system in ui/themes.js and extensions/legacy-fixes.js :
Bidirectional Toggling: window.toggleIgnoreTheme() toggles the override cleanly. Clicking once clears the background to clean white and activates the button; clicking again turns the override off and restores the document's master theme immediately.
Reactive Ribbon Styling: When active, #no-bg-btn highlights with an accent tint, theme border, and an updated tooltip ( Theme Ignored on this page (Click to re-enable) ).
Smart Auto-Reset on Swatch Selection: Clicking any Theme Studio swatch or color palette automatically clears the ignore flag and applies the new theme immediately without watchdog interference.
Ribbon Tab Anchoring: Theme reconstruction mutes tab switches temporarily, keeping the user smoothly anchored on the Page Design ribbon tab.
Per-Page Synchronization: Switching pages dynamically updates the button state to reflect whether that specific page is ignoring themes or displaying one.
Tip: Use Ignore Theme on cover pages and back covers to create clean, untextured title spreads while preserving consistent themes across interior pages.

title: Page Borders
excerpt: Learn how to apply and customise scalable, vector-based SVG page borders in Open Publisher. Choose from 100 styles with adjustable colours and thickness.
content:
Page Borders
Open Publisher includes a library of 100 unique decorative page border styles, all drawn using scalable mathematical SVG paths. Because they are vector-based rather than CSS approximations, they scale proportionally to any document size without loss of quality, and they support custom colours and thickness.
How to Apply a Border
The Borders tool is accessible from two locations in the ribbon:
Page Design tab.
Insert tab (under Graphics).
Click the Borders button to open a scrollable dropdown menu featuring:
Category
Examples
Classic & Technical
Solid, Dashed, Blueprint, Pinstripe, Barcode.
Geometric Corners
Plaque, Ticket, Diamond, Target, Octagon.
Layered & 3D
Outset, Groove, Echo, Neon.
Craft & Deco
Filmstrip, Double-Stitch, Photo-Corners, Art Deco.
Customisation options in the dropdown:
10-colour quick-select palette for instant colour changes.
Custom hex colour picker for any specific colour.
Thickness slider to dial in precise pixel weights.
The dropdown renders an accurate 1:1 scaled preview of each border style (using the exact same SVG math used on the actual page, scaled down proportionally to a small card), so you know exactly what you will get before applying it.
Border Behaviour
Once applied, a border is permanently anchored to the background of your page with pointer-events: none applied, meaning it cannot be accidentally dragged or selected while you work on your design. It is fully print-safe and will appear correctly in all export formats.

title: Per-Page Individual Themes & Multi-Page Customization Persistence
excerpt: Give every page its own unique background, palette, and 6-slider adjustments with Open Publisher
content:
Per-Page Individual Themes & Multi-Page Customization Persistence
Multi-page publications (such as corporate brochures, event catalogs, annual reports, and newsletters) often demand distinct visual atmospheres across different sections: a dark textured cover page, an ivory editorial preface, vibrant content spreads, and clean unthemed body pages. Prior to version 5.5.3, background themes operated as document-wide settings that updated every page uniformly. Version 5.5.3 overhauled the Theme Studio architecture to introduce Per-Page Individual Themes, allowing every page to possess its own independent background theme, custom palette, and 6-slider adjustments with full .opub persistence.
🎨 Multi-Page Document Featuring Distinct Per-Page Themes
Page 1 displays a rich textured background while Page 2 remains clean and unthemed.
Independent Theme Selection & Slider Scoping
Themes and adjustments are decoupled from global document state and attached directly to individual page data structures:
Independent Page Application: Choosing a theme from the Page Design ribbon or Theme Studio popover applies strictly to the currently viewed page without affecting other pages.
Individual Slider Profiles: Adjusting Hue Shift, Saturation, Brightness, Contrast, Texture Opacity, or Pattern Zoom modifies only the active page. Navigating between pages automatically updates the ribbon sliders, badges, and gradient tracks to reflect that specific page's settings.
Unthemed Isolation: Pages can remain completely unthemed or have "Ignore Background" toggled. Unthemed pages display a crisp white canvas with Theme Studio sliders automatically reset to default values.
Robust .opub File Metadata Persistence
Every page's unique theme configuration is serialized into the document file format under docData.pages[i].themeSettings :
Complete Parameter Serialization: Stores theme ID, display name, background fill colors ( c1 , c2 ), texture asset URL, and all six numeric slider values ( sat , bri , con , hue , tex , size ).
Strict Definedness Verification: Uses strict definedness checks ( !== undefined ) so zero-degree hue shifts and 100% default values are never stripped or converted to falsy defaults.
Legacy Migration: Opening older publications safely converts document-level theme metadata into page-level settings without overwriting individual page customizations.
Synchronous Page Rendering & Zero Visual Flash
Earlier versions experienced a momentary 500ms flash where the canvas reverted to unadjusted colors during page transitions. Version 5.5.3 moved theme reconstruction to execute synchronously at the end of renderPage() , applying computed CSS filters immediately and delivering seamless, flash-free page switching.
Tip: You can design a dark front cover, light interior pages, and a patterned back cover all within the same publication file.

title: Theme Studio 300-Theme Overhaul & Lighter Teal Catalog Navigation
excerpt: Transform publication backgrounds with Open Publisher
content:

title: Theme Studio & Backgrounds
excerpt: Use the Open Publisher Theme Studio to apply document-wide colour schemes and background textures. Learn how to format individual backgrounds and exempt pages.
content:
Theme Studio & Backgrounds
The Theme Studio is Open Publisher’s document-wide design system, accessible from the Page Design ribbon tab. It lets you apply consistent visual styling - colour schemes and background textures - across your entire publication with a single click.
Colour Schemes
Open Publisher ships with a curated set of colour palette presets:
Classic - clean, traditional publishing tones.
Pastel - soft, muted hues for a gentle aesthetic.
Neon - vivid, high-energy accent colours.
Corporate - professional, restrained blues and greys.
When a colour scheme is active, shapes, text elements, and other design objects dynamically respond by automatically updating their fills and strokes to match the active document colour language. The active scheme is highlighted in the ribbon so it is immediately obvious which palette is currently applied.
Page Background Themes
Alongside colour schemes, the Theme Studio provides a library of page background themes - solid colours, gradients, and textured patterns - that can be applied to the entire document backdrop. Simply click any swatch in the Theme Studio panel to apply it instantly.
Background themes are applied via a dedicated background layer that sits beneath all your content. Your selected theme is saved into your .opub file and loads automatically when you re-open the document. Backgrounds applied through the Theme Studio render correctly in all export formats, including booklet printing with accurate gradient reproduction.
Tip: If you need more precise control over individual background colours or want to apply a custom solid colour, use the Format Background dialog (see below).
Format Background Dialog
For direct, one-off background colour control on the current page, use the Format Background dialog. Access it by:
Right-clicking anywhere on the page canvas and selecting Format Background .
Using the workspace context menu or the ribbon.
The redesigned dialog features the application’s signature dark-teal header, cleanly styled radio buttons for selecting background type (solid colour, gradient), custom colour inputs, and a tip box directing you to the Theme Studio for advanced textures and patterns.
Gradients applied via Format Background render correctly in all print modes, including Booklet printing.
Ignoring the Theme Background on Specific Pages
Separately from the Master Page elements, Open Publisher’s Theme Studio can apply a decorative background to all pages simultaneously. If you need a single page (such as a back cover or a blank insert) to have a white/plain background while the rest of the document keeps its theme background, use the Ignore Theme feature.
To exempt a page from the theme background:
Navigate to the page you want to exempt.
Open the Theme Studio ribbon (under Page Design).
Click the Ignore Theme button (displayed with a teal cancel icon, next to the Remove Theme button).
The background on that page immediately turns white. All other pages retain their theme background intact. This override is fully supported in the standard print engine, the booklet imposition engine, and the PDF export pipeline.

title: Theme Studio Ribbon Expansion & Pin-Open Popover Auditioning
excerpt: Audition publication aesthetics in real time with an 8-column ribbon gallery, pin-open catalog popover, and 120 curated themes.
content:
Theme Studio Ribbon Expansion & Pin-Open Popover Auditioning
Choosing the visual foundation for a publication involves testing multiple color schemes, gradients, and paper textures against existing text boxes, tables, and images. Prior to version 5.3.6, the Theme Studio dropdown closed immediately whenever a swatch was clicked, forcing designers to reopen the menu dozens of times during creative exploration. Version 5.3.6 introduced persistent pin-open auditioning, expanded the ribbon preview strip to an 8-column layout, and grew the curated library to 120 unique themes.
✨ Pin-Open Theme Auditioning & 8-Column Ribbon Strip
The Theme Studio catalog popover stays open as you click swatches, updating your canvas in real time for effortless auditioning.
Expanded 8-Column Ribbon Gallery
The ribbon gallery container was expanded to provide significantly more immediate choices without taking over the ribbon bar:
16 Simultaneous Swatches: The viewport was widened to 194px (216px total container), displaying an 8-column by 2-row grid of miniature 20px portrait cards (a 60% increase in visible swatches).
Row-by-Row Navigation: Vertical scroll buttons move the strip smoothly in 28px increments, navigating complete rows without cutting off swatches.
Signature Styling: Framed with Open Publisher's 1px teal border and solid action box controls.
Persistent Pin-Open Auditioning
Clicking "More Themes" opens the full Theme Studio catalog popover with live auditioning:
Real-Time Canvas Updates: Clicking any theme swatch applies it to the canvas immediately and synchronizes the active selection highlight without closing the popover.
Frictionless Exploration: Designers can audition dozens of aesthetics consecutively to observe how typography, borders, and charts blend with background tones.
Graceful Dismissal: The popover closes only when you click outside the menu, click the close button ( ✕ ), or press Escape .
120 Curated Themes with Zero Overlaps
The authentic theme library was expanded to 120 production-ready options, thoroughly vetted for unique IDs and color signatures:

Corporate, Legal & Editorial (22 themes): Executive Slate, Oxford Blue, Legal Ivory, Warm Parchment, Nordic Frost, and Manhattan Granite.
