Tip: You can type keywords into the search box at the top of the popover to instantly filter themes across all categories.

title: Creating Master Pages
excerpt: Learn how to create and edit Master Pages in Open Publisher. Add repeating headers and footers, use the quick toggle, and hide master elements on specific pages.
content:
Understanding & Creating Master Pages
A Master Page is a special, dedicated layout layer that sits behind every page in your document. Any element you place on the Master Page - such as a header, a footer, a company logo, a watermark, a decorative border, or a background image - will automatically appear as a non-editable, ghosted background on every subsequent regular page. This eliminates the need to manually copy elements to every page in long publications.
This system is modelled directly on the Master Page concept in Microsoft Publisher and is particularly powerful for:
Company letterheads.
Branded newsletter or magazine templates.
Reports with consistent headers and footers.
Any publication requiring a repeating design element across all pages.
Master Page elements are integrated into every output pathway: standard printing, saddle-stitch booklet printing, PDF export, and HTML export all respect and render Master Page content correctly.
Creating a Master Page
In the left-hand Navigation Pane sidebar, locate the Add Master Page button and click it. This initialises a new Master Page (Page 0) and switches your canvas to it automatically.
You are now editing the Master Page. Design your repeating elements here - add a logo image, draw a header background, insert a footer text box, or place any element you want to appear on every page.
When you are finished, click the Master button in the sidebar (or navigate to any regular page) to return to your normal document pages.
Note: Elements on the Master Page appear on regular pages with pointer-events: none applied, meaning they are permanently in the background and cannot be accidentally selected, moved, or edited from a regular page.
Navigating to the Master Page - The Double-Click Quick Toggle
In addition to using the sidebar button, you can jump directly to the Master Page using a quick double-click gesture on the canvas edge. This is the fastest way to make small header or footer adjustments while deep in your layout work.
Double-click anywhere within the top 100 pixels (the header area) of a regular page canvas to instantly jump to the Master Page and place your cursor in the header.
Double-click anywhere within the bottom 100 pixels (the footer area) to jump to the Master Page and focus in the footer.
Open Publisher is context-aware about this behaviour:
Confirmation dialog: If you double-click the header or footer area of a standard page, a dialog appears asking: “You double-clicked the header/footer area. Would you like to jump to the Master Page to edit the template for all pages?”. Click OK to jump, or Cancel to dismiss with no change.
Smart detection: If you are already editing the Master Page, the system detects this and steps aside - your native browser text-selection behaviour (double-click to select a word, triple-click to select a paragraph) works flawlessly without the toggle intercepting it.
Element avoidance: If you double-click near the edge but directly on an existing design element (a text box, shape, etc.), the toggle ignores the click and lets the element receive the event normally.
Zoom compensation: The detection engine automatically compensates for your current zoom level, so the 100px detection zone remains accurate regardless of how far in or out you are zoomed.
Ignoring the Master Page on Specific Pages
Sometimes a publication requires a specific page - such as a full-bleed cover, a blank divider, or an alternate layout - to be completely free of Master Page elements while all other pages retain them.
To hide the Master Page on a specific page:
Right-click the page thumbnail in the Navigation Pane for the page you want to exempt.
Hover over Master Pages in the context menu.
Select None (Hide) .
The Master Page elements immediately disappear from that page’s canvas. All other pages are completely unaffected. This setting is serialised into the .opub file, so it persists across saves and reloads. It is also fully respected by all export pipelines - Print, Booklet Print, PDF, and HTML will all correctly omit the Master Page layer from exempted pages.
Automatic Dimension Inheritance & Non-Default Page Sync (v5.19.5)
In earlier editions, changing a document page dimensions (for instance, converting an A4 portrait publication to US Letter or a custom square brochure) could leave Master Page layers configured to previous dimensions. OpenPublisher v5.19.5 introduces Dynamic Master Page Dimension Inheritance :
Automatic Master Page dimension and orientation synchronization in OpenPublisher v5.19.5.
Real-Time Dimension Propagation: Whenever you change page dimensions or switch between portrait and landscape in Page Setup , the Master Page canvas coordinates, perimeter margins, and background plates adapt instantly.
Non-Default Formats: Custom millimeters or inch dimensions (such as tabloid spreads, tri-fold cards, or greeting folds) propagate seamlessly without requiring manual master page geometry edits.
Undo/Redo Displacement Fix & Safe Master Detachment (v5.19.3)
Precision layout design requires reliable history tracking. In OpenPublisher v5.19.3 , the undo/redo engine received targeted stabilization:
Master Page undo displacement fix and safe detachment controls in OpenPublisher v5.19.3.
Pressing Ctrl + Z or Ctrl + Y while editing body pages now strictly isolates foreground actions without causing master headers or footers to shift out of alignment. Furthermore, a dedicated Remove from Master Page ribbon command allows designers to safely unbind master layers from specific individual pages without disturbing document-wide master rules.

title: High-DPI Paper Format & Resolution Persistence Architecture
excerpt: Ensure publications saved at 300 DPI retain their exact paper format presets and resolution across file loads and recent document cards in Open Publisher.
content:
High-DPI Paper Format & Resolution Persistence Architecture
In version 5.1.6, Open Publisher established an authoritative format and DPI contract across all layers of the application. In earlier releases, publications configured with high-DPI resolutions (such as A4 or Letter at 300 DPI) were incorrectly identified as "Custom" page sizes when reloaded from disk, and the status bar resolution badge reverted to 96 DPI. Version 5.1.6 guarantees permanent resolution retention across document saves, recent file cards, template loading, and multi-page creation.
💾 High-DPI Publication Format & DPI Persistence Verification
A 300 DPI A4 publication permanently retains its paper preset badge and 300 DPI resolution across saves and reloads.
Authoritative Schema Contract
Resolution loss was resolved by storing explicit format and DPI attributes in publication schemas:
Document & Page Serialization: Both serializeCurrentPage() in core/history.js and saveDocument() now record explicit docData.format , docData.dpi , page.format , and page.dpi properties.
Eliminating Reverse-Engineering Traps: Previously, file loaders attempted to deduce paper size by comparing raw pixel dimensions against 96 DPI presets. A 300 DPI A4 page (2480 x 3508 px) evaluated to over 2 feet wide at 96 DPI, triggering fallback to "Custom". Storing the explicit format string eliminates this guesswork.
History Preservation: Undo and redo snapshots preserve format and DPI, ensuring that resizing operations can be reversed cleanly.
Physical Unit Conversion & Dynamic Tolerance
Mathematical calculations in core/units.js were audited and upgraded:
Millimeter Conversion Precision: Fixed the formula in UnitConversionService.toPixels to divide by 25.4 rather than 2.54 , eliminating a factor-of-10 error in millimeter format checks.
Resolution-Aware Detection Tolerance: Preset format detection dynamically scales its pixel tolerance as Math.max(16, d * 0.08) . This absorbs sub-pixel rounding variances that occur at 300 DPI, reliably identifying A4 and Letter dimensions.
DPI Priority Matching: The format classifier tests against the document's active DPI first before evaluating candidate fallback resolutions.
Dashboard Recent Files & Multi-Page Inheritance
Full state restoration extends across all startup workflows:
Recent Documents Restoration: Clicking recent publication cards in the Startup Dashboard restores full document metadata including state.dpi , state.format , and measurement units, immediately synchronizing the bottom status bar and Ribbon format icon.
Multi-Page DPI Inheritance: Adding a new page via addNewPage() automatically inherits the active page's format and DPI, ensuring consistent resolution throughout multi-page booklets.
Interactive Change Size Dialog: Opening the resize dialog automatically pre-selects the document's current DPI, highlights the active preset button in teal, and recalculates dimensions dynamically upon DPI changes.
Important: If you have existing publications created in earlier versions, open them, confirm your desired format and DPI in the Change Size dialog, and re-save to permanently embed format metadata.

title: Managing Pages
excerpt: Learn how to add, duplicate, move, and delete pages in Open Publisher. Use custom page notes and auto page numbering to organise your document.
content:
Managing Pages
Open Publisher makes it easy to structure your document exactly as you need it, whether you are designing a single-page flyer or a multi-page booklet.
Adding Pages
New pages can be added to your document in several ways:
Click the Add Page button at the bottom of the left-hand Navigation Pane.
Right-click the blank grey area of the Navigation Pane and choose Insert Page from the context menu.
Right-click anywhere in the workspace background (outside the page canvas) and choose Add New Blank Page .
Duplicating, Moving, and Deleting Pages
Right-clicking on any page thumbnail in the Navigation Pane opens a context menu with the following page management options:
Duplicate Page - creates an exact copy of the selected page and inserts it directly after it.
Move Page Up / Move Page Down - shifts the page one position in the document order.
Delete Page - removes the page permanently.
Page Notes
For larger documents, it can be helpful to label individual pages so they are easy to identify without clicking into them. The Page Notes feature lets you attach a short custom identifier to any page.
Right-click a page thumbnail and select Add Note .
Type a short label (e.g., Front Cover , TOC , or Back Cover ).
The note appears directly beneath the page thumbnail in a bold, teal-coloured font.
Note: Page Notes are purely for your own organisational use within the editor; they do not affect printed output or exported files.
Auto Page Numbering
For longer documents, Open Publisher provides dynamic page numbering. Navigate to the Insert ribbon tab and click Page Number . An element is inserted that automatically displays the correct number and updates itself as you add, remove, or reorder pages in your document.

title: Permanent Page Orientation & Rotation Lock
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher locks page layout orientation with dual-layer .opub metadata, in-memory registry guards, and mixed-orientation support.
content:
Permanent Page Orientation & Rotation Lock
Multi-page publications frequently combine portrait text pages with wide landscape foldouts or technical tables. Open Publisher features a rock-solid page orientation architecture that permanently locks orientation across saves, template imports, and session restores without auto-rotation guessing.
🔄 Open Publisher Orientation Controls and Page Tags
Page orientation selector with explicit portrait and landscape metadata tags per publication page.
Dual-Layer Orientation Metadata
Orientation state is recorded explicitly at two architectural levels inside the .opub format:
Root-Level Document Tag: The top-level document manifest records the overall publication format ( "portrait" or "landscape" ) alongside spread mode and master page settings.
Per-Page Orientation Records: Each individual page object in the pages array stores its own independent "orientation" tag, enabling complete support for mixed-orientation publications.
In-Memory Registry Locking
In earlier versions, background helpers occasionally attempted to guess orientation by inspecting canvas contents (such as mistaking a wide banner on a portrait page for a landscape document). Open Publisher introduces an authoritative in-memory lock table ( window._orientedPagesRegistry ):
Hard Guards: Background intervals immediately check if a page has an explicit orientation tag; if present, the page ID is registered and auto-rotation is permanently bypassed.
Deep Cloning on Load: Opening publications from the Dashboard Start Screen or Recent Files performs deep page cloning and normalizes aspect ratios against explicit tags.
History Serialization: Every undo/redo snapshot captured by serializeCurrentPage() locks orientation, ensuring layout integrity across all revisions.
Note: You can switch a page's orientation at any time via Page Design → Orientation on the Ribbon.

title: Page Preview Bleed Prevention & Minimap Clipping
excerpt: Prevent sidebar thumbnail preview panels from bleeding behind the top ribbon bar using dynamic geometric clipping and z-index hardening in Open Publisher.
content:
Page Preview Bleed Prevention & Minimap Clipping
When working on multi-page publications containing dozens of pages, scrolling through the sidebar navigation pane is a frequent task. In version 5.1.3, Open Publisher resolved a visual layering issue where floating page preview frames and thumbnail outlines from the sidebar bled through and rendered behind the top Ribbon bar. This fix introduces dynamic geometric clipping and strict layer stacking across the application chrome.
🖼️ Sidebar Minimap Preview Cleanly Clipped at Ribbon Edge
Floating thumbnail preview panels are dynamically clipped at the top boundary of the sidebar, preventing bleed behind the Ribbon.
Root Cause: Fixed Overlays & Viewport Boundaries
The preview frame issue was located inside the Glass Vault Minimap subsystem in extensions/legacy-fixes.js :
Fixed Overlay Architecture: The enhanced thumbnail preview is rendered inside a position: fixed glass panel mounted to document.body . While the native thumbnail inside the sidebar was clipped by overflow-y: auto , the fixed overlay had no clipping boundary and continued rendering wherever its coordinates landed.
Static Header Stacking: The Ribbon container was previously position: static without an explicit z-index, allowing fixed overlay elements with positive indexes to render visibly on top of the ribbon background.
Dynamic Geometric Clipping with CSS Inset
The clipping engine in extensions/legacy-fixes.js now strictly confines preview panels to the sidebar viewport:
Dynamic Inset Clipping: In syncPositions() , #ts-overlay-wrapper dynamically calculates and applies a clip-path: inset(...) rule matching the exact bounding rectangle of #sidebar .
Boundary Enforcement: Any thumbnail preview panel that crosses above the sidebar's top dividing line (or below the bottom status bar) is cleanly and instantly cut off at the border.
Out-of-Bounds Suppression: Panels that scroll completely outside the visible sidebar area are immediately set to display: 'none' , saving GPU composite cycles.
Layer Stacking Hardening
The application chrome stylesheet ( style.css ) was updated with authoritative layer boundaries:
Title Bar: Configured with position: relative; z-index: 101; .
Ribbon Container: Configured with position: relative; z-index: 100; .
Status Bar: Configured with position: relative; z-index: 100; .
Overlay Panels: Normalized to z-index: 90 , guaranteeing they strictly render underneath all headers, ribbon tabs, and dialog modals.
Tip: Smooth 60fps scrolling performance is maintained across documents with 50+ pages.

title: Page Setup & Dimensions
excerpt: Learn how to configure page setup in Open Publisher. Easily adjust canvas dimensions, toggle orientation, and set custom safe-zone margins for perfect printing.
content:
Page Setup & Dimensions
Configuring your canvas correctly is the foundational step for any publication. Open Publisher provides robust controls for document sizing, margins, and orientation directly from the Page Design ribbon tab.
Page Size & Format
The Page Design ribbon tab houses the Size dropdown, which lets you instantly resize the entire canvas to standard international and regional formats:
Format
Dimensions
A3
297 x 420 mm
A4
210 x 297 mm (European/UK default)
A5
148 x 210 mm
Letter
8.5 x 11 in (US/Canada/Mexico default)
Legal
8.5 x 14 in
Tabloid
11 x 17 in
Business Card
3.5 x 2 in
Locale-Aware Defaults: When you create a new document, Open Publisher automatically selects the correct default size for your region. Users in the US, Canada, Mexico, Colombia, Venezuela, Chile, and the Philippines default to US Letter. Users everywhere else default to A4.
Each preset is represented by a unique icon in the dropdown, and the top-right corner of the canvas always displays the correct format indicator, which updates instantly whenever you change size.
Page Orientation
You can toggle between Portrait and Landscape directly from the Page Design tab. The print and PDF export engines handle mixed-orientation documents correctly, automatically rotating pages in the output to match what you designed.
Page Margins
The Margins button in the Page Design ribbon controls the safe-zone guides on the canvas. Clicking it opens a dropdown with five instant presets:
Preset
Margin Values
Normal
0.5 in on all sides
Narrow
0.25 in on all sides
Moderate
1 in top/bottom, 0.75 in left/right
Wide
1 in on all sides
Zero
0 in - for borderless, full-bleed printing
Each preset shows a small dynamic page icon that visually represents the margin layout before you click.
Custom Margins: For precise control, click Custom Margins… to open a configuration modal where you can set independent top, bottom, left, and right margins down to the pixel. Your custom margins integrate immediately with the blue snap guides visible on the canvas and are saved into your .opub file so they persist when the file is reopened. Margins are automatically excluded from exported images and PDFs, meaning they never appear in your final output.

title: Page Views, Notes & Numbering
excerpt: Master multi-page documents in Open Publisher. Learn to use Multi-Page View, Two-Page Spreads, organise with Page Notes, and insert automatic page numbers.
content:
Page Views, Notes & Numbering
This guide covers essential document management tools that help you navigate, organise, and format multi-page publications efficiently.
Creating a New Document
To start a fresh publication, go to File > New . This opens the template browser, where you can select from a range of professionally designed publication templates (newsletters, flyers, posters, business cards, etc.) or choose a blank canvas at a standard size. Once selected, a new, untitled document opens at the specified dimensions.
Two-Page Spread Mode
For publications designed as booklets or magazines, enable Two-Page Spread Mode from the Navigation Pane context menu. In this view, facing pages are displayed side by side in the sidebar thumbnails, allowing you to visualise the relationship between a left-hand and a right-hand page as readers will see them.
Page Notes
For larger, multi-page documents, it can be helpful to label individual pages so they are easy to identify at a glance without clicking into them. Open Publisher’s Page Notes feature lets you attach a short custom identifier to any page.
How to add a Page Note:
Right-click a page thumbnail in the left-hand Navigation Pane.
Select Add Note from the context menu.
Type a short label - for example: Front Cover, TOC, Back Cover, Chapter 3.
The note appears directly beneath the page thumbnail in a bold, teal-coloured font.
To remove a note, right-click the page, select Add Note, and leave the input field blank before confirming. The note will be cleared automatically.
Note: Page Notes are purely for your own organisational use within the editor. They do not affect page numbering, printed output, or exported files.
Multi-Page View
When you zoom out to 45% or below on a document that contains more than one page, Open Publisher automatically activates Multi-Page View. In this mode, all pages are rendered side-by-side in the workspace, giving you a bird’s-eye overview of your entire publication at once.
Key behaviours of Multi-Page View:
All non-active pages are shown as read-only preview clones, rendered at full 1:1 quality.
The active (editable) page is clearly labelled with an “(Editing)” badge and retains full interactivity - you can type, drag, and select elements normally.
Clicking any preview page instantly swaps it to become the active editable page, while the previously active page converts to a read-only preview in its place - all without changing your zoom level.
Pages are always arranged horizontally in a single row, calculated to fit your display width.
To exit Multi-Page View, simply zoom back in above 45%.
Auto Page Numbering
For longer documents, manually updating page numbers is tedious. Open Publisher provides an Auto Page Numbers feature that inserts dynamic, self-updating number tags.
How to insert auto page numbers:
Navigate to the Insert ribbon tab.
Click Page Number .
A page number element is inserted at your cursor position. It automatically displays the correct number for each page and updates itself as you add, remove, or reorder pages in your document.

title: Perfect Previews & Multi-Page Theme Isolation
excerpt: Explore Open Publisher
content: Perfect Previews & Multi-Page Theme Isolation The pages sidebar is the central command center for navigating and organizing multi-page documents. In earlier versions of Open Publisher, thumbnails suffered from fragility: previews would occasionally blank out to solid white, swap contents across different page slots, hide WordArt and images, or broadcast live slider filters from one page to every thumbnail. Version 5.6.0 delivered an architectural overhaul of the preview system, unifying the sidebar into a native DOM-scaled engine with 60 FPS real-time synchronization and strict per-page theme isolation. 🖼️ Native DOM Scaled Sidebar Previews with Real-Time Element Parity Thumbnails accurately display per-page themes, WordArt, photos, and live canvas movements at 60 FPS. Native DOM Scaled Thumbnail Architecture Version 5.6.0 replaced fragile floating overlay panels with a native, pure CSS-scaled DOM architecture: Independent DOM Subtrees: Every thumbnail inside .page-thumb renders its own lightweight DOM tree, scaled cleanly with GPU acceleration using CSS transforms ( transform: scale(...) ). Direct themeSettings Rendering: renderThumbnailHTML() reads each page's themeSettings directly, building solid fills, gradients, textures, and computed CSS filters without querying or cloning the active canvas. Decommissioned Glass Vault Overlay: Completely removed the legacy #ts-overlay-wrapper and 800ms DOM cloning loop, eliminating the root cause of thumbnail blanking and cross-page thumbnail swapping. Full WordArt & Image Visibility Parity Prior to this release, an obsolete CSS rule ( .page-thumb img { opacity: 0 !important; visibility: hidden !important; } ) hid all image tags in thumbnails. Version 5.6.0 resolved this: Complete Graphics Visibility: Restored thumbnail images with opacity: 1 !important; visibility: visible !important , allowing Beta WordArt renders, Clipart, and imported photos to display with 100% visual fidelity. Native Image Elements: Replaced CSS background image properties with native tags in thumbnails, preventing styling failures on complex data URIs, inline SVGs, and URLs with special characters. Strict Per-Page Theme Isolation & Sanitization Adjusting sliders in the Theme Studio now updates strictly the active page canvas and its corresponding thumbnail ( #thumb-[currentPageIndex] ), preventing filter leakage onto other page previews. Additionally, document deserialization automatically sanitizes ghost boxes and orphaned wrappers, guaranteeing stable element counts across page transitions. Tip: The sidebar thumbnails reflect your document in real time, serving as an instant visual table of contents as you work.

title: Scratch Area & Snapping Guides
excerpt: Master page layouts in Open Publisher using the Scratch Area, pixel rulers, Smart Guides, and precision object snapping tools.
content:
Scratch Area & Snapping Guides
To help you position elements with pixel-perfect accuracy, Open Publisher features a robust snapping system, dynamic guides, and an off-canvas storage area.
The Scratch Area
Objects that you drag partially or completely off the page canvas enter the Scratch Area - an invisible staging zone surrounding the page. These elements are preserved in the document but do not appear in printed or exported output.
To manage scratch area visibility, go to the View ribbon tab and click the Scratch Area toggle button. When toggled off, all off-page elements are instantly hidden from view (but not deleted), allowing you to focus cleanly on your page layout.
Rulers & Custom Origin
Pixel rulers run along the top and left edges of the canvas, giving you a precise spatial reference while you work.
To show or hide rulers:
Go to View > Show > Rulers .
Or, right-click in the workspace background and select Show/Hide Rulers .
By default, the ruler’s 0,0 origin sits at the top-left corner of the canvas. You can redefine this origin to any point on the page:
Drag the grey intersection box (where the horizontal and vertical rulers meet, at the very top-left corner).
As you drag, dashed guide lines follow your cursor across the page to help you visually pinpoint the target coordinates.
Release to set the new zero point. All ruler ticks and labels immediately recalculate from the new origin.
Double-click the intersection box at any time to instantly reset the rulers back to their default position.
Your custom origin is saved into the .opub file, so it persists across sessions.
Snapping Systems
Open Publisher provides three independent snapping systems that can be toggled individually:
Snap Mode
What it does
Snap to Grid
Elements snap to an invisible pixel grid as you drag.
Snap to Guides
Elements snap to the margin guide lines.
Snap to Objects
Elements snap to the edges and centres of other elements on the page.
To manage snapping:
Use the Snap To dropdown in the View tab, the Text Box Tools ribbon, or the Picture Tools ribbon.
Or right-click the canvas and select the snapping options from the context menu.
Hold Ctrl while dragging to temporarily bypass grid snapping without toggling the setting off - the most efficient way to place something between grid positions.
Snap tolerance: The magnetic pull distance for Snap to Guides and Snap to Objects is set to 8 pixels, providing a subtle and predictable snap feel that matches professional desktop publishing software.
Smart Grid Prompt: If you turn off “Snap to Grid” while the visual grid overlay is currently visible, a dialog intelligently asks if you also want to hide the visual grid to clear up your workspace.
Smart Guides (Alignment Lines)
When you drag any element on the canvas, Smart Guides appear as semi-transparent teal lines that indicate when the element is aligned with the edges or centres of other elements on the page.
Smart guides use a smooth fade-in and fade-out transition rather than abruptly flashing on/off. This preserves high responsiveness while eliminating visual flicker.
The guide colour is a soft, semi-transparent teal - visible enough to be useful but not too heavy.
Smart guides work alongside (not instead of) the snapping system. Snapping “pulls” the element to the alignment point; smart guides show you where that alignment point is.

title: Template Saving & Migration
excerpt: Learn how to save reusable templates in Open Publisher and seamlessly migrate text content between different document layouts using the Insert File tool.
content:
Template Saving & Content Migration
Open Publisher includes dedicated tools to help you build reusable layouts and move text between different designs without destroying your precise formatting.
Saving a Document as a Template
You can save any document you have designed as a Publisher Template so that it can be used as a clean starting point for future publications, without the risk of overwriting the original.
Design your publication as normal.
In the File ribbon, click Save Template (located next to the standard Save button).
Save the resulting .opub file to a convenient location.
When you save a template, a hidden isTemplate: true flag is embedded in the file, and your current working session is renamed to “Untitled [DocumentName]”. When someone later opens the template, saving it for the first time will always prompt for a new filename, permanently protecting the original from accidental overwrites.
Content Migration (Insert > File)
Because Open Publisher is a precise page-layout tool where elements are locked to specific coordinates, you cannot simply open an old document inside a new template and expect the layout to transfer automatically. However, you can easily migrate text using the Insert File tool.
Open the new template via File > New and select your desired layout.
Click inside the text box on the new template where you want your content to appear (it must be actively selected).
In the Insert ribbon, click the Insert File button.
Browse to your existing .opub or .json document and select it.
Open Publisher will scan every page of the selected file in the background, extract all text elements, and pour their content directly into your active text box.
Note: Only text content is migrated. Images and shapes require manual placement in the new layout because their positions are tied to specific coordinates that may not correspond to the new template’s design.

title: The Navigation Pane & Views
excerpt: Learn how to add, duplicate, move, and delete pages in Open Publisher. Use custom page notes, auto page numbering to organise your document and more.
content:
The Navigation Pane & Views

The thumbnails are generated automatically using a fast DOM-cloning system and update within 1.5 seconds of your last edit, so you always have an up-to-date visual map of your publication.
Sidebar Context Menus
Right-clicking anywhere on a page thumbnail opens a context menu with options to insert, duplicate, move, or delete pages, as well as add notes or access the Master Pages submenu. Right-clicking the blank grey area of the Navigation Pane (not on a thumbnail) opens a workspace-level context menu for adding a new blank page, toggling Two-Page Spread Mode, collapsing the sidebar, changing Page Design / Size, and exporting or printing the document.
Two-Page Spread Mode

In this view, facing pages are displayed side by side in the sidebar thumbnails, allowing you to visualise the relationship between a left-hand and a right-hand page as readers will see them.
Multi-Page View
When you zoom out to 45% or below on a document that contains more than one page, Open Publisher automatically activates Multi-Page View. In this mode, all pages are rendered side-by-side in the workspace, giving you a bird’s-eye overview of your entire publication at once.
Pages are always arranged horizontally in a single row, calculated to fit your display width.
All non-active pages are shown as read-only preview clones, rendered at full 1:1 quality.
The active (editable) page is clearly labelled with an “(Editing)” badge and retains full interactivity.

title: Clickjacking & UI Occlusion
excerpt: Open Publisher protects users from clickjacking and UI redressing scams using IntersectionObserver v2 occlusion tracking, with no false positives and graceful fallback.
content:
Clickjacking & UI Occlusion Protection
Open Publisher includes a passive, lightweight security system that protects users from clickjacking and UI redressing scams - attacks where a malicious website frames Open Publisher inside a hidden or transparent layer and overlays it with deceptive UI, tricking users into interacting with the attacker’s content while believing they are using Open Publisher normally.
How It Works
Using the IntersectionObserver v2 (occlusion tracking) API, Open Publisher continuously monitors whether the workspace is being covered by unauthorised content from another frame or website. If an occlusion is detected, a clear in-app warning dialog immediately alerts the user that they may be interacting with a scam.
Key Behaviours
No false positives - The system tracks physical pixel occlusion, not domain blacklists, so it never incorrectly triggers against legitimate CMS integrations or creative suite embeds.
No forced redirects - The protection does not force browser redirects, avoiding any risk of triggering Google Safe Browsing flags.
Graceful fallback - On older browsers that do not support occlusion tracking, the system fails silently via a try-catch - no errors, no broken functionality, just no protection on unsupported browsers.
Authorized Platform Exemptions (Puter.com Cloud Desktop)
Open Publisher is officially accepted and available as a cloud desktop application on Puter.com . Within Puter's browser-based desktop operating system, applications run inside container frames where Puter's native floating window controls (minimize, maximize, close buttons and titlebar chrome) naturally float and hover over the upper boundary of the document workspace.
Under standard occlusion tracking, these floating desktop window controls could be perceived by IntersectionObserver v2 as an external occlusion, potentially causing a false-positive "Suspicious Activity Detected" security alert during normal cloud desktop usage.
To ensure a smooth, uninterrupted user experience while maintaining robust anti-clickjacking protection, Open Publisher incorporates an intelligent, multi-vector platform verification engine ( isPuterEnvironment() ) that verifies authorized runtime contexts before initializing the occlusion watcher:
Ancestor Origins Validation: Verifies window.location.ancestorOrigins against trusted Puter endpoints ( puter.com , *.puter.com , and *.puter.site ).
Parent Frame Referrer Verification: Confirms parent frame document.referrer hostnames originate from verified Puter platforms.
Native Hosting Detection: Identifies direct execution hosted under *.puter.site or *.puter.com .
Client SDK Telemetry: Detects genuine runtime window.puter and window.parent.puter client SDK objects.
Security Shield Remains Active: This exemption applies exclusively to origin-verified Puter environments. Any unauthorized third-party iframes, malicious wrapper sites, or unverified external overlays remain fully blocked by the Anti Ad-Overlay security shield.

title: Desktop App Password Encryption & Metadata Bridge
excerpt: Secure publications with AES-GCM 256 encryption and preserve full document metadata in the Open Publisher V5 desktop application.
content:
Desktop App Password Encryption & Metadata Bridge
Protecting sensitive brochures, financial reports, and legal publications requires military-grade cryptographic security. In version 5.1.10, Open Publisher resolved a critical integration bug where password-protected publications saved inside the V5 desktop application wrapper ( wrapper.html ) failed to retain encryption, causing saved .opub files to reopen without password prompts. The defensive desktop save bridge restores full AES-GCM 256 encryption and complete metadata persistence across all desktop platforms.
🔐 Password-Protected Publication Encryption & Decryption
Desktop publications encrypted with AES-GCM 256 require password entry before unpacking document contents.
Desktop Injection Interception & Root Cause
The password vulnerability stemmed from an IPC interaction between the desktop wrapper and web application:
Unencrypted Stub Overwrite: In the desktop wrapper, an injection timer periodically assigned a lightweight stub to window.saveDocument that extracted only raw title and pages. It completely bypassed state.documentPassword and the Web Crypto encryption pipeline.
Dropped Metadata: The wrapper stub also omitted critical document properties including dpi , format , unit , rulerUnit , and isSpreadMode .
Silent Plaintext Persistence: Because the desktop wrapper received unencrypted JSON, the file written to disk lacked the encryption wrapper ( encrypted: true , salt , iv ). When reopened, the loader saw plain JSON and loaded it directly without requesting authentication.
Configurable Declaration & Getter/Setter Traps
The security patch in extensions/system-patches.js establishes a robust defensive barrier:
Configurable Function Assignment: In io/file-io.js , saveDocument was converted from a rigid function declaration into a configurable property assignment: window.saveDocument = function() { ... } .
Defensive Property Trap: Utilizing Object.defineProperty , Open Publisher intercepts attempts by the desktop wrapper to overwrite saveDocument , redirecting execution to masterSaveDocument while flagging _desktopBridgeActive = true .
Zero-Rebuild Deployment: Because the fix resides in the web client, all security protections took effect immediately without requiring re-compilation or redistribution of desktop installers across Windows, macOS, Linux, or FreeBSD.
End-to-End Cryptographic Security
When saving encrypted publications in desktop mode, masterSaveDocument derives a 256-bit key using PBKDF2 with SHA-256 and encrypts the document payload using AES-GCM. An incorrect password entered during load fails cryptographic verification, preventing unauthorized access.
Tip: To set or change a password, open the File menu, select Info, and click Protect Document.

title: Document Properties
excerpt: Add author, company, subject, and keyword metadata to your Open Publisher document via Document Properties, with full visibility and removal through the Document Inspector.
content:
Document Properties
Document Properties lets you embed descriptive metadata directly into your .opub file. This metadata travels invisibly with the document behind the scenes and can be used to identify ownership, categorise content, or provide important context for collaborators.
Whether you are working within a large team, organising a digital archive, or preparing a publication for external distribution, taking a few moments to fill out your document properties ensures your files remain searchable, professional, and properly credited.
How to Set Document Properties
Accessing and updating your file’s metadata is quick and straightforward.
Navigate to File > Info > Properties from the main menu, or simply click the Properties button located in the File ribbon under the Document Info section.
A dialogue box will appear. Fill in the available fields to best describe your document:
Author: The name of the individual, department, or team who created the document. If multiple people are collaborating, you can separate names with commas.
Company: The organisation or agency the document belongs to. Keeping this consistent helps when archiving official corporate templates.
Subject: A brief, high-level description of the document’s topic, purpose, or target audience (e.g., “Q3 Financial Report” or “Employee Onboarding Guide”).
Keywords: Specific tags or terms that help identify the document during a system search. It is best practice to separate multiple keywords with commas (e.g., budget, 2026, marketing, draft ).
Click Save to apply your changes. The properties are now permanently stored within the .opub file until you decide to alter them.
Privacy & The Document Inspector
While Document Properties are completely invisible in your final design layout, this metadata travels with the file wherever it is sent. This is excellent for internal organisation, but can sometimes expose internal working details to external clients or public readers.
Note: Before sharing your publication externally, we highly recommend using the Document Inspector . Navigate to File > Info > Inspect Document to easily review, sanitise, and remove any hidden metadata, personal author names, or internal keywords you do not want recipients to see.

title: Document Conversion Pipeline Security & Threat Shield Audit
excerpt: Explore OpenPublisher
content:
Document Conversion Pipeline Security & Edge Threat Shield Audit
When users migrate legacy publications to OpenPublisher by dragging and dropping .pub , .docx , or .doc files into their browser or desktop client, documents are processed through OpenPublisher's dedicated cloud conversion architecture. To safeguard users, education networks, and server infrastructure from malicious payloads, all incoming uploads pass through an internal automated edge inspection layer known as the Sentinel Content & Threat Shield . Clean files then immediately stream into the containerized document converter (powered by libmspub ) and are returned directly to the user.
USER PRIVACY & TELEMETRY POLICY
Document Content Protection & Internal Analytics Logging
OpenPublisher maintains strict user document confidentiality: original document contents, text frames, and embedded graphics are never stored, indexed, or shared. Files uploaded for conversion are parsed strictly in isolated, volatile memory (RAM) and immediately streamed back to the user as native .opub objects and vector PDF streams. Once conversion completes, the ephemeral memory container is immediately destroyed.
For operational visibility, file names are among the few telemetry attributes logged strictly for internal analytics to populate the operational dashboard, track format ratios, and identify abusive traffic. Telemetry records and quarantined files are maintained solely for detected threats, malware payloads, and automated spam floods.
30-Day Pipeline Ingestion & Velocity Telemetry
The following production telemetry from the v5.4.2-PROD pipeline reflects global conversion activity over a 30-day operational audit:
30-Day Conversions
3,482
+31.4% growth (Avg 116.1 imports/day converted to .opub )
Delivery Success Rate
97.3%
3,385 delivered (51 client aborts, 42 engine conversion errors)
Format Ingestion
65% .PUB
2,394 .pub · 688 .docx (22%) · 400 .doc (13%)
Threats Intercepted
68
100% intercepted (State propaganda, botnets, and weaponized macros)
Engine Velocity
1.38s
26 Languages (14,928 total pages rendered to .opub /PDF)
Multi-Tiered Pre-Flight Edge Inspection Stack
Because older binary formats (specifically legacy Word .doc and Microsoft Publisher .pub ) rely on Complex Binary Compound Document Structures (OLE/CFB), they have historically been exploited by threat actors for buffer overflow triggers and remote code execution. OpenPublisher eliminates these risks via a multi-tiered defense pipeline:
1. Edge Origin & Sanctions Filtering: Connections arriving at Cloudflare edge worker points are validated against statutory export embargoes (OFAC, EU, UK sanctions), halting automated bulk botnets originating from sanctioned infrastructure before file bytes reach processing queues.
2. Magic Byte & Header Structure Validation: Deep heuristic inspection evaluates the binary container to verify genuine compound document streams. Polyglot binaries, disguised executables, and manipulated stream headers are flagged immediately.
3. YARA Disinformation & Abuse Signatures: Text and structural streams are evaluated against custom YARA rules that identify state-sponsored disinformation campaigns, unauthorized commercial mass-mailing syndicates, and fraudulent templates.
4. OLE Macro & Exploit Sandboxing: Embedded VBA macro streams, AutoOpen triggers, and known CVE payloads (such as Equation Editor shellcodes) are quarantined. Legitimate text frames are extracted without executing hostile code.
5. Converter Worker & ServerSide Branch: The conversion server itself is maintained on our main GitHub repository under the dedicated ServerSide branch. This open-source branch contains only the document converter, providing users and system administrators with everything needed to set up their own local or self-hosted conversion node (running containerized libmspub ). The telemetry and threat shield layer is closed for internal production use: incoming uploads quickly pass through the shield, into the converter, and immediately back to the user.
Analysis of 68 Quarantined Files (30-Day Threat Vector Breakdown)
During the 30-day telemetry audit period, 68 malicious or abusive uploads were intercepted and quarantined. An analysis of these intercepted files revealed four distinct categories of malicious activity:
24 INTERCEPTIONS
Russian State Disinformation & Propaganda
Automated botnet submissions attempting to convert official state press kits, election interference leaflets (e.g. Moldova election disinformation), Wagner PMC recruitment handouts, and spoofed government directives.
Signatures: YARA-RU-STATE-MEDIA , DISINFO-DOPPELGANGER-07 , SANCTION-WAGNER-PMCS , YARA-RU-INFLUENCE-14 .
Origin ASNs: Rostelecom ( AS12389 ), MegaFon ( AS31133 ), Mail.Ru Cloud ( AS47764 ).
19 INTERCEPTIONS
Iran Spam & Sanctioned Media Syndicates
Bulk automated conversion attempts originating from Iranian state news agencies (Tasnim News, Fars News, HispanTV Latin America folletos, Kayhan, NourNews) and regional political mass-mailers in direct violation of statutory trade embargoes.
Signatures: SPAM-IR-SYNDICATE-09 , SPAM-IR-BOTNET-22 , SPAM-IR-MASSMAIL-03 , SANCTION-IR-ENTITY-04 .
Origin ASNs: TCI Iran ( AS58224 ), Irancell ( AS44244 ), DCI Iran ( AS12888 ).
14 INTERCEPTIONS
VBA Macros, Shellcode & APT Droppers
Legacy documents containing embedded remote access trojans (Remcos RAT, Agent Tesla), Equation Editor buffer overflow shellcodes ( CVE-2017-11882 ), and North Korean Lazarus Group ( APT38 ) weaponized payloads.
Signatures: MAL-REMCOS-OLE-DROP , CVE-2017-11882-EQNEDT , OLE-VBA-AUTOOPEN-99 , APT-LAZARUS-VBA-DROP .
Origin ASNs: Ryugyong ( AS131279 KP ), M247 ( AS9089 ), IP Volume ( AS202425 ).
11 INTERCEPTIONS
Phishing Templates & QR Code Scams
Deceptive templates engineered to harvest user credentials, including fraudulent IRS tax rebate claims, spoofed Microsoft 365 session expiration alerts, and "quishing" flyers featuring fake Bank of America/Zelle QR payment refund codes.
Signatures: PHISH-GOV-IMPERSONATION , QR-PHISH-BANK-04 , PHISH-CRED-HARVEST-19 , QR-PHISH-CRYPTO-88 .
Origin ASNs: Hetzner ( AS24940 ), AWS Cloud ( AS16509 ), DigitalOcean ( AS14061 ).
Production Threat Shield Telemetry & Interception Preview
Below is the complete, high-resolution production capture from the OpenPublisher Telemetry & Shield (v5.4.2-PROD) dashboard, illustrating the 30-day audit log and real-time quarantine decisions. The preview expands across the full page layout for optimal readability:
Internal Production Dashboard: OpenPublisher Telemetry & Threat Shield (v5.4.2-PROD). Illustrates quarantined uploads intercepted before worker execution. File names are logged strictly for internal analytics; document contents are never stored. Click the preview to open in full resolution.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Are my personal or business documents monitored or logged when converting?
File names and format metrics are logged strictly for internal analytics on our operational dashboard to monitor pipeline performance and traffic ratios. However, document contents, text frames, images, and layout designs are processed strictly in volatile RAM and are never stored, logged, or shared. Quarantined records are only preserved when an upload triggers active threat signatures or statutory sanctions.
Can converting an old .PUB or .DOC file compromise my workstation?
No. Because OpenPublisher converts documents into its native, open .opub web-standard format (pure HTML5, CSS3, and SVG graphics), dangerous binary macros and shellcodes cannot execute in the OpenPublisher canvas. Furthermore, pre-flight edge sandboxing isolates and blocks known exploits before conversion even begins.
Where does the conversion server run and can I host my own?
The conversion server itself is located directly on our main GitHub repository under the dedicated ServerSide branch. This branch contains only the document converter and provides users with the complete instructions and containerized scripts needed to set up their own local or hosted copy using libmspub . OpenPublisher's telemetry shield layer is closed for internal production security: user uploads pass rapidly through the shield, stream into the converter, and return straight back to the user.
Why was this audit log published?
This 30-day telemetry audit is published as a one-off transparency preview to inform schools, charities, businesses, and government teams of the rigorous edge security safeguards protecting OpenPublisher's document conversion infrastructure.

title: Geographic Access Control & Abuse Defense Architecture
excerpt: Safeguard Open Publisher from automated abuse and propaganda conversion with edge CDN trace interception, geo-IP fallbacks, and timezone heuristics.
content:
Geographic Access Control & Abuse Defense Architecture
Open-source, client-side web tools can become targets for automated abuse, proxy-routed scraping, or weaponized propaganda batch processing. Version 5.1.13 introduced a comprehensive, multi-tiered geographic access control and defense engine designed to restrict connections originating from the Russian Federation following sustained service misuse. By pairing edge CDN trace verification with client-side timezone heuristics and early session caching, Open Publisher neutralizes bad-faith traffic before the workspace initializes.
🛡️ Multi-Layered Edge CDN & Heuristic Access Defense
Traffic originating from restricted regions is intercepted at initialization, halting application execution prior to canvas loading.
Edge CDN Trace Interception
The primary detection vector queries the edge reverse proxy during early application startup:
Authoritative Trace Query: Open Publisher fetches the edge trace endpoint ( /cdn-cgi/trace ). This payload returns authoritative Cloudflare edge metadata, including the client's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code ( loc=RU ).
Immediate Execution Halt: If the client country matches restricted territories, the initialization loop breaks immediately, preventing document loading and API interaction.
Redundant Geo-IP Fallback: If the edge trace endpoint is unavailable or obscured, the defense engine invokes secondary low-latency geolocation endpoints ( https://api.country.is ) to verify origin.
Timezone & Locale Heuristic Defense
To protect against residential proxy routing where an edge IP appears neutral but client environment variables leak the true host origin, the engine evaluates browser system telemetry:
Russian Timezone Verification: The client timezone string is audited against 26 Russian timezones (including Europe/Moscow , Asia/Yekaterinburg , Asia/Novosibirsk , and Europe/Kaliningrad ).
Language-Timezone Pairing: When a user's browser exhibits a Russian regional timezone paired with Russian language preferences ( ru , ru-RU ), the defense system engages automatically.
Early DOM Interception & Session Flags
The defense module is positioned at the top of the HTML head ( extensions/geo-defense.js ), running before heavy UI assets, fonts, or templates are fetched. Once identified, flags are written to localStorage and sessionStorage ( op_ru_blocked = '1' ), ensuring subsequent page refreshes terminate instantly without repeated network lookups.
Note: Self-hosted and on-premise enterprise deployments of Open Publisher can customize regional firewall policies in the server configuration.

title: International Sanctions Compliance & Iran Regional Defense
excerpt: Enforce international sanctions and OFAC compliance with automated edge trace detection, Tehran timezone heuristics, and bilingual legal notices.
content:
International Sanctions Compliance & Iran Regional Defense
Global digital publishing software must adhere strictly to statutory export controls, international trade embargoes, and financial sanctions. Version 5.3.1 expanded Open Publisher's application-layer geographic defense engine to enforce full access restrictions on connections originating from the Islamic Republic of Iran (IR) alongside the Russian Federation (RU). This release establishes automated multi-tier geographic interception in strict compliance with United States OFAC regulations, European Union Council directives, and UK statutory sanctions.
⚖️ Statutory Compliance & Regional Restriction Screen
Connections originating from sanctioned territories are intercepted before application startup with bilingual compliance notices.
Statutory Obligations & Compliance Context
Client-side web software distributed globally must operate in full conformity with regulatory frameworks:
International Trade Controls: Under OFAC, EU, and UK sanctions, software platforms are legally prohibited from exporting or facilitating technical services to sanctioned state entities and jurisdictions.
Infrastructure Protection: Automated scraping, unauthorized proxy rotation, and abusive batch workloads originating from restricted IP ranges are halted before consuming server or client resources.
Distinction Between State & People: While enforcing legal compliance, the restriction screen expresses clear solidarity with universal human rights, civil liberties, and fundamental freedoms.
Multi-Tiered Interception Architecture
The defense system in extensions/geo-defense.js executes at the very top of the document head:
Cloudflare Edge CDN Trace: Queries /cdn-cgi/trace during early bootstrap. If the authoritative country code evaluates to loc=IR or loc=RU , the application terminates execution immediately before any stylesheets, fonts, or templates load.
Redundant Public Geolocation: If edge trace data is unreachable, the engine falls back asynchronously to secondary geolocation services ( https://api.country.is/ ).
Timezone & Persian Locale Heuristics: Audits host telemetry against Iranian timezones ( Asia/Tehran , Iran ) and Persian language preferences ( fa , fa-IR , pes ), intercepting connections that leak host environment data through local proxy tunnels.
Session & Local Storage Persistence: Sets persistent flags ( op_ir_blocked = '1' ) so subsequent page reloads engage the restriction screen instantaneously without redundant network lookups.
Bilingual Sanctions Notice Card
When engaged, the entire document DOM is replaced with a standalone compliance screen featuring the Iranian tricolor flag (Green, White, Red), bilingual English and Persian legal text detailing statutory compliance, and a dedicated solidarity footer.
Note: Enterprise administrators can verify compliance rules or simulate regional restrictions using developer audit tools in the system console.

title: Password Protection
excerpt: Fully encrypt any Open Publisher document with a password using AES-GCM encryption. Protected files save as unreadable binary blobs until the correct password is entered.
content:
Password Protection
Open Publisher allows you to fully encrypt any document with a password using the industry-standard AES-GCM encryption algorithm, implemented natively in the browser via the Web Crypto API. Once protected, the file saves as an encrypted binary blob rather than a readable .html or .opub structure - the content is completely unreadable to anyone who does not have the correct password.
How to Protect a Document
Go to File > Protect Document , or click the Protect Document button in the ribbon.
Enter a password and confirm it in the dialog.
Click Protect .
Once protected, a Protected badge appears in the top-right area of the canvas, giving you immediate visual confirmation that the active document is secured.
Opening a Protected Document
Open the .opub file as normal.
A decryption prompt immediately appears.
Enter the correct password. If it matches, the document decrypts and loads instantly.
If the password is incorrect, the document remains locked.
Important: No Password Recovery
There is no password recovery mechanism. If you lose or forget the password, the document cannot be recovered under any circumstances. Always keep a backup copy of the unprotected source file stored securely before applying password protection.

title: Status Bar Password Protection Indicator & Dialog Access
excerpt: Manage document encryption effortlessly with Open Publisher
content: Status Bar Password Protection Indicator & Dialog Access Protecting confidential publications with military-grade AES-GCM password encryption is an essential feature in Open Publisher. In previous releases, the active protection badge was anchored in the top title bar. In the desktop V5 client, this location caused visual overlap and click conflicts with native window action buttons ("Show in file explorer" and "Pin window on top"). Version 5.5.1 relocated the password protection indicator ( #protected-indicator ) to the bottom status bar, nesting it alongside zoom controls with direct 1-click management dialog access. 🔒 Password Protection Indicator Pill Badge in Bottom Status Bar The translucent lock pill badge docks elegantly in the status bar, providing 1-click password management. Eliminating Desktop Window Control Collisions The desktop V5 wrapper includes dedicated window action buttons docked at the right end of the title bar. Relocating the indicator delivers several UX improvements: Zero Button Overlap: Clears the top title bar entirely of floating status badges, ensuring "Show in file explorer" and "Pin window on top" remain unobstructed and fully clickable. Dedicated Title Bar Space: Keeps the top bar focused purely on document name editing, canvas coordinates, and window management controls. Status Bar Zoom Group Docking The indicator is nested as the first child of #zoom-slider-container on the right side of the bottom status bar: Sleek Translucent Pill Badge: Styled with a lock icon ( Protected ), subtle background blur, and white typography that harmonizes across all light, dark, and custom UI themes. Responsive Flexbox Alignment: Automatically aligns vertically with zoom buttons ( #zoom-out-btn , #zoom-in-btn ) and slider without manual pixel offsets. Zero-Width Inactive State: When a document is unencrypted, the badge collapses with display: none , consuming zero layout space. 1-Click Management Dialog & Lifecycle Cleanup Rather than requiring users to search through menus to update protection, the badge provides direct interactive access: Click-to-Manage: Clicking the indicator immediately opens the Password Protection modal ( showProtectDocumentModal() ), prefilling current settings for quick password modification or removal. Automatic Lifecycle Cleanup: Resetting or creating a new document via handleNewDocument() clears state.documentPassword = null and automatically hides the badge via updateProtectionIndicator() . Tip: You can quickly verify whether your document will save with encryption simply by glancing at the bottom-right corner next to the zoom slider.

title: The Document Inspector
excerpt: Use the Open Publisher Document Inspector to scan for hidden metadata, off-canvas elements, and empty text boxes before sharing or publishing your document.
content:
The Document Inspector
Before you share, publish, or hand off a document, it is important to know exactly what is inside it. Open Publisher files can silently accumulate hidden metadata, stray off-canvas objects, and invisible text boxes that you may not want recipients to see - the Document Inspector is a privacy and security tool that finds and removes all of it in one place, before the file leaves your hands.
Opening the Document Inspector
Go to File > Info > Inspect Document . The Inspector immediately scans your entire document across all pages and presents its findings.
What the Inspector Checks
The Inspector scans three categories of potentially sensitive or unwanted content:
Document Properties - Checks for embedded metadata such as Author, Company, Subject, and Keywords. This metadata is invisible in the design but travels with the file - useful to strip before sharing externally so personal or company information is not unintentionally exposed.
Off-Canvas Elements - Detects elements that exist completely outside the page boundary - stored in the Scratch Area or accidentally dragged off-page. These objects are invisible in your printed or exported output but are still present inside the file and visible to anyone who opens it in Open Publisher.
Empty Text Boxes - Flags text boxes containing only whitespace or invisible HTML entities such as   . These are easy to leave behind and can bloat file size or expose placeholder content.
Status Badges & Removing Data
Each category displays a colour-coded status badge:
Found - Data was detected and requires your attention.
Clean - Nothing to report in this category.
A one-click Remove All button is provided for each category, allowing you to instantly purge the detected data without having to locate and delete items manually. Running the Inspector before every export or file handoff is a good habit for keeping your documents clean and your sensitive information private.

title: Advanced Shape Tools
excerpt: Morph vector shapes into custom polygons with the Shape Points Editor, use hollow arrow styles, and freely resize shapes in any proportion in Open Publisher.
content:
Advanced Shape Tools
Beyond standard formatting, Open Publisher includes a set of advanced shape tools that give you precise creative control - from morphing shapes into entirely custom polygons to professional hollow arrow styles for diagrams and flow layouts.
Custom Shape Points Editor
The Edit Shape Points tool lets you manipulate the individual vertices of any standard shape, morphing it freely into a completely custom polygon.
To edit shape points:
Right-click a shape on the canvas.
Select Edit Points from the context menu.
Draggable control vertices appear at the corners of the shape.
Drag any vertex to reshape the polygon - the shape updates in real time using CSS clip-path for the new boundary.
Click away from the shape to finish editing.
The editor supports elements that have been 3D rotated or transformed, allowing vertex manipulation even on skewed shapes.
Note: Because browsers discard clip-path CSS properties during printing, the moment you finish editing and click away, Open Publisher automatically traces the drawn points onto an HTML5 canvas, exports a transparent PNG, and swaps the DOM element with the baked image. This guarantees 100% print and PDF reliability without any manual intervention.
Hollow Arrow Styles
A dedicated Hollow Arrows section within the Shape dropdown menu provides 9 unique arrowed line combinations using three distinct terminator styles:
Standard Hollow Points - Classic arrows with clean, transparent hollow arrowheads.
Flat Stops - Lines terminating in a perpendicular T-bar blocking line.
Hollow Diamonds - Elegant geometric diamond heads with transparent interiors.
All hollow arrows use modern SVG context-stroke mechanics, meaning their arrowheads automatically and perfectly adapt to match whatever stroke colour you apply to the line - no manual recolouring required.
Flexible Shape Resizing
Shapes in Open Publisher dynamically stretch to fill their bounding boxes independently in both directions. Dragging any handle adjusts width or height freely, giving you complete control over proportions - whether you need a wide horizontal banner, a tall narrow column, or any non-square layout.
For proportional resizing, hold Shift while dragging a corner handle to lock the aspect ratio, or hold Ctrl / Cmd + Shift to scale proportionally from the centre point.

title: Authentic Smart Arrows Expansion & Element Interactivity
excerpt: Explore 98 authentic directional Smart Arrows across 7 balanced categories, featuring complete 8-handle resizing, rotation, and amber tip customization.
content:
Authentic Smart Arrows Expansion & Element Interactivity
Directional graphics and flowcharts require clean, unambiguous vector indicators that scale without visual distortion. Following initial user feedback on early arrow prototypes, version 5.3.3 delivered a comprehensive expansion and visual refinement of the Smart Arrows Engine. This release replaced irregular polygons and non-arrow shapes with 98 authentic, high-precision directional arrows, fully restored canvas wrapper interactivity, and organized the catalog into seven balanced categories.
🏹 98-Arrow Symmetrical Gallery & Canvas Interactivity
The expanded 98-style gallery features 7 balanced categories of 14 arrows each, complete with full 8-handle manipulation.
Canvas Interactivity & Unified Wrapper Factory
In earlier iterations, newly inserted arrows were constructed as bare SVG elements that lacked wrapper integration, causing clicks to fall through and deselect the object. Version 5.3.3 resolved this across the core lifecycle:
Unified Wrapper Builder: Arrow insertion now routes strictly through window.createWrapper() , generating full interactive .pub-element containers with robust fallback handling.
Complete 8-Handle Resizing: Full perimeter handles ( .rh-nw , .rh-n , .rh-ne , .rh-e , .rh-se , .rh-s , .rh-sw , .rh-w ) allow intuitive stretching in any direction.
Integrated Rotation Stalk: Includes dedicated rotation handle ( .rotate-stick ) allowing arrows to be angled smoothly across 360 degrees.
Synchronous Overlay Binding: Automatically binds window.updateSelectionObserver() upon creation, ensuring amber tip handles and floating quick action toolbars appear immediately without deselecting.
98 Authentic Arrows across 7 Symmetrical Categories
Irregular shapes (such as stepped zigzags and spring coils) were replaced with clean, authentic arrow vectors. Every category is calibrated to exactly 14 styles (2 full rows of 7 in the gallery), eliminating ragged row wraps:
Block & Directional (14 styles): Standard and rounded cardinal arrows, horizontal/vertical doubles, 4-way quads, and diagonal vectors.
Notched & Shaped (14 styles): Notched, pentagon, multi-directional chevrons, stealth profiles, curved swoops, U-turns, and dovetails.
Slender & Precision (14 styles): Needles, diamond tips, surveyor pins, ball pointers, hairline drafting lines, and triangular callouts.
Callout & Stylized (14 styles): Rectangular callouts, archery arrows, wedge comics, barbed arrows, fishtails, rockets, and harpoons.
Process & Infographic (14 styles): Double/triple chevrons, capsule stems, chamfered blocks, forked branches, merged flows, and 90-degree corner flows.
Modern & Aerodynamic (14 styles): Swept wings, supersonic darts, split stems, conical missiles, flared wings, and delta wings.
Hollow & Technical (14 styles): Hollow blocks, open barbs, technical doubles, and engineering dimension markers.
Tip: Resizing an arrow horizontally or vertically stretches only the connecting shaft, ensuring arrowheads never distort or change angle.

title: Charts & Graphs Studio
excerpt: Generate publication-grade native SVG charts, pie charts, donut charts, column graphs, gauges, and radar charts in OpenPublisher with the interactive Chart Studio.
content:
Charts & Graphs Studio
Open Publisher features a dedicated, zero-dependency Charts & Graphs Studio that empowers creators to generate crisp, publication-grade vector visualizations directly on the canvas. Designed from the ground up for publishing excellence, all charts render as pure, scalable SVG objects that maintain razor-sharp clarity at any canvas zoom level and during 300 DPI high-resolution print and PDF export.
Zero External Dependencies: Unlike web applications that embed heavy external charting libraries (such as Chart.js or D3), Open Publisher generates mathematical, lightweight SVG elements natively. This guarantees instant canvas rendering, zero bundle bloat, and total offline reliability.
9 Distinct Chart & Graph Types
The studio provides nine specialized chart architectures tailored for reports, newsletters, resumes, brochures, and commercial publications:

Interactive 3-Panel Chart Studio Modal
Clicking Chart on the Insert ribbon tab (or right-clicking the canvas and choosing Chart or Graph... ) opens the Chart Studio modal ( window.showChartModal() ). Engineered with an expanded 980px zero-scrollbar layout, all data fields and controls fit comfortably without horizontal overflow:
Left Panel (Chart Selector & Importer): Browse the nine visual chart categories with FontAwesome preview badges. Includes a dedicated fast paste prompt to import tabular datasets in seconds.
Center Panel (Data Grid Editor): Configure title text, toggle chart legends on or off, toggle value labels, and edit data rows. Each row features a native color swatch picker, category label text input, themed number stepper, and quick row deletion button.
Right Panel (Real-Time SVG Preview): Instant WYSIWYG feedback updating simultaneously as numbers are adjusted, rows are added, or colors are customized.
Themed Number Stepper Controls ( .chart-modern-spinner )
To provide effortless numerical adjustments, the data grid utilizes custom themed number steppers styled with Open Publisher's signature teal colorway and stacked up/down chevrons matching the ribbon font size picker:

Fast Spreadsheet Tabular Import
You can paste data directly from spreadsheet software including Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc. Click Import CSV / TSV in the left panel, paste tab-delimited or comma-separated rows, and Open Publisher automatically parses category names and numeric values into the live editor table.
Canvas Interaction, Smart Snapping & Double-Click Re-Editing
Charts operate as first-class canvas elements ( .pub-element[data-type="chart"] ):
Freeform Scaling & Rotation: Scale using corner or edge bounding-box handles. Vector paths recalculate in real time to maintain razor-sharp stroke weights and proportional typography.
Smart Snapping & Guides: Snaps cleanly to margin guides, column guides, ruler guides, and adjacent document objects.
Double-Click Re-Editing: Double-clicking any chart on the canvas immediately reopens the Chart Studio with that chart's existing dataset pre-loaded for rapid updates.
Full Undo & Redo: Every chart insertion, dataset change, and repositioning action registers on the history stack ( pushHistory() ), allowing instant reversal with Ctrl+Z .
Attribute Serialization: All chart configuration data is stored in the data-chart-config attribute, ensuring complete preservation across page switches, auto-saves, and .opub file exports.
Custom Hex & RGB Color Picker in Chart Studio (v5.18.5)
Corporate reports and infographics frequently require brand-accurate colors rather than generic chart defaults. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.18.5 , the Charts & Graphs Studio integrates a full custom color picker directly inside the data editor table:
The Custom Color Picker inside the Charts & Graphs Studio data editor in OpenPublisher v5.18.5.
Per-Slice & Per-Bar Color Selection: Click the color swatch next to any data row in the Chart Studio editor to open the color picker. You can choose from theme palettes or input exact Hex/RGB codes.
Live Chart Synchronization: The SVG vector pie slices, donut rings, or bar columns update immediately on the canvas as you adjust color sliders.
Preserved Serialization: Custom colors are stored permanently in the publication XML/JSON manifest, ensuring charts re-open with exact brand hues.

title: Customizing Shapes and Text with the Format Properties Window
excerpt: Learn how to use Open Publisher
content:
Customizing Shapes and Text with the Format Properties Window
While the ribbon provides quick access to common styles and colors, advanced design projects frequently require precise numeric control over fills, border weights, drop shadows, and object dimensions. Open Publisher features a modernized, Format Properties dialog that consolidates all object attributes into a clean, easy-to-navigate modal with real-time canvas previewing.
⚙️ Format Properties Window for Shapes and Text
Easily switch between Fill, Line, Shadow, and Geometry with real-time live preview updates on your publication canvas.
Opening the Format Properties Dialog
You can access the dialog whenever an editable shape, text box, Smart Arrow, or WordArt object is selected:
Context Menu: Right-click any shape or text container on the canvas and choose Format Properties... from the popup menu.
Ribbon Launcher: On the Format or Text Box Tools tab, click the small dialog launcher icon in the bottom-right corner of the Shape Styles group.
Styling Controls
The dialog organizes styling properties into clearly categorized chunks:
Fill: Configure Solid Fills, Linear Gradients, or Pattern Fills. Adjust color stops, gradient angles, and overall opacity percentage with fine-increment sliders.
Line & Border: Set outline color, exact stroke thickness in points or pixels, dashed or dotted line styles, corner cap joins (round, miter, or bevel), and corner radius.
Shadow & Glow: Add visual depth with directional drop shadows and soft radiant glows. Configure blur radius, offset distance, shadow angle, and color opacity with dedicated sliders.
Size & Geometry: Review and adjust exact width and height dimensions in inches or millimeters, lock aspect ratios, enter rotation angles, and set internal padding margins for text boxes.
Live Canvas Updates & Clean Modern Design
The Format Properties window features real-time interactivity. As you adjust sliders or pick new color swatches inside the dialog, your object on the canvas updates immediately in the background, allowing you to evaluate visual balance without having to repeatedly close and reopen the window.
The dialog layout utilizes a clean white body with subtle neutral dividers, matching standard Open Publisher windows and ensuring color swatches appear true-to-life without ambient color cast.
Tip: You can double-click any slider handle in the Format Properties dialog to quickly reset that attribute back to its default value.

title: Inserting & Formatting Shapes
excerpt: Insert over 200 scalable vector shapes in Open Publisher and format them with solid colours, gradients, textured patterns, and opacity controls for any layout.
content:
Inserting & Formatting Shapes
Open Publisher includes a library of over 200 vector shapes built entirely from mathematical SVG paths. Unlike raster images, these shapes are infinitely scalable - they remain perfectly crisp at any zoom level, any document size, and in any PDF or print output. Shapes support full colour fills, borders, shadows, glows, opacity, 3D rotation, and custom point editing.
The SVG Shape Library
To insert a shape:
Go to the Insert ribbon tab and click the Shape drop-down arrow.
Browse the categorised gallery and click a shape to insert it at a default size on the canvas.
Resize and position it as needed.
Shapes are grouped by category:
Basic Geometry - Rectangle, Ellipse, Triangle, Diamond, Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Parallelogram
Arrows & Lines - Single arrow, Double arrow, Curved arrow, Hollow arrows (Flat stop, Diamond head)
Callouts & Speech - Rectangular callout, Cloud callout, Oval callout, Thought bubble
Stars & Bursts - 4-point, 5-point, 6-point, 8-point, 12-point, 16-point, 24-point, 32-point stars, Sunburst
Hearts & Shields - Heart, Shield, Cross, Fleur-de-lis
Banners & Ribbons - Horizontal banner, Diagonal ribbon, Curved banner
Flow & Process - Process box, Decision diamond, Cylinder, Database
Frames & Borders - Rounded rectangle, Snip corners, Diagonal corner
Tip: For the fastest access to a shape’s formatting options, simply double-click any vector shape on the canvas. The Format Properties dialog opens immediately without requiring navigation through the ribbon.
Shape Fill: Solid Colour & No Fill
With a shape selected, use the Shape Fill button in the Drawing Tools ribbon (the paint bucket icon with a colour swatch) to apply a solid fill colour. Clicking it opens the colour picker.
To make a shape hollow (transparent interior with only a border visible), open the Format Properties dialog and select the No Fill (Transparent) option.
Shape Fill: Gradient Fills
Open Publisher ships with a suite of pre-calculated gradient presets and a custom two-colour tool. To apply a gradient:
Double-click the shape to open Format Properties .
Choose Gradient from the Fill dropdown.
Select a preset or use the custom two-colour tool.
Choose a direction: Linear , Diagonal , or Radial .
Click OK .
Available gradient presets include:
Gold, Chrome, Bronze, Silver - Metallic reflective gradients.
Sunset - Warm orange-to-pink blend.
Ocean - Cool blue-to-teal blend.
Gradients are applied as native SVG <linearGradient> or <radialGradient> definitions, meaning they scale perfectly and are fully print-safe.
Shape Fill: Textured Patterns
Eight distinct texture styles can be applied to any vector shape or text box from the Format Properties dialog:
Tiny Dots - Fine, dense dot matrix.
Polka Dots - Large, evenly spaced circles.
Diagonal Lines - 45° hatching lines.
Vertical Lines - Straight vertical striping.
Horizontal Lines - Straight horizontal striping.
Crosshatch - Overlapping diagonal lines forming a grid.
Checkerboard - High-contrast alternating squares.
Square Grid - Uniform grid overlay.
A Pattern Scale slider in the Format Properties dialog lets you scale textures from 20% (very fine and dense) up to 300% (very large and bold). Textures are rendered as native SVG <pattern> definitions, ensuring they remain infinitely sharp at any zoom level.
Object Transparency (Opacity)
The Format Properties dialog includes an Opacity slider that controls the transparency of the entire object - from fully opaque (100%) down to completely invisible (0%). This applies universally to the whole element, including its fill, borders, and any pattern or gradient applied.
This is ideal for creating semi-opaque overlay effects, letting underlying images, text, and page backgrounds softly show through your design elements.
Note: When you click OK, the transparency is automatically “baked” into the element as a PNG image, ensuring overlays render flawlessly in PDF exports and print output without layering artefacts.

title: Interactive Progress Bars

content:
Interactive Progress Bars
Open Publisher introduces full-featured interactive Progress Bars designed specifically for CVs, resumes, skill demonstrations, project progress indicators, reports, and infographics. Progress bars can be placed anywhere on canvas, resized, customized, and printed with 100% WYSIWYG parity.
Complete Layout Engine Integration: Unlike static shape approximations, Open Publisher progress bars are interactive objects featuring draggable handles, mousewheel adjustments, categorized presets, and dedicated Drawing Tools ribbon routing.
71 Curated Styles Across 5 Distinct Categories
Creators can choose from an expansive catalog of 71 distinct handcrafted styles organized into five clear categories:
