Mathematical Seamless Diagonal Striped Engine
Standard CSS repeating-linear-gradient implementations suffer from severe rendering defects when exported to canvas, PDF, or print spoolers, causing visible horizontal banding, saw-tooth distortion, and seam artifacts. Open Publisher resolves this with a specialized mathematical pattern tile engine:
Periodic Polygon Geometry: Generates seamless offscreen PNG pattern tiles with exact periodic boundary coordinates where horizontal and vertical tile periods equal \(W = ext{round}( ext{stripeWidth} imes \sqrt{2})\) on an \(S imes S\) canvas (\(S = 2W\)).
Linear 45-Degree Continuity: Stripes advance by exactly 1 pixel horizontally for every pixel vertically, ensuring 100% straightness across thin (10px), standard (18px), thick (26px-36px), and monumental (48px-56px) bars.
Pre-Flight Normalization: The print engine automatically normalizes pattern URLs prior to rasterization and printing, ensuring zero artifact degradation in exported files.
Monumental Thickness Options & Container Auto-Expansion

Direct Dragging, Mousewheel & Compact Quick-Toolbar
Direct Handle Dragging: Click and drag the circular thumb handle along the track to adjust percentage continuously from 0% to 100%.
Mousewheel Adjustment: Turn your mouse scroll wheel while hovering or selecting the bar to increment or decrement the percentage by 1% (or 5% when holding Shift).
Compact 2-Row Floating Toolbar: Measuring under 380px wide, the floating toolbar provides immediate access to percentage sliders, exact number inputs, categorized style pickers, custom color pickers, and a dedicated "Designer" button.
Drawing Tools Ribbon Tab: Selecting a progress bar routes directly to the contextual Drawing Tools ribbon tab ( #ribbon-format-shape ), providing access to shape styling, drop shadow, glow, rotation, arrange, and the Bar Designer studio.

title: Resizing, Rotating & 3D Effects
excerpt: Resize, rotate, flip and apply full 3D perspective effects to shapes and text boxes in Open Publisher, with non-destructive smart object editing built in.
content:
Resizing, Rotating & 3D Effects
Open Publisher gives you precise control over how shapes and text boxes are sized and oriented on the canvas, from simple resize modifiers and flip controls through to a full 3D rotation engine with non-destructive smart object editing.
Resizing Shapes
Open Publisher provides several resize modifiers when dragging a shape’s handles:
Drag a resize handle - Scales the shape from the opposite edge (standard behaviour).
Shift + drag corner handle - Scales proportionally, locking the aspect ratio.
Ctrl / Cmd + drag any handle - Scales outward from the exact centre point of the shape.
Ctrl / Cmd + Shift + drag corner - Proportionally scales from the centre - the most precise resize modifier available.
Shapes dynamically stretch to fill their bounding boxes in both width and height, giving you complete freedom over proportions for horizontal bars, tall columns, wide banners, and any non-square layout. Borders intelligently recalculate their thickness when stretching to extreme proportions, maintaining a uniform and even border on all sides.
Precise Size Controls
The Drawing Tools contextual ribbon includes a Size group with Width and Height spinners and a Lock Aspect Ratio checkbox - identical to the Picture Tools size controls. Enter exact pixel values for perfectly precise element dimensions.
Rotation & Flipping Controls
The Rotate dropdown in the Arrange group is available on all contextual ribbons (Drawing Tools, Text Box Tools, Picture Tools, and WordArt Tools) and includes the following options:
Rotate Right 90° - Snaps the element clockwise by 90°.
Rotate Left 90° - Snaps the element counter-clockwise by 90°.
Flip Horizontal - Mirrors the element left-to-right.
Flip Vertical - Mirrors the element top-to-bottom.
More Rotation Options… - Opens a numeric dialog where you can type any specific degree value (e.g. 45, -15, 270). Values above 360° are handled correctly.
For freehand rotation, drag the green circular rotation handle that appears above a selected element.
3D Rotation Engine
Open Publisher features a full 3D rotation engine for shapes and text boxes. Using the Format Properties dialog, you can rotate elements along the X, Y, and Z axes and adjust the depth perspective to create modern 3D aesthetic effects.
To apply 3D rotation:
Double-click a shape, or select it and click Format Properties in the ribbon.
Navigate to the 3D Rotation section.
Adjust the X , Y , and Z axis sliders and the Perspective depth value.
Click OK .
Because browsers cannot reliably print live CSS 3D transforms, the engine automatically flattens the 3D object into a high-quality PNG the moment you click OK. A custom pixel-scanning algorithm tightly crops the baked image around the actual 3D footprint and recalculates the bounding box, so your resize handles perfectly wrap the visual edges of the rotated shape.
Non-Destructive Smart Object Editing
The flattened PNG stores the original live HTML, CSS, and 3D parameters in a hidden data attribute. Double-clicking the PNG instantly restores the live 3D element and reopens the Format Properties dialog, allowing you to adjust any setting and re-render.
If you click Cancel , the previous PNG is restored from memory - no re-rasterization required. A teal loading spinner appears while the 3D projection and smart-trimming calculations run.

title: Smart Arrow Color Picker & Tip Handle Drag Precision Engine
excerpt: Customize arrow styling with Open Publisher
content:
Smart Arrow Color Picker & Tip Handle Drag Precision Engine
Smart Arrows provide publication designers with parametric, responsive directional graphics whose stems stretch dynamically while arrowhead proportions remain crisp. In earlier builds, two subtle interactions required refinement: clicking the Fill or Outline color buttons on the floating Action Toolbar failed to open the color picker due to DOM teardown on mouseup, and dragging the orange arrowhead tip handle on left, up, or down arrows inverted mouse movement (moving right shifted the handle left). Version 5.6.6 delivered a comprehensive precision update, restoring instant color picker access and guaranteeing 1:1 directional tracking across all arrow orientations.
🏹 Smart Arrow Floating HUD Color Swatches & Directional Tip Drag Handle Clicking Fill or Outline opens the palette instantly, while the orange junction handle moves in lockstep with the mouse.
1:1 Directional Handle Drag Precision
When arrows point in directions other than right (such as Left, Up, Down, Double, or Quad), drag delta calculations must respect spatial orientation:
Early SVG Style Inspection: getArrowTipInfo() now inspects child <svg> attributes during element creation, ensuring initial handle directions ( left , right , up , down ) configure properly from the first render.
Dynamic Direction Evaluation: Rather than relying on stale closure variables, mousemove handlers read the active handle direction attribute dynamically, ensuring dragging right moves the handle right and dragging left moves it left.
Flip & Rotation Invariance: Evaluates horizontal ( data-scaleX ) and vertical ( data-scaleY ) flip transforms to guarantee handles track cursor motion accurately on flipped arrows.
HUD Slider Parity: Moving the tip slider in the floating toolbar and dragging the on-canvas junction handle produce identical mathematical results and stay in sync.
Restored Fill & Outline Color Pickers
Clicking color buttons on the floating Action Toolbar now reliably displays the Custom Color Picker:
In-Place Overlay Updates: renderSelectionOverlays() detects existing arrow controls and updates dimensions in place ( updateArrowTipOverlay ) rather than destroying DOM nodes on mouseup, allowing click events to fire normally.
Fill Color Button: Clicking Fill opens the color picker anchored directly to the HUD swatch, immediately updating arrow fill and HUD indicator upon color selection.
Outline Color Button: Clicking Outline adjusts the border stroke dynamically while preserving line thickness.
Right-Click Transparent Toggle: Right-clicking either button toggles transparent No Fill or No Outline cleanly.
Tip: Right-click the Outline swatch on the arrow toolbar to quickly remove borders and create clean flat arrows.

title: Smart Arrows Engine: Parametric Stem Stretching & Tip Controls
excerpt: Create directional arrows that stretch to any length without arrowhead distortion, featuring on-canvas tip resizing and zoom-invariant UI.
content:
Smart Arrows Engine: Parametric Stem Stretching & Tip Controls
Flowcharts, technical schematics, and marketing callouts rely heavily on directional arrows to guide reader attention. In traditional vector drawing programs, resizing an arrow element scales all path coordinates uniformly, causing arrowheads to become unnaturally stretched, flattened, or bloated. Version 5.2.4 introduced Open Publisher's dedicated Smart Arrows Engine: a parametric vector architecture where element resizing stretches only the stem or shaft while keeping arrowheads perfectly proportioned.
🏹 Smart Arrows Gallery & Parametric Tip Drag Handle
Drag arrow stems to any length without distorting arrowhead proportions, and adjust tip sizes with on-canvas amber handles.
The Categorized 29-Style Arrow Gallery
Located directly adjacent to the Shapes menu in the Insert ribbon tab, the Arrows button opens a 7-column gallery organized across four functional categories:
Block Arrows: Right Arrow, Left Arrow, Up Arrow, Down Arrow, Horizontal Double Arrow, Vertical Double Arrow, and 4-Way Quad Arrow.
Notched & Shaped: Notched Right, Notched Left, Pentagon Arrow, Chevron Arrow, Stealth Arrow, Curved Swoop, and U-Turn Loop.
Slender & Precision: Slender Right, Slender Left, Slender Up, Slender Down, Needle Arrow, Diamond Tip, Ball Base Pointer, and Callout Arrow.
Hollow & Technical: Hollow Right, Hollow Left, Hollow Double, Open Barb, Technical Open Left, Technical Double, and Dimension Marker.
Parametric Stem Stretching & Cross-Section Scaling
Traditional vector scaling distorts geometry because width multipliers affect every point equally. Open Publisher's parametric engine calculates geometry dynamically:
Stem-Only Vector Calculation: Dragging resize handles recalculates only shaft vertices ( stemTop , stemBottom , stemLen ). Arrowhead points, barb angles, and wing cuts stay locked to their designed aspect ratio.
Proportional Cross-Section Scaling: For horizontal arrows, default head width evaluates to Math.round(height * 0.7) ; for vertical arrows, Math.round(width * 0.7) . Expanding arrow thickness naturally scales the arrowhead without squashing.
Interactive Tip Customization & Zoom Invariance
Selecting any Smart Arrow displays an intuitive on-canvas tuning overlay:
Inner Tip Sub-Selection Box: A dashed amber box highlights the arrowhead tip with a live dimension badge (for example, Tip: 120px ).
On-Canvas Amber Drag Handle: Positioned at the stem/tip junction. Dragging the handle slides the junction along the arrow's axis, updating geometry at 60 FPS. Rotated arrows automatically transform mouse deltas into local coordinate space.
Zoom-Invariant Optical Scaling: Overlays and handles scale inversely with canvas magnification ( --arrow-ui-scale: 1 / zoom ). Controls remain crisp, comfortable, and easy to grab whether viewed at 35% or 200% zoom.
Tip: Custom tip ratios are saved in document metadata, ensuring arrows retain their customized appearance across saves and exports.

title: Smart Arrows Floating Action Toolbar & Responsive Controls
excerpt: Style arrows directly on canvas with Open Publisher
content:
Smart Arrows Floating Action Toolbar & Responsive Controls
Creating complex diagrams, process charts, and infographic callouts requires rapid access to styling controls without constant menu navigation. Version 5.3.0 introduced a dedicated Two-Tier Floating Action Toolbar for Smart Arrows that docks directly below selected elements. Featuring direct color pickers, tip size sliders, and an innovative outline thickness control supporting mouse wheel scrolling down to 0px, designers can style directional graphics with unmatched speed.
🎯 Compact Two-Tier Floating Action Toolbar on Canvas
The compact 320px toolbar docks to selected arrows, offering tip sizing, live color swatches, and line thickness tuning.
The Mobile-Optimized Two-Tier Layout
In initial prototypes, arranging all arrow controls horizontally produced an unwieldy 550px toolbar that overflowed on laptops and tablets. Version 5.3.0 introduced a compact two-tier architecture measuring only 320px wide:
Top Tier (Tip Sizing & Colors): Houses the interactive tip size slider, a vertical divider, and circular live color swatches for Fill and Outline.
Bottom Tier (Outline Thickness): Separated by a clean hairline divider, the lower tier contains the outline width icon, minus/plus single-pixel steppers, a continuous range slider, and a live pixel readout.
Intelligent Viewport Docking: When an arrow is near the bottom edge of the canvas, the toolbar automatically flips to dock cleanly above the element, preventing clipping.
Direct Color Pickers & Theme Decoupling
Styling arrows no longer requires opening the Page Design or Format Shape ribbon tabs:
Live Swatch Pickers: Left-clicking either the Fill or Outline swatch opens the full Open Publisher color modal (HSV spectrum canvas, theme palette, hex/RGB inputs, and eyedropper).
Quick Transparency Toggle: Right-clicking either color button instantly toggles transparent mode ( none ), displayed by a red diagonal strike-through on the swatch.
Theme Clobber Protection: Setting a custom color removes theme scheme attributes, ensuring subsequent global theme switches do not overwrite custom diagram branding.
Outline Thickness Control with 0px Scroll Support
Fine-tuning outline width is fluid and intuitive:
Multi-Modal Input: Adjust thickness via the range slider (0px to 24px), single-pixel -1px / +1px stepper buttons, or mouse wheel scrolling.
Zero-Pixel Stroke Removal: Scrolling down to 0px completely removes the stroke ( stroke="none" , stroke-width="0" ) for clean, borderless solid vector shapes.
Automatic Stroke Restoration: Scrolling back up to 1px or higher automatically restores the previous outline color from element memory.
Tip: Hover over the thickness section of the floating toolbar and roll your mouse wheel up or down for rapid, tactile border adjustments.

title: Smart Arrows Stroke Bleed & Print Overflow Precision
excerpt: Prevent flat clipped edges on thick arrow borders during print and PDF export with dynamic stroke bleed padding and negative coordinate translation.
content:
Smart Arrows Stroke Bleed & Print Overflow Precision
Digital publishing workflows demand that on-screen document designs translate with 100% precision onto physical paper and exported PDF files. Following the introduction of the Smart Arrows Engine in version 5.3.0, users designing directional arrows with thick borders (such as 16px to 24px outlines) discovered that arrowheads and corner joins were occasionally truncated with flat, chopped edges in printed output. Version 5.3.2 resolved this issue by implementing dynamic stroke bleed padding and coordinate translation in the print rasterizer.
🖨️ High-DPI Arrow Print Rasterization with Stroke Bleed Margin
Arrow outlines with rounded corner joins and end caps print with full fidelity without flat edge clipping.
The Geometry of Centred Vector Strokes
Investigation revealed why the on-screen canvas rendered strokes smoothly while print rasterizers clipped them:
Centred Stroke Expansion: In SVG rendering, vector strokes expand symmetrically outward and inward from the path geometry. For a 24px stroke, the outline extends 12px beyond the path bounds. At sharp corners (such as arrow tip vertices and barb wings), rounded joins ( stroke-linejoin="round" ) project up to 1.5x the stroke width beyond nominal boundaries.
Canvas Bounding Box Discrepancy: In the live editor, the parent container uses overflow: visible , allowing strokes to render beyond the dotted selection box. However, during print preparation, bakeSmartArrowForPrint() created an offscreen canvas strictly sized to [w * scaleFactor] x [h * scaleFactor] .
Hard Canvas Clipping: Because HTML5 2D canvases hard-clip any pixel coordinates below zero or beyond canvas dimensions, the outer half of the stroke was truncated into unsightly flat edges in printouts and PDFs.
Dynamic Bleed Padding & Coordinate Translation
Version 5.3.2 updated the print rasterizer in extensions/print-engine.js :
Dynamic Padding Calculation: Evaluates active stroke width and applies a safety margin: pad = Math.ceil(Math.max(20, strokeWidth * 1.5 + 4)) . For a 24px border, this provides 40px of transparent safety bleed on all four sides.
Canvas Expansion & Coordinate Translation: The offscreen raster canvas expands by pad * 2 , and the 2D context executes ctx.translate(pad, pad) . Any corner join or cap extending into negative coordinates lands safely in the transparent bleed margin.
Negative Offset Positioning: The resulting baked image is inserted with top: -pad and left: -pad . Because -pad + pad = 0px , the vector arrow aligns with 100% subpixel precision to original canvas positions.
Asynchronous Pre-Print Decoding: The print engine awaits complete image decoding via loadImageStrict() before triggering final page rasterization, eliminating race conditions.
Tip: You can safely apply heavy decorative outlines (up to 24px) to Smart Arrows with full confidence that exported PDFs and printouts will preserve round caps and crisp corners.

title: The Drawing Engine
excerpt: Use Open Publisher's built-in drawing engine to sketch freehand with a pencil, brush, or spray paint tool, annotate images, and export print-safe transparent PNGs.
content:
The Drawing Engine
Open Publisher includes a built-in freehand drawing engine for annotating documents, sketching layouts, or drawing directly over images. All finished drawings are automatically exported as transparent, print-safe PNGs and placed directly onto your document page.
Accessing the Drawing Tools
To open the drawing tools:
Go to the Insert ribbon tab.
Locate the Drawing group at the far right of the ribbon.
Select a tool from the group to begin drawing.
Four drawing tools are available:
Pencil - Classic, aliased pixel-perfect strokes for sharp, solid lines.
Brush - Anti-aliased paintbrush with rounded caps for smooth, organic strokes.
Spray Paint - Authentically scatters dots within a radius around your cursor for texture and shading effects. Radius and density scale with the brush size slider.
Eraser - Wipes away pixels from your drawing.
Brush Size & Colour
A Brush Size slider spanning the Drawing group controls brush size dynamically from 1px to 50px. This also mathematically scales the Spray Paint dot radius and density.
Use the Colour button in the Drawing group to set the active drawing colour before or during your drawing session.
Undo
Press Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z while drawing, or click the Undo button in the ribbon, to instantly erase your last stroke.
Finishing a Drawing
Click anywhere outside the drawing canvas to exit drawing mode.
OpenPublisher will then automatically:
Scans the entire canvas and calculates the exact bounding box of your artwork.
Crops away all empty transparent space.
Exports a transparent, print-safe PNG and places it directly onto your document page.
Editing a Drawing
Double-click any finished drawing on the canvas to restore it to the full-screen drawing canvas with all raw layer data intact, allowing seamless re-editing without any pixel degradation.
Drawing Over Images
Select any image on the canvas and click Edit in the Picture Tools ribbon. The drawing engine overlays the canvas at the image’s exact coordinates, letting you annotate, spray-paint, or sketch directly on top of any photo or clipart in your document.

title: Special Characters, Typographic Symbols & Glyph Palette
excerpt: Master the insertion of mathematical operators, international currency symbols, typographic punctuation, and whitespace glyphs within Open Publisher.
content:
Special Characters, Typographic Symbols & Glyph Palette
Professional publication layout demands access to typographic punctuation, international currency markers, and mathematical operators that do not exist on standard physical keyboards. While casual computer users often resort to copying symbols from external web pages or memorizing four-digit numerical Alt-codes, Open Publisher provides a dedicated Special Characters and Glyph Palette integrated directly into its text formatting suite. This allows authors and graphic designers to insert precise typographic characters with exact font matching and line height preservation.
🔣 Typographic Symbols & Special Characters Palette
Access international currency marks, typographic punctuation, and mathematical operators directly from the Insert ribbon.
Accessing the Symbol Palette
The Symbol Palette can be opened at any time while editing text:
Ribbon Location: Click the Insert tab and select Symbols > Special Characters to open the interactive character grid.
International Currency Symbols: Insert major global currency notations including Euro (€), British Pound (£), Japanese/Chinese Yen (¥), Indian Rupee (₹), and Cent (¢) with correct baseline alignment.
Legal & Commercial Marks: One-click insertion for Copyright (©), Registered Trademark (®), Trademark (™), Service Mark (℠), and Section (§) symbols.
Mathematical Operators: Insert precision mathematical signs including Multiplication (×), Division (÷), Plus-Minus (±), Not Equal (≠), Almost Equal (≈), Less Than or Equal (≤), Greater Than or Equal (≥), and Infinity (∞).
Whitespace & Flow Control Glyphs
Precision typography often depends on invisible flow characters to prevent awkward line breaks:
Non-Breaking Space ( ): Binds words, numbers, and units together so they never separate across a line wrap (for example, keeping "100 km" or "Figure 3" on the same line).
Zero-Width Space (U+200B): Marks invisible potential break points within long URLs, file paths, or complex compounds without displaying an unwanted hyphen.
Soft Hyphen (­): Specifies a discretionary hyphenation point that only appears if the word falls at the end of a line.
Caret Insertion & Font Fallback Resilience
When a symbol is selected from the palette, it is inserted directly at the active text caret, inheriting the current font family, font size, weight, and color. If an active font lacks a specific mathematical or rare currency glyph, Open Publisher's font rendering engine triggers system Unicode fallback without distorting text frame dimensions.
Tip: You can quickly insert a non-breaking space inside any active text box by pressing Ctrl+Shift+Space.
Unicode & Typographic Mojibake Restoration
Version 5.8.6 resolved character corruption (mojibake) across special typographic glyphs. Curly quotes (both single and double), em and en dashes, bullet points, and degree symbols imported from external documents or pasted from web pages retain their exact Unicode UTF-8 encoding across all document save and export cycles.

title: Symbols
excerpt: Insert special characters, currency signs, maths symbols, arrows and accented letters in Open Publisher using the built-in Symbol modal with live search and preview.
content:
Symbols
For special characters that would otherwise require memorising Unicode codes or copying from an external site, Open Publisher provides a rich Insert Symbol modal with hundreds of characters, live search, and a recently used tracker.
Inserting a Symbol
To insert a symbol:
Click inside any text box to position your cursor at the point where you want the symbol to appear.
Go to Insert > Symbol (Ω icon in the toolbar).
The Symbol modal opens, grouping hundreds of characters into easy-to-navigate categories (see below).
Use the Search bar to find a symbol by name (for example: “check”, “euro”, or “arrow”).
Click any symbol to insert it instantly at your cursor position.
Symbols are inserted using native execCommand(‘insertText’) , integrating flawlessly into both standard text boxes and advanced Flexbox text blocks.
Symbol Categories
The modal organises hundreds of characters into the following categories:
Common - Copyright ©, trademark ™, registered ®, and frequently used punctuation.
Dashes & Quotes - Em dash, en dash, curly quotes, and ellipsis.
Currency - £, €, ¥, ¢, and more.
Math & Science - ÷, ×, √, π, ∞, and Greek letters.
Arrows - Directional arrows in multiple styles.
Shapes & Stars - Geometric shapes and decorative stars.
Accented Letters - Accented Latin characters for international text.
Recently Used Symbols
The modal automatically tracks your 20 most recently used symbols in browser LocalStorage. They appear in a Recently Used row at the top of the modal every time you open it - your most frequent symbols are always one click away.
Live Preview
Hovering over or clicking any symbol shows its name, character, and Unicode value in a live preview panel at the bottom of the modal, so you can confirm exactly what you are inserting before it goes into your document.

title: Formatting & Managing Cells
excerpt: Master table formatting in Open Publisher. Learn how to resize, merge, and split cells, adjust border thickness and padding, and convert tables to text.
content:
Formatting & Managing Cells Once your table is inserted, Open Publisher provides a comprehensive suite of tools for precise cell manipulation, border styling, and data management. Cell Resizing (Cross-Browser) Open Publisher ships with its own custom Table Cell Resizer that works reliably across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge, bypassing the browsers’ inconsistent native implementations. To resize a row or column: Hover your mouse over any vertical or horizontal dividing line inside the table. The cursor changes to a resize arrow (col-resize or row-resize). Click and drag to adjust the cell width or height. The boundary follows your cursor precisely. Key behaviours: Dimension locking: The moment you grab a border to resize it, all columns and rows in the table have their widths and heights locked to absolute pixel values. This prevents the browser’s layout engine from implicitly resizing other cells and causing unpredictable shifts. Zero-sum resizing: Shrinking column A by 10px and increasing column B by 10px moves the boundary cleanly while leaving all other columns unchanged. Smart drag detection: Clicking the exact border engages the resizer. Clicking in the middle of a cell and dragging engages the multi-cell selection highlighter. Both modes coexist without conflict. Element drag: Hovering over the outer edge of the table (not an inner divider) shows a move cursor, letting you drag the entire table around the page. Merge & Split Cells Merge Cells Click and drag across the cells you want to merge to highlight them. Right-click anywhere within the highlighted boundary. Select Merge Cells from the context menu. The cells collapse into one expanded cell. If the cells contained text, only non-empty cells contribute their content to the merged result - empty cells ( , whitespace,
) are stripped to prevent the merged cell from expanding unexpectedly. Split Cells To split a previously merged cell back into its original grid structure: Right-click inside the merged cell. The context menu detects the rowspan/colspan attributes and offers Split Cells (revert) . Click it. The merged cell immediately pops back into the individual rows and columns it had absorbed, with its layout perfectly restored. Distribute Rows & Columns The Table Layout sidebar contains Distribute Rows and Distribute Columns buttons for making multiple rows or columns exactly equal in size. Full-table distribution: Click anywhere inside the table (with no specific cells highlighted) and press Distribute Columns. All columns in the table are instantly resized to equal widths. Distribute Rows does the same for heights. Targeted distribution: Highlight a specific subset of cells by click-and-dragging across them, then press Distribute Columns. Only those selected columns are redistributed proportionally - the rest of the table is completely untouched. All redistribution uses sub-pixel accuracy and freezes widths/heights to absolute pixel values to prevent unexpected layout shifts. Cell Margins (Padding) The Table Layout sidebar includes a Cell Margins slider (range: 0 - 50px) that controls the internal padding - the whitespace between your text and the cell’s borders. Universal padding: Clicking anywhere in the table (without specific cells highlighted) and adjusting the slider applies padding uniformly across all cells. Targeted padding: Highlight specific cells first, then adjust the slider to apply padding only to those cells. The slider reads the padding of the currently active cell when you click into it, so the control always reflects the real current state. Border Thickness & Colour The Table Design ribbon provides full control over table borders. Targeting: Open Publisher uses a hyper-accurate targeting system: Multi-cell selection: Select multiple cells by dragging, then apply a border colour or thickness to all selected cells at once. Single cell: Click into one cell so the cursor is blinking - changes apply only to that cell. Whole table: Click the outermost edge of the table without focusing a cell - changes apply to the entire table. Maximum thickness: The border thickness slider and spinner accept values up to 64px, allowing you to create bold, ultra-thick grid lines for design purposes. Colour: Use the colour picker in the Table Design ribbon to apply any colour to selected cell borders. All changes are enforced via explicit borderWidth and borderStyle: solid CSS to guarantee correct rendering regardless of border-collapse state. Clear Cell Text To clear the text content from one or more cells without deleting the cells themselves: Right-click inside a cell (or select multiple cells first). Choose Clear Cell Text from the context menu. When multiple cells are selected, the menu option dynamically shows the count: e.g., “Clear Cell Text (4 cells)”. The cells remain structurally intact and fully editable after clearing. The action is registered in the undo history, so Ctrl+Z will restore the cleared text immediately. Line Spacing in Tables The Spacing group within the Table Design ribbon includes the same Line Spacing button available for text boxes. Select one or more cells and click it to set an exact point value for the line height of text within those cells, giving you the same precise typographic control available in text boxes. Convert Table to Text If you need to repurpose structured table data as free-flowing paragraph text, use the Convert Table to Text tool: Select the table (click its outer edge). Access Convert Table to Text from either the Table Design ribbon or the table’s right-click context menu. A dialog appears asking how the extracted text should be separated: Tabs (each cell separated by a tab character), Commas (CSV-style output), Paragraph marks (each cell on its own line), or Custom (type any string to use as the separator). Click OK. The table grid is removed, the cell data is extracted with your chosen separator, and the result appears as a standard, editable text box in the same location. The conversion preserves the element’s resize handles and rotation control. The active ribbon automatically transitions from Table Design to Text Box Tools for a seamless editing handoff.

title: Importing Tabular Data from CSV, TSV & Spreadsheets
excerpt: Discover how to import external CSV, TSV, and spreadsheet data into Open Publisher tables with automatic delimiter parsing and style mapping.
content:
Importing Tabular Data from CSV, TSV & Spreadsheets
Manually typing numerical datasets, inventory catalogs, event schedules, and financial tables cell-by-cell into desktop publishing software is tedious and introduces transcription errors. Open Publisher features a comprehensive tabular data import engine that converts external Comma-Separated Values (CSV), Tab-Separated Values (TSV), and operating system clipboard data directly into beautifully formatted, styled publication tables.
📊 CSV Import Dialog & Column Mapping Preview
Import external CSV data with automatic delimiter detection, header row formatting, and style presets.
Importing CSV & TSV Files
The import assistant simplifies importing structured files from disk:
Ribbon Access: Open the Table Tools tab and select Import Data > From File (CSV/TSV) .
Automatic Delimiter Sniffing: The parser analyzes data buffers to differentiate commas, semicolons, and tabs while respecting quoted strings containing embedded punctuation.
UTF-8 Character Encoding: Full Unicode compliance ensures special characters, currency symbols, and accented international names import without corruption.
Direct Clipboard Spreadsheet Conversion
Users can copy cell ranges directly from Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or LibreOffice Calc and paste them onto the canvas:
Intelligent Table Paste Detection: Open Publisher identifies TSV-formatted clipboard buffers and prompts the user to generate a new table or populate the currently selected cell range.
Auto Column Distribution: Table columns automatically calculate optimal widths based on cell text length while clamping securely to page margin guidelines.
Header Row Formatting & Alternating Fills
During import, checking First Row as Header automatically applies bold typographic hierarchy, contrasting background shading, and bottom border accents. Enabling Banded Rows applies alternating zebra fills to enhance reading comfort across dense rows.
Tip: You can sort table rows alphabetically or numerically at any time by selecting a column and clicking Sort Ascending or Sort Descending.

title: Inserting & Selecting Tables
excerpt: Learn how to create and manage tables in Open Publisher. Explore styled table templates, multi-cell selection, and how to import Excel spreadsheets directly.
content:
Inserting & Selecting Tables
Open Publisher treats tables as interactive, movable canvas elements, offering multiple ways to build grids from scratch or import existing data.
Inserting Tables
Tables can be inserted in several ways:
Standard Grid: Go to Insert > Table and drag over the grid to select the number of rows and columns you want. Release to insert.
Styled Table Templates: Click Insert > Styled Templates to open the 100-layout template browser. Here you can choose from a library of beautifully pre-formatted table designs with colour themes and border styles already applied. Double-click any template to insert it.
Right-Click Context Menu: Right-click anywhere on the canvas and hover over Insert… to access both a standard Table and Styled Tables option directly.
Drag-and-Drop Excel Spreadsheet: Drag a .xlsx or .xls file from your desktop directly onto the canvas. An Import Wizard appears (see below).
Importing Excel Spreadsheets
Open Publisher can import .xlsx and .xls spreadsheets directly onto the canvas by dragging and dropping the file from your desktop. Dropping a spreadsheet triggers the Import Spreadsheet Wizard, which presents two processing modes:
Styled Data Mode (ExcelJS - .xlsx only)
The high-fidelity parser reads through your cells and translates Microsoft’s internal colour codes into standard web CSS. This allows you to perfectly retain:
Background cell colours
Font colours
Bold and italic formatting
Custom text alignment
Raw Data Mode (SheetJS)
A robust secondary parser that extracts the raw text and structure of your spreadsheet without any formatting. Use this if you want a clean, neutral-styled table, or if you are importing a legacy .xls file (which does not support the Styled Data Mode).
The wizard features intelligent safeguards: if you drop a legacy .xls file that does not support styling extraction, the Styled Data Mode option is automatically dimmed to prevent errors. Once imported, the spreadsheet is rendered as a fully interactive, movable, and resizable table object. Because table cells retain their contenteditable attributes, you can click directly into the imported data to fix typos or update values on the fly.
The Table Design Ribbon & Layout Sidebar
Clicking into any table activates the Table Design contextual ribbon at the top of the screen and simultaneously opens the Table Layout sidebar on the right-hand side of the workspace.
Table Design ribbon: Controls borders (colour, thickness), cell shading (fill colour), and table-wide styles.
Table Layout sidebar: Contains insert/delete row and column controls, distribute rows and columns tools, and the 9-way cell alignment grid. The sidebar uses the same frosted-glass, card-based aesthetic as the Image and WordArt formatting panels.
Selection Mechanics
Multi-Cell Selection
Click and drag your mouse across a group of cells to highlight them. Selected cells are shown with a light blue .op-selected-cell highlight. You can then apply border colours, fill colours, or line spacing to the entire highlighted group in one action.
One-Click Select-All Handle
Whenever you hover over any table on the canvas, a small floating four-way arrow handle appears just outside the top-left corner of the table. Clicking this handle instantly highlights every cell in the table and switches your ribbon to the Table Layout and Table Design tools, ready for bulk formatting. The handle disappears automatically when you move the mouse away or start dragging other elements, keeping your workspace uncluttered.

title: Modern Styled Tables Architecture & Solid Cell Fills
excerpt: Discover OpenPublisher modernized table engine featuring solid cell fills, alternating zebra rows, modern design gallery styles, and cell padding controls.
content:
Modern Styled Tables Architecture: Solid Cell Fills & Design Gallery
Tables in desktop publishing must do more than organize raw rows and columns: they need to capture attention, reinforce visual hierarchy, and present data with elegance. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.17.9 , the Modern Styled Tables Architecture transforms table design: introducing rich solid cell fills, alternating zebra row fills, a curated Modern Design Gallery, independent cell border controls, and zero-bleed vector print fidelity.
The Modern Styled Tables Design Gallery and Solid Cell Fill controls in OpenPublisher v5.17.9.
Zero-Bleed Vector Rendering: In v5.17.9, table cell backgrounds and stroke borders are rendered using SVG vector clipping rects. When exported to PDF or printed, there are zero gaps or pixel bleed between adjacent colored cells.
Solid Cell Fill Controls
OpenPublisher provides granular styling options to make key data points stand out:
Header Row Emphasis: Set a distinct primary theme color for table headers with automatic white or high-contrast text adjustment.
Alternating Zebra Striping: Toggle automatic alternating background tints (e.g. crisp white alternating with subtle 4% gray or soft teal) to enhance scanning comfort across dense financial reports.
Individual Cell Shading: Select specific cells, total rows, or comparison columns and apply custom accent fills (e.g. Emerald for positive growth, Coral for overdue items).
Cell Inset & Padding Sliders: Customize top, bottom, and side cell padding so text breathes comfortably without touching borders.
The Modern Design Gallery Presets
Rather than styling tables manually from scratch, you can apply professionally curated table presets directly from the Table Design ribbon:
Style Preset
Design Characteristics
Recommended Use
Corporate Teal
Signature deep teal header row, subtle light mint zebra rows, and crisp hairline dividers.
Annual reports, executive summaries, and business proposals.
Midnight Executive
Charcoal header with golden accent rule, white body rows, and bold totals row.
Financial balance sheets, contracts, and investor decks.
Clean Minimalist
No vertical borders; horizontal accent lines only beneath header and total rows.
Modern magazine articles, restaurant menus, and price lists.
Pastel Invoice
Soft warm background tint with rounded outer table container and padded cells.
Invoices, service estimates, and event schedules.
How to Insert & Style a Table
Go to Insert > Table and drag across the grid picker to specify initial rows and columns.
Click inside the table to reveal the contextual Table Design and Table Layout ribbon tabs.
In the Table Design gallery, click any style thumbnail to re-theme your entire table instantly.
To color specific cells, highlight the target cells and click the Shading paint bucket icon in the ribbon.
Use the Zebra Striping checkbox to toggle alternating rows on or off.
Related Articles:
- Creating & Customizing Tables in OpenPublisher
- Merging & Splitting Table Cells
- Charts & Graphs Studio Guide

title: Multi-Cell Table Formatting
excerpt: Quickly apply text formatting, alignment, and colours to an entire table at once using Open Publisher's Select All Cells tool and multi-cell formatting engine.
content:
Multi-Cell Table Formatting
When working with large data grids, complex schedules, or detailed financial reports, formatting each cell individually can be incredibly tedious and time-consuming. To streamline your workflow and keep your designs consistent, Open Publisher features a powerful, high-performance bulk-formatting engine. This allows you to apply text alignments, fonts, typography styles, and colours to multiple table cells simultaneously, completely eliminating repetitive manual clicking.
Selecting Multiple Cells
To format an entire table at once, you first need to select all of its active cells. Open Publisher provides two quick methods to achieve this,
allowing you to choose the one that best fits your current workflow:
The Green Cross Handle - Click the green cross icon that appears at the top-left corner of the table’s bounding box when it is selected. This is usually the fastest method for quick, visual layout edits.
Context Menu - Right-click anywhere inside an active table and choose Select All Cells from the dropdown menu. This is highly convenient if your cursor is already active inside a specific cell and you don’t want to move your mouse away.
Applying Bulk Formatting
Once multiple cells (or the entire table) are selected and highlighted, any text-formatting action you trigger will cascade across all highlighted cells simultaneously. For example:
Clicking Center Align from either the quick floating text toolbar or the main Home Ribbon will instantly center the text horizontally in every single selected cell.
Clicking the 3×3 alignment grid located in the Table Design sidebar allows you to dictate both the horizontal and vertical alignment (such as middle-center or bottom-right) for the entire table in one single click.
Applying typography changes - such as toggling Bold , changing the master font family, resizing the text, or adjusting the font colour - will dynamically update all selected cells in a rapid, seamless sequence to ensure visual uniformity.
Smart Cursor Restoration
Applying sweeping changes to large tables in some software can leave you wondering where your cursor disappeared to. After the bulk-formatting action is complete, Open Publisher’s editor safely and automatically restores your blinking cursor directly to the top-left cell of your selection. This thoughtful detail ensures you can immediately continue typing, tabbing, or navigating your grid using your keyboard without ever losing your place.

title: Table Spellchecker & Context Menu Proofing Integration
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher brings full spellchecking and contextual proofing to table cells with seamless right-click suggestions and text range extraction.
content:
Table Spellchecker & Context Menu Proofing Integration
Tables provide essential structure for presenting tabular information: financial balance sheets, product comparison matrices, event itineraries, and price schedules. While standard text boxes in Open Publisher have long featured comprehensive spellchecking and right-click suggestion menus, table cells historically operated in an isolated contextual evaluation branch. While misspelled words inside cells displayed red wavy underlines, right-clicking on them only presented structural table tools without proofing suggestions. Version 4.19.1 resolved this gap by hoisting word extraction and integrating the proofing suggestion interface natively into table context menus.
📊 Table Cell Context Menu with Spellcheck Suggestions
Right-clicking a misspelled word inside any table cell displays spelling suggestions right above table editing tools.
Text-Range Extraction Across Table Cells
Bringing proofing suggestions into table elements required unifying word extraction across editable DOM structures:
Hoisted Word Extraction: In ui/menus.js , word-extraction logic was previously scoped strictly to standard text boxes and WordArt elements. The function was rewritten and hoisted ( extractWordFromRange ) to evaluate globally across all text-editable blocks, including table cells ( [contenteditable="true"] inside <td> and <th> ).
Caret Hit-Testing: When the user right-clicks inside a table cell, the context menu builder performs pixel-precise hit-testing at the cursor position, identifying the targeted word and verifying its proofing status.
Context Menu Suggestion Hierarchy
The right-click menu seamlessly balances proofing suggestions with table management tools:
Top-Level Suggestion Placement: When a misspelled word is right-clicked inside a table cell, suggestion buttons ( #spell-check-results ) render prominently at the very top of the contextual menu, directly above table manipulation commands.
Integrated Table Commands: Standard table operations ("Insert Row Above", "Insert Row Below", "Insert Column Left", "Insert Column Right", "Delete Row", "Delete Column", "Table Properties...") remain immediately accessible directly beneath the proofing suggestions.
One-Click Word Replacement: Clicking any spelling suggestion swaps the misspelled word in place within the table cell, preserving cell background colors, borders, and column widths.
Full Table Proofing Workflow Parity
Proofing inside tables works in complete harmony with general document proofing:
Continuous Cell Proofing: The proofing scanner automatically analyzes text as you type across table cells, painting crisp wavy underlines for misspelled words.
Keyboard Navigation Flow: Pressing Tab to advance to the next cell or Shift+Tab to return to previous cells preserves active proofing highlights without flicker.
Tip: You can highlight text across multiple table cells to check word count and character statistics in the Review tab.

title: Adding Custom Templates
excerpt: Learn how to easily add your own custom .opub templates to the Open Publisher gallery when self-hosting, using the template-index.json configuration file.
content:
Adding Custom Templates
If you are self-hosting Open Publisher, you can add your own custom templates to the Publication Templates Gallery . Because templates use a modular architecture, you can add as many as you like without ever needing to modify the core JavaScript bundle.
Step 1: Create your .opub File
Create a new publication in the editor and design your template.
Export your work and save it as an .opub file.
Place this file into the elements/templates/files/ directory on your server.
(Example: elements/templates/files/my_custom_flyer.opub)
Step 2: Register the Template
Next, open the elements/templates/template-index.json file in a text editor. Add a new JSON entry for your template using the following keys:
{
"c": "Flyers",
"n": "My Custom Flyer",
"file": "my_custom_flyer.opub"
}
c (Category) - The exact name of the Category tab the template should appear under (e.g., “Flyers”, “Resumes”, “Business Cards”).
n (Name) - The human-readable display name for the template.
file (Filename) - The exact filename of your .opub file.
Step 3: Refresh the Gallery
Reload Open Publisher and open the Publication Templates gallery. Your new template will automatically appear in the grid under the assigned category, complete with an auto-generated page size badge, and will load flawlessly when clicked.

title: Comprehensive Template Library Visual Overhaul & Modernization
excerpt: Explore the modernized OpenPublisher template library with 289+ overhauled publication designs, interactive resume progress bars, and print-safe rotated image rendering.
content:
Comprehensive Template Library Visual Overhaul & Modernization
A desktop publishing application is only as versatile as the designs you can build with it. Across the v5.14 release cycle (v5.14.1 through v5.14.5) , OpenPublisher conducted a massive visual overhaul and technical modernization of its entire built-in template catalog. With over 289 publication templates indexed across 15 distinct categories, every document was audited and refined with modern typography pairings, normalized box-sizing, print-safe rotated image engines, and live interactive progress bar widgets.
Figure 1: The modernized OpenPublisher template library featuring refined typography, high-definition photography, and structured layouts across multiple publication types.
What Was Modernized Across the Library
Unified Typography & Zero Top-Margin Alignment: Standardized font stacks across all templates, enforcing margin-top: 0 on first-child headings, sub-headings, and paragraphs so text lines stay locked to their expected canvas baselines without awkward vertical offsets.
Nested Media Isolation: Scoped internal image and SVG selectors strictly to direct container children ( .element-content > img ), preventing multi-column cards, portfolio grids, and badges from stretching unintentionally across parent bounding boxes.
Hollow Decorative Frame Click-Through: Elaborate vintage borders, certificate scrolls, and ornamental frames now utilize intelligent interior pass-through. Clicking inside the center of a frame immediately selects the underlying text or photo, while clicking the outer decorative edges selects the frame.
Full-Box Container Normalization: Replaced collapsed zero-height banners and divider divs across 56 templates with explicit width: 100%; height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; styling, ensuring background color accents always render as intended.
Rotated Image Print Precision (v5.14.1)
In earlier desktop publishing releases, photos rotated at playful angles (such as polaroid-style snapshots or tilted menu illustrations) could suffer from clipped borders or truncated corners when exported to PDF or sent to physical printers.
Version 5.14.1 completely overhauled image rotation and print spooling:
Native Element Transforms: Inner rotation transforms are elevated to top-level container elements ( transform: rotate(5deg) ), ensuring rotation is recognized by both the interactive canvas and the physical print engine.
Uncropped Print Overflow: For images that are not clipped into custom shapes, the print engine sets overflow: visible and contain: none , allowing rotated drop shadows and borders to bleed naturally without edge clipping.
Border & Shadow Serialization: Custom frame borders, rounded corners, and soft drop shadows are serialized cleanly into document state, preserving your styling across undo/redo snapshots, page switches, and high-DPI export queues.
Figure 2: Rotated images, tilted illustrations, and decorative frames print with 100% border fidelity without clipping or bounding box truncation.
Functional Progress Bar Widgets in Resumes (v5.14.4)
In professional curriculum vitae and modern resume layouts, skill proficiencies are often represented with horizontal bars. While many software suites render these as static rectangles, OpenPublisher v5.14.4 upgraded all resume templates to use native, interactive Progress Bar Widgets :
Interactive Percentage Dragging: Simply click on any skill bar in a resume template to reveal a drag handle. Slide it left or right to set the exact percentage (e.g., 85% or 95%) with real-time numeric readouts.
Mouse Wheel Adjustment: Hover over any progress bar widget and scroll your mouse wheel to nudge values up or down by 1% increments.
Floating Edit Controls: A dedicated floating Edit Progress Bar pill lets you switch between 71 built-in styles, change theme tints, and apply striped gradient patterns on the fly.
Nostalgic Template Restoration & Asset Swapping (v5.14.5)
Version 5.14.5 restored beloved nostalgic designs from classic desktop publishing history, modernizing them for 2026 print standards:
Classic Lost Dog Flyer: Rebuilt with bold high-contrast headline typography, clear contact rip-off tabs, and a dedicated photo placeholder ready for immediate image replacement.
Chalkboard Restaurant Menu ("The Burger Joint"): Restored with authentic chalkboard background textures, playful angled burger photography, and editable multi-column price lists.
Baby Shower Photography Showcase: Updated with high-resolution, royalty-free photography assets and soft pastel watercolor accents.
Combine Any Template: Remember that you can insert pages from multiple templates into the same working document using the Multi-Page Template Insertion Studio .

title: CSS Color, Gradient & Theme Studio for Templates

content:
CSS Color, Gradient & Theme Studio for Templates
Pre-designed templates are wonderful for getting a publication off the ground quickly, but tailoring them to match your personal taste or brand identity can often feel daunting. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.14.0 , the Template CSS Color, Gradient & Theme Studio transforms how you customize template artwork, headers, and backgrounds. With live multi-stop gradient editing, real-time swatch detection, whole-page palette replacement, and 12 one-click designer themes, you can recolor entire publications in seconds.
Live CSS Variable Resolution: OpenPublisher parses intricate CSS stylesheets, SVG fills, and design tokens automatically. When you click any card, banner, or badge, the studio resolves underlying CSS variables (like var(--ui-theme-color) ) into accessible color pickers, ensuring your changes look uniform across all pages.
Accessing the Studio
OpenPublisher provides three convenient ways to launch the Color & Theme Studio:
The Floating "Colors & Style" Quick-Pill: Whenever you select any CSS-styled template card, banner, or shape, a floating quick-action button labeled Colors & Style appears right alongside your element.
Context Menu: Right-click any styled element on the canvas and choose Customize Colors & CSS Style... from the menu.
Ribbon Integration: When an element is selected, look under the contextual Shape Format , Text Box Tools , or Table Design ribbon tabs. Live color swatches directly reflect the detected colors of your element.
Key Studio Features
Multi-Stop Gradient Editor
Easily create smooth linear or radial gradients. Add or remove color stops, drag stop positions from 0% to 100%, and adjust gradient rotation angles with instant WYSIWYG feedback on the canvas.
Whole-Page Palette Replacement
Want to replace a corporate blue with your organization's emerald green everywhere? The studio scans the active page, gathers all active hues, and lets you swap a color globally across every text box, border, and banner in a single click.
12 Curated Designer Themes
Not sure which colors complement each other? Pick from 12 professionally balanced color schemes (such as Midnight & Gold, Oceanic Teal, Emerald Executive, Cyberpunk Neon, and Rose Gold Luxury) to re-theme your document instantly.
Component-Level Photo & Widget Tuning

Custom Templates Expansion: Holiday, School & Club Showcase

Through OpenPublisher v5.15.6 and v5.16.7 , a suite of beautifully handcrafted, print-ready templates arrived for classrooms, libraries, extracurricular clubs, and seasonal holiday festivities. Backed by an intelligent print engine CORS fix and a lightweight asset architecture, each template delivers rich visual appeal with blazing fast load times.
Figure 1: Newly released custom templates spanning school library schedules, student activity clubs, and holiday celebration certificates.
Featured Custom Templates
Santa's Official Nice List Certificate
A delightful festive award featuring arched OpenPublisher WordArt ("SANTA'S OFFICIAL"), elegant Cinzel Decorative small caps, scalloped gold Santa seals, symmetrical geometric Christmas trees, and gingerbread cookie accents. Includes editable cursive name fields and official signature lines.

Figure 2: The Dear Santa Letter template highlighted within the curated Dashboard Featured carousel, ready for instant editing or printing.
Selective CORS Print Engine Normalization (v5.15.6)
Under strict Chromium browser security rules, setting crossOrigin = 'anonymous' unconditionally on local images or file protocol paths (such as file:/// or relative assets like elements/templates/files/santa_seal.png ) can cause the browser to reject the asset, resulting in missing images on printouts or blank PDF exports.
Version 5.15.6 resolved this with a refined selective CORS pipeline:
The shouldApplyCors(url) Utility: Inspects asset sources dynamically during print spooling and canvas image baking. External HTTP/HTTPS URLs (such as online photo libraries) receive standard anonymous CORS headers, while local application assets, bundled template graphics, and data URIs load directly without triggering security denials.
Lightweight File Architecture: Multi-megabyte raw embedded template files were optimized into clean external PNG assets, shrinking template definitions from over 11 MB down to just 15 KB to 50 KB each for instantaneous canvas rendering.
Interactive Box Containers: Graphic elements are wrapped in standardized interactive box containers ( isImageFallback: true ), ensuring that clicking on any illustration allows easy repositioning, resizing, or layer reordering.
Discovering New Templates: Open the Startup Dashboard and navigate to the Flyers or Certificates tabs, or check the top Featured carousel where these custom additions are pinned for quick access.

title: Export Template Package Modal, Metadata Embedding & ZIP Packaging
excerpt: Learn how to package OpenPublisher publications into shareable template archives (.optpkg / .zip) with embedded metadata, bundled fonts, and graphics.
content:
Export Template Package: Bundling, Metadata & ZIP Distribution
Creating custom publication templates for your business, school, or design team is a great way to ensure brand consistency across documents. Introduced in OpenPublisher v5.17.0 , the Export Template Package Modal provides an automated pipeline to package entire publications into self-contained, shareable template archives ( .optpkg / .zip ) complete with rich metadata, custom color themes, embedded graphics, and font references.
The Export Template Package modal in OpenPublisher v5.17.0, showing metadata fields and automated ZIP asset bundling.
Self-Contained Portability: A template package bundles everything needed to reproduce your layout on another computer, including linked images, master page rules, custom palettes, and thumbnail previews, preventing missing file errors.
How to Export a Template Package
To bundle your active document into a template package, follow these straightforward steps:
Open the publication you want to turn into a template.
Navigate to File > Export > Export Template Package (.optpkg) .
The interactive Template Exporter Modal will appear on screen.
Fill in the descriptive metadata fields (detailed below).
Click Package & Download ZIP . OpenPublisher will generate and download your bundled package.
Embedded Template Metadata
The modal enables you to define comprehensive metadata that displays directly inside the Startup Dashboard when other users import your template:
Metadata Field
Description
Example
Template Title
Clear, user-friendly name of the publication layout.
Quarterly Corporate Newsletter
Category
Dashboard category tab where this template will reside.
Marketing, Flyers, School, Brochures
Author / Organization
The creator, agency, or department who designed the layout.
Acme Communications Dept.
Search Tags
Comma-separated keywords for dashboard search discovery.
annual, finance, teal, report, multi-page
Inside the Generated Archive
The generated .optpkg file is a standard ZIP archive that contains:
template.opub : The primary publication document containing all canvas objects, master pages, and layout geometry.
manifest.json : Machine-readable metadata file storing title, dimensions, category, and author details.
preview.webp : An auto-generated lightweight thumbnail image used in the dashboard gallery.
assets/ : A dedicated subfolder containing high-resolution embedded logos, raster illustrations, and custom clipart.
Importing a Template Package
To import a received .optpkg or template ZIP file, simply drag and drop the archive directly onto the Startup Dashboard or canvas, or go to File > Import Template Package . OpenPublisher automatically unpacks the assets and adds the layout to your personal template library.

title: Exporting, Distributing & Sharing Custom Templates
excerpt: Learn how to package publication designs into reusable template bundles with embedded manifests, layout metadata, and high-fidelity preview thumbnails.
content:
Exporting, Distributing & Sharing Custom Templates
Custom templates enable design studios, educational institutions, and corporate teams to maintain visual consistency across recurring publications such as weekly newsletters, product flyers, menus, and corporate stationery. While Open Publisher allows users to save any active layout directly into local browser storage as a personal template, production workflows require sharing these templates across multiple workstations, design teams, and community galleries. Open Publisher supports an exportable template packaging architecture that encapsulates layout geometry, embedded assets, and metadata into portable template packages.
📑 Custom Template Export Dialog & Manifest Packaging
Package publication designs into portable template bundles with custom metadata and high-DPI thumbnails.
The Template Package Architecture
An Open Publisher template package encapsulates complete publication parameters in a standardized structure:
Template Manifest (manifest.json): Stores metadata including template title, creator name, category classification (e.g., Newsletters, Brochures, Cards, Certificates), descriptive summary, and search tags.
Canvas Geometry & Grid Specs: Records paper format (Letter, A4, Tabloid, custom), orientation, margin guidelines, multi-column snap grids, and bleed dimensions.
Asset Self-Containment: Embedded raster imagery, vector shape coordinates, custom color themes, and typography references are bundled into the package, ensuring the layout opens identically on any target system.
Automated High-DPI Thumbnail Generation
To ensure templates appear prominently in gallery pickers:
Offscreen Canvas Capture: During the export sequence, Open Publisher automatically renders an offscreen high-resolution capture of the front cover spread.
Crisp Gallery Previews: The snapshot is downsampled into a crisp 400x300 preview image bundled directly inside the template archive. When other users browse templates in the Startup Dashboard, preview images display instantly without parsing the full document DOM.
Importing & Distributing Shared Templates
Template packages can be shared across teams via network storage, cloud drives, or email attachments. Recipients can import shared templates by dragging the package file directly onto the Startup Dashboard or selecting Import Template from the Template Gallery. Once imported, the template appears permanently under the Custom Templates section ready for immediate creation.
Tip: Before exporting a template for team distribution, replace specific company or personal details with clear placeholder labels (e.g., "[Your Organization Name]").

title: Multi-Page Template Insertion Studio
excerpt: Combine multiple templates into a single document with OpenPublisher Multi-Page Template Insertion Studio, flexible insertion modes, and context menu integration.
content:
Multi-Page Template Insertion Studio
Open Publisher's Multi-Page Template Insertion Studio allows creators to seamlessly incorporate any of Open Publisher's 270+ professional templates directly into existing multi-page publications. Rather than being restricted to starting with a single template or duplicating identical page layouts, users can now combine diverse templates across different pages of the same document (e.g., combining a newsletter cover, an article layout, a photo spread, and a back-cover brochure).
Non-Destructive Multi-Page Workflows: Previously, selecting a template in traditional publishing suites would overwrite your entire workspace. Open Publisher gives you granular control over where and how each template page is introduced into your publication.
5 Flexible Insertion Modes
The dedicated insertion studio modal ( window.showInsertTemplateModal() ) provides five precise insertion modes:
Insertion Mode
Target Page Action
Resulting Page Order
Ideal Use Case
Insert as New Page (After Target)
Creates a new blank page directly after active page
Target + 1
Default mode: adding a follow-up story or sub-article
Insert as New Page (At End of Document)
Appends a new page at the very end of publication
Final Page (N+1)
Adding back covers, contact forms, or summary pages
Insert as New Page (Before Target)
Creates a new page preceding the selected page
Target Page
Inserting a missed cover or table of contents page
Replace Target Page Content
Clears current elements on active page and applies template
Unchanged
Restyling an existing page without modifying document page count
Append Elements onto Target Page
Preserves existing elements and pastes template on top
Unchanged
Composing hybrid designs (e.g., adding sidebar widgets to a flyer)
Page Dimension & Orientation Handling
When incorporating templates into a publication, Open Publisher provides two intelligent sizing modes:
Use Template Page Size: Preserves the template's authentic dimensions, orientation (Portrait or Landscape), and aspect ratio for the imported page. Open Publisher supports mixed page orientations within the same publication.
Match Target Page Size: Automatically adapts the template elements to fit the current target page's width and height.
Non-Destructive Unique Element IDs & Full History Integration
When a template is inserted, every element receives a freshly generated unique ID, completely preventing ID collisions with existing document elements. The entire insertion registers on Open Publisher's history stack ( pushHistory() ), allowing instant one-click reversal with Ctrl+Z . Instant floating toast notifications confirm the inserted template name and target page destination.
Direct Access Points Across the Interface
Insert Ribbon Tab: Click the dedicated Template button in the Illustrations group.
Minimap Context Menu: Right-click any page thumbnail in the left navigation minimap and select Insert Template Page... .
Canvas Context Menu: Right-click empty canvas space and choose Insert Template Page... .
Standard Template Modal: When browsing templates with an active document open, Open Publisher presents a non-destructive choice dialog ("Insert as New Page", "Apply to Current Page", or "Start Fresh").

title: Template Page Size Badges
excerpt: Instantly identify document formats in the Open Publisher Template Gallery using intelligent page size badges, covering A4, Letter, Square, and video resolutions.
content:
Template Page Size Badges
Starting a new project with the correct canvas dimensions is crucial for ensuring your final design prints correctly or looks sharp on a digital screen. When browsing the Publication Templates Gallery (accessible via the Startup Dashboard or the File menu), you can instantly identify the exact document dimensions of any template before you even click it, thanks to our intelligent Page Size Badges . This eliminates the frustration of opening a great-looking template only to discover it’s the completely wrong aspect ratio for your specific needs.
Identifying Template Formats
Finding a template’s size is incredibly easy at a glance. Look at the bottom-right corner of any template thumbnail preview card in the gallery. You will see a small, semi-transparent teal pill with a sleek frosted-glass effect displaying the page format. This badge is designed to be highly legible without covering up important design details on the thumbnail itself.
-
How the Badges Work
Instead of relying on manually typed descriptions that can sometimes be inaccurate, Open Publisher dynamically scans the internal geometric data of every template as the gallery loads and automatically assigns the correct, verified badge label:
Standard Paper - Essential for physical publishing. The engine automatically recognises and labels standard print formats including A4, Letter, A5, A3, Legal, and Tabloid . If the document is intentionally rotated for a wide layout, it will dynamically display a Landscape suffix (for example, “A4 Landscape”).
Square - Documents built with equal width and height dimensions are labelled cleanly as Square . These templates are perfect for Instagram posts, CD covers, or grid-based digital portfolios.
Video Resolutions - Digital-first templates tailored for screens are recognised by their standard resolution (e.g., 1080p, 4K, 720p ). Portrait variants, such as a tall 1080×1920 design intended for a mobile social media story or digital signage, are accurately labelled with a Portrait suffix.
Custom Sizes - If a template uses a completely custom, non-standard layout (such as a slim web banner, specialized merchandise, or unique fold-out brochure), the badge seamlessly falls back to displaying the raw pixel dimensions (e.g., 632 × 900 ) so you always know exactly what size canvas you are about to open.
Eliminating Guesswork
By bringing this data to the surface of the gallery, Page Size Badges save you the hassle of loading a document, opening the page setup menu just to check its size, and then closing it to find another. You can browse with total confidence knowing the template you choose is technically ready for your final output.

title: Bright Themes, WCAG Contrast Inversion & High-Luminance Adaptation
excerpt: Discover how Open Publisher dynamically adapts its user interface for high-luminance themes using WCAG contrast inversion and desktop window clearance.
content:
Bright Themes, WCAG Contrast Inversion & High-Luminance Adaptation
Personalizing application aesthetics with vibrant colors enhances focus and workflow enjoyment. However, when users select high-luminance UI accent colors (such as Canary Yellow, Lime Green, Peach, or Warm Gold), standard user interface conventions can fail: white header text, light logos, and translucent buttons quickly become illegible against bright backgrounds. Version 4.17.2 introduced intelligent high-luminance adaptation to Open Publisher, enabling real-time Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) contrast inversion across the Startup Dashboard, modals, contextual toolbars, and desktop client titlebars.
☀️ Bright Theme Dynamic Contrast Inversion & Ghost Buttons High-luminance themes automatically invert foreground typography and logos to dark charcoal for maximum contrast.
The .bright-theme Global State
To preserve accessibility across more than 700 theme combinations, Open Publisher evaluates the perceptual luminance of the active palette:
Automated Luminance Calculation: When a user auditions or applies a theme in the Theme Studio, the color engine calculates relative luminance using standard sRGB coefficients.
Global Class Activation: If the calculated background luminance exceeds predefined accessibility thresholds, the application attaches the .bright-theme class to the document root, triggering coordinated CSS overrides across all UI layers.
Dynamic WCAG Contrast Inversion
Under the .bright-theme state, critical interface elements adapt automatically:
Logo & Header Typography: The application brand logo and primary title text flip dynamically from white to dark charcoal ( #111111 ), guaranteeing compliance with WCAG AAA contrast ratios.
Ghost Button Styling: Primary action triggers (such as the "Skip / Open Editor" button in the Startup Dashboard) transition from solid white fills into high-contrast ghost buttons with dark borders and crisp charcoal typography.
Close Controls & Sidebar Highlights: The modal close button ( .custom-dialog-close ) adopts a dark translucent pill styling while preserving its red hover state. Active sidebar navigation links invert their label text to dark gray when highlighted by bright accent colors.
Native Desktop Drag Zone Clearance
In standalone desktop client wrappers (such as NW.js or Electron), modal dialogs must coexist with operating system window frames. Version 4.17.2 tuned the dashboard positioning to a top offset of 7vh and maximum height of 88vh . This ensures the modal never obstructs native window controls (such as Windows minimize/maximize/close icons or macOS window traffic lights) regardless of display scaling.
Tip: You can preview how your publication canvas looks against both bright accent themes and Dark Mode by opening the UI Themes dialog from the View tab.

title: Dark Mode
excerpt: Enable Dark Mode in Open Publisher for a sleek, eye-comfortable dark interface that intelligently adapts icons, sidebars, scrollbars, and menus to your chosen theme.
content:
Dark Mode
Open Publisher includes a full Dark Mode that transforms the entire application interface into a sleek, eye-comfortable dark palette. The Dark Mode engine is deeply integrated throughout every part of the application - the ribbon, sidebars, canvases, rulers, context menus, modals, and scrollbars all adapt automatically.
Enabling Dark Mode
Toggle Dark Mode directly from the ribbon. The entire interface smoothly transitions to a dark grey palette ranging from #1a1a1a to #2d2d2d . Toggle it off at any time to return to the standard light interface.
Intelligent Icon Brightening
Standard dark UI elements are not legible against a dark ribbon. Open Publisher’s Dark Mode engine automatically boosts the brightness and saturation of all ribbon icons, labels, and dropdowns by 1.5x when Dark Mode is active, keeping your chosen theme colours rich and vivid while maximising legibility against the dark background.
Pitch-Black Theme Support
Ultra-dark themes such as Midnight Dark or Notion Black include special fallback logic. Rather than letting elements like the UI Theme label, moon icon, and colour scheme text vanish into the dark ribbon, the engine forcefully snaps them to a crisp #e0e0e0 white - guaranteeing every element remains legible even at the most extreme end of the darkness spectrum.
Adaptive Scrollbars
The scrollbar engine is fully rebuilt for Dark Mode:
The scrollbar track flips to dark grey ( #2d2d2d ) in Dark Mode to match the app UI.
Extreme dark themes force the scrollbar drag handle to a clearly visible #777 grey, so it is never invisible against the dark track.
Bright and neon themes gracefully drop to a translucent dark-grey drag handle in Light Mode so they remain visible, while retaining their vivid theme colours in Dark Mode.
What Adapts in Dark Mode
Dark Mode is applied comprehensively across the entire application. Every major UI surface is covered:
Ribbon & Toolbar - The main ribbon, contextual tabs (Text Box Tools, Picture Tools, WordArt Tools, Table Design, Drawing Tools), and the floating text editing toolbar all adopt the dark grey background automatically.
Sidebars - The Format Picture sidebar, Graphics Manager, Selection Pane, WordArt pane, and all other side panels replace their light-grey backgrounds with the dark acrylic panel colour.
Right-Click Context Menus - All custom context menus switch to dark backgrounds with native hover states, subtle divider lines, and dimmed disabled states.
Modal Windows - Dialogs including the Accessibility Checker, Custom Colour Picker, Clipart Gallery, Export as Image dialog, and Insert Symbol modal all adapt to dark panel backgrounds, dark inputs, and themed borders.
Clipart Gallery - The gallery grid background, search bar, and section dividers all switch to the dark palette, eliminating white gaps between sections.
Custom Colour Picker - The colour picker window, tabs, hex input, RGB spinners, swatches, and gradient canvas all inherit dark mode styling.
Delete Buttons - Delete buttons automatically brighten to a readable pastel red in Dark Mode, ensuring they remain clearly visible against the dark ribbon.
Dropdown Menus - Ribbon dropdowns dynamically detect if they would render outside the browser window and invert their alignment to stay fully on-screen.
Bright Theme Compatibility
Dark Mode works in combination with all 100+ UI themes, including high-brightness themes like Snapchat Yellow. When a bright theme is active alongside Dark Mode, the engine detects the conflict and intelligently inverts text colours on buttons, labels, and navigation items to maintain strict contrast - so you never end up with white text on a yellow button or dark text disappearing into a dark panel.
